overview.main_flow_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Program Start]):::start

    P1[1: Program Initialization
Initialize working storage,
set transaction ID, clear error messages]:::process

    P2[2: Communication Area Processing
Restore session context from commarea
or initialize fresh context]:::process

    P37[37: Function Key Capture
Identify which function key
was pressed by user]:::process

    P3[3: PF Key Validation
Validate function key is appropriate
for current screen state]:::process

    P4[4: State Reset on Completion
Reset screen state to initial entry
mode on completion conditions]:::process

    D_PFK03{F3 Pressed?
Exit to Calling Program?}:::decision

    P5[5: Exit and Return to Calling Program
Navigate back to admin menu
or list screen via XCTL]:::process

    D_INITIAL{New Session or
First Entry?}:::decision

    P6[6: Initial Screen Display
Clear all data and display
empty transaction type search screen]:::process

    D_PFK04_CONFIRM{F4 Pressed AND
Delete Confirmation
State?}:::decision

    P7[7: Delete Confirmation Processing
Execute actual deletion of
transaction type record]:::process

    DB_DELETE[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
DB2 Table)]:::datasource

    D_PFK04_SHOW{F4 Pressed AND
Showing Details?}:::decision

    P8[8: Delete Confirmation Request
Prompt user to confirm
deletion before proceeding]:::process

    D_PFK05_NOTFOUND{F5 Pressed AND
Record Not Found?}:::decision

    P9[9: New Record Creation Initiation
Transition to new record
creation mode]:::process

    D_PFK05_CONFIRMED{F5 Pressed AND
Changes Confirmed?}:::decision

    P10[10: Save Confirmed Changes
Execute database write
update or insert]:::process

    D_PFK12_CANCEL{F12 Pressed AND
Confirmation or
Detail State?}:::decision

    P11[11: Cancel Action
Cancel pending action and
return to prior state]:::process

    D_INVALID{Invalid Key
Pressed?}:::decision

    P12[12: Invalid Key Handling
Redisplay current screen
with invalid key message]:::process

    P13[13: User Input Processing
Receive input, store values,
perform validation edits]:::process

    P14[14: Receive Screen Input
Accept and capture all field
values from screen map]:::process

    P15[15: Store Screen Input to Working Variables
Transfer screen field values
into internal working storage]:::process

    P16[16: Transaction Type Code Validation
Validate code is numeric,
non-blank, non-zero; format with leading zeros]:::process

    P17[17: Transaction Description Validation
Validate description is supplied
and contains only alphanumeric characters]:::process

    P18[18: Change Detection
Compare new values against
originally fetched values]:::process

    P19[19: Action Decision Logic
Determine next appropriate action
based on state flags and user actions]:::process

    P20[20: Transaction Type Lookup
Query TRANSACTION_TYPE table
using entered type code]:::process

    DB_READ[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
DB2 Table)]:::datasource

    P21[21: Store Fetched Transaction Type Data
Save retrieved type code and
description into old-details storage]:::process

    D_FOUND{Record
Found?}:::decision

    P22[22: Transaction Type Update
Execute SQL UPDATE to modify
transaction type description]:::process

    DB_UPDATE[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
DB2 Table)]:::datasource

    D_UPDATE_RESULT{Update
Result?}:::decision

    P23[23: Transaction Type Insert
Execute SQL INSERT to create
new transaction type record]:::process

    DB_INSERT[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
DB2 Table)]:::datasource

    P24[24: Transaction Type Delete
Execute SQL DELETE to remove
transaction type record]:::process

    DB_DEL[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
DB2 Table)]:::datasource

    D_DELETE_RESULT{Delete
Result?}:::decision

    P25[25: Screen Initialization
Prepare output screen with date,
time, program name, transaction ID]:::process

    P26[26: Screen Variable Setup
Populate screen fields with
appropriate data based on state]:::process

    P27[27: Information Message Setup
Determine and set appropriate
informational message for user]:::process

    P28[28: Screen Field Attribute Setup
Set field protection attributes
and cursor position]:::process

    P29[29: Screen Color Attribute Setup
Set color attributes to
highlight errors in red]:::process

    P30[30: PF Key Attribute Setup
Enable or disable available
function key options on screen]:::process

    P31[31: Send Screen to User
Transmit fully prepared screen
map to user terminal]:::process

    P34[34: Session State Persistence
Save current program state
and commarea before returning to CICS]:::process

    P35[35: Concurrent Update Conflict Handling
Detect record locked by another user
and inform user to retry]:::process

    LOCK_ERROR[Lock Error:
Record could not be updated
due to concurrent access conflict]:::error

    DELETE_SUCCESS[Delete Successful:
Transaction type record
has been deleted]:::success

    DELETE_CHILD_ERROR[Delete Failed:
Please delete associated
child records first]:::error

    UPDATE_SUCCESS[Save Successful:
Transaction type record
has been updated or created]:::success

    RETURN_END([Return to CICS
Await Next User Interaction]):::final

    EXIT_END([Exit to Calling Program
Admin Menu or List Screen]):::final

rules.rule_name: Program Initialization and Working Storage Setup
rules.rule_description: On every entry to the Transaction Type Update screen, the program initializes all working storage areas, sets the current transaction identifier, and clears any prior error messages to ensure a clean processing environment.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Initialization
Initialize working storage,
set transaction ID, clear error messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program is invoked by CICS
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: All working storage areas (CC-WORK-AREA, WS-MISC-STORAGE, WS-COMMAREA) are initialized to their default values, the transaction ID is set to the current transaction literal (LIT-THISTRANID), and the return message flag is set to OFF (no error message displayed)

rules.rule_name: Session Context Restoration from Communication Area
rules.rule_description: Determines whether to restore a prior session's state from the communication area or initialize a completely fresh context, based on whether this is a first-time entry or a return from another program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Communication Area Processing
Restore session context from commarea
or initialize fresh context

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The communication area length (EIBCALEN) is zero (no prior session), OR the calling program is the Admin program (LIT-ADMINPGM) and the program-reenter flag is NOT set, OR the calling program is the List program (LIT-LISTTPGM) and the program-reenter flag is NOT set
acceptance_criteria.Then: Both CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA are initialized to defaults, the program-enter flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is set to TRUE, and the details-not-fetched flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) is set to TRUE; OTHERWISE the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA is restored from the first portion of DFHCOMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA is restored from the second portion of DFHCOMMAREA

rules.rule_name: Function Key Identification from Terminal Input
rules.rule_description: Captures and identifies which function key the user pressed on the terminal by mapping the CICS attention identifier (EIBAID) to a named program flag for subsequent processing logic.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
37: Function Key Capture
Identify which function key
was pressed by user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed a key on the terminal and control has returned to the program
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the EIBAID value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The corresponding program flag is set to TRUE: ENTER key sets CCARD-AID-ENTER, CLEAR sets CCARD-AID-CLEAR, PA1 sets CCARD-AID-PA1, PA2 sets CCARD-AID-PA2, PF1/PF13 sets CCARD-AID-PFK01, PF2/PF14 sets CCARD-AID-PFK02, PF3/PF15 sets CCARD-AID-PFK03, PF4/PF16 sets CCARD-AID-PFK04, PF5/PF17 sets CCARD-AID-PFK05, PF6/PF18 sets CCARD-AID-PFK06, PF7/PF19 sets CCARD-AID-PFK07, PF8/PF20 sets CCARD-AID-PFK08, PF9/PF21 sets CCARD-AID-PFK09, PF10/PF22 sets CCARD-AID-PFK10, PF11/PF23 sets CCARD-AID-PFK11, PF12/PF24 sets CCARD-AID-PFK12

rules.rule_name: Valid Function Key Combinations per Screen State
rules.rule_description: Enforces that only contextually appropriate function keys are accepted for the current screen state. Keys that are not valid for the current state are rejected with an invalid key indicator.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: PF Key Validation
Validate function key is appropriate
for current screen state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed a function key and the current screen state is known
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the pressed key against the current state
acceptance_criteria.Then: PFK-VALID is set to TRUE if any of the following conditions are met: (1) PF3 is pressed (always valid), (2) ENTER is pressed AND the state is NOT Confirm-Delete, (3) PF4 is pressed AND state is Show-Details OR Confirm-Delete, (4) PF5 is pressed AND state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Details-Not-Found OR Delete-In-Progress, (5) PF12 is pressed AND state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Show-Details OR Details-Not-Found OR Confirm-Delete OR Create-New-Record; OTHERWISE PFK-INVALID is set to TRUE and if no prior return message exists, WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED is set to TRUE

rules.rule_name: Automatic State Reset After Terminal Operations
rules.rule_description: After certain terminal conditions (completed operations, failures, or cancellations), the program automatically resets the screen state back to the initial entry mode so the user starts fresh.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: State Reset on Completion
Reset screen state to initial entry
mode on completion conditions

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has evaluated the pressed key and current state
acceptance_criteria.When: Any of the following conditions are true: (1) PF12 is pressed AND state is Show-Details OR Create-New-Record OR Details-Not-Found, (2) state is Changes-Okayed-And-Done, (3) state is Changes-Failed, (4) state is Changes-Backed-Out AND old details are LOW-VALUES or SPACES, (5) state is Delete-Done, (6) state is Delete-Failed
acceptance_criteria.Then: CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is set to TRUE and TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is set to TRUE, resetting the screen to initial search mode

rules.rule_name: Exit and Return to Calling Program via PF3
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3, the program exits and transfers control back to the originating program (Admin menu or List screen), committing any pending database changes before navigating away.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Exit and Return to Calling Program
Navigate back to admin menu
or list screen via XCTL

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user presses PF3 on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: PF3 is detected as the pressed key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If CDEMO-FROM-TRANID is LOW-VALUES or SPACES, the destination transaction is set to LIT-ADMINTRANID; otherwise it is set to CDEMO-FROM-TRANID. If CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is LOW-VALUES or SPACES, the destination program is set to LIT-ADMINPGM; otherwise it is set to CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM. The current transaction (LIT-THISTRANID) and program (LIT-THISPGM) are recorded as the source. CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is set to TRUE, CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is set to TRUE, the current mapset and map are saved, a database SYNCPOINT (commit) is issued, and control is transferred (XCTL) to the destination program with the communication area

rules.rule_name: Initial Empty Search Screen Display on First Entry
rules.rule_description: On first entry or after a full reset, the program displays a blank Transaction Type search screen, clearing all prior data and prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Initial Screen Display
Clear all data and display
empty transaction type search screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in first-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE) AND the state is Details-Not-Fetched
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the entry condition as a new session
acceptance_criteria.Then: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, WS-MISC-STORAGE, and CDEMO-ACCT-ID are all initialized to defaults; the send-map routine is performed to display an empty screen with a prompt for the user to enter a Transaction Type code; CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is set to TRUE and TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is set to TRUE before returning to CICS

rules.rule_name: Delete Confirmation Request on First PF4 Press
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF4 while a Transaction Type record is displayed, the program does not immediately delete but instead transitions to a confirmation state, requiring the user to press PF4 a second time to confirm the deletion.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Delete Confirmation Request
Prompt user to confirm
deletion before proceeding

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record is currently displayed on screen (state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF4
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen state is changed to TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE and the screen is redisplayed with a delete confirmation prompt message, awaiting the user's confirmation or cancellation

rules.rule_name: Delete Execution on Second PF4 Press (Confirmed Delete)
rules.rule_description: When the user confirms deletion by pressing PF4 a second time while in the Confirm-Delete state, the program executes the actual deletion of the Transaction Type record from the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Delete Confirmation Processing
Execute actual deletion of
transaction type record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is in Confirm-Delete state (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF4 again to confirm
acceptance_criteria.Then: TTUP-START-DELETE is set to TRUE, the delete processing routine (9800-DELETE-PROCESSING) is performed, and the screen is redisplayed with the result

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Record Deletion from Database
rules.rule_description: Executes the physical deletion of a Transaction Type record from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the stored original type code, and handles all possible outcomes including success, referential integrity violations, and other failures.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
24: Transaction Type Delete
Execute SQL DELETE to remove
transaction type record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The delete operation has been confirmed and TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE contains the Transaction Type code to be deleted
acceptance_criteria.When: A SQL DELETE is executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE WHERE TR_TYPE = the stored original type code
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the delete succeeds (SQLCODE = 0): TTUP-DELETE-DONE is set to TRUE and the transaction is committed (SYNCPOINT); If the delete fails because child records exist (SQLCODE = -532): RECORD-DELETE-FAILED is set to TRUE and the message 'Please delete associated child records first: SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is displayed; If the delete fails for any other reason: RECORD-DELETE-FAILED and TTUP-DELETE-FAILED are both set to TRUE and the message 'Delete failed with message: SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is displayed

rules.rule_name: New Record Creation Mode Initiation via PF5
rules.rule_description: When a search returns no matching Transaction Type record and the user presses PF5, the program transitions to new record creation mode, allowing the user to enter details for the new Transaction Type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: New Record Creation Initiation
Transition to new record
creation mode

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is Details-Not-Found (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF5
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen state is changed to TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD and the screen is redisplayed prompting the user to enter the new Transaction Type data (description)

rules.rule_name: Save Confirmed Changes via PF5
rules.rule_description: When the user has reviewed validated changes and presses PF5 to confirm, the program executes the database write operation (update or insert) to persist the Transaction Type data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Save Confirmed Changes
Execute database write
update or insert

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE), meaning the user's input has passed validation and is awaiting final confirmation
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF5 to confirm the save
acceptance_criteria.Then: The write processing routine (9600-WRITE-PROCESSING) is performed, followed by redisplaying the screen with the result of the save operation

rules.rule_name: Cancel Pending Action and Refresh via PF12
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF12 while in a confirmation or detail-viewing state, the program cancels the pending action and re-fetches the original record from the database to restore the prior state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Cancel Action
Cancel pending action and
return to prior state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user presses PF12 AND the current state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Confirm-Delete OR Show-Details
acceptance_criteria.When: PF12 is detected and the state qualifies for cancellation
acceptance_criteria.Then: FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE is set to TRUE, the action decision logic (2000-DECIDE-ACTION) is performed to re-fetch the original record from the database, and the screen is redisplayed with the original values; if the state was Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed, WS-UPDATE-WAS-CANCELLED is set; if the state was Confirm-Delete, WS-DELETE-WAS-CANCELLED is set

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Press Handling and Screen Redisplay
rules.rule_description: When the user presses a function key that is not valid for the current screen state, the program redisplays the current screen unchanged with an invalid key message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: Invalid Key Handling
Redisplay current screen
with invalid key message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed a function key
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed is not valid for the current screen state (WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is redisplayed as-is with the invalid key message shown to the user; no data processing or state changes occur

rules.rule_name: User Input Processing Sequence
rules.rule_description: Orchestrates the complete sequence of receiving screen input, storing it to working variables, and performing all validation edits when the user presses ENTER or another valid key for normal processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: User Input Processing
Receive input, store values,
perform validation edits

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER or a valid key that triggers normal input processing (not PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12, or an invalid key)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program routes to the input processing path
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following sequence is performed in order: (1) receive screen map input (1100-RECEIVE-MAP), (2) store screen values to working variables (1150-STORE-MAP-IN-NEW), (3) perform all validation edits (1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS); after processing, the current program name, mapset, and map are set as the next navigation targets

rules.rule_name: Screen Map Input Reception
rules.rule_description: Receives and captures all field values entered by the user from the screen map into the program's input area for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: Receive Screen Input
Accept and capture all field
values from screen map

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the screen with data entered
acceptance_criteria.When: The receive map operation is executed for the current map (LIT-THISMAP) and mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) into CTRTUPAI
acceptance_criteria.Then: All screen field values entered by the user are captured into the CTRTUPAI input area and response codes are stored in WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD for subsequent processing

rules.rule_name: Screen Input Storage to Working Variables
rules.rule_description: Transfers the captured screen field values into internal working storage variables, handling special input values and preserving search context when appropriate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Store Screen Input to Working Variables
Transfer screen field values
into internal working storage

acceptance_criteria.Given: Screen input has been received into CTRTUPAI
acceptance_criteria.When: The store-map-in-new routine (1150-STORE-MAP-IN-NEW) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: Special case: if the state is Details-Not-Found AND PF5 was NOT pressed AND the trimmed value of TRTYPCDI equals the previously stored TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, skip re-storing (preserve existing context); Otherwise: TTUP-NEW-DETAILS is initialized, then if TRTYPCDI is '*' or SPACES it is stored as LOW-VALUES in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, else the trimmed value is stored; if TRTYDSCI is '*' or SPACES it is stored as LOW-VALUES in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, else the trimmed value is stored

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Validation Rules
rules.rule_description: Validates that the entered Transaction Type code meets all business rules: it must be provided, must be numeric, must not be zero, and is automatically formatted with leading zeros to ensure consistent 2-digit representation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16: Transaction Type Code Validation
Validate code is numeric,
non-blank, non-zero; format with leading zeros

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a value in the Transaction Type Code field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction type code validation routine (1210-EDIT-TRANTYPE) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The field label 'Tran Type code' is used in all error messages; (1) If the value is blank, LOW-VALUES, or empty (trimmed length = 0): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK is set, and the message '[field] must be supplied.' is generated; (2) If the value is not numeric (TEST-NUMVAL fails): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK is set, and the message '[field] must be numeric.' is generated; (3) If the numeric value equals zero: INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK is set, and the message '[field] must not be zero.' is generated; (4) If all validations pass: FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID) is set to TRUE and the numeric value is computed, converted to a 2-character string, spaces replaced with zeros (zero-padded), and stored back into TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Description Validation Rules
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Transaction Type description is provided and contains only alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers), enforcing data quality for the description field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17: Transaction Description Validation
Validate description is supplied
and contains only alphanumeric characters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the Transaction Type Description field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) and changes have been detected
acceptance_criteria.When: The alphanumeric required validation routine (1230-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD) is performed with field label 'Transaction Desc' and maximum length 50
acceptance_criteria.Then: (1) If the value is blank, LOW-VALUES, or empty (trimmed length = 0): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK is set, and the message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' is generated; (2) If the value contains non-alphanumeric characters (after converting all valid alphanumeric characters to spaces, the trimmed result is non-empty): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK is set, and the message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' is generated; (3) If all validations pass: FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID is set to TRUE; the validation result flags are stored in WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAGS; if INPUT-ERROR is not set, TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is set to TRUE

rules.rule_name: Change Detection Between Original and New Values
rules.rule_description: Compares the user's newly entered values against the originally fetched database values to determine whether any actual changes have been made, preventing unnecessary database updates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18: Change Detection
Compare new values against
originally fetched values

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both old details (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE, TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) and new details (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) are available
acceptance_criteria.When: The compare old-new routine (1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: NO-CHANGES-FOUND is set initially; if the UPPER-CASE of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE equals UPPER-CASE of TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE AND the UPPER-CASE of trimmed TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC equals UPPER-CASE of trimmed TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC AND the trimmed lengths are equal: if no prior return message exists, NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is set to TRUE; otherwise if any difference is found: if no prior return message exists, CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED is set to TRUE and processing continues to description validation; if NO-CHANGES-FOUND or TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED or TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE is true, WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS are cleared and validation exits

rules.rule_name: Action Decision Logic Based on State and Input
rules.rule_description: Evaluates the current program state and input results to determine the next appropriate action, orchestrating state transitions for the Transaction Type maintenance workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
19: Action Decision Logic
Determine next appropriate action
based on state flags and user actions

acceptance_criteria.Given: Input processing and validation have completed and the current state flags are set
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision routine (2000-DECIDE-ACTION) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following state transitions apply: (1) If state is Details-Not-Fetched OR PF12 was pressed: if FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID, perform database lookup (9000-READ-TRANTYPE) and set Show-Details if found or Details-Not-Found if not found; if NOT valid: if Confirm-Delete state, set WS-DELETE-WAS-CANCELLED and Details-Not-Fetched; if Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed state, set WS-UPDATE-WAS-CANCELLED and Changes-Backed-Out; otherwise set Details-Not-Fetched; (2) If Show-Details: if INPUT-ERROR or NO-CHANGES-DETECTED or WS-INVALID-KEY, keep current state; else set Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed; (3) If Changes-Not-OK: no state change; (4) If Changes-Backed-Out: set Changes-Not-OK; (5) If Invalid-Search-Keys: no state change; (6) If PF5 and Details-Not-Found: set Create-New-Record; (7) If Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed: no state change; (8) If Changes-Okayed-And-Done: set Show-Details and if no calling transaction context, clear CDEMO-ACCT-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM to zeroes and CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS to LOW-VALUES

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Database Lookup by Type Code
rules.rule_description: Queries the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table to retrieve the Transaction Type record matching the entered type code, determining whether the record exists for subsequent display or update operations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
20: Transaction Type Lookup
Query TRANSACTION_TYPE table
using entered type code

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid Transaction Type code is stored in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE and has been moved to DCL-TR-TYPE
acceptance_criteria.When: A SQL SELECT is executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE retrieving TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION WHERE TR_TYPE equals the entered type code
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the record is found (SQLCODE = 0): FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE is set to TRUE; if the record is not found (SQLCODE = +100): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and if no prior message exists WS-RECORD-NOT-FOUND message is set; if a database error occurs (SQLCODE < 0): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and the message 'Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is generated

rules.rule_name: Store Fetched Transaction Type Data as Original Values
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving a Transaction Type record from the database, stores the fetched values as the 'original' baseline data to enable change detection and screen display of original values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
21: Store Fetched Transaction Type Data
Save retrieved type code and
description into old-details storage

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been successfully retrieved from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
acceptance_criteria.When: The store-fetched-data routine (9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: TTUP-OLD-DETAILS is initialized to defaults, then DCL-TR-TYPE is moved to TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE, and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT (trimmed to the actual length specified by DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN) is moved to TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Description Update in Database
rules.rule_description: Executes a SQL UPDATE to modify the description of an existing Transaction Type record in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table, handling all possible outcomes including success, record not found (triggers insert), and lock conflicts.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
22: Transaction Type Update
Execute SQL UPDATE to modify
transaction type description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed changes and TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE contains the type code and TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC contains the new description; DCL-TR-TYPE is set from TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT is set from trimmed TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN is computed as the length of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC
acceptance_criteria.When: A SQL UPDATE is executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE setting TR_DESCRIPTION = DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION WHERE TR_TYPE = DCL-TR-TYPE
acceptance_criteria.Then: If update succeeds (SQLCODE = 0): the transaction is committed (SYNCPOINT) and TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE is set; if no row was updated (SQLCODE = +100): the insert routine (9700-INSERT-RECORD) is performed; if the record is locked (SQLCODE = -911): INPUT-ERROR is set, COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE is set, and TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR is set; if any other error (SQLCODE < 0): TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED is set, TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED is set, and the message 'Error updating: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is generated

rules.rule_name: New Transaction Type Record Insertion into Database
rules.rule_description: When an UPDATE finds no existing record (the type code does not exist in the database), executes a SQL INSERT to create a new Transaction Type record with the provided type code and description.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
23: Transaction Type Insert
Execute SQL INSERT to create
new transaction type record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The UPDATE operation returned no rows found (SQLCODE = +100), indicating the Transaction Type code does not yet exist in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
acceptance_criteria.When: A SQL INSERT is executed into CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE with values (DCL-TR-TYPE, DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the insert succeeds (SQLCODE = 0): the transaction is committed (SYNCPOINT) and TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE is set; if the insert fails for any other reason: TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED is set and the message 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is generated

rules.rule_name: Concurrent Update Lock Conflict Detection and Handling
rules.rule_description: Detects when a Transaction Type record cannot be updated because it is currently locked by another user's concurrent access, and informs the user of the conflict.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
35: Concurrent Update Conflict Handling
Detect record locked by another user
and inform user to retry

acceptance_criteria.Given: A SQL UPDATE is attempted on CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
acceptance_criteria.When: The update fails with a lock conflict (SQLCODE = -911)
acceptance_criteria.Then: INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE, COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE is set to TRUE (if no prior return message exists), and TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR is set to TRUE; the screen is redisplayed with a failure message informing the user that the record could not be updated due to a concurrent access conflict

rules.rule_name: Screen Header Initialization with Date, Time, and Program Identity
rules.rule_description: Initializes the output screen map with standard header information including the current date, current time, program name, and transaction ID before populating business data fields.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
25: Screen Initialization
Prepare output screen with date,
time, program name, transaction ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is preparing to send a screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (3100-SCREEN-INIT) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The output area CTRTUPAO is set to LOW-VALUES; the current date and time are obtained; CCDA-TITLE01 is moved to TITLE01O, CCDA-TITLE02 is moved to TITLE02O, LIT-THISTRANID is moved to TRNNAMEO, LIT-THISPGM is moved to PGMNAMEO; the current date is formatted as MM/DD/YY and moved to CURDATEO; the current time is formatted as HH:MM:SS and moved to CURTIMEO

rules.rule_name: Screen Field Population Based on Program State
rules.rule_description: Determines which set of values (blank, original database values, or user-entered new values) to display in the screen fields based on the current program state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
26: Screen Variable Setup
Populate screen fields with
appropriate data based on state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen variable setup routine (3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: If CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE: no field values are set (blank screen); Otherwise based on state: (1) Details-Not-Fetched: show initial blank values (LOW-VALUES in TRTYPCDO); (2) Show-Details, Confirm-Delete, Delete-Failed, Delete-Done, Changes-Backed-Out: initialize TTUP-NEW-DETAILS and display ORIGINAL values (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE to TRTYPCDO, TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC to TRTYDSCO); (3) Changes-Made, Changes-Not-OK, Details-Not-Found, Invalid-Search-Keys, Create-New-Record, Changes-Okayed-And-Done: display NEW/user-entered values (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE to TRTYPCDO, TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC to TRTYDSCO); (4) Any other state: initialize TTUP-NEW-DETAILS and display original values

rules.rule_name: Informational Message Selection and Display Based on State
rules.rule_description: Selects and formats the appropriate informational guidance message for the user based on the current screen state, centering it on the screen for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
27: Information Message Setup
Determine and set appropriate
informational message for user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display and the current state is known
acceptance_criteria.When: The information message setup routine (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message is selected based on state: CDEMO-PGM-ENTER OR Details-Not-Fetched OR Invalid-Search-Keys → PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS; Details-Not-Found → PROMPT-CREATE-NEW-RECORD; Show-Details OR Changes-Backed-Out with no old type code → PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS; Changes-Backed-Out OR Changes-Not-OK → PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES; Confirm-Delete → PROMPT-DELETE-CONFIRM; Delete-Failed → INFORM-FAILURE; Delete-Done → CONFIRM-DELETE-SUCCESS; Create-New-Record → PROMPT-FOR-NEWDATA; Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed → PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION; Changes-Okayed-And-Done → CONFIRM-UPDATE-SUCCESS; Changes-Okayed-Lock-Error OR Changes-Okayed-But-Failed → INFORM-FAILURE; No-Info-Message → PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS; The selected message is trimmed, its length and midpoint are computed, and it is centered in WS-STRING-OUT before being moved to INFOMSGO; WS-RETURN-MSG is moved to ERRMSGO

rules.rule_name: Screen Field Protection and Cursor Positioning Based on State
rules.rule_description: Controls which screen fields are editable versus protected (read-only) and positions the cursor at the appropriate field based on the current program state and validation results.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
28: Screen Field Attribute Setup
Set field protection attributes
and cursor position

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields are first set to protected (DFHBMPRF) via 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS (TRTYPCDA, TRTYDSCA, INFOMSGA); Then field protection is adjusted: if state is Details-Not-Fetched OR Invalid-Search-Keys OR Details-Not-Found OR (Changes-Backed-Out with no old type code): TRTYPCDA is set to DFHBMFSE (editable); if state is Show-Details OR Changes-Not-OK OR Create-New-Record OR Changes-Backed-Out (with old data): TRTYDSCA is set to DFHBMFSE (editable) and INFOMSGA is set to DFHBMPRF via 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS; Cursor position (-1) is set: to TRTYPCDL when state is Details-Not-Fetched OR Details-Not-Found OR Invalid-Search-Keys OR filter errors OR Changes-Okayed-And-Done OR Changes-Backed-Out with no old data; to TRTYDSCL when state is Create-New-Record OR No-Changes-Detected OR Description errors OR Changes-Made OR Changes-Backed-Out OR Show-Details; to TRTYPCDL for all other states

rules.rule_name: Error Field Color Highlighting in Red
rules.rule_description: Sets the color of screen fields to red to visually highlight error conditions, drawing the user's attention to fields that require correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
29: Screen Color Attribute Setup
Set color attributes to
highlight errors in red

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) evaluates error conditions
acceptance_criteria.Then: If FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE OR TTUP-DELETE-FAILED is TRUE: TRTYPCDC (color attribute of Transaction Type Code field) is set to DFHRED (red); If FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK is TRUE AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE: TRTYPCDO (display value of Transaction Type Code field) is set to '*' as a placeholder AND TRTYPCDC is set to DFHRED (red)

rules.rule_name: Function Key Availability Display Based on Screen State
rules.rule_description: Controls the visual appearance of function key labels on the screen, highlighting available keys and dimming unavailable ones based on the current program state to guide the user on valid actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
30: PF Key Attribute Setup
Enable or disable available
function key options on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The PF key attribute setup routine (3391-SETUP-PFKEY-ATTRS) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: If state is Confirm-Delete: FKEYSA (all PF key labels area) is set to DFHBMDAR (dark/dimmed); otherwise FKEYSA is set to DFHBMASB (bright/visible); If state is Show-Details OR Confirm-Delete: FKEY04A (PF4 label) is set to DFHBMASB (bright/active); If state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Details-Not-Found: FKEY05A (PF5 label) is set to DFHBMASB (bright/active); If state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Show-Details OR Details-Not-Found OR Confirm-Delete OR Create-New-Record: FKEY12A (PF12 label) is set to DFHBMASB (bright/active)

rules.rule_name: Screen Transmission to User Terminal
rules.rule_description: Transmits the fully prepared screen map to the user's terminal, erasing the prior screen content and freeing the keyboard for user input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
31: Send Screen to User
Transmit fully prepared screen
map to user terminal

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen map (CTRTUPAO) has been fully populated with data, messages, and field attributes
acceptance_criteria.When: The send screen routine (3400-SEND-SCREEN) is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: LIT-THISMAPSET is moved to CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and LIT-THISMAP is moved to CCARD-NEXT-MAP; a CICS SEND MAP command is issued with the map name, mapset name, FROM CTRTUPAO, with CURSOR positioning, ERASE (clear prior screen), and FREEKB (unlock keyboard) options; response codes are stored in WS-RESP-CD

rules.rule_name: Session State Persistence Before Returning to CICS
rules.rule_description: Before returning control to CICS to await the next user interaction, saves the current program state and error messages into the communication area so the session context is preserved for the next entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
34: Session State Persistence
Save current program state
and commarea before returning to CICS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed its current processing cycle and is ready to return to CICS
acceptance_criteria.When: The COMMON-RETURN routine is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: WS-RETURN-MSG is moved to CCARD-ERROR-MSG; CARDDEMO-COMMAREA is moved to the first portion of WS-COMMAREA; WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA is moved to the second portion of WS-COMMAREA (starting at position LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1); a CICS RETURN command is issued with the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID), the full WS-COMMAREA, and its length, causing CICS to await the next user interaction and re-invoke this program

key_functionalities.title: Program Initialization
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Program Start]) --> B[Clear Working Storage Areas
Reset all work areas and
miscellaneous storage to initial values]
    B --> C[Clear Communication Area
Reset the session communication
area to initial values]
    C --> D[Set Transaction ID Context
Record the current transaction
identifier for this program session]
    D --> E[Clear Error Messages
Turn off any existing
error or return messages]
    E --> F([Initialization Complete
Proceed to Session Context Processing])

rules.rule_name: Reset Working Storage Areas at Program Startup
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution, all working storage areas including the card work area and miscellaneous storage must be reset to their initial default values to ensure no residual data from a previous session affects the current transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Working Storage Areas
Reset all work areas and
miscellaneous storage to initial values

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program has been invoked and is beginning execution
acceptance_criteria.When: The program starts its main processing routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card work area (CC-WORK-AREA) and the miscellaneous storage area (WS-MISC-STORAGE) must both be fully initialized to their default empty values, clearing any data that may have existed from a prior execution or session

rules.rule_name: Reset Session Communication Area at Program Startup
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution, the session communication area (WS-COMMAREA) used to pass data between programs must be reset to its initial default values to ensure a clean state before any session context is loaded or evaluated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Communication Area
Reset the session communication
area to initial values

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program has been invoked and is beginning execution
acceptance_criteria.When: The program starts its main processing routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session communication area (WS-COMMAREA) must be fully initialized to its default empty values, clearing any previously held inter-program communication data

rules.rule_name: Record Current Transaction Identifier in Session Context
rules.rule_description: At program startup, the system must record the current transaction identifier into the working session context so that the transaction identity is available throughout the program's execution for tracking, navigation, and return-routing purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Transaction ID Context
Record the current transaction
identifier for this program session

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program has been invoked and working storage areas have been initialized
acceptance_criteria.When: The program sets up its session context during startup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The literal transaction identifier for this program (LIT-THISTRANID) must be moved into the working storage transaction ID field (WS-TRANID), establishing the current transaction identity for the session

rules.rule_name: Clear Error and Return Messages at Program Startup
rules.rule_description: At program startup, any existing error or return messages from a prior interaction must be cleared so that stale messages are not displayed to the user during the new program execution cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Error Messages
Turn off any existing
error or return messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program has been invoked and working storage areas have been initialized
acceptance_criteria.When: The program completes its initial setup during startup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The return message flag (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF) must be set to TRUE, suppressing any previously held error or informational return messages and ensuring the screen starts with a clean message state

key_functionalities.title: Communication Area Processing
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Communication Area Processing])
    B{Is this a\nBrand New Session?\nNo prior interaction data}
    C{Coming from\nAdmin Menu or List Screen\nfor the first time?}
    D[Initialize Fresh Session Context\nClear all program state flags\nClear all transaction type data]
    E[Mark Session as:\nFirst Entry - Not Yet Re-entered\nTransaction Type Details Not Yet Fetched]
    F[Restore Previously Saved Session\nReload General Program State\nand Navigation Flags]
    G[Restore Transaction Type\nWorking Data from Prior Interaction\nIncluding State Flags and Type Details]
    H([End: Session Context Ready\nfor Processing])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - No Prior Session Data| D
    B -->|No - Prior Session Exists| C
    C -->|Yes - First Visit from\nAdmin or List Screen| D
    C -->|No - Returning Interaction| F
    D --> E
    E --> H
    F --> G
    G --> H

rules.rule_name: Detect Brand New Session with No Prior Interaction Data
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the current interaction is a completely new session by checking if there is no communication area data passed from a prior interaction. This is the primary gateway condition that routes the program to either initialize fresh context or restore prior session state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this a Brand New Session? No prior interaction data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user initiates the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The communication area length (EIBCALEN) is equal to zero, indicating no prior session data exists
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session is identified as brand new and the program proceeds to initialize a completely fresh session context, clearing all program state flags and transaction type working data

rules.rule_name: Detect First Visit from Admin Menu or List Screen
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the user is arriving at the Transaction Type Update screen for the first time from either the Admin Menu program or the Transaction List program, even when a communication area exists. This prevents stale session state from a prior visit to this screen from being incorrectly restored.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Coming from Admin Menu or List Screen for the first time?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A communication area exists from a prior interaction (EIBCALEN is not zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The originating program is the Admin Menu program (LIT-ADMINPGM) AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set (meaning this is not a return back to this same screen), OR the originating program is the Transaction List program (LIT-LISTTPGM) AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session is treated as a first visit and the program proceeds to initialize a completely fresh session context, discarding any previously saved state

rules.rule_name: Initialize Fresh Session Context for New or First-Visit Sessions
rules.rule_description: Establishes a clean starting state for the Transaction Type Update screen when the session is brand new or the user is visiting for the first time from the Admin Menu or List screen. All previously held program state flags and transaction type working data are cleared to prevent carry-over from prior interactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Initialize Fresh Session Context
Clear all program state flags
Clear all transaction type data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The session has been identified as brand new (no prior communication area data) OR the user is arriving for the first time from the Admin Menu or Transaction List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The fresh session initialization is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The general program communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is fully initialized to its default empty state, AND the Transaction Type Update program-specific working area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is fully initialized to its default empty state, clearing all transaction type codes, descriptions, old values, new values, and all program state flags

rules.rule_name: Mark Session as First Entry with Transaction Type Details Not Yet Fetched
rules.rule_description: After initializing a fresh session context, the program sets specific state markers to indicate that this is the first entry into the screen and that no transaction type record has been fetched from the database yet. These markers drive the screen display logic to show an empty search prompt to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Session as: First Entry - Not Yet Re-entered
Transaction Type Details Not Yet Fetched

acceptance_criteria.Given: A fresh session context has just been initialized (either for a brand new session or a first visit from Admin Menu or List screen)
acceptance_criteria.When: The session state markers are being set after initialization
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program entry state flag is set to 'First Entry' (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE), indicating the screen has not yet been re-entered by the user, AND the transaction type details fetch state is set to 'Details Not Yet Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), indicating no transaction type record has been retrieved from the database

rules.rule_name: Restore General Program State from Prior Session Communication Area
rules.rule_description: When a returning user interaction is detected (prior session data exists and it is not a first visit from Admin or List), the general program state including navigation context, calling program identity, calling transaction identity, and user type flags are restored from the communication area passed by CICS.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Restore Previously Saved Session
Reload General Program State
and Navigation Flags

acceptance_criteria.Given: A prior session exists (communication area length is not zero) AND the interaction is not a first visit from the Admin Menu or Transaction List program
acceptance_criteria.When: The session context restoration is triggered for a returning interaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The general program communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is restored by copying the first segment of the CICS communication area (DFHCOMMAREA) with a length equal to the size of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, reloading all general navigation flags, calling program name, calling transaction ID, user type, and last map/mapset information

rules.rule_name: Restore Transaction Type Working Data from Prior Session
rules.rule_description: As the second part of session restoration for returning interactions, the Transaction Type Update program-specific working data is restored from the communication area. This includes all transaction type state flags (such as whether details were fetched, whether changes are pending confirmation, whether delete is in progress) and the actual transaction type code and description values from the prior interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Restore Transaction Type
Working Data from Prior Interaction
Including State Flags and Type Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: The general program communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) has already been restored from the CICS communication area for a returning interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The program-specific working data restoration is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Update program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is restored by copying the second segment of the CICS communication area (DFHCOMMAREA), starting at the position immediately after the general CARDDEMO-COMMAREA segment, with a length equal to the size of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, reloading all transaction type state flags (TTUP flags such as details-fetched state, change confirmation state, delete state) and all transaction type old and new detail values (type codes and descriptions) from the prior interaction

key_functionalities.title: PF Key Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([User Presses a Key])

    D_F3{F3 Pressed?}
    D_ENTER{Enter Pressed?}
    D_ENTER_STATE{Currently in\nDelete Confirmation\nState?}
    D_F4{F4 Pressed?}
    D_F4_STATE{Currently Showing\nDetails OR in Delete\nConfirmation State?}
    D_F5{F5 Pressed?}
    D_F5_STATE{Currently in:\nChanges Confirmed,\nRecord Not Found, OR\nDelete In Progress?}
    D_F12{F12 Pressed?}
    D_F12_STATE{Currently in:\nChanges Confirmed,\nShowing Details,\nRecord Not Found,\nDelete Confirmation, OR\nCreating New Record?}

    VALID[✅ Mark Key as VALID\nProceed with action]
    INVALID[❌ Mark Key as INVALID\nSet Invalid Key Message]

    START --> D_F3
    D_F3 -->|Yes| VALID
    D_F3 -->|No| D_ENTER

    D_ENTER -->|Yes| D_ENTER_STATE
    D_ENTER_STATE -->|Not in Delete\nConfirmation| VALID
    D_ENTER_STATE -->|In Delete\nConfirmation| INVALID
    D_ENTER -->|No| D_F4

    D_F4 -->|Yes| D_F4_STATE
    D_F4_STATE -->|Yes - Valid State| VALID
    D_F4_STATE -->|No - Wrong State| INVALID
    D_F4 -->|No| D_F5

    D_F5 -->|Yes| D_F5_STATE
    D_F5_STATE -->|Yes - Valid State| VALID
    D_F5_STATE -->|No - Wrong State| INVALID
    D_F5 -->|No| D_F12

    D_F12 -->|Yes| D_F12_STATE
    D_F12_STATE -->|Yes - Valid State| VALID
    D_F12_STATE -->|No - Wrong State| INVALID
    D_F12 -->|No - Any Other Key| INVALID

rules.rule_name: F3 Key Always Valid for Exit
rules.rule_description: The F3 key (Exit/Return) is unconditionally valid regardless of the current screen state. Pressing F3 always allows the user to exit the Transaction Type Update screen and return to the calling program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: F3 Pressed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in any screen state (Details Not Fetched, Showing Details, Confirm Delete, Creating New Record, Changes Pending Confirmation, etc.)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the F3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F3 key is marked as VALID and the exit action is allowed to proceed without any restriction

rules.rule_name: Enter Key Valid Except During Delete Confirmation
rules.rule_description: The Enter key is valid for submitting input or triggering a search in all screen states, with one exception: when the screen is in the Delete Confirmation state, pressing Enter is not a valid action and must be rejected to prevent accidental processing during a sensitive delete workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enter Pressed? / Currently in Delete Confirmation State?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key AND the screen is NOT currently in the Delete Confirmation state (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE is not active)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Enter key is marked as VALID and input processing proceeds; BUT if the screen IS currently in the Delete Confirmation state, the Enter key is marked as INVALID and an Invalid Key message is set

rules.rule_name: F4 Key Valid Only When Record Is Displayed or Delete Is Awaiting Confirmation
rules.rule_description: The F4 key (Delete) is only valid when there is an active record displayed on screen or when the system is already waiting for the user to confirm a pending delete. F4 cannot be used in any other state, such as during initial search, record not found, or while changes are being confirmed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: F4 Pressed? / Currently Showing Details OR in Delete Confirmation State?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the F4 key AND the screen is currently in either the 'Showing Details' state (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS) OR the 'Delete Confirmation' state (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F4 key is marked as VALID and the delete action is allowed to proceed; BUT if the screen is in any other state (e.g., Details Not Fetched, Details Not Found, Creating New Record, Changes Pending), the F4 key is marked as INVALID and an Invalid Key message is set

rules.rule_name: F5 Key Valid Only for Save Confirmation or New Record Creation or Delete In Progress
rules.rule_description: The F5 key (Save/Confirm) is only valid in three specific states: when validated changes are awaiting user confirmation before saving, when a search returned no record and the user may choose to create a new one, or when a delete operation is in progress. F5 is not valid in any other state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: F5 Pressed? / Currently in: Changes Confirmed, Record Not Found, OR Delete In Progress?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the F5 key AND the screen is currently in one of the following states: 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED) meaning validated changes are awaiting save confirmation, OR 'Details Not Found' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND) meaning the searched record does not exist and a new record can be created, OR 'Delete In Progress' (TTUP-DELETE-IN-PROGRESS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F5 key is marked as VALID and the corresponding save or create action is allowed to proceed; BUT if the screen is in any other state (e.g., Showing Details without pending changes, Details Not Fetched, Confirm Delete), the F5 key is marked as INVALID and an Invalid Key message is set

rules.rule_name: F12 Key Valid Only for Cancel or Refresh in Specific Active States
rules.rule_description: The F12 key (Cancel/Refresh) is only valid when the screen is in one of five active operational states where a cancellation or refresh action is meaningful: changes are pending confirmation, a record is currently displayed, a record was not found, delete confirmation is pending, or a new record is being created. F12 is not valid in any other state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: F12 Pressed? / Currently in: Changes Confirmed, Showing Details, Record Not Found, Delete Confirmation, OR Creating New Record?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the F12 key AND the screen is currently in one of the following states: 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), OR 'Showing Details' (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS), OR 'Details Not Found' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND), OR 'Confirm Delete' (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE), OR 'Create New Record' (TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F12 key is marked as VALID and the cancel or refresh action is allowed to proceed; BUT if the screen is in any other state (e.g., Details Not Fetched, Invalid Search Keys, Changes Not OK), the F12 key is marked as INVALID and an Invalid Key message is set

rules.rule_name: Any Unrecognized or Context-Invalid Key Press Is Rejected
rules.rule_description: Any key press that is not F3, Enter, F4, F5, or F12, or any of those keys pressed in a screen state where they are not permitted, results in the key being marked as invalid. An Invalid Key message is set to inform the user that the action is not allowed in the current context, and the screen is redisplayed without processing the input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: ❌ Mark Key as INVALID / Set Invalid Key Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in any state
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses a key that is either: not one of the recognized function keys (F3, Enter, F4, F5, F12), OR one of those keys but pressed in a screen state where it is not permitted (e.g., F4 pressed when no record is displayed, F5 pressed when showing details without pending changes, F12 pressed when in initial/not-fetched state)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is marked as INVALID (PFK-INVALID is set to TRUE), an 'Invalid Key Pressed' message (WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED) is set to notify the user, and the screen is redisplayed in its current state without performing any data processing or state change

key_functionalities.title: State Reset on Completion
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Check if State Reset is Required])

    D1{F12 Cancel Pressed\nwhile Viewing Details,\nCreating New Record,\nor Record Not Found?}
    D2{Update Completed\nSuccessfully?}
    D3{Update Operation\nFailed?}
    D4{Changes Were Cancelled\nAND No Prior Record\nData Available?}
    D5{Delete Completed\nSuccessfully?}
    D6{Delete Operation\nFailed?}

    RESET[Reset Screen State:\nMark as Fresh Entry\nClear Fetched Data Flag]
    NO_RESET[No State Reset Required:\nContinue with Current State]

    END_RESET([Proceed to Display\nEmpty Search Screen])
    END_NO_RESET([Proceed with\nExisting Screen State])

    START --> D1
    D1 -->|Yes| RESET
    D1 -->|No| D2
    D2 -->|Yes - Record Saved| RESET
    D2 -->|No| D3
    D3 -->|Yes - Save Failed| RESET
    D3 -->|No| D4
    D4 -->|Yes - Cancelled with No Data| RESET
    D4 -->|No| D5
    D5 -->|Yes - Record Deleted| RESET
    D5 -->|No| D6
    D6 -->|Yes - Delete Failed| RESET
    D6 -->|No - None of Above| NO_RESET

    RESET --> END_RESET
    NO_RESET --> END_NO_RESET

rules.rule_name: Reset Screen State When User Cancels via F12 While Viewing, Creating, or Record Not Found
rules.rule_description: When the user presses F12 (Cancel) while the screen is in one of three active states — viewing an existing transaction type record, creating a new transaction type record, or after a search returned no record — the system must discard the current context and reset the screen to its initial empty search state, prompting the user to start a fresh search.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: F12 Cancel Pressed while Viewing Details, Creating New Record, or Record Not Found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the current screen state is one of: (a) showing details of an existing transaction type record, (b) in the process of creating a new transaction type record, or (c) displaying a 'record not found' result from a previous search
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses F12 (Cancel/Refresh key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: Reset Screen State After Successful Transaction Type Update or Insert
rules.rule_description: When a transaction type record has been successfully saved to the database — either by updating an existing record or inserting a new one — the system must automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode so the user can perform a new search or operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Completed Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the system has just completed a successful save operation (update or insert) to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, with the screen state set to 'Changes Okayed And Done' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE = TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: Reset Screen State After Failed Transaction Type Update
rules.rule_description: When a transaction type save operation has failed (e.g., due to a database error during update or insert), the system must automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode so the user can start a fresh search rather than remaining in a failed/inconsistent state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Operation Failed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the system has encountered a failure during a save operation to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, with the screen state set to 'Changes Failed' (TTUP-CHANGES-FAILED = TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: Reset Screen State When Changes Are Cancelled and No Prior Record Data Exists
rules.rule_description: When a user cancels pending changes (backs out of an update) AND there is no previously fetched original record data available to restore (the old details area is empty), the system must reset the screen to its initial empty search state rather than attempting to redisplay non-existent original values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Changes Were Cancelled AND No Prior Record Data Available?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the current screen state is 'Changes Backed Out' (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT = TRUE) AND the original record data area (TTUP-OLD-DETAILS) contains either LOW-VALUES or SPACES, meaning no prior record data is available to restore
acceptance_criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: Reset Screen State After Successful Transaction Type Deletion
rules.rule_description: When a transaction type record has been successfully deleted from the database, the system must automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode since the deleted record no longer exists and cannot be displayed or operated upon.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Delete Completed Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the system has just completed a successful deletion of a transaction type record from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, with the screen state set to 'Delete Done' (TTUP-DELETE-DONE = TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: Reset Screen State After Failed Transaction Type Deletion
rules.rule_description: When a transaction type delete operation has failed (e.g., due to existing child records or a database error), the system must automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode so the user can start a fresh search rather than remaining in a failed delete state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Delete Operation Failed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the system has encountered a failure during a delete operation on the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, with the screen state set to 'Delete Failed' (TTUP-DELETE-FAILED = TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: No State Reset Required When None of the Terminal Conditions Are Met
rules.rule_description: When the current screen state does not match any of the terminal conditions that require a reset (not F12 cancel from active states, not a completed/failed update, not a cancelled change with no data, not a completed/failed delete), the system preserves the existing screen state and continues processing with the current context intact.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No State Reset Required: Continue with Current State

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the current screen state is NOT any of the following: (a) F12 pressed while showing details, creating new record, or record not found; (b) changes okayed and done; (c) changes failed; (d) changes backed out with no prior record data; (e) delete done; (f) delete failed
acceptance_criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT reset the program state — CDEMO-PGM-ENTER and TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED flags remain unchanged — and processing continues with the existing screen state and previously fetched data

key_functionalities.title: Exit and Return to Calling Program
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses F3
Exit Key]) --> B{Was this screen
launched from a
specific program?}
    B -->|No - No calling program
recorded| C[Default destination:
Admin Menu Program]
    B -->|Yes - Calling program
is recorded| D[Use the recorded
calling program
as destination]
    C --> E[Commit any
pending work]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Transfer control
to destination program
Admin Menu or List Screen]
    F --> G([User is now on
Admin Menu or
List Screen])

rules.rule_name: Default to Admin Menu When No Calling Transaction Is Recorded
rules.rule_description: When the user presses F3 to exit and no originating transaction ID was recorded in the communication area, the system defaults the return destination transaction to the Admin Menu transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default destination: Admin Menu Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the communication area is either empty (LOW-VALUES) or blank (SPACES), indicating no specific calling transaction was recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses F3 to exit the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination transaction ID (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) to the Admin Menu transaction ID (LIT-ADMINTRANID) as the default return destination

rules.rule_name: Return to Recorded Calling Transaction When One Exists
rules.rule_description: When the user presses F3 to exit and a specific originating transaction ID was recorded in the communication area, the system uses that recorded transaction as the return destination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use the recorded calling program as destination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the communication area contains a valid non-blank, non-empty transaction ID, indicating this screen was launched from a specific transaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses F3 to exit the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination transaction ID (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) to the previously recorded calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), directing the user back to the originating transaction

rules.rule_name: Default to Admin Menu Program When No Calling Program Is Recorded
rules.rule_description: When the user presses F3 to exit and no originating program name was recorded in the communication area, the system defaults the return destination program to the Admin Menu program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default destination: Admin Menu Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and the originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area is either empty (LOW-VALUES) or blank (SPACES), indicating no specific calling program was recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses F3 to exit the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) to the Admin Menu program (LIT-ADMINPGM) as the default return destination

rules.rule_name: Return to Recorded Calling Program When One Exists
rules.rule_description: When the user presses F3 to exit and a specific originating program name was recorded in the communication area, the system uses that recorded program as the return destination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use the recorded calling program as destination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and the originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area contains a valid non-blank, non-empty program name, indicating this screen was launched from a specific program
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses F3 to exit the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) to the previously recorded calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), directing the user back to the originating program

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program Context Before Exiting
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system records the current Transaction Type Update screen's transaction ID and program name as the originating context in the communication area, so the destination program knows where the user came from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to destination program Admin Menu or List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed F3 to exit the Transaction Type Update screen and the destination program has been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is preparing to transfer control to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current screen's transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) into the originating transaction field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) and the current program name (LIT-THISPGM) into the originating program field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area, and sets the current map set (LIT-THISMAPSET) and map name (LIT-THISMAP) into the last-used map fields (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET, CDEMO-LAST-MAP), so the destination program has full context of the navigation origin

rules.rule_name: Set User Type to Admin Before Exiting
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program on F3 exit, the system sets the user type indicator to Admin in the communication area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to destination program Admin Menu or List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed F3 to exit the Transaction Type Update screen and the destination program has been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is preparing to transfer control to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the user type flag (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN) to Admin and sets the program entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) to indicate a fresh entry into the destination program

rules.rule_name: Commit Pending Work Before Exiting to Destination Program
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system commits any pending database changes to ensure data consistency.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Commit any pending work

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed F3 to exit the Transaction Type Update screen, the destination program has been determined, and the current program context has been recorded in the communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is about to transfer control to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system issues a SYNCPOINT to commit any pending database changes before transferring control, ensuring all work performed during this session is permanently saved and the database is in a consistent state

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Program on F3 Exit
rules.rule_description: After committing pending work, the system transfers control directly to the determined destination program (Admin Menu or List Screen), passing the full communication area so the destination program has all necessary context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to destination program Admin Menu or List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed F3 to exit, the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been set to either the Admin Menu program or the recorded calling program, the current program context has been recorded, and pending work has been committed via SYNCPOINT
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control directly to the destination program identified in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, passing the full CARDDEMO-COMMAREA communication area containing all session context (originating transaction, originating program, user type, last map set, last map), and the current Transaction Type Update screen is exited — the user is now on the Admin Menu or List Screen

key_functionalities.title: Initial Screen Display
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter Program Fresh\nor from Admin/List Screen])
    B[Clear All Working Data\nInitialize program commarea\nand working storage areas]
    C[Set Program State:\nEntering Fresh\nDetails Not Yet Fetched]
    D[Prepare Screen Header\nSet current date, time,\nprogram name, transaction ID]
    E[Clear Screen Data Fields\nSet transaction type code\nand description to empty]
