rules.rule_name: Map Terminal Key Press to Internal Key Indicator
rules.rule_description: When a user presses any function key or action key on the terminal, the system identifies and maps the physical key press to an internal key indicator flag that the program can evaluate for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Identify Key Pressed
Map terminal key press to
internal key indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and presses any key (ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, PF1 through PF12, or PF13 through PF24)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the terminal key press event (EIBAID value)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system maps the key to exactly one internal indicator flag: ENTER maps to CCARD-AID-ENTER, CLEAR maps to CCARD-AID-CLEAR, PA1 maps to CCARD-AID-PA1, PA2 maps to CCARD-AID-PA2, PF1/PF13 map to CCARD-AID-PFK01, PF2/PF14 map to CCARD-AID-PFK02, PF3/PF15 map to CCARD-AID-PFK03, PF4/PF16 map to CCARD-AID-PFK04, PF5/PF17 map to CCARD-AID-PFK05, PF6/PF18 map to CCARD-AID-PFK06, PF7/PF19 map to CCARD-AID-PFK07, PF8/PF20 map to CCARD-AID-PFK08, PF9/PF21 map to CCARD-AID-PFK09, PF10/PF22 map to CCARD-AID-PFK10, PF11/PF23 map to CCARD-AID-PFK11, PF12/PF24 map to CCARD-AID-PFK12. Shifted PF keys (PF13-PF24) are treated identically to their base equivalents (PF1-PF12).

rules.rule_name: Validate Function Key Against Current Screen State
rules.rule_description: The system enforces that only contextually appropriate function keys are accepted based on the current screen state. Keys that are not valid for the current state are rejected to prevent unintended operations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is the Key Valid
for Current
Screen State?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in any given state (Details Not Fetched, Show Details, Confirm Delete, Details Not Found, Changes OK Not Confirmed, Create New Record, Delete In Progress, etc.) and a key press has been mapped to an internal indicator
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the pressed key against the current screen state
acceptance_criteria.Then: The key is considered VALID only under these specific combinations: (1) PF3 is always valid regardless of state; (2) ENTER is valid in any state EXCEPT when the current state is Confirm Delete; (3) PF4 is valid only when the current state is Show Details OR Confirm Delete; (4) PF5 is valid only when the current state is Changes OK Not Confirmed, OR Details Not Found, OR Delete In Progress; (5) PF12 is valid only when the current state is Changes OK Not Confirmed, OR Show Details, OR Details Not Found, OR Confirm Delete, OR Create New Record. Any key press that does not match one of these valid combinations is considered INVALID.

rules.rule_name: Mark Key as Invalid and Set Invalid Key Pressed Flag
rules.rule_description: When a key press is determined to be invalid for the current screen state, the system marks the key as invalid and sets a flag to trigger the invalid key message flow, ensuring the user receives feedback about the inappropriate key press.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Key as Invalid
Set Invalid Key Pressed Flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key that is not valid for the current screen state on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The key validation check determines the key is not in the list of valid key-state combinations
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the PFK-INVALID flag to TRUE, and if no return message is currently set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE), the system additionally sets the WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED flag to TRUE to indicate an invalid key was pressed

rules.rule_name: Prepare Invalid Key Error Message for Display
rules.rule_description: When an invalid key is pressed, the system prepares an appropriate error message to inform the user that the key they pressed is not valid in the current context, without altering any data or screen state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Invalid Key Message
Prepare appropriate message
for display to user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED flag has been set to TRUE because the user pressed a key not valid for the current screen state
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the invalid key condition in the main action router (EVALUATE TRUE block in 0000-MAIN)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes directly to the screen send routine (3000-SEND-MAP) without performing any input processing, database access, or state changes. The WS-RETURN-MSG field (which was set when WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED was flagged) is carried forward as the error message to be displayed in the ERRMSGO field on the screen

rules.rule_name: Preserve Current Screen State on Invalid Key
rules.rule_description: When an invalid key is pressed, the system must not alter the current program state, screen data, or perform any database operations. All existing state flags and data values are preserved exactly as they were before the invalid key was pressed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Any Other
Conditions to
Reset State?
No - Preserve Current State
Keep All Current Data
Unchanged
No database access performed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has identified an invalid key press and is preparing to redisplay the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The WHEN WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED branch is taken in the main action router
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system performs ONLY the screen send routine (3000-SEND-MAP) and then goes directly to COMMON-RETURN. No input processing (1000-PROCESS-INPUTS) is performed, no action decision logic (2000-DECIDE-ACTION) is executed, no database reads or writes occur, and all current state flags (TTUP-* states, CDEMO-* flags) remain unchanged from their values before the key was pressed

rules.rule_name: Initialize Screen Header with Current Date, Time and Program Information
rules.rule_description: Before redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system refreshes the screen header area with the current system date, current system time, transaction ID, and program name to ensure the header information is always current and accurate.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Prepare Screen for Redisplay
Load current date, time,
program name and titles

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redisplay the Transaction Type Update screen after an invalid key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (3100-SCREEN-INIT) is executed as part of the screen send process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen output area (CTRTUPAO) is cleared to LOW-VALUES, then populated with: (1) Application title lines from CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 in TITLE01O and TITLE02O fields; (2) The current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) in the TRNNAMEO field; (3) The current program name (LIT-THISPGM) in the PGMNAMEO field; (4) The current system date formatted as MM/DD/YY in the CURDATEO field; (5) The current system time formatted as HH:MM:SS in the CURTIMEO field

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Fields with Existing Data Values Based on Unchanged State
rules.rule_description: When redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system populates the screen data fields using the existing data values appropriate to the current (unchanged) screen state, ensuring the user sees the same data they were working with before pressing the invalid key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Screen Fields
with Existing Data Values
No changes to displayed data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating screen fields for redisplay after an invalid key press, and the current screen state is unchanged
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen variable setup routine (3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen fields are populated based on the current state as follows: (1) If state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED: Transaction Type Code (TRTYPCDO) and description fields are set to LOW-VALUES (blank); (2) If state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, TTUP-DELETE-FAILED, TTUP-DELETE-DONE, or TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT: TTUP-NEW-DETAILS is initialized and the ORIGINAL database values are displayed — TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE is moved to TRTYPCDO and TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC is moved to TRTYDSCO; (3) If state is TTUP-CHANGES-MADE, TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, or TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE: the NEW (user-entered) values are displayed — TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE is moved to TRTYPCDO and TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC is moved to TRTYDSCO; (4) If the program is in initial entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER): no field population is performed (CONTINUE)

rules.rule_name: Set Informational Message on Screen for Invalid Key Redisplay
rules.rule_description: When redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system sets both the informational guidance message (centered) and the error message area to provide the user with context about what action is expected and what went wrong.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Invalid Key
Error Message on Screen
Display reason key was invalid

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is setting up messages for screen redisplay after an invalid key press, with the current screen state unchanged
acceptance_criteria.When: The information message setup routine (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message (INFOMSGO) is determined by the current (unchanged) state: if state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED or TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, the message prompts for search keys; if state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, the message prompts to create a new record; if state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS or TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT with no old type data, the message prompts for search keys; if state is TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT or TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, the message prompts for changes; if state is TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, the message prompts for delete confirmation; if state is TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, the message prompts for new data entry; if state is TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, the message prompts for confirmation; if state is TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, the message confirms update success. The informational message is centered in the display field. Additionally, the WS-RETURN-MSG (containing the invalid key error text) is moved to ERRMSGO to display the error reason to the user

rules.rule_name: Set Screen Field Protection Attributes Based on Unchanged Current State
rules.rule_description: When redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system applies the same field protection rules as would normally apply for the current (unchanged) state, ensuring fields remain editable or protected exactly as they were before the invalid key was pressed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Screen Field Attributes
Protect or unprotect fields
based on unchanged current state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is setting field attributes for screen redisplay after an invalid key press, with the current screen state unchanged
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields are first set to protected (DFHBMPRF applied to TRTYPCDA, TRTYDSCA, and INFOMSGA). Then based on the current state: (1) If state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, or TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT with no old type data: the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDA) is set to unprotected with cursor (DFHBMFSE); (2) If state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, or TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT with old data: the Description field (TRTYDSCA) is set to unprotected with cursor (DFHBMFSE) and the info message field remains protected (DFHBMPRF); (3) If state is TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, or TTUP-DELETE-IN-PROGRESS: all fields remain protected (no change). Additionally, if the Transaction Type filter flag is invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK) or delete has failed (TTUP-DELETE-FAILED), the Transaction Type Code field color is set to RED (DFHRED). If the filter is blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK) and the program is in re-entry mode, the Transaction Type Code field displays '*' and is colored RED

rules.rule_name: Set Informational Message Display Attributes
rules.rule_description: The system controls the visual display attribute of the informational message area to distinguish between states where no guidance message is needed versus states where an active guidance message should be prominently displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Screen Field Attributes
Protect or unprotect fields
based on unchanged current state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is finalizing screen attributes for redisplay after an invalid key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The informational message attribute setup routine (3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current state has no informational message to display (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is TRUE), the informational message field attribute (INFOMSGA) is set to dark/non-display (DFHBMDAR); otherwise, if there is an informational message to display, the informational message field attribute is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB)

rules.rule_name: Set Available Function Key Indicators Based on Unchanged Current State
rules.rule_description: When redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system highlights only the function keys that are valid and available for the current (unchanged) screen state, providing clear visual guidance to the user about which keys they can legitimately press.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Available Function Keys
based on unchanged
current screen state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is setting function key display attributes for screen redisplay after an invalid key press, with the current screen state unchanged
acceptance_criteria.When: The function key attribute setup routine (3391-SETUP-PFKEY-ATTRS) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following function key visibility rules are applied: (1) If the current state is TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE: the general function keys area (FKEYSA) is set to dark/dimmed (DFHBMDAR); otherwise FKEYSA is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB); (2) If the current state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS OR TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE: the PF4 key indicator (FKEY04A) is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB); (3) If the current state is TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED OR TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND: the PF5 key indicator (FKEY05A) is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB); (4) If the current state is TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, OR TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, OR TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, OR TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, OR TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD: the PF12 key indicator (FKEY12A) is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB). Keys not meeting these conditions remain at their default (non-highlighted) state

rules.rule_name: Send Redisplayed Screen Back to User After Invalid Key
rules.rule_description: After preparing all screen content, messages, and field attributes following an invalid key press, the system transmits the fully prepared screen back to the user's terminal, erasing the previous screen content and displaying the refreshed screen with the invalid key error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Send Screen Back to User
Redisplay with invalid key
message and unchanged data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed all screen preparation steps (header initialization, field population, message setup, attribute setting) following an invalid key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen send routine (3400-SEND-SCREEN) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sends the screen map (identified by LIT-THISMAP within LIT-THISMAPSET) with the fully populated output area (CTRTUPAO) to the user's terminal. The screen is sent with CURSOR positioning (cursor placed at the field designated during attribute setup), ERASE (previous screen content is cleared), and FREEKB (keyboard is unlocked for the next user input). The next map and mapset names are set to LIT-THISMAP and LIT-THISMAPSET respectively in the communication area before sending

rules.rule_name: Return Control to CICS Preserving State for Next Interaction
rules.rule_description: After sending the screen back to the user following an invalid key press, the system returns control to CICS while preserving the complete current program state in the communication area, so that when the user presses the next key, the program can resume with full context of the previous interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Await Next User Input

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen has been sent back to the user with the invalid key error message and unchanged data after an invalid key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The COMMON-RETURN routine is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies WS-RETURN-MSG to CCARD-ERROR-MSG, assembles the full communication area by combining CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA into WS-COMMAREA, and returns control to CICS specifying the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) as the next transaction to invoke, passing the assembled WS-COMMAREA as the communication data. This ensures the program state (including all TTUP-* state flags and data values) is preserved for the next user interaction

key_functionalities.title: User Input Processing
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: User Input Processing])

    RCV[Receive Screen Input\nCapture transaction type code\nand description from screen]

    STORE_CHK{Is state 'Record Not Found'\nAND F5 not pressed\nAND same code re-entered?}
    SKIP_STORE[Skip storing input\nNo change in search criteria]

    STORE[Store Screen Input\nSave transaction type code\nand description to working storage]
    STORE_NOTE[Special handling:\nAsterisk or spaces stored\nas blank low-values]

    STATE_CHK{Is current state\n'Create New Record' OR\n'Changes Pending Confirmation'?}

    SKIP_TYPEVAL[Skip Transaction Type\nCode Validation\nAlready validated previously]

    TYPEVAL[Validate Transaction Type Code]
    TV1{Is code blank\nor empty?}
    TV1Y[Error: Transaction Type Code\nmust be supplied]
    TV2{Is code\nnumeric?}
    TV2N[Error: Transaction Type Code\nmust be numeric]
    TV3{Is code\nnon-zero?}
    TV3N[Error: Transaction Type Code\nmust not be zero]
    TV_OK[Format code with\nleading zeros]

    BLANK_CHK{Was code blank\nor invalid?}
    BLANK_ERR[Set state: No search\ncriteria received\nReturn to search prompt]
    INVALID_ERR[Set state: Invalid search keys\nReturn to search prompt]

    FETCH_CHK{Was record\nalready fetched?}
    SKIP_DESC[Skip further validation\nAwait database lookup]

    COMPARE[Compare New Values\nAgainst Original Fetched Values]
    CMP1{Are type code AND\ndescription unchanged?}
    NO_CHANGE[No Changes Detected\nNotify user no changes were made]
    CHANGE_FOUND[Changes Detected\nProceed to description validation]

    DESCVAL[Validate Transaction Description]
    DV1{Is description\nblank or empty?}
    DV1Y[Error: Transaction Description\nmust be supplied]
    DV2{Does description contain\nonly alphanumeric characters\nwithin 50 characters?}
    DV2N[Error: Transaction Description\ncan have numbers or\nalphabets only]
    DV_OK[Description Valid\nSet state: Changes ready\nfor user confirmation]

    END_ERR([End: Validation Failed\nRedisplay screen with error])
    END_OK([End: Input Valid\nProceed to Action Decision])

    START --> RCV
    RCV --> STORE_CHK
    STORE_CHK -->|Yes - Same code, no F5| SKIP_STORE
    SKIP_STORE --> END_OK
    STORE_CHK -->|No| STORE
    STORE --> STORE_NOTE
    STORE_NOTE --> STATE_CHK

    STATE_CHK -->|Yes - Create New or\nPending Confirmation| SKIP_TYPEVAL
    SKIP_TYPEVAL --> COMPARE

    STATE_CHK -->|No - Normal entry| TYPEVAL
    TYPEVAL --> TV1
    TV1 -->|Yes - Blank| TV1Y
    TV1Y --> BLANK_ERR
    BLANK_ERR --> END_ERR
    TV1 -->|No| TV2
    TV2 -->|Not Numeric| TV2N
    TV2N --> INVALID_ERR
    INVALID_ERR --> END_ERR
    TV2 -->|Numeric| TV3
    TV3 -->|Zero| TV3N
    TV3N --> INVALID_ERR
    TV3 -->|Non-Zero| TV_OK

    TV_OK --> BLANK_CHK
    BLANK_CHK -->|Blank| BLANK_ERR
    BLANK_CHK -->|Invalid| INVALID_ERR
    BLANK_CHK -->|Valid| FETCH_CHK
    FETCH_CHK -->|Not yet fetched| SKIP_DESC
    SKIP_DESC --> END_OK

    FETCH_CHK -->|Already fetched| COMPARE
    COMPARE --> CMP1
    CMP1 -->|Unchanged| NO_CHANGE
    NO_CHANGE --> END_OK
    CMP1 -->|Changed| CHANGE_FOUND

    CHANGE_FOUND --> DESCVAL
    DESCVAL --> DV1
    DV1 -->|Yes - Blank| DV1Y
    DV1Y --> END_ERR
    DV1 -->|No| DV2
    DV2 -->|Invalid characters| DV2N
    DV2N --> END_ERR
    DV2 -->|Valid| DV_OK
    DV_OK --> END_OK

rules.rule_name: Receive Screen Input for Transaction Type Maintenance
rules.rule_description: The system captures the transaction type code and description entered by the user from the Transaction Type Update screen into working storage for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Receive Screen Input
Capture transaction type code
and description from screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and has entered values in the transaction type code and/or description fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the screen input from the Transaction Type Update map (CTRTUPAI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction type code (TRTYPCDI) and description (TRTYDSCI) entered by the user are captured into working storage for further validation and processing

rules.rule_name: Skip Storing Input When Same Code Re-entered in Not-Found State Without PF5
rules.rule_description: When the system is in 'Record Not Found' state, the user has not pressed PF5, and the same transaction type code is re-entered, the system skips re-storing the input to preserve the existing search context and avoids redundant processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is state 'Record Not Found'
AND F5 not pressed
AND same code re-entered?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current program state is 'Record Not Found' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND), PF5 was NOT pressed, and the trimmed value of the transaction type code entered on screen equals the previously searched transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to store the newly received screen input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips storing the screen input and exits the store-input step without updating working storage, preserving the existing search context

rules.rule_name: Store Transaction Type Code from Screen Input
rules.rule_description: The system stores the user-entered transaction type code from the screen into the new-details working storage area, treating asterisk or spaces as blank (low-values).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store Screen Input
Save transaction type code
and description to working storage

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has received screen input and the skip-store condition is not met
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the transaction type code from the screen field TRTYPCDI of CTRTUPAI
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the entered code is an asterisk ('*') or spaces, the transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) is set to LOW-VALUES (blank); otherwise, the trimmed value of the entered code is stored in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE

rules.rule_name: Store Transaction Type Description from Screen Input
rules.rule_description: The system stores the user-entered transaction type description from the screen into the new-details working storage area, treating asterisk or spaces as blank (low-values).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Special handling:
Asterisk or spaces stored
as blank low-values

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has received screen input and the skip-store condition is not met
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the transaction type description from the screen field TRTYDSCI of CTRTUPAI
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the entered description is an asterisk ('*') or spaces, the transaction type description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) is set to LOW-VALUES (blank); otherwise, the trimmed value of the entered description is stored in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC

rules.rule_name: Skip Transaction Type Code Validation When Creating New Record or Changes Pending Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When the program is in 'Create New Record' state or 'Changes Pending Confirmation' state, the transaction type code has already been validated in a prior step, so the system bypasses the type code validation and proceeds directly to comparing old and new values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is current state
'Create New Record' OR
'Changes Pending Confirmation'?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current program state is either 'Create New Record' (TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD) or 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to perform transaction type code validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips the transaction type code validation entirely and proceeds directly to the compare old-versus-new values step

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Supplied
rules.rule_description: The transaction type code is a mandatory field. If the user leaves it blank or empty, the system raises a validation error and prompts the user to supply the value.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is code blank
or empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is performing transaction type code validation and the current state is not 'Create New Record' or 'Changes Pending Confirmation'
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) is evaluated and found to be LOW-VALUES, spaces, or has a trimmed length of zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state, marks the transaction type code flag as blank (FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK), and sets the error message to 'Tran Type code must be supplied.'

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Numeric
rules.rule_description: The transaction type code must contain only numeric digits. If the entered value contains non-numeric characters, the system raises a validation error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is code
numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction type code has been supplied (is not blank) and the system is performing numeric validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system tests the transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, up to 2 characters) using FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL and the result is not zero (i.e., the value is not numeric)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state, marks the transaction type code flag as not-ok (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), and sets the error message to 'Tran Type code must be numeric.'

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Not Be Zero
rules.rule_description: The transaction type code must be a non-zero numeric value. A value of zero is not a valid transaction type code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is code
non-zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction type code has been supplied and confirmed to be numeric
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the numeric value of the transaction type code using FUNCTION NUMVAL and the result equals zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state, marks the transaction type code flag as not-ok (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), and sets the error message to 'Tran Type code must not be zero.'

rules.rule_name: Format Valid Transaction Type Code with Leading Zeros
rules.rule_description: After a transaction type code passes all validations, the system formats it by converting the numeric value and replacing any spaces with zeros to ensure consistent 2-digit zero-padded representation (e.g., '5' becomes '05').
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Format code with
leading zeros

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction type code has passed all validations (non-blank, numeric, non-zero) and the filter flag is set to valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the transaction type code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system computes the numeric value of the code using FUNCTION NUMVAL, moves it to a 2-character alphanumeric field, replaces all spaces with zeros using INSPECT, and stores the zero-padded result back into TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE

rules.rule_name: Route to No Search Criteria Error When Code Is Blank
rules.rule_description: When the transaction type code validation results in a blank code, the system sets the program state to indicate no search criteria was received and resets to the search prompt state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Was code blank
or invalid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction type code validation has completed and the code was found to be blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK is set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the transaction type code validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Search Criteria Received' message (if no prior error message exists), sets the program state to 'Details Not Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED), and exits the input editing step, returning the user to the search prompt

rules.rule_name: Route to Invalid Search Keys Error When Code Is Invalid
rules.rule_description: When the transaction type code validation results in an invalid (non-numeric or zero) code, the system sets the program state to 'Invalid Search Keys' and resets to the search prompt state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Was code blank
or invalid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction type code validation has completed and the code was found to be invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is set, meaning non-numeric or zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the transaction type code validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program state to 'Invalid Search Keys' (TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS), sets the program state to 'Details Not Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED), and exits the input editing step

rules.rule_name: Skip Description Validation When Record Has Not Yet Been Fetched
rules.rule_description: When the transaction type code is valid but the corresponding record has not yet been retrieved from the database, the system skips description validation and proceeds to the database lookup step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Was record
already fetched?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction type code has passed validation and the filter flag is valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID), but the program state is still 'Details Not Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the record has already been fetched from the database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips all further input validation (including description validation and old-versus-new comparison) and exits the input editing step to proceed to the database lookup

rules.rule_name: Compare New Values Against Original Fetched Values for Changes
rules.rule_description: After a record has been fetched from the database, the system compares the user's newly entered transaction type code and description against the original values retrieved from the database to determine whether any changes have been made.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Compare New Values
Against Original Fetched Values

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction type record has previously been fetched from the database and the original values (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE and TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) are available in working storage
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the new transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) and new description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) against the original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The comparison is performed case-insensitively (using FUNCTION UPPER-CASE) and with leading/trailing spaces trimmed (using FUNCTION TRIM) on both the type code and description; additionally the trimmed lengths of both descriptions must match for the values to be considered unchanged

rules.rule_name: No Changes Detected Between New and Original Values
rules.rule_description: When the user's entered values are identical to the original database values (case-insensitive, trimmed), the system notifies the user that no changes were made and does not proceed to save.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Are type code AND
description unchanged?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has compared the new and original transaction type code and description
acceptance_criteria.When: The upper-cased trimmed new transaction type code equals the upper-cased trimmed original type code AND the upper-cased trimmed new description equals the upper-cased trimmed original description AND the trimmed lengths of both descriptions are equal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Changes Detected' flag (NO-CHANGES-DETECTED) if no prior error message exists, clears non-key flags (WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS to LOW-VALUES), and exits the input editing step without proceeding to description validation or save

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Must Be Supplied
rules.rule_description: The transaction type description is a mandatory field when changes have been detected. If the description is blank or empty, the system raises a validation error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is description
blank or empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: Changes have been detected between the new and original values and the system is validating the transaction description field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, up to 50 characters)
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction description is evaluated and found to be LOW-VALUES, spaces, or has a trimmed length of zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state (INPUT-ERROR), marks the description flag as blank (FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK), and sets the error message to 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.'

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Must Contain Only Alphanumeric Characters
rules.rule_description: The transaction type description must contain only letters and numbers. Special characters are not permitted. The description is validated up to 50 characters in length.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Does description contain
only alphanumeric characters
within 50 characters?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction description has been supplied (is not blank) and the system is performing character-type validation on the description field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, up to 50 characters)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system inspects the description by converting all valid alphanumeric characters (LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM) to spaces (LIT-ALPHANUM-SPACES-TO) and checks whether any non-alphanumeric characters remain (trimmed length is not zero)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If non-alphanumeric characters are found, the system sets the input to an error state (INPUT-ERROR), marks the description flag as not-ok (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), and sets the error message to 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.'

rules.rule_name: Set Changes Ready for User Confirmation After Successful Description Validation
rules.rule_description: When the transaction description passes all validation checks (non-blank and alphanumeric only), the system advances the program state to indicate that the changes are valid and ready for the user to confirm before saving.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Description Valid
Set state: Changes ready
for user confirmation

acceptance_criteria.Given: Changes have been detected between new and original values, and the transaction description has passed all validation checks (non-blank and alphanumeric characters only)
acceptance_criteria.When: The description validation completes successfully with no input errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the program state to 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), indicating the changes are validated and awaiting explicit user confirmation before being saved to the database

sub_functionalities.title: Validate Transaction Type Code
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Validate Transaction Type Code])

    A[Take entered Transaction Type Code\nfrom working storage]

    B{Is code blank\nor empty?}

    ERR1[Error:\nTransaction Type Code\nmust be supplied]

    C{Is code\nnumeric?}

    ERR2[Error:\nTransaction Type Code\nmust be numeric]

    D{Is code\nequal to zero?}

rules.rule_name: Initialize Transaction Type Code Validation
rules.rule_description: Before validating the Transaction Type Code entered by the user, the system prepares the validation context by defaulting the code status to INVALID, setting the field name to 'Tran Type code', loading the entered value into the validation area, and setting the expected length to 2 characters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Take entered Transaction Type Code from working storage

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the validation process for the Transaction Type Code field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Default the Transaction Type Code status to INVALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK), (2) Identify the field under validation as 'Tran Type code', (3) Load the entered Transaction Type Code value (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) into the validation working area (WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY), and (4) Set the expected field length to 2 characters (WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH = 2), before proceeding to individual validation checks

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Supplied
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Code is a mandatory field. If the user submits the screen without entering a Transaction Type Code, or enters only spaces, the system must reject the input with a specific error message indicating the field is required.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is code blank or empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and has submitted the screen (pressed ENTER or a valid PF key)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field contains LOW-VALUES, spaces only, or has a trimmed length of zero (i.e., is effectively blank or empty)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Input Error flag (INPUT-ERROR) to TRUE, (2) Mark the Transaction Type Code flag as BLANK (FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK), (3) Display the error message 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' to the user (stored in WS-RETURN-MSG, only if no prior error message exists), and (4) Stop further validation of this field immediately

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Numeric
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Code must consist entirely of numeric digits. If the entered value contains any non-numeric characters (letters, special characters, etc.), the system must reject the input with a specific error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is code numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered Transaction Type Code value (up to 2 characters) fails the numeric test — meaning it contains one or more non-numeric characters
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Input Error flag (INPUT-ERROR) to TRUE, (2) Mark the Transaction Type Code flag as NOT OK (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), (3) Display the error message 'Tran Type code must be numeric.' to the user (stored in WS-RETURN-MSG, only if no prior error message exists), and (4) Stop further validation of this field immediately

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Not Be Zero
rules.rule_description: Even if the Transaction Type Code is numeric, a value of zero (0 or 00) is not a valid Transaction Type Code. The system must reject zero as an invalid code with a specific error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is code equal to zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank, numeric Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The numeric value of the entered Transaction Type Code evaluates to zero (e.g., '0' or '00')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Input Error flag (INPUT-ERROR) to TRUE, (2) Mark the Transaction Type Code flag as NOT OK (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), (3) Display the error message 'Tran Type code must not be zero.' to the user (stored in WS-RETURN-MSG, only if no prior error message exists), and (4) Stop further validation of this field immediately

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Passes All Validations — Mark as Valid
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type Code passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, non-zero), the system marks the code as valid, enabling subsequent processing such as database lookup or record creation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Code is valid
Convert to numeric value

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a Transaction Type Code that is non-blank, fully numeric, and not equal to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: All three validation checks (blank, numeric, zero) have passed successfully
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the Transaction Type Code filter flag to VALID (FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID = TRUE), indicating the code is acceptable for further processing (e.g., database search or save operation)

rules.rule_name: Format Transaction Type Code with Leading Zeros
rules.rule_description: A valid Transaction Type Code must always be stored and used as a 2-digit zero-padded number. If the user enters a single digit (e.g., '5'), the system automatically formats it to its 2-digit equivalent (e.g., '05') before using it for any database operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format with leading zeros to ensure 2-digit representation e.g. 1 becomes 01

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code has passed all validation checks and is marked as VALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID = TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the validated Transaction Type Code for formatting
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Convert the entered Transaction Type Code to its numeric value using NUMVAL function, (2) Move the numeric value to a 2-character alphanumeric field (WS-EDIT-ALPHANUMERIC-2), (3) Replace all spaces in that field with zeros (leading zero padding), and (4) Store the resulting zero-padded 2-digit code back into the Transaction Type Code working field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE), so that, for example, an entry of '5' becomes '05' and '1' becomes '01'

rules.rule_name: Propagate Transaction Type Code Validation Result
rules.rule_description: After the numeric validation routine completes, the resulting validation status flags (valid, blank, or not-ok) are transferred from the generic validation working area back to the Transaction Type Code-specific flag, so that subsequent screen display and processing logic can correctly respond to the validation outcome.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Transaction Type Code as VALID / Mark Transaction Type Code as INVALID
Set Input Error flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code validation routine (1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD) has completed execution — either successfully or with an error
acceptance_criteria.When: Control returns from the numeric validation routine to the Transaction Type Code validation procedure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must copy the validation outcome flags from the generic alphanumeric validation flags (WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY-FLAGS) into the Transaction Type Code-specific flag (WS-EDIT-TTYP-FLAG), so that the Transaction Type Code field is correctly marked as either VALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID) or INVALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK / FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK) for use by downstream screen attribute and error display logic

rules.rule_name: Set Up Transaction Description Validation Parameters
rules.rule_description: Before validating the Transaction Description, the system prepares the validation context by identifying the field name as 'Transaction Desc', loading the user-entered description value, and setting the maximum allowable length to 50 characters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set field name to 'Transaction Desc'
Set description value for validation
Set maximum length to 50 characters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified a Transaction Type Description on the Transaction Type Update screen, and changes have been detected between the old and new description values
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the Transaction Description validation process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the field label to 'Transaction Desc', load the new description value (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) into the validation work area, and set the maximum validation length to 50 characters before performing any validation checks

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Must Not Be Blank or Missing
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Description is a mandatory field. The system must reject any submission where the description is blank, contains only spaces, or is entirely empty (low-values). The error message must clearly identify the field and the requirement.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is description
blank, empty,
or missing?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and has submitted a Transaction Type Description value for validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The description field contains only spaces, is entirely empty (low-values), or has zero non-space characters after trimming
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the overall input as invalid, (2) mark the description field specifically as blank, and (3) display the error message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' to the user

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Must Contain Only Alphanumeric Characters
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Description may only contain letters (A-Z, a-z) and digits (0-9). Any special characters, punctuation, or symbols are not permitted. The system validates this by converting all valid alphanumeric characters to spaces and checking if any non-alphanumeric characters remain.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Does description contain
only alphanumeric characters?
Numbers and letters only

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a non-blank Transaction Type Description on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: After removing all valid alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers) from the description, any non-space characters still remain within the 50-character validation length
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the overall input as invalid, (2) mark the description field as containing invalid characters, and (3) display the error message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' to the user

rules.rule_name: Mark Transaction Description as Valid When All Checks Pass
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type Description passes all validation checks — it is non-blank and contains only alphanumeric characters — the system marks the description field as valid, allowing the process to proceed to the final outcome determination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark description as valid

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Description has been submitted for validation on the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The description is non-blank AND contains only alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers) within the 50-character limit
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the description validation flag as valid (FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID), indicating the description field has passed all validation requirements

rules.rule_name: Determine Transaction Update State Based on Description Validation Outcome
rules.rule_description: After completing the Transaction Description validation, the system evaluates the overall validation result to determine the next program state. If validation passed, the changes are marked as ready for user confirmation before saving. If validation failed, the program remains in an error state requiring the user to correct the description.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Any input
errors found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Description validation process has completed and the description validation flags have been stored in the description flag work area (WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAGS)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether any input errors were found during the description validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If no input errors exist: the system must set the program state to 'Changes OK - Pending Confirmation' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), indicating the changes are valid and ready for the user to confirm before saving; If input errors exist: the system must keep the program state as 'Changes Not OK' (TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), requiring the user to correct the description before proceeding

sub_functionalities.title: Compare New Values Against Original Fetched Values
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Compare New Values\nAgainst Original Values])
    INIT[Set initial status:\nNo Changes Found]
    COMPARE_CODE{Do Type Codes Match?\nCase-insensitive comparison\nof new vs original type code}
    COMPARE_DESC{Do Descriptions Match?\nCase-insensitive comparison\nof trimmed new vs original description}
    COMPARE_LEN{Do Trimmed Description\nLengths Match?\nNew vs original description length}
    ALL_MATCH{All Three\nConditions Match?}
    NO_CHANGE[Set Status:\nNo Changes Detected\nUser made no modifications]
    CHANGE[Set Status:\nChange Has Occurred\nUser modified one or more fields]
    END_NO_CHANGE([End: No Changes -\nNo update action needed])
    END_CHANGE([End: Changes Detected -\nProceed to validate\nand confirm changes])

    START --> INIT
    INIT --> COMPARE_CODE
    COMPARE_CODE -->|Codes Match| COMPARE_DESC
    COMPARE_CODE -->|Codes Differ| CHANGE
    COMPARE_DESC -->|Descriptions Match| COMPARE_LEN
    COMPARE_DESC -->|Descriptions Differ| CHANGE
    COMPARE_LEN -->|Lengths Match| ALL_MATCH
    COMPARE_LEN -->|Lengths Differ| CHANGE
    ALL_MATCH -->|Yes - All Match| NO_CHANGE
    ALL_MATCH -->|No - Any Mismatch| CHANGE
    NO_CHANGE --> END_NO_CHANGE
    CHANGE --> END_CHANGE

rules.rule_name: Initialize Comparison Status Before Evaluating Changes
rules.rule_description: Before comparing new user-entered values against the original database values, the comparison status is initialized to 'No Changes Found' as the default assumption. This ensures a clean baseline before any field-level comparisons are performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set initial status: No Changes Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has retrieved a Transaction Type record and has submitted the screen with potentially modified values for Transaction Type Code and/or Transaction Type Description
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the process of comparing the newly entered values against the original values fetched from the database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The comparison status is initialized to 'No Changes Found' as the default starting state before any field-level comparison is evaluated

rules.rule_name: Compare Transaction Type Codes Case-Insensitively to Detect Changes
rules.rule_description: The system compares the newly entered Transaction Type Code against the original Transaction Type Code retrieved from the database. The comparison is performed in a case-insensitive manner. If the codes differ, a change is immediately flagged without evaluating the description fields.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Do Type Codes Match? Case-insensitive comparison of new vs original type code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The comparison status has been initialized to 'No Changes Found', and both the original Transaction Type Code (from the database) and the newly entered Transaction Type Code (from the screen) are available for comparison
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a case-insensitive comparison between the new Transaction Type Code and the original Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the two Transaction Type Codes differ (case-insensitively), the system immediately sets the status to 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process without evaluating the description; if they match, the system proceeds to compare the Transaction Type Descriptions

rules.rule_name: Compare Transaction Type Descriptions Case-Insensitively After Trimming Whitespace
rules.rule_description: After confirming the Transaction Type Codes match, the system compares the newly entered Transaction Type Description against the original description from the database. Both descriptions are trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace before the case-insensitive comparison is performed. If the trimmed descriptions differ, a change is flagged.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Do Descriptions Match? Case-insensitive comparison of trimmed new vs original description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Codes have been confirmed to match, and both the original Transaction Type Description (from the database) and the newly entered Transaction Type Description (from the screen) are available for comparison
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a case-insensitive comparison between the trimmed new Transaction Type Description and the trimmed original Transaction Type Description
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the trimmed descriptions differ (case-insensitively), the system sets the status to 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process without evaluating description lengths; if they match, the system proceeds to compare the trimmed description lengths

rules.rule_name: Compare Trimmed Description Lengths to Detect Whitespace-Only Differences
rules.rule_description: After confirming the trimmed descriptions match case-insensitively, the system additionally compares the character lengths of the trimmed new and original descriptions. This extra length check ensures that descriptions that appear identical after trimming but have different effective content lengths are still correctly identified as changed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Do Trimmed Description Lengths Match? New vs original description length

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the Transaction Type Codes and the trimmed case-insensitive descriptions have been confirmed to match, and the trimmed lengths of both the new and original Transaction Type Descriptions are available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the character length of the trimmed new Transaction Type Description against the character length of the trimmed original Transaction Type Description
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the trimmed lengths differ, the system sets the status to 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if the trimmed lengths are equal, the system proceeds to evaluate whether all three conditions collectively confirm no changes

rules.rule_name: Confirm No Changes When All Three Comparison Conditions Are Satisfied
rules.rule_description: When all three comparison conditions are simultaneously satisfied — the Transaction Type Codes match case-insensitively, the trimmed descriptions match case-insensitively, and the trimmed description lengths are equal — the system confirms that the user has made no effective modifications to the record. The status is set to 'No Changes Detected', which prevents an unnecessary database update from being triggered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All Three Conditions Match? / Set Status: No Changes Detected - User made no modifications

acceptance_criteria.Given: The comparison of Transaction Type Code (case-insensitive), Transaction Type Description (case-insensitive, trimmed), and trimmed Description Length between the newly entered values and the original database values has been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: All three conditions are simultaneously true: the Transaction Type Codes match case-insensitively, AND the trimmed descriptions match case-insensitively, AND the trimmed description lengths are equal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the comparison status to 'No Changes Detected', indicating the user has not made any effective modifications, and no database update action will be triggered for this record

rules.rule_name: Flag Change Has Occurred When Any Comparison Condition Fails
rules.rule_description: If any one of the three comparison conditions fails — the Transaction Type Codes differ, or the trimmed descriptions differ case-insensitively, or the trimmed description lengths differ — the system sets the status to 'Change Has Occurred'. This triggers the downstream validation and confirmation workflow to process the user's modifications before saving to the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Status: Change Has Occurred - User modified one or more fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is comparing the newly entered Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description against the original values retrieved from the database
acceptance_criteria.When: At least one of the following conditions is true: the Transaction Type Codes differ (case-insensitively), OR the trimmed Transaction Type Descriptions differ (case-insensitively), OR the trimmed description lengths differ
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the comparison status to 'Change Has Occurred', indicating the user has made at least one effective modification, and the comparison process exits immediately to proceed with validating and confirming the detected changes before any database update is performed

rules.rule_name: Accept User-Submitted Transaction Type Update Screen Data
rules.rule_description: When a user submits the Transaction Type Update screen, the system must accept and capture all field values entered by the user from the screen map into memory for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: System Accepts All Field Values Entered by the User from the Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered data on the Transaction Type Update screen and submitted the screen (pressed a key such as ENTER or a PF key)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the screen input from the Transaction Type Update screen map (CTRTUPAI) using the defined map set
acceptance_criteria.Then: All field values entered by the user are captured from the screen and held in memory (CTRTUPAI) ready for further processing, including the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDI) and the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCI)

rules.rule_name: Capture Transaction Type Code Field from Screen
rules.rule_description: The system captures the Transaction Type Code field value entered by the user on the Transaction Type Update screen. This field accepts up to 2 characters and is the primary key used to identify or search for a transaction type record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Transaction Type Code Field TRTYPCDI - up to 2 characters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Type Update screen with a value entered in the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDI)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the screen map input from the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field value (TRTYPCDI), up to 2 characters in length, is captured from the screen map (CTRTUPAI) and held in memory for subsequent validation and processing

rules.rule_name: Capture Transaction Type Description Field from Screen
rules.rule_description: The system captures the Transaction Type Description field value entered by the user on the Transaction Type Update screen. This field accepts up to 50 characters and holds the descriptive text associated with a transaction type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Transaction Description Field TRTYDSCI - up to 50 characters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Type Update screen with a value entered in the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCI)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the screen map input from the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Description field value (TRTYDSCI), up to 50 characters in length, is captured from the screen map (CTRTUPAI) and held in memory for subsequent validation and processing

rules.rule_name: Screen Input Values Ready for Further Processing
rules.rule_description: After the system successfully receives all screen field values from the Transaction Type Update screen, the captured data (Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description) is available in memory and the process proceeds to store and validate the input values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All Screen Field Values Now Held in Memory Ready for Further Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully received the screen map input from the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: Both the Transaction Type Code (TRTYPCDI) and Transaction Type Description (TRTYDSCI) field values have been captured from the screen into memory (CTRTUPAI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All captured screen field values are held in memory and the process proceeds to the next step of storing the screen input values for validation and business logic processing

rules.rule_name: Skip Re-Storing Input When Search Context Is Unchanged
rules.rule_description: When the user is in a 'Record Not Found' state and has not pressed PF5 (Save/Create), and the Transaction Type Code entered on screen matches the value already stored from the previous search, the system skips re-processing the screen inputs to preserve the existing search context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Not Found state AND F5 not pressed AND entered Transaction Type Code matches already stored value?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is in 'Record Not Found' state (a previous search returned no matching Transaction Type), AND the user has NOT pressed PF5 (Save/Create), AND the Transaction Type Code currently entered on screen (after trimming) is identical to the Transaction Type Code already stored in working storage from the previous search
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to store screen input values into working variables
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips all input storage processing and exits immediately without modifying any working storage variables, preserving the existing search context unchanged

rules.rule_name: Reset New Details Storage Before Storing Fresh Input
rules.rule_description: Before storing any new screen input values into working variables, the system clears and resets the entire new details storage area to ensure no residual data from a previous interaction contaminates the current input processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear and Reset New Details Storage Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that screen input must be stored (the skip condition was not met), AND there are working storage variables holding new Transaction Type details (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS) that may contain values from a prior screen interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to store the current screen input into working variables
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears and resets the entire new details storage area (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS) to its initial empty state before storing any new values, ensuring a clean slate for the current input

rules.rule_name: Treat Asterisk or Spaces as Empty Transaction Type Code
rules.rule_description: When the user enters an asterisk ('*') or spaces in the Transaction Type Code field, the system interprets this as an intentionally blank or cleared entry and stores an empty value internally, rather than treating the literal character as a valid code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transaction Type Code entered as asterisk or spaces?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is storing screen input into working variables, AND the Transaction Type Code field on the screen contains either an asterisk character ('*') or only space characters
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Type Code field value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system stores an empty value (LOW-VALUES) for the Transaction Type Code in working storage (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE), treating the asterisk or spaces as a signal that no Transaction Type Code was provided

rules.rule_name: Store Trimmed Transaction Type Code from Screen Input
rules.rule_description: When the user enters a valid (non-asterisk, non-space) Transaction Type Code on the screen, the system stores the value with leading and trailing spaces removed into the working storage variable for subsequent validation and processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store trimmed entered value for Transaction Type Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is storing screen input into working variables, AND the Transaction Type Code field on the screen contains a value that is neither an asterisk ('*') nor spaces
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Type Code field value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system trims leading and trailing spaces from the entered Transaction Type Code and stores the resulting trimmed value into the Transaction Type Code working storage variable (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE)

rules.rule_name: Treat Asterisk or Spaces as Empty Transaction Description
rules.rule_description: When the user enters an asterisk ('*') or spaces in the Transaction Description field, the system interprets this as an intentionally blank or cleared entry and stores an empty value internally, rather than treating the literal character as a valid description.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transaction Description entered as asterisk or spaces?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is storing screen input into working variables, AND the Transaction Description field on the screen contains either an asterisk character ('*') or only space characters
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Description field value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system stores an empty value (LOW-VALUES) for the Transaction Description in working storage (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC), treating the asterisk or spaces as a signal that no description was provided

rules.rule_name: Store Trimmed Transaction Description from Screen Input
rules.rule_description: When the user enters a valid (non-asterisk, non-space) Transaction Description on the screen, the system stores the value with leading and trailing spaces removed into the working storage variable for subsequent validation and processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store trimmed entered value for Transaction Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is storing screen input into working variables, AND the Transaction Description field on the screen contains a value that is neither an asterisk ('*') nor spaces
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Description field value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system trims leading and trailing spaces from the entered Transaction Description and stores the resulting trimmed value into the Transaction Description working storage variable (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC)

key_functionalities.description: Store Screen Input to Working Variables

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Type Code Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Transaction Type Code Validation])

    S1[Set validation status to Not Valid\nSet field name to 'Tran Type code'\nPrepare code for validation check\nSet maximum length to 2 characters]

    D1{Is Transaction\nType Code blank\nor empty?}

    E1[Set Error:\n'Tran Type code must be supplied']

    D2{Is Transaction\nType Code\npurely numeric?}

    S2[Mark Transaction Type Code\nas Valid]

    E1 --> END_ERR
    D1 -->|No - Has a Value| D2

    E3 --> END_ERR

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Supplied
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code field is not left blank or empty before any further validation is performed. This ensures users always provide a value to search or create a transaction type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Transaction Type Code blank or empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has submitted the form with a Transaction Type Code field
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field is blank, contains only spaces, contains only LOW-VALUES, or has a trimmed length of zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: Validation fails, an input error is flagged, the Transaction Type Code is marked as blank/invalid, and the error message 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' is set for display on the screen

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Numeric
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code contains only numeric digits. Non-numeric characters such as letters or special characters are not permitted in the Transaction Type Code field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Transaction Type Code purely numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code contains any non-numeric characters (i.e., it fails the numeric test)
acceptance_criteria.Then: Validation fails, an input error is flagged, the Transaction Type Code is marked as invalid, and the error message 'Tran Type code must be numeric.' is set for display on the screen

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Not Be Zero
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code, after confirming it is numeric, does not have a value of zero. A Transaction Type Code of zero is not a valid business identifier.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Transaction Type Code equal to zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank, numeric Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The numeric value of the Transaction Type Code evaluates to zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: Validation fails, an input error is flagged, the Transaction Type Code is marked as invalid, and the error message 'Tran Type code must not be zero.' is set for display on the screen

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Marked as Valid After Passing All Checks
rules.rule_description: Once the Transaction Type Code passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, non-zero), it is formally marked as valid so that downstream processing can proceed with confidence.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Transaction Type Code as Valid

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a Transaction Type Code that is non-blank, purely numeric, and non-zero
acceptance_criteria.When: All three validation checks (blank check, numeric check, zero check) have passed successfully
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code validation status is set to valid, allowing the system to proceed with formatting and database lookup

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Leading Zero Formatting
rules.rule_description: After a Transaction Type Code passes all validations, it is standardized to a 2-digit format by converting it to its numeric value and replacing any leading spaces with zeros. This ensures consistent storage and lookup (e.g., entering '5' is treated the same as '05').
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Convert code to numeric value
Replace any spaces with zeros
to format with leading zeros
e.g. '5' becomes '05'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type Code has passed all validation checks and is marked as valid
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the validated Transaction Type Code for use
acceptance_criteria.Then: The numeric value of the code is computed, any spaces within the 2-character field are replaced with zeros to produce a zero-padded result (e.g., '5 ' becomes '05'), and the formatted value is stored back as the Transaction Type Code for use in database operations

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Maximum Length Constraint
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Code is defined as a 2-character field. All validation checks are applied only to the first 2 characters of the input, enforcing the maximum allowable length for this business identifier.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set validation status to Not Valid
Set field name to 'Tran Type code'
Prepare code for validation check
Set maximum length to 2 characters

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Transaction Type Code field on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates validation of the Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The validation is applied to exactly 2 characters of the input field, the field is initially marked as not valid, the field label 'Tran Type code' is set for use in any error messages, and the input value is prepared for the blank, numeric, and zero checks

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Description Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Validate Transaction Description])

    CHK_BLANK{Is Description\nblank or empty?}

    ERR_BLANK[Validation Failed:\nTransaction Desc\nmust be supplied]

    CHK_ALPHANUM{Does Description\ncontain only letters\nand numbers?}

    ERR_ALPHANUM[Validation Failed:\nTransaction Desc can have\nnumbers or alphabets only]
