    START --> CHK_BLANK
    CHK_BLANK -->|Yes - Blank or Empty| ERR_BLANK
    CHK_BLANK -->|No - Value Provided| CHK_ALPHANUM
    CHK_ALPHANUM -->|No - Invalid Characters Found| ERR_ALPHANUM
    CHK_ALPHANUM -->|Yes - All Characters Valid| CHK_LENGTH
    CHK_LENGTH -->|No - Exceeds 50 Characters| ERR_LENGTH
    CHK_LENGTH -->|Yes - Within Limit| VALID
    VALID --> SET_CONFIRM
    SET_CONFIRM --> END_OK
    ERR_BLANK --> SET_NOT_OK
    ERR_ALPHANUM --> SET_NOT_OK
    ERR_LENGTH --> SET_NOT_OK
    SET_NOT_OK --> END_FAIL

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Mandatory Field Validation
rules.rule_description: Ensures that the Transaction Description field is not left blank or empty when a user attempts to save a new or updated Transaction Type record. The description must contain at least one non-space character.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Description blank or empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered or modified a Transaction Type record and the system is validating the Transaction Description field (labeled 'Transaction Desc') with a maximum allowed length of 50 characters
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Description value is entirely blank spaces, contains only low-value (null) characters, or has a trimmed length of zero — meaning no meaningful content has been provided
acceptance_criteria.Then: Validation fails; the Transaction Description field is flagged as blank; an error message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' is generated and stored as the return message; the overall input is marked as invalid; and processing of the description validation exits immediately without performing the alphanumeric character check

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Alphanumeric Character Validation
rules.rule_description: Ensures that the Transaction Description contains only valid alphanumeric characters (letters A–Z, a–z, and digits 0–9). Any special characters, punctuation, or symbols are not permitted in the Transaction Description field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does Description contain only letters and numbers?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field has passed the mandatory (non-blank) check and contains at least one non-space character, and the system proceeds to validate the character content of the description against the allowed alphanumeric character set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system converts all valid alphanumeric characters in the description to spaces and then checks whether any non-space characters remain — if non-space characters remain after conversion, it means the description contains at least one invalid (non-alphanumeric) character
acceptance_criteria.Then: If invalid characters are found: validation fails; the Transaction Description field is flagged as invalid (not-ok); an error message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' is generated and stored as the return message; the overall input is marked as invalid; and validation exits immediately. If no invalid characters are found: the Transaction Description is marked as valid and processing continues

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Maximum Length Enforcement
rules.rule_description: Enforces that the Transaction Description does not exceed the maximum allowed length of 50 characters. The validation operates on only the first 50 characters of the description field, effectively enforcing the 50-character limit by design of the field boundary used during validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Description within 50 characters?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is entering or updating a Transaction Type Description and the system is preparing to validate the description content
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the maximum validation length to 50 characters and performs all character-level checks (blank check and alphanumeric check) strictly within the first 50 characters of the description field
acceptance_criteria.Then: Only the first 50 characters of the Transaction Description are evaluated during validation; any content beyond 50 characters is outside the validated boundary, effectively enforcing the 50-character maximum length constraint on the Transaction Description

rules.rule_name: Transaction Description Validation Invocation and Field Setup
rules.rule_description: Defines the process by which the Transaction Description validation is triggered during input editing. Before invoking the validation routine, the system pre-sets the state to 'Changes Not OK' as a default, then passes the description value and its maximum length (50) to the validation routine. This ensures that validation failure is the default outcome unless the validation routine explicitly marks the input as valid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Validate that the transaction description is supplied and contains only alphanumeric characters within the allowed 50-character length

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted changes to a Transaction Type record (the record is in 'Show Details' state with detected changes), and the Transaction Type Code has already been validated successfully, and the system is now ready to validate the Transaction Description
acceptance_criteria.When: The system pre-marks the change state as 'Changes Not OK', assigns the field label 'Transaction Desc', copies the user-entered description into the validation work area, sets the maximum validation length to 50 characters, and invokes the alphanumeric validation routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The validation routine is executed against the Transaction Description with a 50-character limit; the resulting validation flags are stored back into the description-specific flag area for use in screen attribute setup and error display

rules.rule_name: Mark Transaction Description Changes as Valid and Ready for User Confirmation
rules.rule_description: After the Transaction Description passes all validation checks (non-blank and alphanumeric-only), the system transitions the record state to indicate that the proposed changes are valid and are now awaiting explicit user confirmation before being saved to the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Changes as Valid and Ready for Confirmation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Description has been validated and no input errors were detected — meaning the description is non-blank, contains only alphanumeric characters, and is within the 50-character limit
acceptance_criteria.When: The validation routine completes without setting the input-error flag
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), indicating that the user's changes are valid and the screen should prompt the user to press PF5 to confirm and save the changes, or PF12 to cancel

rules.rule_name: Mark Transaction Description Input as Invalid and Prompt User to Correct
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Description fails any validation check (blank/empty or contains non-alphanumeric characters), the system marks the overall input state as invalid and retains the 'Changes Not OK' state, causing the screen to be redisplayed with the appropriate error message so the user can correct the description.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Input as Invalid - Prompt User to Correct

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has invoked the Transaction Description validation routine and the validation has detected an error — either the description is blank/empty or it contains characters that are not letters or numbers
acceptance_criteria.When: The validation routine sets the input-error flag (INPUT-ERROR) due to a blank description or invalid characters in the description
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Changes Not OK' (TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), which was pre-set before validation was invoked; the corresponding error message ('Transaction Desc must be supplied.' or 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.') is retained as the screen error message; and the screen is redisplayed to the user with the error highlighted so the user can correct the Transaction Description

key_functionalities.title: Change Detection
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start Change Detection])

    COMPARE1{Does new Transaction\nType Code match\noriginal Type Code?\nCase-insensitive comparison}

    COMPARE2{Does new Transaction\nDescription match\noriginal Description?\nCase-insensitive, trimmed,\nsame length comparison}

    NO_CHANGE[Mark as:\nNo Changes Detected\nNo update action needed]

    CHANGE[Mark as:\nChange Has Occurred\nProceed to validate\nand confirm changes]

    END_NO_CHANGE([Exit:\nReturn to Input Processing\nwith No-Change status])
    END_CHANGE([Exit:\nReturn to Input Processing\nwith Change-Detected status])

    START --> COMPARE1
    COMPARE1 -->|Yes - Codes Match| COMPARE2
    COMPARE1 -->|No - Codes Differ| CHANGE
    COMPARE2 -->|Yes - Descriptions Match| NO_CHANGE
    COMPARE2 -->|No - Descriptions Differ| CHANGE
    NO_CHANGE --> END_NO_CHANGE
    CHANGE --> END_CHANGE

rules.rule_name: Initialize Change Detection Status Before Comparison
rules.rule_description: Before comparing old and new transaction type values, the change detection status is initialized to a neutral 'No Changes Found' state to ensure a clean baseline for the comparison process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Start Change Detection

acceptance_criteria.Given: The change detection process has been invoked to compare the user-entered transaction type details against the originally fetched database values
acceptance_criteria.When: The change detection routine begins execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The change status flag is set to 'No Changes Found' as the default starting state before any comparison is performed

rules.rule_name: Compare Transaction Type Code for Changes
rules.rule_description: The newly entered Transaction Type Code is compared against the originally fetched Transaction Type Code using a case-insensitive comparison to determine if the code has been modified by the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does new Transaction Type Code match original Type Code? Case-insensitive comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted transaction type details on the screen and the system holds both the newly entered Transaction Type Code and the originally fetched Transaction Type Code from the database
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a case-insensitive comparison between the new Transaction Type Code and the original Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the two codes match (case-insensitively), the system proceeds to compare the Transaction Type Description; if the codes do not match, the system immediately marks the status as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison

rules.rule_name: Compare Transaction Type Description for Changes
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type Codes match, the system further compares the Transaction Type Descriptions using a case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed, and length-equal comparison to detect any description-level changes made by the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does new Transaction Description match original Description? Case-insensitive, trimmed, same length comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The newly entered Transaction Type Code matches the originally fetched Transaction Type Code, and the system holds both the newly entered Transaction Type Description and the originally fetched Transaction Type Description
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a three-part comparison of the descriptions: (1) case-insensitive equality of trimmed new description versus trimmed original description, AND (2) the trimmed length of the new description equals the trimmed length of the original description — both conditions must be true simultaneously
acceptance_criteria.Then: If both the trimmed case-insensitive content AND the trimmed lengths match, the system marks the status as 'No Changes Detected'; if either the content or the length differs, the system marks the status as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison

rules.rule_name: Mark No Changes Detected When All Values Are Identical
rules.rule_description: When both the Transaction Type Code and the Transaction Type Description are found to be identical to the originally fetched database values (after case-insensitive and trimmed comparison), the system marks the result as 'No Changes Detected', indicating that no update action is required.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark as: No Changes Detected - No update action needed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted transaction type details, the system has compared the new Transaction Type Code and new Transaction Type Description against the original database values, and all comparisons have returned a match (case-insensitive, trimmed, same length), AND no prior error or return message is currently active
acceptance_criteria.When: All three comparison conditions are satisfied: the Transaction Type Codes match case-insensitively, the trimmed Transaction Type Descriptions match case-insensitively, and the trimmed lengths of the descriptions are equal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the change status to 'No Changes Detected', signalling that no update to the database is needed and the user should be informed that no changes were made

rules.rule_name: Mark Change Has Occurred When Any Value Differs
rules.rule_description: When either the Transaction Type Code or the Transaction Type Description differs from the originally fetched database values, the system marks the result as 'Change Has Occurred', triggering the validation and confirmation workflow for the detected changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark as: Change Has Occurred - Proceed to validate and confirm changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted transaction type details, the system is comparing the new values against the original database values, AND no prior error or return message is currently active
acceptance_criteria.When: At least one of the following conditions is true: (1) the new Transaction Type Code does not match the original Transaction Type Code (case-insensitive), OR (2) the trimmed new Transaction Type Description does not match the trimmed original Transaction Type Description (case-insensitive), OR (3) the trimmed length of the new Transaction Type Description does not equal the trimmed length of the original Transaction Type Description
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the change status to 'Change Has Occurred', and the comparison process exits immediately to return control to the input processing routine with a change-detected status, which will proceed to validate the changed values and prompt the user for confirmation before saving

rules.rule_name: Suppress Change Status Update When Prior Message Exists
rules.rule_description: The 'No Changes Detected' and 'Change Has Occurred' status flags are only set when there is no prior active return message on the screen. If a return message is already present, the comparison result is determined but the status flags are not updated, preserving the existing message context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark as: No Changes Detected - No update action needed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The change detection comparison has completed and a result (either match or mismatch) has been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to set the change status flag ('No Changes Detected' or 'Change Has Occurred') but a prior return message is already active (the return message flag is not in the 'off' state)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not update the change status flag and continues processing without overwriting the existing message context; the status flags 'No Changes Detected' and 'Change Has Occurred' are only set when the return message is in the 'off' (inactive) state

    SET_UPDATE_CANCEL --> END_EXIT
    SET_NOTFETCHED --> END_EXIT

    D_CONFIRM_DEL_F12 -->|Yes| KEEP_CONFIRM
    KEEP_CONFIRM --> END_EXIT
    D_CONFIRM_DEL_F12 -->|No| D_SHOW_DETAILS
    D_SHOW_DETAILS -->|Yes| D_INPUT_ERR
    D_INPUT_ERR -->|Yes - No Action Needed| STAY_SHOW
    D_INPUT_ERR -->|No - Valid Changes Made| SET_CHANGES_CONFIRM
    STAY_SHOW --> END_EXIT
    SET_CHANGES_CONFIRM --> END_EXIT
    D_SHOW_DETAILS -->|No| D_CHANGES_NOTOK
    D_CHANGES_NOTOK -->|Yes| STAY_NOTOK
    STAY_NOTOK --> END_EXIT
    D_CHANGES_NOTOK -->|No| D_BACKED_OUT
    D_BACKED_OUT -->|Yes| SET_NOTOK
    SET_NOTOK --> END_EXIT
    D_BACKED_OUT -->|No| D_INVALID_KEYS
    D_INVALID_KEYS -->|Yes| STAY_INVALID
    STAY_INVALID --> END_EXIT
    D_INVALID_KEYS -->|No| D_PFK05_NOTFOUND
    D_PFK05_NOTFOUND -->|Yes| SET_CREATE
    SET_CREATE --> END_EXIT
    D_PFK05_NOTFOUND -->|No| D_CHANGES_OK_NOTCONF

rules.rule_name: Trigger Database Lookup When Details Not Yet Fetched or F12 Pressed with Valid Type Code
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the 'Details Not Fetched' state or the user presses F12, and the Transaction Type code entered is valid, the system initiates a database lookup to retrieve the Transaction Type record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Details Not Yet Fetched OR F12 Pressed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Fetched' state OR the user has pressed F12, AND the Transaction Type code has been validated as a non-blank, non-zero, 2-digit numeric value
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system performs a lookup of the Transaction Type in the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table using the entered type code as the search key

rules.rule_name: Display Transaction Type Details When Record Found in Database
rules.rule_description: After a database lookup, if a matching Transaction Type record is found, the system transitions to the 'Show Details' state so the record can be viewed or edited.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Found in Database?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A database lookup has been performed for the entered Transaction Type code
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns a matching record (successful retrieval)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Show Transaction Type Details', and the retrieved Transaction Type code and description are displayed on screen for the user to view or modify

rules.rule_name: Mark Record Not Found When No Matching Transaction Type Exists
rules.rule_description: After a database lookup, if no matching Transaction Type record is found for the entered type code, the system marks the state as 'Record Not Found' and prompts the user with the option to create a new record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Record Not Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: A database lookup has been performed for the entered Transaction Type code
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns no matching record (record not found)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Details Not Found', and the user is prompted with the option to create a new Transaction Type record using the entered type code

rules.rule_name: Cancel Delete Operation When F12 Pressed with Invalid Type Code During Delete Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type code is not valid and the program was in the 'Confirm Delete' state, pressing F12 cancels the pending delete operation and resets the screen to the initial search state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Cancel Due to Delete or Update?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Fetched' state or F12 was pressed, AND the Transaction Type code is not valid, AND the program was previously in the 'Confirm Delete' state
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic evaluates the cancellation context
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the delete as cancelled ('Delete Was Cancelled'), resets the program state to 'Details Not Fetched', and the screen returns to the initial search prompt

rules.rule_name: Cancel Update Operation When F12 Pressed with Invalid Type Code During Update Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type code is not valid and the program was in the 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state, pressing F12 cancels the pending update and sets the state to 'Changes Backed Out'.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Cancel Due to Delete or Update?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Fetched' state or F12 was pressed, AND the Transaction Type code is not valid, AND the program was previously in the 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (awaiting save confirmation) state
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic evaluates the cancellation context
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the update as cancelled ('Update Was Cancelled'), sets the program state to 'Changes Backed Out', and the screen returns to display the original unmodified values

rules.rule_name: Reset to Initial Search State When Type Code Invalid with No Specific Cancel Context
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type code is not valid and the program was not in a delete confirmation or update confirmation state, the program resets to the initial 'Details Not Fetched' state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset to Not Fetched State

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Fetched' state or F12 was pressed, AND the Transaction Type code is not valid, AND the program was NOT in 'Confirm Delete' or 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic evaluates the cancellation context
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is reset to 'Details Not Fetched' and the screen returns to the initial search prompt

rules.rule_name: Maintain Delete Confirmation State When F12 Pressed During Confirm Delete
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the 'Confirm Delete' state and the user presses F12 (with a valid type code context), the delete confirmation state is preserved and the confirmation prompt remains displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Keep Delete Confirmation State

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is NOT in 'Details Not Fetched' state and F12 was NOT the triggering key for a reset, AND the program is currently in 'Confirm Delete' state, AND F12 is pressed
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Confirm Delete' and the delete confirmation prompt continues to be displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Remain on Details View When Input Has Errors, No Changes, or Invalid Key While Showing Details
rules.rule_description: When the program is showing transaction type details and the user's input contains errors, no changes were detected compared to the original values, or an invalid key was pressed, the screen remains in the 'Show Details' state without transitioning.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Remain on Details View

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Show Details' state displaying a Transaction Type record
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic detects that: an input validation error exists, OR no changes were detected between old and new values (type code and description are identical case-insensitively after trimming), OR an invalid key was pressed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Show Details' and the screen is redisplayed with the current values and any applicable error or informational message

rules.rule_name: Mark Changes Ready for Confirmation When Valid Modifications Detected While Showing Details
rules.rule_description: When the program is showing transaction type details and the user has made valid changes to the description (no input errors, changes detected), the system transitions to the 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state to prompt the user to confirm before saving.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Changes Ready for Confirmation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Show Details' state displaying a Transaction Type record
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic detects that: there are no input validation errors, AND changes have been detected between the old and new values (description differs case-insensitively or in trimmed length), AND no invalid key was pressed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Changes OK Not Confirmed', and the screen prompts the user to confirm the changes before they are saved to the database

rules.rule_name: Remain in Changes Not OK State When Validation Errors Persist
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the 'Changes Not OK' state (validation errors were found in the previous input), the state is maintained and the user is prompted to correct the errors.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Remain on Changes Not OK State

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Changes Not OK' state due to prior validation failures
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Changes Not OK', the screen is redisplayed with the validation error message, and the user is prompted to re-enter valid data

rules.rule_name: Transition to Changes Not OK State After Changes Are Backed Out
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the 'Changes Backed Out' state (a previous update was cancelled), the system transitions to 'Changes Not OK' to prompt the user to re-enter their modifications.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Changes Not OK - Prompt User to Re-enter

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Changes Backed Out' state, indicating a prior update was cancelled by the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Changes Not OK', the original values are displayed, and the user is prompted to make changes to the Transaction Type description

rules.rule_name: Remain in Invalid Search Keys State When Search Keys Were Invalid
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the 'Invalid Search Keys' state due to a prior invalid Transaction Type code entry, the state is maintained and the user is prompted to re-enter a valid search key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Remain on Invalid Keys State

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Invalid Search Keys' state due to a previously entered Transaction Type code that failed validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Invalid Search Keys', the screen is redisplayed with the appropriate error message, and the user is prompted to enter a valid Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: Switch to Create New Record Mode When F5 Pressed and Record Not Found
rules.rule_description: When the user presses F5 after a search returns no matching record, the system switches to 'Create New Record' mode, allowing the user to enter details for a new Transaction Type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Switch to Create New Record Mode

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Found' state, indicating no Transaction Type record exists for the entered type code
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses F5 (Save/Confirm key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Create New Record', the screen transitions to allow entry of a new Transaction Type description, and the user is prompted to enter the new record details

rules.rule_name: Remain on Confirmation Prompt When Changes Are Validated But Not Yet Confirmed
rules.rule_description: When the program is in the 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state (changes have passed validation and are awaiting user confirmation to save), the state is maintained and the confirmation prompt remains displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Remain on Confirmation Prompt

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state, meaning the user's changes have passed all validation checks and are awaiting final confirmation
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Changes OK Not Confirmed', the screen continues to display the confirmation prompt asking the user to press F5 to save or F12 to cancel

rules.rule_name: Return to Show Details View After Changes Are Successfully Saved
rules.rule_description: After a Transaction Type update or insert has been successfully committed to the database, the program transitions back to the 'Show Details' state to display the saved record. If no calling transaction context exists, account-related fields are cleared.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return to Show Details View

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in 'Changes Okayed And Done' state, meaning the Transaction Type record has been successfully updated or inserted in the database and committed
acceptance_criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Show Details' to display the saved Transaction Type record; additionally, if no calling transaction ID or program is present (values are blank or low-values), the account ID, card number, and account status fields are cleared to zero or low-values respectively

sub_functionalities.title: Look Up Transaction Type in Database
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Look Up Transaction Type])

    A[Use entered Transaction Type Code\nas search key]

    B[(Query CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nWhere TR_TYPE = Entered Code)]

    D_RESULT{Query\nOutcome?}

    FOUND[Record Found\nRetrieve Transaction Type Code\nand Description]

    NOT_FOUND[Record Not Found\nNo matching transaction type\nexists in the database]

    STORE[Save Retrieved Details\nStore Transaction Type Code\nand Description for display\nand comparison]

    STATE_SHOW[Set State: Show Details\nPrepare to display the\nfound transaction type to user]

    STATE_NOTFOUND[Set State: Record Not Found\nPrepare to offer user option\nto create a new record]

    START --> A
    A --> B
    B --> D_RESULT

    D_RESULT -->|Record Exists| FOUND
    D_RESULT -->|Record Does Not Exist| NOT_FOUND

    FOUND --> STORE
    STORE --> STATE_SHOW
    NOT_FOUND --> STATE_NOTFOUND

    STATE_SHOW --> END_FOUND([End: Proceed to Display\nTransaction Type Details])
    STATE_NOTFOUND --> END_NOTFOUND([End: Proceed to\nNot Found Handling])

rules.rule_name: Use Entered Transaction Type Code as Database Search Key
rules.rule_description: The system uses the Transaction Type Code entered by the user as the exact search key to query the TRANSACTION_TYPE table. The entered code is moved directly into the database host variable before the query is executed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use entered Transaction Type Code as search key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a Transaction Type Code on the screen and the system is ready to perform a database lookup
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the Transaction Type lookup process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system uses the user-entered Transaction Type Code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) as the exact search key by assigning it to the database query parameter (DCL-TR-TYPE) before querying the TRANSACTION_TYPE table

rules.rule_name: Query TRANSACTION_TYPE Table by Transaction Type Code
rules.rule_description: The system queries the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table to retrieve the Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and its Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) for the exact Transaction Type Code provided by the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Query CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE Where TR_TYPE = Entered Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user-entered Transaction Type Code has been assigned as the search key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes a SELECT query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using an exact match condition on TR_TYPE equal to the entered code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves both the TR_TYPE (Transaction Type Code) and TR_DESCRIPTION (Transaction Type Description) fields from the matching record, if one exists

rules.rule_name: Handle Successful Transaction Type Record Found
rules.rule_description: When the database query returns a matching record for the entered Transaction Type Code, the system marks the lookup as successful, indicating the transaction type exists and its details are available for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Found
Retrieve Transaction Type Code
and Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has executed a query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the entered Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The query returns a matching record (successful retrieval with no errors)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the indicator FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE to TRUE, confirming that the Transaction Type Code and its Description have been successfully retrieved from the database

rules.rule_name: Handle Transaction Type Record Not Found
rules.rule_description: When the database query finds no matching record for the entered Transaction Type Code, the system marks the search as unsuccessful and sets an informational message to notify the user that the record does not exist.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Not Found
No matching transaction type
exists in the database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has executed a query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the entered Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The query returns a 'no data found' result indicating no record exists for the entered Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state, marks the transaction type filter as not valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK), and sets the message indicator to 'Record Not Found' to inform the user that no matching transaction type exists in the database

rules.rule_name: Save Retrieved Transaction Type Details for Display and Comparison
rules.rule_description: When a Transaction Type record is successfully found, the system saves the retrieved Transaction Type Code and Description as the original (old) values. These stored values are used for screen display and to detect any subsequent changes made by the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Retrieved Details
Store Transaction Type Code
and Description for display
and comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The database query has successfully retrieved a Transaction Type record with its Code (TR_TYPE) and Description (TR_DESCRIPTION)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched data into the working storage area for original values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system saves the retrieved Transaction Type Code into TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE and saves the retrieved Transaction Type Description (trimmed to its actual stored length as indicated by DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN) into TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, making both values available for screen display and future change-detection comparison

rules.rule_name: Set Screen State to Show Details After Successful Lookup
rules.rule_description: After a Transaction Type record is successfully found and its details are stored, the system transitions the screen state to 'Show Details', enabling the user to view the record and take further actions such as editing or deleting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set State: Show Details
Prepare to display the
found transaction type to user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type lookup has completed and the FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE indicator is set to TRUE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the lookup within the action decision logic
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, which prepares the screen to display the retrieved Transaction Type Code and Description to the user and enables edit and delete options

rules.rule_name: Set Screen State to Record Not Found After Unsuccessful Lookup
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type lookup finds no matching record, the system transitions the screen state to 'Details Not Found', which informs the user that the entered Transaction Type Code does not exist and offers the option to create a new record with that code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set State: Record Not Found
Prepare to offer user option
to create a new record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type lookup has completed and the FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE indicator is NOT set to TRUE (record was not found in the database)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the lookup within the action decision logic
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, which prepares the screen to inform the user that no matching Transaction Type exists and activates the option (PF5) for the user to create a new Transaction Type record using the entered code

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Type Lookup
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Transaction Type Lookup])

    INIT[Clear any previously fetched\ntransaction type details]

    PREP[Prepare search using\nentered Transaction Type Code]

    QUERY[(Query CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nWHERE TR_TYPE = Entered Code\nRetrieve: Type Code and Description)]

    D_RESULT{What was the\nquery result?}

    FOUND[Record Located:\nMark transaction type\nas found in table]

    NOT_FOUND[Record Not Found:\nNo matching transaction type\nexists for entered code]

    STORE[Store retrieved Type Code\nand Description for\ndisplay and comparison]

    END_FOUND([End: Record Available\nfor Display])
    END_NOTFOUND([End: Record Not Found\nUser may create new record])

    START --> INIT
    INIT --> PREP
    PREP --> QUERY
    QUERY --> D_RESULT

    D_RESULT -->|Record Found| FOUND
    D_RESULT -->|No Record Exists| NOT_FOUND

    FOUND --> STORE

    NOT_FOUND --> END_NOTFOUND

rules.rule_name: Clear Previously Fetched Transaction Type Details Before New Lookup
rules.rule_description: Before performing a new transaction type lookup, any previously retrieved transaction type details stored in memory must be cleared to prevent stale data from being displayed or compared against new results.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear any previously fetched transaction type details

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has initiated a transaction type lookup by entering a Transaction Type Code on the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the Transaction Type Lookup process
acceptance_criteria.Then: All previously stored transaction type details (old Transaction Type Code and old Transaction Type Description) are cleared/reset before the new database query is executed, ensuring no residual data from a prior lookup remains

rules.rule_name: Prepare Transaction Type Code as Search Key for Database Query
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Code entered by the user on the screen must be used as the exact search key when querying the Transaction Type database table.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prepare search using entered Transaction Type Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a valid, non-blank, numeric, non-zero Transaction Type Code (2 digits, zero-padded if necessary, e.g., '05') on the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to query the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entered Transaction Type Code is set as the search parameter (TR_TYPE) to be used in the database query for an exact match lookup

rules.rule_name: Query TRANSACTION_TYPE Table for Matching Record
rules.rule_description: The system queries the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table using the entered Transaction Type Code as an exact match filter to retrieve the corresponding Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Query CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE WHERE TR_TYPE = Entered Code Retrieve: Type Code and Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code has been prepared as the search key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the database query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the condition that TR_TYPE exactly equals the entered Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the TR_TYPE (Transaction Type Code, 2 characters) and TR_DESCRIPTION (Transaction Type Description, up to 50 characters) for the matching record, if one exists

rules.rule_name: Mark Transaction Type as Found When Record Exists in Table
rules.rule_description: When the database query returns a matching record for the entered Transaction Type Code, the system marks the transaction type as successfully found, enabling the record details to be displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Located: Mark transaction type as found in table

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has executed a query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the entered Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The query returns exactly one matching record (successful retrieval with no errors)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the transaction type as 'Found in Table', indicating that a valid record exists and its details are available for display, editing, or deletion

rules.rule_name: Handle No Matching Transaction Type Record Found
rules.rule_description: When the database query finds no record matching the entered Transaction Type Code, the system marks the search as unsuccessful and sets the appropriate status so the user can be informed and optionally prompted to create a new record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Not Found: No matching transaction type exists for entered code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has executed a query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the entered Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The query returns no matching record (the entered Transaction Type Code does not exist in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the input as having an error, flags the Transaction Type Code filter as invalid/not-found, and sets a 'Record Not Found' message to inform the user that no transaction type exists for the entered code; the user may subsequently be offered the option to create a new record with that code

rules.rule_name: Store Retrieved Transaction Type Details for Display and Comparison
rules.rule_description: After successfully retrieving a transaction type record from the database, the system stores the retrieved Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description as the original baseline values. These stored values are used for screen display and to detect whether the user has made any changes during an edit operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store retrieved Type Code and Description for display and comparison

acceptance_criteria.Given: The database query has successfully retrieved a transaction type record with a Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and a Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched record details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The retrieved Transaction Type Code is stored as the original Transaction Type Code, and the retrieved Transaction Type Description is stored as the original Transaction Type Description (trimmed to its actual character length, up to 50 characters); these original values serve as the baseline for display on screen and for comparison against any user modifications to detect changes

key_functionalities.title: Store Fetched Transaction Type Data
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Store Fetched Transaction Type Data])

    A[Clear any previously held\nTransaction Type details\nfrom working storage]

    B[Save retrieved Transaction Type Code\ninto Old-Details storage area\nfor later comparison and display]

    C[Save retrieved Transaction Description\nusing exact character length returned\nfrom database into Old-Details storage area]

    D[Old-Details storage now holds\nthe current database values:\n- Transaction Type Code\n- Transaction Description]

    END_NODE([End: Data Ready for\nComparison and Display])

    START --> A
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> END_NODE

rules.rule_name: Clear Previously Held Transaction Type Details Before Storing New Data
rules.rule_description: Before storing newly retrieved transaction type data from the database, any previously held old-details in working storage must be cleared to prevent stale data from persisting across lookups.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear any previously held Transaction Type details from working storage

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully retrieved a Transaction Type record from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table and is about to store the fetched data into the Old-Details working storage area
acceptance_criteria.When: The store-fetched-data process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields within the Old-Details working storage area (TTUP-OLD-DETAILS), including the Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description, are reset to their initial empty state before any new values are moved in, ensuring no previously retrieved transaction type data remains

rules.rule_name: Save Retrieved Transaction Type Code into Old-Details Storage
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Code retrieved from the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table must be saved into the Old-Details working storage area so it can be used for subsequent comparison against user-entered values and for display on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save retrieved Transaction Type Code into Old-Details storage area for later comparison and display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The TRANSACTION_TYPE table has returned a valid Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE, 2-character field) and the Old-Details working storage area has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched transaction type data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The retrieved Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) is saved exactly as-is into the Old-Details Transaction Type Code field (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE), making it available for old-versus-new comparison and for redisplaying the original database value on the screen

rules.rule_name: Save Retrieved Transaction Type Description Using Exact Character Length into Old-Details Storage
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Type Description retrieved from the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table must be saved into the Old-Details working storage area using only the exact number of characters returned by the database (variable length), so it can be used for accurate comparison against user-entered values and for display on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save retrieved Transaction Description using exact character length returned from database into Old-Details storage area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The TRANSACTION_TYPE table has returned a Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION, variable-length up to 50 characters) along with its actual character length indicator (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN), and the Old-Details working storage area has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the fetched transaction type description data
acceptance_criteria.Then: Only the exact number of characters specified by the database-returned length indicator (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN) are copied from the retrieved description text (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT) into the Old-Details Transaction Type Description field (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC), ensuring the stored description precisely matches the database value without padding or truncation beyond the actual data length, making it available for old-versus-new comparison and for redisplaying the original database value on the screen

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Type Update
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Save Confirmed Changes\nF5 Pressed with Validated Data])

    PREP[Prepare Update Data\nSet transaction type code\nand description for database write]

    EXEC_UPDATE[Execute UPDATE on\nTRANSACTION_TYPE Table\nModify description for given type code]

    DB[(CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nDB2 Table)]

    D_SQLCODE{What was the\nUpdate Result?}

    SUCCESS[Update Successful\nCommit changes to database]

    NOT_FOUND[Record Does Not Exist\nNo existing record found\nfor this transaction type code]

    INSERT_NEW[Create New Record Instead\nInsert new transaction type\ninto TRANSACTION_TYPE table]

    INSERT_RESULT{Insert\nSuccessful?}

    INSERT_SUCCESS[New Record Created\nCommit new record\nto database]

    INSERT_FAIL[Save Failed\nUnable to create\nnew transaction type record]

    LOCK_CONFLICT[Record Locked by Another User\nTransaction type is currently\nbeing updated by someone else\nPlease retry]

    UPDATE_FAIL[Update Failed\nUnable to modify\ntransaction type record]

    SHOW_SUCCESS([Show Success Message\nTransaction type updated\nor created successfully])

    SHOW_LOCK([Show Lock Message\nRecord could not be updated\ndue to concurrent access])

    SHOW_FAIL([Show Failure Message\nUpdate operation\nwas unsuccessful])

    START --> PREP
    PREP --> EXEC_UPDATE
    EXEC_UPDATE -.->|Write to Database| DB
    DB -.->|Result Returned| D_SQLCODE

    D_SQLCODE -->|Success| SUCCESS
    D_SQLCODE -->|Record Not Found| NOT_FOUND
    D_SQLCODE -->|Record Locked by Another User| LOCK_CONFLICT
    D_SQLCODE -->|Other Failure| UPDATE_FAIL

    NOT_FOUND --> INSERT_NEW
    INSERT_NEW -.->|Insert into Database| DB
    DB -.->|Insert Result| INSERT_RESULT
    INSERT_RESULT -->|Success| INSERT_SUCCESS
    INSERT_RESULT -->|Failure| INSERT_FAIL

    SUCCESS --> SHOW_SUCCESS
    INSERT_SUCCESS --> SHOW_SUCCESS
    LOCK_CONFLICT --> SHOW_LOCK
    UPDATE_FAIL --> SHOW_FAIL
    INSERT_FAIL --> SHOW_FAIL

rules.rule_name: Prepare Transaction Type Data for Database Write
rules.rule_description: Before executing a database update, the system prepares the transaction type code and description by mapping the validated user-entered values into the database host variables, trimming the description to its actual content length.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Prepare Update Data
Set transaction type code
and description for database write

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed changes to a transaction type record and PF5 has been pressed with validated data, where TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE contains the transaction type code and TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC contains the new description
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the data for the database write operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets DCL-TR-TYPE to the value of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, sets DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT to the trimmed value of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, and sets DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN to the full length of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, making the data ready for the UPDATE statement

rules.rule_name: Execute Update on Transaction Type Record
rules.rule_description: The system attempts to modify an existing transaction type description in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table by matching on the transaction type code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Execute UPDATE on
TRANSACTION_TYPE Table
Modify description for given type code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The host variables DCL-TR-TYPE and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION have been populated with the transaction type code and new description respectively
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the SQL UPDATE statement against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table setting TR_DESCRIPTION equal to DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION where TR_TYPE equals DCL-TR-TYPE
acceptance_criteria.Then: The database attempts to update the TR_DESCRIPTION column for the matching TR_TYPE row, and the resulting SQLCODE is stored in WS-DISP-SQLCODE for subsequent outcome evaluation

rules.rule_name: Commit Successful Transaction Type Update
rules.rule_description: When the database UPDATE completes successfully, the changes are permanently committed to the database and the screen state is set to reflect a successful update.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Update Successful
Commit changes to database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned equals zero, indicating the UPDATE was successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system issues a SYNCPOINT to permanently commit the changes to the database, and the program state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, which triggers a success confirmation message to be displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Attempt Insert When Transaction Type Record Does Not Exist
rules.rule_description: When the UPDATE finds no existing record for the given transaction type code, the system automatically attempts to create a new record by switching to an INSERT operation instead.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Does Not Exist
No existing record found
for this transaction type code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned equals +100, indicating no existing row was found for the specified transaction type code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to execute the INSERT operation (9700-INSERT-RECORD) to create a new transaction type record using the same DCL-TR-TYPE and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION host variables, without displaying an error to the user

rules.rule_name: Insert New Transaction Type Record into Database
rules.rule_description: When no existing record is found during the UPDATE attempt, the system inserts a new transaction type record into the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the prepared type code and description values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Create New Record Instead
Insert new transaction type
into TRANSACTION_TYPE table

acceptance_criteria.Given: The UPDATE operation returned SQLCODE +100 indicating no existing record, and DCL-TR-TYPE and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION host variables are populated with the transaction type code and description
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the SQL INSERT INTO CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE statement providing values for TR_TYPE from DCL-TR-TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION from DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION
acceptance_criteria.Then: The database attempts to insert a new row into the TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the specified type code and description, and the resulting SQLCODE is evaluated for success or failure

rules.rule_name: Commit Successfully Inserted New Transaction Type Record
rules.rule_description: When a new transaction type record is successfully inserted into the database, the changes are permanently committed and the screen state reflects a successful creation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
New Record Created
Commit new record
to database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The SQL INSERT INTO CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE statement has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned from the INSERT equals zero, indicating the new record was successfully created
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system issues a SYNCPOINT to permanently commit the new record to the database, and the program state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, which triggers a success confirmation message to be displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Handle Insert Failure for New Transaction Type Record
rules.rule_description: When the INSERT operation fails for any reason, the system sets a failure state and constructs an error message containing the SQL error code and database error text to inform the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Failed
Unable to create
new transaction type record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The SQL INSERT INTO CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE statement has been executed
acceptance_criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned from the INSERT is any value other than zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED to TRUE, constructs an error message in WS-RETURN-MSG by concatenating the literal 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:' with WS-DISP-SQLCODE and SQLERRM from SQLCA, and the program state is subsequently set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED, which triggers a failure message to be displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Handle Record Lock Conflict During Transaction Type Update
rules.rule_description: When the UPDATE operation cannot proceed because another user currently holds a lock on the transaction type record, the system informs the user of the concurrent access conflict.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Locked by Another User
Transaction type is currently
being updated by someone else
Please retry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned equals -911, indicating the record is currently locked by another user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets INPUT-ERROR to TRUE, and when WS-RETURN-MSG is currently off (no prior message), sets COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE to TRUE; the program state is subsequently set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR, which triggers a lock conflict message to be displayed to the user indicating the record could not be updated due to concurrent access

rules.rule_name: Handle General Update Failure for Transaction Type Record
rules.rule_description: When the UPDATE operation fails due to any database error other than record-not-found or lock conflict, the system sets a failure state and constructs a detailed error message for the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Update Failed
Unable to modify
transaction type record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned is a negative value other than -911, indicating a general database error
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED to TRUE, constructs an error message in WS-RETURN-MSG by concatenating the literal 'Error updating: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:' with WS-DISP-SQLCODE and SQLERRM from SQLCA, and the program state is subsequently set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED, which triggers a failure message to be displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Set Final Program State After Write Processing Outcome
rules.rule_description: After all write processing outcomes are evaluated, the system sets the final program state that determines which message and screen layout will be presented to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Show Success Message
Transaction type updated
or created successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: The write processing (UPDATE and optionally INSERT) has completed and the outcome flags have been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the final outcome flags in order: COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE, TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED, DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE, or none of the above
acceptance_criteria.Then: If COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE is TRUE, the state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR and a lock error message is shown; if TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED is TRUE, the state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED and a failure message is shown; if DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE is TRUE, the state is set to TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS and the current database values are redisplayed; otherwise (all other cases including successful UPDATE or INSERT), the state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE and a success confirmation message is shown

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Type Insert
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Update Attempted\nNo Existing Record Found\nSQL Code +100])

    D{INSERT\nResult?}

    B --> C
    C --> D

    E --> F
    F --> I
    D -->|Any Failure| G
    G --> H
    H --> I

rules.rule_name: Trigger Insert When Update Finds No Existing Transaction Type Record
rules.rule_description: When an attempt to update a Transaction Type record finds that no matching record exists in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, the system automatically switches from an update operation to an insert operation to create the new record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Update Attempted
No Existing Record Found
SQL Code +100

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted a Transaction Type Code and Description for saving, and the system attempted to update an existing record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The update operation determines that no existing record matches the provided Transaction Type Code (record not found condition)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must automatically initiate an INSERT operation to create a new Transaction Type record using the same Transaction Type Code and Description values that were prepared for the update

rules.rule_name: Prepare Transaction Type Values for Insert
rules.rule_description: Before executing the INSERT, the system prepares the Transaction Type Code and Description values that were already validated and staged during the write processing phase, ensuring the correct data is used for the new record creation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Prepare INSERT Values
Transaction Type Code
and Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that a new Transaction Type record must be inserted because no existing record was found during the update attempt
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the data for the INSERT operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (2-character numeric, zero-padded) and the trimmed Transaction Type Description (up to 50 characters, alphanumeric only) that were previously validated and staged must be used as the values for the new record

rules.rule_name: Execute SQL INSERT for New Transaction Type Record
rules.rule_description: The system executes a SQL INSERT statement to create a new Transaction Type record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the prepared Transaction Type Code and Description values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Execute SQL INSERT
into TRANSACTION_TYPE Table
with Type Code and Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code and Description values have been prepared and validated, and no existing record was found for the given Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the INSERT operation against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.Then: A new record must be created in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the provided Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) as the column values

rules.rule_name: Commit New Transaction Type Record on Successful Insert
rules.rule_description: When the INSERT operation completes successfully, the system immediately commits the transaction to permanently persist the new Transaction Type record to the database, ensuring data durability.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Commit Transaction
Persist New Record
to Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has executed an INSERT operation for a new Transaction Type record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The INSERT operation completes successfully with no errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must immediately commit the transaction to permanently save the new Transaction Type record to the database before proceeding

rules.rule_name: Set Success Status After New Transaction Type Record Created
rules.rule_description: After a successful INSERT and commit, the system sets the program state to indicate that the Transaction Type record was successfully created, which drives the subsequent screen display to show a success confirmation message to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Success Status
New Transaction Type
Record Created Successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: The INSERT operation for the new Transaction Type record has completed successfully and the transaction has been committed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the final outcome of the write processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the program state to 'Changes Okayed And Done' (success), which will cause the screen to display a success confirmation message and transition to showing the newly created record details

rules.rule_name: Set Failure Status When Transaction Type Insert Fails
rules.rule_description: When the INSERT operation fails for any reason, the system sets a failure status flag to indicate that the record creation was unsuccessful, which drives the subsequent error handling and user notification.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Failure Status
Record Insert
Failed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has executed an INSERT operation for a new Transaction Type record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
acceptance_criteria.When: The INSERT operation fails for any reason (any SQL error condition other than success)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the internal status to 'Table Update Failed' to indicate the record creation was unsuccessful, and this failure status must be carried back to the write processing routine to set the final program state to 'Changes Okayed But Failed'

rules.rule_name: Build User-Facing Error Message When Transaction Type Insert Fails
rules.rule_description: When the INSERT operation fails, the system constructs a descriptive error message combining a fixed error description, the SQL error code, and the SQL error message text, to inform the user about the nature of the failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Build Error Message
Capture SQL Error Details
for User Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The INSERT operation for a new Transaction Type record has failed with any SQL error
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the INSERT failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must build an error message for display to the user that includes all of the following components concatenated together: the text 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:' followed by the actual SQL error code number, followed by ':', followed by the SQL error message text describing the specific error — and this complete message must be stored for display on the screen

rules.rule_name: Map Insert Failure to Final Program State for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: After the INSERT operation completes (success or failure), control returns to the write processing routine which evaluates the outcome flags and sets the final program state that determines what message and screen state the user will see.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Return to
Write Processing
for Final Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: The INSERT operation has completed and control has returned to the write processing routine
acceptance_criteria.When: The write processing routine evaluates the final outcome of the insert attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the insert failed (Table Update Failed status is set), the program state must be set to 'Changes Okayed But Failed' which will display a failure message to the user; if no failure status is set (insert succeeded), the program state must be set to 'Changes Okayed And Done' which will display a success confirmation to the user

key_functionalities.title: Transaction Type Delete
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Delete Transaction Type])
    A[Use confirmed Transaction Type Code\nas the key for deletion]
    B[(Execute DELETE on\nCARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE\nWhere TR_TYPE matches entered code)]
    D{What was the\ndelete outcome?}
    E[Deletion Successful\nCommit the change permanently]

    END_FAIL([End: Record NOT Deleted\nFailure message displayed in red])

    START --> A
    A --> B
    B --> D
    D -->|Success| E
    D -->|Child Records Exist\nReferential Integrity Violation| F
    D -->|Other Failure| G
    E --> END_SUCCESS
    F --> END_CHILD
    G --> END_FAIL

rules.rule_name: Use Confirmed Transaction Type Code as Delete Key
rules.rule_description: When a delete operation is initiated, the system must use the previously confirmed (original) Transaction Type Code — not any newly entered value — as the key to identify the exact record to be removed from the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use confirmed Transaction Type Code as the key for deletion

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been retrieved and displayed, the user has confirmed the delete intent by pressing PF4 a second time, and the original Transaction Type Code is stored as the confirmed delete key (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The delete processing begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must use the original confirmed Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE) — not any user-entered or modified value — as the sole key to identify the record targeted for deletion in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table

rules.rule_name: Execute Delete on Transaction Type Table
rules.rule_description: The system executes a SQL DELETE statement against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the confirmed Transaction Type Code as the exact match key to remove the record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Execute DELETE on CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE Where TR_TYPE matches entered code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The confirmed Transaction Type Code has been set as the delete key and the delete processing has been initiated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the DELETE operation against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table with a WHERE clause matching TR_TYPE equal to the confirmed Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The database attempts to remove the matching Transaction Type record; the outcome (success, referential integrity violation, or other failure) is captured for subsequent processing

rules.rule_name: Commit Transaction Type Deletion on Success
rules.rule_description: When the DELETE operation completes successfully, the system must permanently commit the deletion to the database and set the screen state to indicate the record has been deleted successfully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Deletion Successful Commit the change permanently

acceptance_criteria.Given: The DELETE statement has been executed against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the confirmed Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The DELETE operation returns a successful outcome (no errors, record was found and deleted)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system permanently commits the deletion to the database (SYNCPOINT), sets the program state to 'Delete Done', and the screen subsequently displays a delete success confirmation message to the user

rules.rule_name: Block Deletion When Child Records Exist
rules.rule_description: A Transaction Type record cannot be deleted if other records in the system reference it (child records exist). The system must detect this referential integrity violation and instruct the user to remove the dependent child records before attempting to delete the Transaction Type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Inform User: Please delete associated child records first before deleting this transaction type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The DELETE statement has been executed against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the confirmed Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The DELETE operation fails because other records in the database reference this Transaction Type Code (referential integrity constraint violation — child records exist)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must NOT delete the record, must NOT commit any change, must set the record-delete-failed indicator, and must display the message 'Please delete associated child records first:' along with the database error code to inform the user they must first remove all dependent child records before this Transaction Type can be deleted

rules.rule_name: Handle General Delete Failure
rules.rule_description: When the DELETE operation fails for any reason other than a referential integrity violation, the system must set the delete-failed state and display an error message containing the failure details to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Inform User: Delete operation failed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The DELETE statement has been executed against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the confirmed Transaction Type Code
acceptance_criteria.When: The DELETE operation fails for any reason other than child records existing (i.e., any database error that is not a referential integrity violation)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must NOT delete the record, must NOT commit any change, must set both the record-delete-failed indicator and the 'Delete Failed' program state, and must display an error message to the user containing the text 'Delete failed with message:' followed by the database error code and the database error message text, so the user is informed of the specific reason for the failure

rules.rule_name: Clear Screen Output Before Initialization
rules.rule_description: Before populating the Transaction Type Update screen with fresh data, all existing screen output fields must be cleared to prevent stale or residual data from appearing to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear all existing screen output fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Transaction Type Update screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization process begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: All existing output fields on the Transaction Type Update screen are cleared (set to LOW-VALUES), ensuring no residual data from a previous display remains visible

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The system must retrieve the current system date and time at the moment of screen preparation so that the screen header reflects the accurate date and time of the current user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve current system date and time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header preparation step is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current system date and time are retrieved from the system clock and stored in the working storage date-time area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

rules.rule_name: Display Screen Title Line 1 in Header
rules.rule_description: The first line of the application screen title must be placed in the screen header area to identify the application context to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Screen Title Line 1 on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized and the screen output area has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header fields are being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first screen title line (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the Title Line 1 output field (TITLE01O) of the screen map, displaying the application title to the user

rules.rule_name: Display Screen Title Line 2 in Header
rules.rule_description: The second line of the application screen title must be placed in the screen header area to provide the secondary title or subtitle context to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Screen Title Line 2 on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized and Title Line 1 has been placed on the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header fields are being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The second screen title line (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the Title Line 2 output field (TITLE02O) of the screen map, displaying the secondary application title to the user

rules.rule_name: Display Current Transaction ID in Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The identifier of the currently executing transaction must be displayed in the screen header so the user can identify which transaction they are working with.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Transaction ID on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header fields are being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID) is placed into the Transaction Name output field (TRNNAMEO) of the screen map, making the active transaction ID visible to the user in the screen header

rules.rule_name: Display Current Program Name in Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The name of the currently executing program must be displayed in the screen header to allow the user and support staff to identify which program is active.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Program Name on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header fields are being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current program name (LIT-THISPGM) is placed into the Program Name output field (PGMNAMEO) of the screen map, making the active program name visible to the user in the screen header

rules.rule_name: Format and Display Current Date as MM-DD-YY in Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The current system date must be formatted in MM-DD-YY format and displayed in the screen header. The year is represented as a 2-digit value extracted from positions 3 and 4 of the 4-digit year.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format current date as MM-DD-YY

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in the working storage date area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
acceptance_criteria.When: The date is being formatted for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) is moved to the MM position (WS-CURDATE-MM), the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) is moved to the DD position (WS-CURDATE-DD), and the last two digits of the year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR positions 3 through 4) are moved to the YY position (WS-CURDATE-YY), resulting in a combined MM-DD-YY formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) that is placed into the Current Date output field (CURDATEO) of the screen map

rules.rule_name: Format and Display Current Time as HH-MM-SS in Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The current system time must be formatted in HH-MM-SS format and displayed in the screen header, showing hours, minutes, and seconds to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format current time as HH-MM-SS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date and time have been retrieved and stored in the working storage date-time area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
acceptance_criteria.When: The time is being formatted for screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) is moved to the HH position (WS-CURTIME-HH), the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) is moved to the MM position (WS-CURTIME-MM), and the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) is moved to the SS position (WS-CURTIME-SS), resulting in a combined HH-MM-SS formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) that is placed into the Current Time output field (CURTIMEO) of the screen map
