rules.rule_name: Skip Screen Field Population on Fresh Program Entry
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type Update screen is accessed for the very first time in a session (fresh program entry), the screen field population step is bypassed entirely because the screen has already been initialized with empty values during screen initialization.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Skip Screen Variable Population
Screen already initialized

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step
acceptance_criteria.When: The program state indicates this is a fresh program entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER flag is set to TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen field population logic is skipped entirely — no Transaction Type Code, no Transaction Type Description, and no other field values are populated or overwritten; the screen retains the blank initialized state from the screen initialization step

rules.rule_name: Display Empty Search Screen for Initial or Invalid Search States
rules.rule_description: When the program is in an initial state (details not yet fetched) or the user has entered invalid search keys, the screen is populated with empty/blank values to present a clean search entry screen to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Show Initial Empty Values
Clear Transaction Type Code field
Display blank search screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step AND this is not a fresh program entry
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is either 'Details Not Yet Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) OR 'Invalid Search Keys Entered' (TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code display field (TRTYPCDO) on the screen is set to LOW-VALUES (blank/empty); the screen is presented as a clean blank search screen ready for the user to enter a Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: Display Original Database Values for View, Delete, and Backed-Out States
rules.rule_description: When the program is in a state where the original database record should be shown — such as viewing details, confirming or completing a delete, or when a user has backed out of changes — the screen is populated with the original values fetched from the database, and any pending new/changed values are cleared.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Show Original Fetched Values
Display original Transaction Type Code
Display original Transaction Description
Reset any new/pending changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step AND this is not a fresh program entry
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: 'Showing Record Details' (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS), 'Confirming Delete' (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE), 'Delete Failed' (TTUP-DELETE-FAILED), 'Delete Completed' (TTUP-DELETE-DONE), or 'Changes Backed Out' (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All pending new/changed detail fields (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS) are reset to their initial empty state; the Transaction Type Code display field (TRTYPCDO) is populated with the original Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE) fetched from the database; the Transaction Type Description display field (TRTYDSCO) is populated with the original Transaction Type Description (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) fetched from the database; the non-key flags (WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS) are reset to LOW-VALUES

rules.rule_name: Display User-Entered New or Updated Values for Change and Creation States
rules.rule_description: When the program is in a state where the user's newly entered or modified data should be shown — such as during active editing, validation failure, creating a new record, record not found, or after a successful save — the screen is populated with the user's most recently entered values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Show Updated or New Values
Display newly entered Transaction Type Code
Display newly entered Transaction Description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step AND this is not a fresh program entry
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: 'Changes Made' (TTUP-CHANGES-MADE), 'Changes Not Valid' (TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), 'Record Not Found' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND), 'Invalid Search Keys' (TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS), 'Creating New Record' (TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD), or 'Changes Confirmed and Saved' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code display field (TRTYPCDO) is populated with the newly entered Transaction Type Code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE); the Transaction Type Description display field (TRTYDSCO) is populated with the newly entered Transaction Type Description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC)

rules.rule_name: Default to Original Values Display for Unrecognized Program States
rules.rule_description: As a safety fallback, if the program encounters any program state not explicitly handled by the screen variable setup logic, it defaults to displaying the original database-fetched values and clearing any pending new changes, ensuring the screen always shows consistent and safe data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Show Original Fetched Values
Display original Transaction Type Code
Display original Transaction Description
Reset any new/pending changes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step AND this is not a fresh program entry
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state does not match any of the explicitly handled states (none of the defined TTUP state flags match — falls into the WHEN OTHER branch)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All pending new/changed detail fields (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS) are reset to their initial empty state; the Transaction Type Code display field (TRTYPCDO) is populated with the original Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE); the Transaction Type Description display field (TRTYDSCO) is populated with the original Transaction Type Description (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC); the non-key flags (WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS) are reset to LOW-VALUES

rules.rule_name: Display Search Prompt on Fresh Entry or Reset State
rules.rule_description: When the program is in an initial, reset, or invalid-search state, the informational message area should prompt the user to enter a Transaction Type code to begin a search.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Fresh Entry OR Details Not Yet Fetched OR Invalid Search Keys Entered → Display: Prompt user to enter Transaction Type code to search

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is any of: Fresh Entry (first time on screen), Details Not Yet Fetched (initial/reset state), Invalid Search Keys Entered (previous search had invalid input), or no informational message is currently set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search

rules.rule_name: Display Create New Record Prompt When Record Not Found
rules.rule_description: When a search for a Transaction Type code returns no matching record in the database, the informational message should notify the user that the record was not found and offer the option to create a new record using PF5.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Not Found in Database → Display: Record not found - Prompt user to create a new record with F5

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has submitted a valid Transaction Type code for search
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is 'Details Not Found' (the searched Transaction Type code does not exist in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to notify the user that the record was not found and prompt them to press PF5 to create a new record with that Transaction Type code

rules.rule_name: Display Change Prompt When Record is Displayed or Changes Were Cancelled
rules.rule_description: When a Transaction Type record is currently displayed on screen, or when a previously initiated change was cancelled and original values restored, the informational message should prompt the user to make changes to the displayed record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Showing Record Details OR Changes Were Backed Out → Display: Prompt user to make changes to the displayed record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and a Transaction Type record has been retrieved from the database
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is either 'Show Details' (record found and displayed) OR 'Changes Backed Out' (user cancelled a pending update and original values are restored, meaning old Transaction Type code is not blank or low-values) OR 'Changes Not OK' (validation failed on entered changes)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to make changes to the displayed record

rules.rule_name: Display Search Prompt When Changes Backed Out With No Prior Record
rules.rule_description: When changes are backed out but there is no previously loaded record (old Transaction Type code is blank or empty), the informational message should revert to prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search, rather than prompting for changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Showing Record Details OR Changes Were Backed Out → Display: Prompt user to enter Transaction Type code to search

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user had initiated changes that were subsequently cancelled
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is 'Changes Backed Out' AND the previously stored original Transaction Type code (old type code) is blank or contains only low-values (no prior record was loaded)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search (same as initial state), not to prompt for changes

rules.rule_name: Display Delete Confirmation Prompt When Awaiting Delete Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When the user has pressed PF4 to initiate a delete and the system is awaiting confirmation, the informational message should prompt the user to confirm the deletion by pressing PF4 again or cancel by pressing PF12.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Awaiting Delete Confirmation from User → Display: Prompt user to confirm deletion with F4 or cancel with F12

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and a Transaction Type record is currently displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is 'Confirm Delete' (user has pressed PF4 once and the system is waiting for confirmation)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to confirm the deletion by pressing PF4 or cancel the deletion by pressing PF12

rules.rule_name: Display Failure Notification When Delete Operation Fails
rules.rule_description: When a delete operation on a Transaction Type record fails (e.g., due to referential integrity constraints or other database errors), the informational message area should display a failure notification to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Delete Operation Failed → Display: Delete operation failed notification

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has confirmed a delete operation
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is 'Delete Failed' (the delete operation was attempted but did not complete successfully)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to a failure notification informing the user that the delete operation did not succeed

rules.rule_name: Display Delete Success Confirmation When Delete Completes Successfully
rules.rule_description: When a Transaction Type record has been successfully deleted from the database, the informational message should confirm to the user that the delete operation completed successfully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Delete Completed Successfully → Display: Delete completed successfully confirmation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has confirmed a delete operation
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is 'Delete Done' (the delete operation completed successfully and was committed to the database)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to confirm that the delete operation completed successfully

rules.rule_name: Display New Data Entry Prompt When Creating a New Record
rules.rule_description: When the user has chosen to create a new Transaction Type record (after a search returned no results and PF5 was pressed), the informational message should prompt the user to enter the details for the new record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Creating a New Record → Display: Prompt user to enter details for the new record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and a previous search returned no matching record
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is 'Create New Record' (user pressed PF5 after being informed the record was not found)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to enter the details (Transaction Type Description) for the new Transaction Type record

rules.rule_name: Display Confirmation Prompt When Changes Are Validated and Awaiting Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When the user has entered changes to a Transaction Type record and those changes have passed all validation rules, the informational message should prompt the user to confirm the changes by pressing PF5 or cancel them by pressing PF12.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Changes Validated - Awaiting User Confirmation → Display: Prompt user to confirm changes with F5 or cancel with F12

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active, a Transaction Type record is displayed, and the user has entered changes that have passed all validation checks
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (changes are validated and waiting for user confirmation before being saved to the database)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to confirm the changes by pressing PF5 to save, or cancel the changes by pressing PF12 to revert to original values

rules.rule_name: Display Update Success Confirmation When Changes Are Saved Successfully
rules.rule_description: When a Transaction Type record has been successfully updated or inserted into the database, the informational message should confirm to the user that the update completed successfully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Changes Saved Successfully → Display: Update completed successfully confirmation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is 'Changes Okayed And Done' (the update or insert operation completed successfully and was committed to the database)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to confirm that the update completed successfully

rules.rule_name: Display Failure Notification for Lock Error or Update Failure
rules.rule_description: When a save operation fails due to a record being locked by another user, a database update failure, or any other operational failure, the informational message area should display a failure notification to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Lock Error OR Update Failed OR Other Failure → Display: Operation failed - Failure notification to user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is any of: 'Changes Okayed Lock Error' (record was locked by another user at time of update), 'Changes Okayed But Failed' (the database update operation failed for a non-lock reason), or any other unhandled failure state
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message is set to a failure notification informing the user that the operation did not succeed

rules.rule_name: Center Informational Message Text Within Display Area
rules.rule_description: After the appropriate informational message is determined based on program state, the message text must be centered within the available display area before being placed on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Center the message text within the available display area on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: An informational message has been selected based on the current program state
acceptance_criteria.When: The message text is being prepared for display on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The length of the trimmed message text is calculated, the starting position is computed as: (total message field length minus trimmed message length) divided by 2 plus 1, and the trimmed message text is placed at that calculated starting position within the output string so that it appears centered in the display area

rules.rule_name: Place Centered Informational Message onto Screen Display Area
rules.rule_description: After the informational message has been centered, the centered message string is moved to the informational message output field on the screen so it is visible to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place centered informational message onto screen display area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The informational message text has been centered within the output string
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The centered message string is placed into the informational message display field (INFOMSGO) on the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Place Validation or Error Message onto Screen Error Area
rules.rule_description: In addition to the informational message, any validation error or system error message that was generated during input processing or database operations must be placed into the dedicated error message area on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place any validation or error message onto screen error area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display and there may be a validation or system error message present
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen output fields are being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current error or validation message (WS-RETURN-MSG, which may contain messages such as field validation errors, database error details, or operation failure descriptions) is placed into the error message display field (ERRMSGO) on the screen output area

key_functionalities.title: Screen Field Attribute Setup
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Screen Field Attribute Setup\nBusiness Process 28])

    PROTECT_ALL[Protect All Fields\nSet Transaction Type Code,\nTransaction Description, and\nInfo Message as Read-Only]

    D_STATE1{What is the\nCurrent Program State?}

    UNPROTECT_CODE[Make Transaction Type Code\nField Editable\nPosition Cursor to\nTransaction Type Code Field]

    UNPROTECT_DESC[Make Transaction Description\nField Editable\nKeep Info Message Read-Only\nPosition Cursor to\nDescription Field]

    KEEP_PROTECTED[Keep All Fields\nRead-Only\nNo Cursor Change]

    D_CURSOR{Where Should\nCursor Be Positioned?}

    CURSOR_CODE[Position Cursor to\nTransaction Type Code Field]

    CURSOR_DESC[Position Cursor to\nTransaction Description Field]

    D_COLOR_RED1{Is Transaction Type\nCode Invalid OR\nDelete Failed?}

    COLOR_RED[Highlight Transaction Type\nCode Field in Red\nto Indicate Error]

    D_COLOR_BLANK{Is Transaction Type\nCode Blank AND\nUser Has Returned to Screen?}

    SHOW_ASTERISK[Display Asterisk in\nTransaction Type Code Field\nHighlight Field in Red]

    D_EARLY_EXIT{Is Screen in\nSearch/Not Found/\nInvalid Keys State?}

    EARLY_EXIT[No Further\nAttribute Changes Needed]

    END_ATTRS([Screen Field Attributes\nSetup Complete])

    START --> PROTECT_ALL
    PROTECT_ALL --> D_STATE1

    D_STATE1 -->|Waiting for Search Input\nOR Invalid Search Keys\nOR Record Not Found\nOR Cancelled with No Prior Data| UNPROTECT_CODE

    D_STATE1 -->|Showing Record Details\nOR Changes Have Errors\nOR Creating New Record\nOR Changes Backed Out with Prior Data| UNPROTECT_DESC

    D_STATE1 -->|Changes Confirmed and Saved\nOR Delete In Progress| KEEP_PROTECTED

    UNPROTECT_CODE --> D_CURSOR
    UNPROTECT_DESC --> D_CURSOR
    KEEP_PROTECTED --> D_CURSOR

    D_CURSOR -->|Waiting for Search\nOR Not Found\nOR Invalid Keys\nOR Filter Blank or Invalid\nOR Changes Saved\nOR Backed Out with No Data| CURSOR_CODE

    D_CURSOR -->|Creating New Record\nOR No Changes Detected\nOR Description Invalid\nOR Changes Made\nOR Backed Out with Data\nOR Showing Details| CURSOR_DESC

    CURSOR_CODE --> D_COLOR_RED1
    CURSOR_DESC --> D_COLOR_RED1

    D_COLOR_RED1 -->|Yes| COLOR_RED
    D_COLOR_RED1 -->|No| D_COLOR_BLANK

    COLOR_RED --> D_COLOR_BLANK

    D_COLOR_BLANK -->|Yes| SHOW_ASTERISK
    D_COLOR_BLANK -->|No| D_EARLY_EXIT

    SHOW_ASTERISK --> D_EARLY_EXIT

    D_EARLY_EXIT -->|Yes - Waiting for Search\nOR Not Found\nOR Invalid Keys\nOR Blank or Invalid Filter| EARLY_EXIT
    D_EARLY_EXIT -->|No - Continue to\nAdditional Attribute Setup| END_ATTRS

    EARLY_EXIT --> END_ATTRS

rules.rule_name: Protect All Screen Fields Before State-Based Attribute Assignment
rules.rule_description: Before applying any state-specific field editability rules, all screen fields are set to read-only (protected) as a baseline. This ensures no field is accidentally left editable from a prior interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Protect All Fields
Set Transaction Type Code,
Transaction Description, and
Info Message as Read-Only

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is about to be displayed to the user and field attributes are being prepared
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attribute setup process begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field, the Transaction Description field, and the Informational Message field are all set to read-only (protected) as the default baseline before any state-specific rules are applied

rules.rule_name: Make Transaction Type Code Field Editable When Awaiting Search Input
rules.rule_description: When the program is in a state that requires the user to enter or re-enter a Transaction Type code for searching, the Transaction Type Code field is made editable so the user can type in it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Make Transaction Type Code
Field Editable
Position Cursor to
Transaction Type Code Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured after the baseline protection is applied
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Waiting for Search Input (Details Not Fetched), Invalid Search Keys entered, Record Not Found, or Changes were Backed Out and there is no prior record data (old Transaction Type Code is blank or LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field is set to editable (unprotected with cursor entry enabled), allowing the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search

rules.rule_name: Make Transaction Description Field Editable When Viewing or Editing a Record
rules.rule_description: When a record is being displayed for editing, a new record is being created, or changes have validation errors requiring correction, the Transaction Description field is made editable while the Informational Message field remains read-only.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Make Transaction Description
Field Editable
Keep Info Message Read-Only
Position Cursor to
Description Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured after the baseline protection is applied
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Showing Record Details, Changes Have Validation Errors (Changes Not OK), Creating a New Record, or Changes were Backed Out but prior record data exists (old Transaction Type Code has a value)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Description field is set to editable (unprotected with cursor entry enabled), and the Informational Message field remains read-only (protected)

rules.rule_name: Keep All Fields Read-Only When Changes Are Confirmed or Delete Is In Progress
rules.rule_description: When the user has already confirmed changes awaiting save, when a save has been completed, or when a delete operation is in progress, all fields remain read-only to prevent further input until the operation resolves.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Keep All Fields
Read-Only
No Cursor Change

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured after the baseline protection is applied
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Changes Confirmed and Not Yet Saved (Changes OK Not Confirmed), Changes Successfully Saved (Changes Okayed And Done), or Delete In Progress
acceptance_criteria.Then: All screen fields remain read-only (protected) with no cursor repositioning change applied at this stage

rules.rule_name: Position Cursor to Transaction Type Code Field for Search-Related States
rules.rule_description: The cursor is automatically moved to the Transaction Type Code field when the user needs to enter or correct a search key, when a search returned no results, when the filter input was invalid or blank, or when changes have been saved and the screen resets.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Position Cursor to
Transaction Type Code Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured and cursor positioning is being determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state or condition is one of: Waiting for Search Input (Details Not Fetched), Record Not Found, Invalid Search Keys, Transaction Type Code filter flag is blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK), Transaction Type Code filter flag is invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK), Changes Successfully Saved (Changes Okayed And Done), or Changes Backed Out with no prior record data (old Transaction Type Code is blank or LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Type Code field is set to -1, positioning the cursor to that field when the screen is displayed

rules.rule_name: Position Cursor to Transaction Description Field for Edit and Data Entry States
rules.rule_description: The cursor is automatically moved to the Transaction Description field when the user is expected to enter or correct description data, such as when creating a new record, editing an existing record, or when description validation has failed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Position Cursor to
Transaction Description Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured and cursor positioning is being determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state or condition is one of: Creating a New Record, No Changes Detected between old and new values, Transaction Description validation failed (Description Not OK flag or Description Blank flag), Changes Have Been Made, Changes Backed Out with prior record data, or Showing Record Details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Description field is set to -1, positioning the cursor to that field when the screen is displayed

rules.rule_name: Highlight Transaction Type Code Field in Red When Input Is Invalid or Delete Failed
rules.rule_description: To visually alert the user to an error condition, the Transaction Type Code field is displayed in red when the entered code failed validation or when a delete operation has failed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Highlight Transaction Type
Code Field in Red
to Indicate Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured after cursor positioning has been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code filter flag is set to invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is true) OR the current program state is Delete Failed (TTUP-DELETE-FAILED)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The color attribute of the Transaction Type Code field is set to red (DFHRED) to visually indicate an error to the user

rules.rule_name: Display Asterisk Placeholder and Red Highlight When Transaction Type Code Is Blank on Re-Entry
rules.rule_description: When the user has returned to the screen (re-entry mode) and the Transaction Type Code field was left blank, an asterisk '*' is displayed as a placeholder in the field and the field is highlighted in red to draw attention to the missing required input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Asterisk in
Transaction Type Code Field
Highlight Field in Red

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured and the Transaction Type Code color attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code filter flag is blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK is true) AND the program is in re-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code output field value is set to '*' (asterisk) as a visual placeholder, and the color attribute of the Transaction Type Code field is set to red (DFHRED)

rules.rule_name: Stop Further Attribute Processing When Screen Is in a Search or Not-Found State
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in a state where only the Transaction Type Code search field is relevant (no record data to display), no further field attribute changes are needed beyond what has already been set, and processing exits early.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Screen in
Search/Not Found/
Invalid Keys State?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen field attributes have been configured for field protection, cursor positioning, and color highlighting
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state or condition is one of: Waiting for Search Input (Details Not Fetched), Record Not Found (Details Not Found), Invalid Search Keys, Transaction Type Code filter flag is blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK), or Transaction Type Code filter flag is invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: No further screen attribute changes are applied and the screen attribute setup process completes immediately, skipping any additional attribute configuration steps

rules.rule_name: Cursor Positioned on Transaction Type Code Field When Search Input Is Needed or Invalid
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in a state where the user needs to provide or correct a Transaction Type Code for searching (no details fetched, record not found, invalid or blank search key, or search filter error), the cursor is automatically placed on the Transaction Type Code field to guide the user to enter a valid search value.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field - Prompt user to enter a transaction type to search

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is one of: (1) Details Not Fetched - no search has been performed yet, (2) Details Not Found - the searched Transaction Type Code does not exist in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, (3) Invalid Search Keys - the entered Transaction Type Code failed validation, (4) Transaction Type Filter is flagged as Not OK - the code is non-numeric or zero, OR (5) Transaction Type Filter is flagged as Blank - no code was entered
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL set to -1), prompting the user to enter or correct the Transaction Type Code to initiate or retry a search

rules.rule_name: Cursor Positioned on Transaction Type Code Field When Changes Are Backed Out With No Prior Record Data
rules.rule_description: When the user cancels an in-progress operation (changes backed out) but there is no previously fetched record data available (the old Transaction Type Code is empty or blank), the cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field to prompt the user to start a fresh search.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field - Prompt user to start a new search

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is Changes Backed Out (user cancelled a pending update or delete), AND the previously stored original Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE) contains either LOW-VALUES or SPACES, meaning no prior record data is available to restore
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL set to -1), prompting the user to enter a new Transaction Type Code to start a fresh search, since there is no prior record to return to

rules.rule_name: Cursor Positioned on Transaction Type Code Field After Successful Update
rules.rule_description: After a Transaction Type record has been successfully updated or inserted, the cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field to allow the user to perform a new search or look up another transaction type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field - Ready for next search after successful update

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is Changes Okayed And Done, meaning the update or insert to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table was completed successfully and committed
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL set to -1), signalling that the update is complete and the screen is ready for the user to search for another Transaction Type Code

rules.rule_name: Cursor Positioned on Description Field When Description Input or Correction Is Required
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in a state where the user needs to enter, review, or correct the Transaction Type Description — such as when creating a new record, when no changes were detected, when description validation failed, when changes are in progress, when details are being shown, or when changes were backed out with prior record data available — the cursor is placed on the Description field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Cursor on Description Field - Prompt user to enter or correct the description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is one of: (1) Create New Record - user is entering a new transaction type, (2) No Changes Detected - the entered description is identical to the existing one, (3) Description field flagged as Not OK - description contains invalid characters, (4) Description field flagged as Blank - description was not provided, (5) Changes Made - user has made modifications, (6) Changes Backed Out - user cancelled changes but prior record data exists (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE is not LOW-VALUES or SPACES), OR (7) Show Details - the fetched record is being displayed for potential editing
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCL set to -1), directing the user's attention to enter, review, or correct the description value

rules.rule_name: Cursor Defaults to Transaction Type Code Field for All Other Unspecified States
rules.rule_description: For any screen state not explicitly handled by the cursor positioning rules above, the cursor defaults to the Transaction Type Code field as a safe fallback, ensuring the user always has a clear starting point for interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field - Default positioning

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state does not match any of the explicitly defined cursor positioning conditions: not Details Not Fetched, not Details Not Found, not Invalid Search Keys, not Filter Not OK, not Filter Blank, not Changes Okayed And Done, not Changes Backed Out with no prior data, not Create New Record, not No Changes Detected, not Description Not OK, not Description Blank, not Changes Made, not Changes Backed Out with prior data, and not Show Details
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor must default to the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL set to -1) as the standard fallback positioning, ensuring the user always has a defined field to interact with regardless of the program state

rules.rule_name: Overall Cursor Placement Determination Based on Program State Hierarchy
rules.rule_description: The cursor placement on the Transaction Type Update screen is determined by evaluating a prioritized hierarchy of program state flags. The evaluation follows a specific order: search-needed states take highest priority, followed by backed-out-with-no-data, then successful update, then description-related states, and finally a default fallback. This ensures the cursor always guides the user to the most relevant field for their next action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Determine Cursor Position

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display after any user interaction, and the program has evaluated all current state flags including: TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK, FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK, TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT with TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE value, TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, NO-CHANGES-DETECTED, FLG-DESCRIPTION-NOT-OK, FLG-DESCRIPTION-BLANK, TTUP-CHANGES-MADE, and TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS
acceptance_criteria.When: The cursor positioning logic evaluates all state flags in priority order using an EVALUATE TRUE construct
acceptance_criteria.Then: Exactly one cursor position is selected: (1) Transaction Type Code field when search input is needed or invalid (highest priority), (2) Transaction Type Code field when changes are backed out with no prior record data, (3) Transaction Type Code field when update was just completed successfully, (4) Description field when description input or correction is needed, OR (5) Transaction Type Code field as the default fallback for all other states — ensuring the screen is always ready for the user's next appropriate action

rules.rule_name: Lock All Fields as Read-Only Before State-Based Unlocking
rules.rule_description: Before applying any state-specific field access rules, all input fields on the Transaction Type Update screen are locked as read-only by default. This ensures no field is accidentally left open for editing unless explicitly permitted by the current program state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Lock ALL Fields as Read-Only
Transaction Type Code
Transaction Description
Info Message Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display in any program state
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen field protection attributes are being set up
acceptance_criteria.Then: All three fields — Transaction Type Code, Transaction Description, and Info Message Area — must be set to protected (read-only) as the baseline before any state-specific rules are applied

rules.rule_name: Open Transaction Type Code Field for Input During Search States
rules.rule_description: When the program is in a state that requires the user to enter or re-enter a Transaction Type code for searching — including the initial search state, invalid search key state, record not found state, or when changes were backed out and no prior record data exists — the Transaction Type Code field must be made editable while all other fields remain read-only.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Initial Search /
Invalid Search Keys /
Details Not Found /
Changes Backed Out with No Prior Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Details Not Fetched (initial search), Invalid Search Keys, Details Not Found, or Changes Backed Out with no prior Transaction Type data (old type code is LOW-VALUES or SPACES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field must be set to unprotected (open for user input), allowing the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search; all other fields remain read-only

rules.rule_name: Open Transaction Description Field for Editing During Data Entry States
rules.rule_description: When the program is displaying an existing record for editing, showing validation errors, allowing creation of a new record, or restoring after a cancelled change where prior data exists, the Transaction Description field must be made editable. The Transaction Type Code field remains read-only (the key cannot be changed), and the Info Message Area remains read-only.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Showing Details /
Changes Not OK /
Create New Record /
Changes Backed Out with Prior Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Show Details, Changes Not OK, Create New Record, or Changes Backed Out with prior Transaction Type data present (old type code is not LOW-VALUES and not SPACES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Description field must be set to unprotected (open for user input) to allow the user to enter or modify the description; the Transaction Type Code field and Info Message Area must remain read-only (protected)

rules.rule_name: Keep All Fields Locked During Confirmation and Completion States
rules.rule_description: When the program is in a state where changes have been confirmed and are pending save, have already been saved successfully, or a delete operation is in progress, no user input is permitted. All fields remain locked as read-only to prevent any modification during these transitional states.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Changes Confirmed Pending Save /
Changes Saved Successfully /
Delete In Progress

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Changes OK Not Confirmed (pending save), Changes Okayed And Done (saved successfully), or Delete In Progress
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields — Transaction Type Code, Transaction Description, and Info Message Area — must remain protected (read-only); no field is opened for user input

rules.rule_name: Default Cursor to Transaction Type Code Field for Unrecognized States
rules.rule_description: For any program state not explicitly handled by the field protection rules, the system defaults to positioning the cursor on the Transaction Type Code field, ensuring the user can always initiate a search even in unexpected situations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any Other State

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state does not match any of the explicitly defined states (not: Details Not Fetched, Invalid Search Keys, Details Not Found, Changes Backed Out, Show Details, Changes Not OK, Create New Record, Changes OK Not Confirmed, Changes Okayed And Done, Delete In Progress)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field must be set to unprotected (open for user input) and the cursor must be positioned on the Transaction Type Code field as the default fallback

rules.rule_name: Highlight Transaction Type Code Field in Red on Validation Error or Delete Failure
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type code entered by the user fails validation (is not a valid numeric code) or when a delete operation has failed, the Transaction Type Code field must be visually highlighted in red to draw the user's attention to the problem area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Transaction Type Code
Validation Error OR
Delete Failed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes are being configured
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type code filter flag is set to 'Not OK' (validation failed — code is non-numeric, zero, or blank) OR the current state is Delete Failed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field color attribute must be set to RED to visually indicate an error condition to the user

rules.rule_name: Display Asterisk Placeholder and Red Highlight When Transaction Type Code Was Left Blank on Return
rules.rule_description: When the user returns to the screen (re-entry mode) and the Transaction Type Code field was left blank in the previous interaction, the system must display an asterisk '*' as a visual placeholder in the field and highlight it in red, prompting the user to provide the required search key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Transaction Type Code
Was Blank AND
User is Returning?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes are being configured and the program is in re-entry mode (user has previously interacted with the screen)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type code filter flag is set to 'Blank' (the user submitted the screen without entering a Transaction Type code) AND the program is in re-entry mode
acceptance_criteria.Then: An asterisk character '*' must be displayed in the Transaction Type Code output field AND the Transaction Type Code field color attribute must be set to RED to alert the user that the field is required

rules.rule_name: Stop Further Cursor Refinement When Screen is in Search-Required or Error State
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in a state where the user needs to enter a Transaction Type code (initial search, not found, invalid keys) or when the Transaction Type code field has a validation error (blank or invalid), no further cursor refinement is needed — the cursor is already correctly positioned on the Transaction Type Code field and processing of field attributes ends.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is State: Not Fetched /
Not Found / Invalid Keys /
Blank or Invalid Code?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes have been configured including any error highlighting
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Details Not Fetched, Details Not Found, Invalid Search Keys; OR the Transaction Type code filter flag is Blank or Not OK
acceptance_criteria.Then: Field attribute setup must terminate immediately without performing any additional cursor positioning logic; the cursor remains on the Transaction Type Code field as already set

rules.rule_name: Refine Cursor Position to Description Field Based on Editing Context
rules.rule_description: After passing the early-exit check, the system performs a final cursor refinement. When the context indicates the user needs to work with the description field — such as a description validation error, no changes were detected, changes were made or backed out, or details are being shown — the cursor is moved to the Transaction Description field. Otherwise, the cursor defaults to the Transaction Type Code field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Description Error /
No Changes Detected /
Changes Made / Backed Out /
Showing Details?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes have been fully configured and the early-exit condition was not triggered
acceptance_criteria.When: Any of the following conditions are true: the Description field has a validation error (blank or invalid characters), no changes were detected between old and new values, changes have been made (TTUP-CHANGES-MADE), changes were backed out (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT), or the screen is showing existing record details (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor must be positioned on the Transaction Description field (cursor length set to -1 for the description field); otherwise, the cursor must be positioned on the Transaction Type Code field (cursor length set to -1 for the type code field)

rules.rule_name: Position Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field for Search and Error Recovery
rules.rule_description: The cursor is directed to the Transaction Type Code field when the user needs to enter or correct a search key. This applies during initial search, after invalid search keys, when a record was not found, when changes were backed out with no prior data, after a successful save, or in any default/unrecognized state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Position Cursor on
Transaction Type Code Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes are being configured
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Details Not Fetched, Details Not Found, Invalid Search Keys, Transaction Type filter flag is Not OK or Blank, Changes Okayed And Done, Changes Backed Out with no prior data (old type code is LOW-VALUES or SPACES), or any unrecognized state
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Type Code field must be set to -1, directing the cursor to that field when the screen is displayed

rules.rule_name: Position Cursor on Transaction Description Field for Data Entry and Editing
rules.rule_description: The cursor is directed to the Transaction Description field when the user is expected to enter or modify the description. This applies when creating a new record, when description validation has failed, when no changes were detected, when changes have been made or backed out with prior data, or when existing record details are being shown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Position Cursor on
Transaction Description Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes are being configured
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state or condition is one of: Create New Record, Description validation error (blank or invalid), No Changes Detected, Changes Made (TTUP-CHANGES-MADE), Changes Backed Out with prior data present, or Show Details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Description field must be set to -1, directing the cursor to that field when the screen is displayed

rules.rule_name: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field When No Record Context Exists

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is one of: Details Not Fetched (initial/reset state), Invalid Search Keys (type code failed validation), Record Not Found (search returned no match), OR Changes Backed Out where no prior Transaction Type Code was loaded (old Transaction Type Code is empty or blank)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display and determines where to position the cursor
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field, prompting the user to enter or correct the Transaction Type Code

rules.rule_name: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field After Successful Save
rules.rule_description: After a Transaction Type record has been successfully updated or inserted, the cursor is repositioned on the Transaction Type Code field, allowing the user to initiate a new search or review the saved record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is current state: Details Not Fetched, Record Not Found, Invalid Search Keys, Type Code Invalid, Type Code Blank, Changes Saved Successfully, OR Backed Out with no prior record loaded?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is Changes Saved Successfully (update or insert was committed to the database)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display and determines where to position the cursor
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field

rules.rule_name: Place Cursor on Transaction Description Field When Record Is Loaded or Description Needs Attention
rules.rule_description: When a transaction type record is currently displayed, being created, or when the description field requires user attention due to validation errors or no changes being detected, the cursor is automatically positioned on the Transaction Description field to guide the user to the appropriate input area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is current state: Creating New Record, No Changes Detected, Description Invalid, Description Blank, Changes Made, Changes Backed Out with prior record loaded, OR Showing Details?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is one of: Creating New Record (user is entering a new transaction type), No Changes Detected (user submitted without modifying any data), Description Validation Failed — either Description is invalid (non-alphanumeric characters) or Description is blank/empty, Changes Made (edits are in progress), Changes Backed Out where a prior Transaction Type Code was loaded (old Transaction Type Code is not empty), OR Showing Details (an existing record is displayed for review or editing)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display and determines where to position the cursor
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor is placed on the Transaction Description field, directing the user to enter or correct the transaction description

rules.rule_name: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field as Default Fallback
rules.rule_description: When the current program state does not match any of the specifically handled cursor-positioning conditions, the system defaults to placing the cursor on the Transaction Type Code field as a safe fallback to ensure the user always has a field focused for input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field Default

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state does not match any of the following: Details Not Fetched, Invalid Search Keys, Record Not Found, Changes Backed Out with no prior record, Changes Saved Successfully, Creating New Record, No Changes Detected, Description Invalid, Description Blank, Changes Made, Changes Backed Out with prior record, or Showing Details
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display and determines where to position the cursor
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field as the default fallback position

rules.rule_name: Apply Red Highlighting to Transaction Type Code Field on Validation Failure or Delete Failure

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Highlight Transaction Type Code Field in RED

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update/Maintenance screen and has either: (a) entered a Transaction Type Code that failed validation — meaning it was non-numeric, equal to zero, or otherwise invalid — setting the 'Transaction Type Code Validation Failed' flag; OR (b) a delete operation was attempted on the currently displayed Transaction Type record and that delete operation failed, setting the 'Delete Failed' state
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display after processing the user's input or the failed delete operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field on the screen is highlighted in red color to visually indicate the error condition to the user; no asterisk placeholder is added by this rule alone; the red highlighting applies regardless of whether the failure was due to invalid input or a failed delete

rules.rule_name: Display Asterisk Placeholder in Red for Blank Transaction Type Code During Re-entry
rules.rule_description: When the user has left the Transaction Type Code field blank and the screen is in a re-entry state (the user has already interacted with the screen at least once and is returning to it), the system must display an asterisk ('*') as a placeholder in the Transaction Type Code field and highlight that field in red, prompting the user that a value is required.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Asterisk Placeholder in Transaction Type Code Field Highlighted in RED

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update/Maintenance screen in a re-entry state (the program has been previously entered and is now being re-entered, meaning this is not the very first interaction with the screen) AND the Transaction Type Code field was left blank by the user — meaning the field contained no value, spaces, or low-values — setting the 'Transaction Type Code Blank' flag
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field is populated with an asterisk character ('*') as a visual placeholder to indicate that input is required, AND the Transaction Type Code field is highlighted in red color; both the asterisk placeholder and the red color are applied together as a combined visual indicator that the field is mandatory and was left empty

rules.rule_name: No Error Color Applied to Transaction Type Code Field When No Error Conditions Are Present
rules.rule_description: When neither a Transaction Type Code validation failure, nor a delete operation failure, nor a blank field during re-entry condition is present, the Transaction Type Code field is displayed without any error color highlighting, retaining its default appearance.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No Error Color Applied to Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update/Maintenance screen AND the Transaction Type Code validation has not failed (the 'Transaction Type Code Validation Failed' flag is not set) AND no delete operation failure has occurred (the 'Delete Failed' state is not active) AND it is NOT the case that both the Transaction Type Code field is blank AND the screen is in a re-entry state
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: No red color highlighting is applied to the Transaction Type Code field; no asterisk placeholder is inserted into the Transaction Type Code field; the field is displayed in its default color and appearance without any error indicators

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Highlight Transaction Type Code Field in RED

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display after user interaction, and the Transaction Type Code field has been evaluated for validity and/or a delete operation has been attempted
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code is flagged as invalid (failed numeric, zero, or format validation) OR the delete operation on the Transaction Type record has failed

rules.rule_name: Display Asterisk Placeholder and Red Highlight for Blank Transaction Type Code on Re-entry

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Asterisk in Transaction Type Code Field and Highlight in RED

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display and the program is in re-entry mode (the user has previously submitted the screen at least once)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field was left blank or contained only spaces by the user during re-entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: An asterisk character ('*') is placed into the Transaction Type Code display field as a placeholder, AND the Transaction Type Code field color attribute is set to RED, visually indicating to the user that the Transaction Type Code is a required field that must be supplied

rules.rule_name: Retain Default Color for Transaction Type Code Field When No Error Condition Exists
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Type Code is valid and no delete failure has occurred, and the field was not left blank during re-entry, the Transaction Type Code field retains its default display color with no special highlighting, indicating normal screen state to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No Color Change Fields Display in Default Color

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display after user interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code is not flagged as invalid AND no delete operation has failed AND the Transaction Type Code field was not left blank during re-entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: No color attribute change is applied to the Transaction Type Code field, and the field is displayed in its default color, indicating no error condition exists for that field

key_functionalities.title: PF Key Attribute Setup
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([30: PF Key Attribute Setup\nDetermine which function keys\nto show based on current state])

    D_FKEYS{Is current state\nDelete Confirmation?}
    FKEYS_HIDE[Hide all PF Key options\nfrom display]
    FKEYS_SHOW[Show all PF Key options\non display]

    D_F4{Is current state\nShowing Details\nOR Delete Confirmation?}
    F4_ENABLE[Enable F4 - Delete\nOption on Screen]
    F4_SKIP[F4 - Delete\nNot Available]

    D_F5{Is current state\nChanges Confirmed but Pending Save\nOR Record Not Found?}
    F5_ENABLE[Enable F5 - Save\nOption on Screen]
    F5_SKIP[F5 - Save\nNot Available]

    D_F12{Is current state\nChanges Confirmed but Pending Save\nOR Showing Details\nOR Record Not Found\nOR Delete Confirmation\nOR Creating New Record?}

    END_STATE([Screen PF Key Display\nAttributes Applied\nReady to Send to User])

    START --> D_FKEYS

    D_F4 -->|No| F4_SKIP
