    F4_SKIP --> D_F5

    D_F5 -->|Yes| F5_ENABLE
    D_F5 -->|No| F5_SKIP
    F5_ENABLE --> D_F12
    F5_SKIP --> D_F12

    D_F12 -->|Yes| F12_ENABLE
    D_F12 -->|No| F12_SKIP
    F12_ENABLE --> END_STATE
    F12_SKIP --> END_STATE

rules.rule_name: Hide All PF Key Options During Delete Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in Delete Confirmation state, all available function key option labels are hidden from the user to prevent unintended actions during the critical delete confirmation step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Hide all PF Key options from display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and the current program state is Delete Confirmation (user has pressed F4 once and is being asked to confirm the deletion of the displayed Transaction Type record)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared to send to the user and PF Key display attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.Then: All PF Key option labels (FKEYSA) on the screen are set to hidden/dark (non-displayed) so that no function key options are visible to the user on the screen

rules.rule_name: Show All PF Key Options in Non-Delete-Confirmation States
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in any state other than Delete Confirmation, all available function key option labels are shown to the user so they can see which actions are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Show all PF Key options on display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and the current program state is NOT Delete Confirmation (i.e., the state is any of: initial search, showing details, record not found, creating new record, changes pending confirmation, changes completed, delete done, delete failed, or invalid search keys)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is being prepared to send to the user and PF Key display attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.Then: All PF Key option labels (FKEYSA) on the screen are set to visible/bright (displayed) so that the function key options area is visible to the user on the screen

rules.rule_name: Enable F4 Delete Option When Record Is Displayed or Delete Is Pending Confirmation
rules.rule_description: The F4 Delete function key option is made visible and active on the screen only when a Transaction Type record is currently being displayed to the user, or when the user is being asked to confirm a pending delete operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enable F4 - Delete Option on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is either Showing Details (a Transaction Type record has been retrieved from the database and is displayed on screen) OR Delete Confirmation (user has already pressed F4 once and is being prompted to confirm the deletion)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F4 Delete function key option label (FKEY04A) on the screen is set to visible/bright (enabled), indicating to the user that the Delete action is available

rules.rule_name: F4 Delete Option Not Available in All Other States
rules.rule_description: The F4 Delete function key option remains hidden and inactive when the screen is not in a state where a record is displayed or a delete is pending confirmation, preventing accidental deletion attempts.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: F4 - Delete Not Available

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is NOT Showing Details AND NOT Delete Confirmation (i.e., the state is any of: initial search, record not found, creating new record, changes pending confirmation, changes completed, delete done, delete failed, or invalid search keys)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F4 Delete function key option label (FKEY04A) on the screen is NOT set to visible/bright, meaning the Delete option is not highlighted or enabled for the user

rules.rule_name: Enable F5 Save Option When Changes Are Pending Confirmation or Record Was Not Found
rules.rule_description: The F5 Save function key option is made visible and active on the screen only when validated changes are awaiting the user's final confirmation to be saved, or when a search returned no record and the user has the option to create a new one.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enable F5 - Save Option on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is either Changes Confirmed but Pending Save (user has entered and validated changes to the Transaction Type Description and the system is awaiting final confirmation to write to the database) OR Record Not Found (a search was performed but no matching Transaction Type record exists in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F5 Save function key option label (FKEY05A) on the screen is set to visible/bright (enabled), indicating to the user that the Save/Confirm action is available

rules.rule_name: F5 Save Option Not Available in All Other States
rules.rule_description: The F5 Save function key option remains hidden and inactive when there are no pending changes awaiting confirmation and no opportunity to create a new record, preventing premature or unintended save actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: F5 - Save Not Available

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is NOT Changes Confirmed but Pending Save AND NOT Record Not Found (i.e., the state is any of: initial search, showing details, delete confirmation, creating new record, changes completed, delete done, delete failed, or invalid search keys)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F5 Save function key option label (FKEY05A) on the screen is NOT set to visible/bright, meaning the Save option is not highlighted or enabled for the user

rules.rule_name: Enable F12 Cancel Option Across Multiple Active States
rules.rule_description: The F12 Cancel function key option is made visible and active on the screen whenever the user is in a state where cancelling the current operation and returning to a prior state is a meaningful and valid action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Enable F12 - Cancel Option on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is any one of the following: (1) Changes Confirmed but Pending Save - validated changes are awaiting final confirmation, (2) Showing Details - a Transaction Type record is currently displayed, (3) Record Not Found - search returned no matching record, (4) Delete Confirmation - user is being asked to confirm deletion of the displayed record, OR (5) Creating New Record - user is entering data for a new Transaction Type
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F12 Cancel function key option label (FKEY12A) on the screen is set to visible/bright (enabled), indicating to the user that the Cancel action is available to abandon the current operation

rules.rule_name: F12 Cancel Option Not Available in All Other States
rules.rule_description: The F12 Cancel function key option remains hidden and inactive when there is no active operation in progress that can be meaningfully cancelled.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: F12 - Cancel Not Available

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
acceptance_criteria.When: The current program state is NOT Changes Confirmed but Pending Save AND NOT Showing Details AND NOT Record Not Found AND NOT Delete Confirmation AND NOT Creating New Record (i.e., the state is any of: initial search/not fetched, changes completed successfully, delete done, delete failed, invalid search keys, or changes backed out)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The F12 Cancel function key option label (FKEY12A) on the screen is NOT set to visible/bright, meaning the Cancel option is not highlighted or enabled for the user

key_functionalities.title: Send Screen to User
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Send Screen to User])
    B[Set Target Screen Map\nand Map Set for Transmission]
    C[Transmit Prepared Screen\nto User Terminal]
    D[Erase Previous Screen Content\nso User Sees Fresh Display]
    E[Free the Keyboard\nso User Can Enter Input]
    F([End: Screen Displayed\nUser Can Interact])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Set Target Screen Map and Map Set for Transmission
rules.rule_description: Before transmitting the screen to the user, the system identifies and assigns the correct screen map and map set that should be displayed. This ensures the right Transaction Type Update screen layout is used for the current interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Target Screen Map
and Map Set for Transmission

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed preparing all screen content, field values, informational messages, field protection attributes, and PF key attributes for the Transaction Type Update screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is ready to transmit the screen to the user terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must assign the Transaction Type Update screen map name (LIT-THISMAP) to the target map field (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and assign the Transaction Type Update map set name (LIT-THISMAPSET) to the target map set field (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET), so that the correct screen layout is used for display

rules.rule_name: Transmit Prepared Screen to User Terminal
rules.rule_description: The system sends the fully prepared Transaction Type Update screen — including all field values, informational messages, error messages, field attributes, and cursor position — to the user's terminal for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Transmit Prepared Screen
to User Terminal

acceptance_criteria.Given: The target screen map (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and map set (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET) have been assigned, and the output screen area (CTRTUPAO) has been fully populated with field values, informational messages, error messages, field colors, field protection attributes, and cursor positioning
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the screen transmission command
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must send the prepared screen output area (CTRTUPAO) using the assigned map name and map set to the user's terminal, with the cursor positioned at the field designated during screen attribute setup

rules.rule_name: Erase Previous Screen Content so User Sees Fresh Display
rules.rule_description: When displaying the Transaction Type Update screen, the system must clear any previously displayed content on the user's terminal so that the user always sees a clean, current screen without residual data from prior interactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Erase Previous Screen Content
so User Sees Fresh Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is transmitting the Transaction Type Update screen to the user terminal
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is sent to the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must erase all previously displayed content on the terminal screen before rendering the new screen, ensuring the user sees only the current screen content without any leftover data from the previous screen display

rules.rule_name: Free the Keyboard so User Can Enter Input
rules.rule_description: After the Transaction Type Update screen is displayed, the system must release the keyboard lock so the user is able to type input, enter data into fields, and press PF keys to interact with the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Free the Keyboard
so User Can Enter Input

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen has been successfully transmitted and displayed on the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen transmission is complete
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must release (free) the keyboard so that the user can immediately begin entering data into the available input fields or press PF keys (PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12, or ENTER) to perform the next action without any keyboard inhibit delay

key_functionalities.title: Alphanumeric Field Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Alphanumeric Field Validation])
    S1[Mark Field as Invalid\nPrepare for validation checks]
    D1{Is the field\nempty, blank,\nor not supplied?}
    E1[Set Error:\nField must be supplied]
    S2[Check each character\nin the field up to\nspecified length]
    S3[Replace all valid alphanumeric\ncharacters A-Z, a-z, 0-9\nwith spaces temporarily]
    D2{Are there any\nnon-space characters\nremaining after replacement?}
    E2[Set Error:\nField can have\nnumbers or alphabets only]
    S4[Mark Field as VALID\nValidation Passed]
    END_FAIL([End: Validation Failed\nError Message Set])
    END_OK([End: Validation Passed\nField Accepted])

    START --> S1
    S1 --> D1
    D1 -->|Yes - Field is Empty| E1
    E1 --> END_FAIL
    D1 -->|No - Field has Content| S2
    S2 --> S3
    S3 --> D2
    D2 -->|Yes - Invalid Characters Found| E2
    E2 --> END_FAIL
    D2 -->|No - All Characters Valid| S4
    S4 --> END_OK

rules.rule_name: Initialize Alphanumeric Field Validation State
rules.rule_description: Before any validation checks are performed on an alphanumeric field, the field's validation status is pre-set to 'Not OK' (invalid). This ensures that the field must explicitly pass all checks to be considered valid, preventing any accidental acceptance of unvalidated data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Field as Invalid
Prepare for validation checks

acceptance_criteria.Given: A request has been made to validate an alphanumeric field (e.g., Transaction Description) with a specified maximum length
acceptance_criteria.When: The alphanumeric field validation routine is invoked
acceptance_criteria.Then: The field validation status flag is immediately set to 'Not OK' (invalid) as the default state before any content checks are performed

rules.rule_name: Alphanumeric Field Must Not Be Blank or Empty
rules.rule_description: An alphanumeric field under validation must contain at least one non-blank, non-empty character within its specified length. If the field is entirely empty, contains only spaces, or has no meaningful content after trimming, it is rejected with a mandatory supply error. This rule applies to the Transaction Description field (up to 50 characters).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is the field
empty, blank,
or not supplied?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field is being validated with a maximum length of 50 characters
acceptance_criteria.When: The field value within the specified length is entirely LOW-VALUES (null), entirely spaces, or has a trimmed length of zero (no meaningful content)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The validation status is set to 'Input Error' and 'Field Blank', and the error message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' is generated; validation ends immediately with a failure result

rules.rule_name: Scan Alphanumeric Field for Valid Characters
rules.rule_description: To determine whether a field contains only permitted characters, all valid alphanumeric characters (uppercase A-Z, lowercase a-z, and digits 0-9) within the field's specified length are temporarily replaced with spaces. Any characters that remain non-space after this replacement are considered invalid. This technique isolates invalid characters for detection.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Check each character
in the field up to
specified length
Replace all valid alphanumeric
characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9
with spaces temporarily

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field has been confirmed as non-blank and contains at least one character within the specified 50-character length
acceptance_criteria.When: The character scan is performed on the field content up to the specified length
acceptance_criteria.Then: All characters that are valid alphanumeric characters (A through Z uppercase, a through z lowercase, 0 through 9 digits) within the specified length are replaced with spaces, leaving only any invalid/special characters visible as non-space characters for subsequent detection

rules.rule_name: Reject Alphanumeric Field Containing Non-Alphanumeric Characters
rules.rule_description: After replacing all valid alphanumeric characters with spaces, if any non-space characters remain in the field, it means the original field contained special characters, punctuation, or other non-alphanumeric content. Such a field is rejected with a character-type error. The Transaction Description field must contain only letters and numbers.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Are there any
non-space characters
remaining after replacement?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field has been scanned and all valid alphanumeric characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9) have been temporarily replaced with spaces within the 50-character length
acceptance_criteria.When: The trimmed length of the modified field content is greater than zero, meaning non-space (invalid) characters remain after the replacement
acceptance_criteria.Then: The validation status is set to 'Input Error' and 'Field Not OK', and the error message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' is generated; validation ends immediately with a failure result

rules.rule_name: Mark Alphanumeric Field as Successfully Validated
rules.rule_description: When an alphanumeric field passes all validation checks — it is non-blank, non-empty, and contains only letters and digits — the field is marked as valid. This successful validation status signals that the field's content is acceptable for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Field as VALID
Validation Passed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field has been checked and confirmed as non-blank and containing only alphanumeric characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9) within the 50-character length
acceptance_criteria.When: All validation checks pass without any errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The field validation status flag is set to 'Valid' (FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID), indicating the field content is accepted and no error messages are generated

rules.rule_name: Apply Alphanumeric Validation to Transaction Description and Determine Change Confirmation Eligibility
rules.rule_description: The Transaction Description field entered by the user is submitted to the alphanumeric validation routine. The field name 'Transaction Desc', the user-entered description value, and the maximum allowed length of 50 characters are passed to the validation routine. Based on the validation outcome, the program either retains the error state or advances the transaction to the 'Changes OK - Awaiting Confirmation' state, enabling the user to confirm and save the changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Field as VALID
Validation Passed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the Transaction Description field on the Transaction Type Update screen, and the system has detected that a change has occurred compared to the original value
acceptance_criteria.When: The alphanumeric validation routine is invoked for the Transaction Description field with a maximum length of 50 characters
acceptance_criteria.Then: If validation fails (field is blank or contains non-alphanumeric characters), the error state is retained and the description-level error flags are set from the validation result flags; if validation passes, the transaction state is advanced to 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed', enabling the user to confirm and save the update

key_functionalities.title: Numeric Field Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Numeric Field Validation])

    D_BLANK{Is the field\nempty or blank?}

    ERR_BLANK[Mark Input as Error\nField is Blank\nMessage: Field name\n'must be supplied']

    D_NUMERIC{Is the field\npurely numeric?}

    ERR_NUMERIC[Mark Input as Error\nField is Not Numeric\nMessage: Field name\n'must be numeric']

    D_ZERO{Is the numeric\nvalue zero?}

    ERR_ZERO[Mark Input as Error\nField Value is Zero\nMessage: Field name\n'must not be zero']

    VALID[Mark Field as Valid\nValidation Passed]

    END_EXIT([End: Return to Calling Process])

    START --> D_BLANK
    D_BLANK -->|Yes - Empty or Blank| ERR_BLANK
    ERR_BLANK --> END_EXIT
    D_BLANK -->|No - Field Has Value| D_NUMERIC
    D_NUMERIC -->|No - Contains Non-Numeric Characters| ERR_NUMERIC
    ERR_NUMERIC --> END_EXIT
    D_NUMERIC -->|Yes - All Numeric| D_ZERO
    D_ZERO -->|Yes - Value is Zero| ERR_ZERO
    ERR_ZERO --> END_EXIT
    D_ZERO -->|No - Non-Zero Value| VALID
    VALID --> END_EXIT

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Supplied
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code field has been entered by the user and is not left blank or empty before any further validation is performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the field empty or blank?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the Numeric Field Validation routine is invoked for the 'Tran Type code' field with a maximum length of 2 characters
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field is empty, contains only spaces, or has no trimmed content (length of trimmed value equals zero)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The input is marked as an error, the field status is set to 'Blank', and the error message 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' is generated and stored as the return message for display to the user; validation exits immediately without checking further rules

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Purely Numeric
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code entered by the user contains only numeric digits, rejecting any value that includes alphabetic characters or special characters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the field purely numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank value in the Transaction Type Code field and the Numeric Field Validation routine has confirmed the field is not empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered value fails the numeric test, meaning it contains one or more non-numeric characters (letters, symbols, or mixed content) within the 2-character length
acceptance_criteria.Then: The input is marked as an error, the field status is set to 'Not OK', and the error message 'Tran Type code must be numeric.' is generated and stored as the return message for display to the user; validation exits immediately without checking further rules

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Must Not Be Zero
rules.rule_description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code, after passing the numeric check, has a meaningful non-zero value, preventing the use of '00' or '0' as a valid transaction type identifier.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the numeric value zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank, purely numeric value in the Transaction Type Code field and the Numeric Field Validation routine has confirmed the field is not empty and is numeric
acceptance_criteria.When: The numeric value of the entered Transaction Type Code evaluates to zero (e.g., '00' or '0')
acceptance_criteria.Then: The input is marked as an error, the field status is set to 'Not OK', and the error message 'Tran Type code must not be zero.' is generated and stored as the return message for display to the user; validation exits immediately without proceeding to mark the field as valid

rules.rule_name: Transaction Type Code Passes All Numeric Validations
rules.rule_description: Confirms that the Transaction Type Code has successfully passed all numeric validation checks — it is supplied, purely numeric, and non-zero — and is therefore accepted as a valid input for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Field as Valid - Validation Passed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Transaction Type Code field and the Numeric Field Validation routine has been invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code is non-blank, contains only numeric digits, and its numeric value is greater than zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The field is marked as valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID is set to TRUE), no error message is generated, and the validation routine exits successfully allowing the calling process to proceed with the zero-padded Transaction Type Code

key_functionalities.title: Session State Persistence
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Session State Persistence Begins])
    B[Copy any pending error or\nreturn message into the\nshared communication area]
    C[Save general session data\ninto combined workspace\ncommarea]
    D[Append program-specific state data\ninto combined workspace:\n- Current screen state flags\n- Transaction type code\n- Transaction type description]
    E[Return control to CICS\nwith full combined commarea\nready for next user interaction]
    F([Awaiting Next User Interaction])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Persist Pending Error or Return Message into Shared Session Area
rules.rule_description: Before returning control to CICS, any pending error or informational return message generated during the current interaction must be copied into the shared communication area so it is available for display on the next screen interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Copy any pending error or return message into the shared communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current user interaction has completed processing and the program is preparing to return control to CICS, and a return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) may or may not have been set during processing (e.g., validation error, record not found, update success, invalid key message)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches the session state persistence step (COMMON-RETURN) prior to returning control to CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) must be copied into the error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG) of the shared communication area so that the message is preserved and available for display during the next user interaction

rules.rule_name: Save General Session Data into Combined Workspace Communication Area
rules.rule_description: The general CardDemo session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which includes shared session context such as calling program identity, transaction IDs, user type, and navigation state, must be saved into the combined workspace communication area before returning to CICS.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save general session data into combined workspace commarea

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed processing the current user interaction and is preparing to return control to CICS, and the general session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains current values for shared session context including: calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), destination transaction (CDEMO-TO-TRANID), user type (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN), program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER / CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), last mapset (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), last map (CDEMO-LAST-MAP), account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID), card number (CDEMO-CARD-NUM), and account status (CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches the session state persistence step (COMMON-RETURN) and begins building the combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire general session data area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied into the beginning of the combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA), occupying the first portion of the combined area, so that all shared session context is preserved for the next interaction

rules.rule_name: Append Program-Specific Transaction Type State Data into Combined Communication Area
rules.rule_description: The program-specific state data for the Transaction Type Update screen (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), which includes the current screen state flags, the transaction type code being worked on, and the transaction type description (both old/original and new/updated values), must be appended into the combined workspace communication area immediately after the general session data, so the program can resume from the correct state on the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Append program-specific state data into combined workspace:
- Current screen state flags
- Transaction type code
- Transaction type description

acceptance_criteria.Given: The general session data has already been saved into the first portion of the combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA), and the program-specific state area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) contains the current values for: screen state flags (e.g., TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, TTUP-DELETE-DONE, TTUP-DELETE-FAILED, TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), the original transaction type code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE), the original transaction type description (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC), the new/updated transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE), and the new/updated transaction type description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches the session state persistence step (COMMON-RETURN) and appends program-specific data into the combined workspace communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire program-specific state data area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be copied into the combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA) starting immediately after the end of the general session data area (at offset: LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1), for a length equal to the size of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, so that all screen state flags and transaction type data values are preserved contiguously in the combined area for the next user interaction

rules.rule_name: Return Control to CICS with Full Combined Communication Area for Next User Interaction
rules.rule_description: After all session state data has been assembled into the combined workspace communication area, control must be returned to CICS specifying the same transaction ID so the screen remains active and ready for the next user interaction, passing the full combined communication area so all state is available when the user next interacts with the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return control to CICS with full combined commarea ready for next user interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully populated with both the general session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific state data (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), and the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) identifies this Transaction Type Update screen transaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The program executes the CICS RETURN command at the end of COMMON-RETURN
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control must be returned to CICS specifying: the same transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) so the Transaction Type Update screen remains active and will be re-invoked on the next user action, the full combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) as the COMMAREA to be passed to the next invocation, and the exact byte length of WS-COMMAREA as the LENGTH parameter, ensuring the complete state (general session context plus program-specific screen state, transaction type code, and transaction type description) is available when the user next interacts with the screen

key_functionalities.title: Concurrent Update Conflict Handling
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses F5\nTo Save Confirmed Changes])
    B[Attempt to Update\nTransaction Type Record\nin Database]
    C{Is Record\nLocked by\nAnother User?}
    D[Record Lock\nConflict Detected\nSQL Code -911]
    E[Set State:\nChanges Could Not Be\nApplied Due to Lock]
    F[Prepare Failure\nNotification Message:\nRecord could not be\nupdated - concurrent access conflict]
    G[Display Screen\nWith Failure Message\nAll Fields Protected\nNo Save Option Available]
    H[User Reviews\nFailure Message]
    I{User Chooses\nTo Retry?}
    J[User Re-enters\nTransaction Type Code\nTo Search Again]
    K[User Presses F12\nTo Cancel and\nReturn to Search]
    L([Return to\nSearch Screen\nTo Retry Later])
    M([Proceed with\nNew Search\nand Retry Save])
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|No - Save Proceeds Normally| N([Save Completes\nSuccessfully])
    C -->|Yes - Lock Conflict| D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I -->|Yes - Retry| J
    J --> M
    I -->|No - Cancel| K
    K --> L

rules.rule_name: Detect Record Lock Conflict During Transaction Type Update
rules.rule_description: When a user attempts to save confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record, the system must detect if the record is currently locked by another user (concurrent access conflict) and handle it appropriately without saving.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Record Locked by Another User? / Record Lock Conflict Detected SQL Code -911

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record and pressed F5 to save, and the system attempts to update the TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the new TR_DESCRIPTION for the matching TR_TYPE code
acceptance_criteria.When: The database returns a lock conflict error (record is currently held by another user's active transaction) during the UPDATE attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the save attempt as failed due to a lock conflict, (2) set the program state to 'Changes Could Not Be Applied Due to Lock' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR), and (3) NOT commit the transaction or apply any changes to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table

rules.rule_name: Prepare Lock Conflict Failure Notification Message
rules.rule_description: When a record lock conflict is detected during a Transaction Type update attempt, the system must prepare and display an appropriate failure notification message to inform the user that the record could not be updated due to concurrent access.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prepare Failure Notification Message: Record could not be updated - concurrent access conflict

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has detected a record lock conflict (SQLCODE -911) during an attempt to update the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, and the program state has been set to 'Changes Could Not Be Applied Due to Lock' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the informational message for the screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the information message to a failure notification (INFORM-FAILURE) indicating that the update could not be completed, and this failure message must be displayed in the information message area (INFOMSGO) of the screen

rules.rule_name: Protect All Screen Fields After Lock Conflict - No Save Option Available
rules.rule_description: After a lock conflict failure, the screen must be displayed with all input fields protected (read-only) and no save option (F5) available, preventing the user from attempting another save directly from the failure screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Screen With Failure Message / All Fields Protected / No Save Option Available

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program state is 'Changes Could Not Be Applied Due to Lock' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR) after a failed update attempt due to a concurrent access conflict
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the screen attributes for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) protect ALL input fields (Transaction Type Code field TRTYPCDA and Transaction Type Description field TRTYDSCA and Information Message field INFOMSGA are all set to protected/read-only), (2) NOT activate the F5 Save key (F5 is only highlighted when state is CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED or DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, neither of which applies here), and (3) NOT activate the F12 Cancel key (F12 is only highlighted for CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, SHOW-DETAILS, DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, CONFIRM-DELETE, or CREATE-NEW-RECORD states)

rules.rule_name: Reset to Search State After Lock Conflict on Next Entry
rules.rule_description: After a lock conflict failure is displayed, when the user returns to the screen (next interaction), the program must automatically reset to the initial search state so the user can re-enter the Transaction Type code and retry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Reviews Failure Message / User Chooses To Retry?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is displaying a lock conflict failure message with program state 'TTUP-CHANGES-FAILED' (which encompasses the lock error and other failure states) and all fields are protected
acceptance_criteria.When: The user interacts with the screen on the next program entry (e.g., presses a key to proceed)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must reset the program to the initial entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) and set the details state to 'Not Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), effectively returning the user to a clean search screen where they can re-enter a Transaction Type code to search and retry the update

rules.rule_name: Cancel Lock Conflict and Return to Search via F12
rules.rule_description: When a user is in a state where changes were pending confirmation (prior to the lock conflict scenario) and presses F12, the system cancels the pending update and returns to the search state, allowing the user to start over.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Presses F12 To Cancel and Return to Search / Return to Search Screen To Retry Later

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pending confirmed changes (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED state) and the Transaction Type code input is not valid or the user presses F12 to cancel
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the cancel action in the action decision logic (2000-DECIDE-ACTION) and the transaction type filter is not valid
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set a 'Update Was Cancelled' indicator (WS-UPDATE-WAS-CANCELLED = TRUE), (2) set the program state to 'Changes Backed Out' (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT = TRUE), and (3) redisplay the screen showing the original database values, effectively returning the user to the search/view state so they can retry later

rules.rule_name: Retry Save by Re-entering Transaction Type Code After Lock Conflict
rules.rule_description: After a lock conflict failure, the user can retry the save by re-entering the Transaction Type code to search for the record again, then re-entering their changes and confirming the save.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Re-enters Transaction Type Code To Search Again / Proceed with New Search and Retry Save

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen has been reset to the initial search state (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) following a lock conflict failure, with the Transaction Type Code field editable (set to DFHBMFSE - unprotected with cursor)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user enters a Transaction Type code and presses ENTER to search
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) validate that the entered Transaction Type code is numeric, non-zero, and exactly 2 digits (zero-padded if needed, e.g., '5' becomes '05'), (2) search the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for an exact match on TR_TYPE, (3) if found, display the current record values and set state to 'Show Details' (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS), and (4) position the cursor on the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCL = -1) so the user can re-enter their changes and attempt the save again

key_functionalities.title: Information Message Centering
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Start: Information Message Centering])
    S1[Determine the actual message text\nto be displayed based on current program state]
    S2[Measure the length of the message\nafter removing trailing spaces]
    S3[Calculate the center starting position\nby finding the midpoint of the\navailable display area minus message length]
    S4[Place the message text at the\ncalculated center position\nwithin the display area]
    S5[Set the centered message\ninto the screen information\nmessage field for display]
    END([End: Message Ready for Display\non Screen])

    START --> S1
    S1 --> S2
    S2 --> S3
    S3 --> S4
    S4 --> S5
    S5 --> END

rules.rule_name: Measure Actual Information Message Length After Trimming
rules.rule_description: Before centering the informational message on screen, the system determines the actual printable length of the message by removing trailing spaces and measuring only the meaningful content.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Measure the length of the message after removing trailing spaces

acceptance_criteria.Given: An informational message text (WS-INFO-MSG) has been selected based on the current program state and is ready to be formatted for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the display length of the message by trimming all trailing spaces from WS-INFO-MSG and measuring the length of the remaining text
acceptance_criteria.Then: The actual message length (WS-STRING-LEN) is stored as the count of non-trailing-space characters in the informational message, representing only the meaningful content to be displayed

rules.rule_name: Calculate Center Starting Position for Information Message
rules.rule_description: The system calculates the exact starting position within the screen display area where the message text should begin so that it appears visually centered to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Calculate the center starting position by finding the midpoint of the available display area minus message length

acceptance_criteria.Given: The actual message length (WS-STRING-LEN) has been determined by trimming trailing spaces, and the total available display field length for the information message (WS-INFO-MSG full field length) is known
acceptance_criteria.When: The system computes the center starting position using the formula: (Total Display Field Length minus Actual Message Length) divided by 2, plus 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The calculated center starting position (WS-STRING-MID) represents the character position within the display area at which the message text must begin so that it appears horizontally centered on screen

rules.rule_name: Place Information Message Text at Calculated Center Position
rules.rule_description: The system positions the trimmed message text into the output display buffer starting at the pre-calculated center position, ensuring the message appears centered within the available screen area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Place the message text at the calculated center position within the display area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The actual message length (WS-STRING-LEN) and the center starting position (WS-STRING-MID) have both been calculated, and the output display buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The system copies the message content from WS-INFO-MSG starting at position 1 for a length of WS-STRING-LEN characters into the output buffer WS-STRING-OUT starting at position WS-STRING-MID for a length of WS-STRING-LEN characters
acceptance_criteria.Then: The output display buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) contains the message text placed at the center position, with surrounding positions remaining as spaces, producing a visually centered message

rules.rule_name: Set Centered Information Message into Screen Display Field
rules.rule_description: The fully centered and formatted informational message is transferred from the internal output buffer into the actual screen map field so it is presented to the user on the next screen send.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set the centered message into the screen information message field for display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The output display buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) contains the informational message text correctly positioned at the calculated center location within the available display area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system moves the contents of the output display buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) into the screen information message output field (INFOMSGO of CTRTUPAO)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen information message field (INFOMSGO) contains the centered message text and is ready to be rendered on the user's screen during the next screen send operation, displaying the message centered within the information message area

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the key press as the F10 key indicator (CCARD-AID-PFK10 is set to TRUE), treating PF10 and PF22 as equivalent keys, making it available for subsequent PF key validation and action routing

rules.rule_name: Capture PF11 or PF23 Key Press and Record as F11 Key Indicator
rules.rule_description: When a user presses either PF11 or its shifted equivalent PF23 on the terminal, the system treats both as the same function and records the key press as the F11 key indicator for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF11 or PF23?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is interacting with the Transaction Type Update screen and the system is ready to receive a key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses either PF11 (EIBAID equals DFHPF11) or PF23 (EIBAID equals DFHPF23) on the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the key press as the F11 key indicator (CCARD-AID-PFK11 is set to TRUE), treating PF11 and PF23 as equivalent keys, making it available for subsequent PF key validation and action routing

rules.rule_name: Capture PF12 or PF24 Key Press and Record as F12 Cancel Key Indicator
rules.rule_description: When a user presses either PF12 or its shifted equivalent PF24 on the terminal, the system treats both as the Cancel function and records the key press as the F12 Cancel key indicator for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: PF12 or PF24?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is interacting with the Transaction Type Update screen and the system is ready to receive a key press
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses either PF12 (EIBAID equals DFHPF12) or PF24 (EIBAID equals DFHPF24) on the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the key press as the F12 Cancel key indicator (CCARD-AID-PFK12 is set to TRUE), treating PF12 and PF24 as equivalent Cancel keys, making it available for subsequent PF key validation and action routing

rules.rule_name: Proceed to PF Key Validation After Key Indicator is Recorded
rules.rule_description: Once any terminal key press has been captured and recorded as a standardized internal key indicator, the system proceeds to the PF key validation step to determine whether the pressed key is valid for the current screen state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to PF Key Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has pressed any key on the terminal and the system has captured and recorded the corresponding internal key indicator (one of: ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, F1 through F12)
acceptance_criteria.When: The key indicator has been successfully set to TRUE
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the PF Key Validation step (0001-CHECK-PFKEYS) where the recorded key indicator will be evaluated against the current screen state to determine if the key press is a valid action

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program is invoked by CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All working storage areas (CC-WORK-AREA, WS-MISC-STORAGE, WS-COMMAREA) are initialized to their default values, the transaction ID is set to the current transaction literal (LIT-THISTRANID), and the return message flag is set to OFF (no error message displayed)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization and Working Storage Setup
all_rules.Rule_Description: On every entry to the Transaction Type Update screen, the program initializes all working storage areas, sets the current transaction identifier, and clears any prior error messages to ensure a clean processing environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The communication area length (EIBCALEN) is zero (no prior session), OR the calling program is the Admin program (LIT-ADMINPGM) and the program-reenter flag is NOT set, OR the calling program is the List program (LIT-LISTTPGM) and the program-reenter flag is NOT set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA are initialized to defaults, the program-enter flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is set to TRUE, and the details-not-fetched flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) is set to TRUE; OTHERWISE the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA is restored from the first portion of DFHCOMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA is restored from the second portion of DFHCOMMAREA

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Context Restoration from Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether to restore a prior session's state from the communication area or initialize a completely fresh context, based on whether this is a first-time entry or a return from another program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed a key on the terminal and control has returned to the program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the EIBAID value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The corresponding program flag is set to TRUE: ENTER key sets CCARD-AID-ENTER, CLEAR sets CCARD-AID-CLEAR, PA1 sets CCARD-AID-PA1, PA2 sets CCARD-AID-PA2, PF1/PF13 sets CCARD-AID-PFK01, PF2/PF14 sets CCARD-AID-PFK02, PF3/PF15 sets CCARD-AID-PFK03, PF4/PF16 sets CCARD-AID-PFK04, PF5/PF17 sets CCARD-AID-PFK05, PF6/PF18 sets CCARD-AID-PFK06, PF7/PF19 sets CCARD-AID-PFK07, PF8/PF20 sets CCARD-AID-PFK08, PF9/PF21 sets CCARD-AID-PFK09, PF10/PF22 sets CCARD-AID-PFK10, PF11/PF23 sets CCARD-AID-PFK11, PF12/PF24 sets CCARD-AID-PFK12

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Identification from Terminal Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: Captures and identifies which function key the user pressed on the terminal by mapping the CICS attention identifier (EIBAID) to a named program flag for subsequent processing logic.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed a function key and the current screen state is known
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the pressed key against the current state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: PFK-VALID is set to TRUE if any of the following conditions are met: (1) PF3 is pressed (always valid), (2) ENTER is pressed AND the state is NOT Confirm-Delete, (3) PF4 is pressed AND state is Show-Details OR Confirm-Delete, (4) PF5 is pressed AND state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Details-Not-Found OR Delete-In-Progress, (5) PF12 is pressed AND state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Show-Details OR Details-Not-Found OR Confirm-Delete OR Create-New-Record; OTHERWISE PFK-INVALID is set to TRUE and if no prior return message exists, WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED is set to TRUE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Valid Function Key Combinations per Screen State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Enforces that only contextually appropriate function keys are accepted for the current screen state. Keys that are not valid for the current state are rejected with an invalid key indicator.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has evaluated the pressed key and current state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any of the following conditions are true: (1) PF12 is pressed AND state is Show-Details OR Create-New-Record OR Details-Not-Found, (2) state is Changes-Okayed-And-Done, (3) state is Changes-Failed, (4) state is Changes-Backed-Out AND old details are LOW-VALUES or SPACES, (5) state is Delete-Done, (6) state is Delete-Failed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is set to TRUE and TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is set to TRUE, resetting the screen to initial search mode

all_rules.Rule_Name: Automatic State Reset After Terminal Operations
all_rules.Rule_Description: After certain terminal conditions (completed operations, failures, or cancellations), the program automatically resets the screen state back to the initial entry mode so the user starts fresh.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user presses PF3 on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: PF3 is detected as the pressed key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If CDEMO-FROM-TRANID is LOW-VALUES or SPACES, the destination transaction is set to LIT-ADMINTRANID; otherwise it is set to CDEMO-FROM-TRANID. If CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is LOW-VALUES or SPACES, the destination program is set to LIT-ADMINPGM; otherwise it is set to CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM. The current transaction (LIT-THISTRANID) and program (LIT-THISPGM) are recorded as the source. CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is set to TRUE, CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is set to TRUE, the current mapset and map are saved, a database SYNCPOINT (commit) is issued, and control is transferred (XCTL) to the destination program with the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exit and Return to Calling Program via PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3, the program exits and transfers control back to the originating program (Admin menu or List screen), committing any pending database changes before navigating away.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in first-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE) AND the state is Details-Not-Fetched
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the entry condition as a new session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, WS-MISC-STORAGE, and CDEMO-ACCT-ID are all initialized to defaults; the send-map routine is performed to display an empty screen with a prompt for the user to enter a Transaction Type code; CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is set to TRUE and TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is set to TRUE before returning to CICS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initial Empty Search Screen Display on First Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: On first entry or after a full reset, the program displays a blank Transaction Type search screen, clearing all prior data and prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record is currently displayed on screen (state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF4
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state is changed to TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE and the screen is redisplayed with a delete confirmation prompt message, awaiting the user's confirmation or cancellation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Delete Confirmation Request on First PF4 Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF4 while a Transaction Type record is displayed, the program does not immediately delete but instead transitions to a confirmation state, requiring the user to press PF4 a second time to confirm the deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in Confirm-Delete state (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF4 again to confirm
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: TTUP-START-DELETE is set to TRUE, the delete processing routine (9800-DELETE-PROCESSING) is performed, and the screen is redisplayed with the result

all_rules.Rule_Name: Delete Execution on Second PF4 Press (Confirmed Delete)
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user confirms deletion by pressing PF4 a second time while in the Confirm-Delete state, the program executes the actual deletion of the Transaction Type record from the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The delete operation has been confirmed and TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE contains the Transaction Type code to be deleted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A SQL DELETE is executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE WHERE TR_TYPE = the stored original type code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the delete succeeds (SQLCODE = 0): TTUP-DELETE-DONE is set to TRUE and the transaction is committed (SYNCPOINT); If the delete fails because child records exist (SQLCODE = -532): RECORD-DELETE-FAILED is set to TRUE and the message 'Please delete associated child records first: SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is displayed; If the delete fails for any other reason: RECORD-DELETE-FAILED and TTUP-DELETE-FAILED are both set to TRUE and the message 'Delete failed with message: SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Record Deletion from Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: Executes the physical deletion of a Transaction Type record from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the stored original type code, and handles all possible outcomes including success, referential integrity violations, and other failures.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is Details-Not-Found (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF5
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state is changed to TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD and the screen is redisplayed prompting the user to enter the new Transaction Type data (description)

all_rules.Rule_Name: New Record Creation Mode Initiation via PF5
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a search returns no matching Transaction Type record and the user presses PF5, the program transitions to new record creation mode, allowing the user to enter details for the new Transaction Type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is TRUE), meaning the user's input has passed validation and is awaiting final confirmation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF5 to confirm the save
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The write processing routine (9600-WRITE-PROCESSING) is performed, followed by redisplaying the screen with the result of the save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Confirmed Changes via PF5
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has reviewed validated changes and presses PF5 to confirm, the program executes the database write operation (update or insert) to persist the Transaction Type data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user presses PF12 AND the current state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Confirm-Delete OR Show-Details
Acceptance_Criteria.When: PF12 is detected and the state qualifies for cancellation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE is set to TRUE, the action decision logic (2000-DECIDE-ACTION) is performed to re-fetch the original record from the database, and the screen is redisplayed with the original values; if the state was Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed, WS-UPDATE-WAS-CANCELLED is set; if the state was Confirm-Delete, WS-DELETE-WAS-CANCELLED is set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cancel Pending Action and Refresh via PF12
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF12 while in a confirmation or detail-viewing state, the program cancels the pending action and re-fetches the original record from the database to restore the prior state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed a function key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is not valid for the current screen state (WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is redisplayed as-is with the invalid key message shown to the user; no data processing or state changes occur

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Press Handling and Screen Redisplay
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses a function key that is not valid for the current screen state, the program redisplays the current screen unchanged with an invalid key message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER or a valid key that triggers normal input processing (not PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12, or an invalid key)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program routes to the input processing path
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following sequence is performed in order: (1) receive screen map input (1100-RECEIVE-MAP), (2) store screen values to working variables (1150-STORE-MAP-IN-NEW), (3) perform all validation edits (1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS); after processing, the current program name, mapset, and map are set as the next navigation targets

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Input Processing Sequence
all_rules.Rule_Description: Orchestrates the complete sequence of receiving screen input, storing it to working variables, and performing all validation edits when the user presses ENTER or another valid key for normal processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the screen with data entered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The receive map operation is executed for the current map (LIT-THISMAP) and mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) into CTRTUPAI
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All screen field values entered by the user are captured into the CTRTUPAI input area and response codes are stored in WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Map Input Reception
all_rules.Rule_Description: Receives and captures all field values entered by the user from the screen map into the program's input area for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Screen input has been received into CTRTUPAI
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The store-map-in-new routine (1150-STORE-MAP-IN-NEW) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Special case: if the state is Details-Not-Found AND PF5 was NOT pressed AND the trimmed value of TRTYPCDI equals the previously stored TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, skip re-storing (preserve existing context); Otherwise: TTUP-NEW-DETAILS is initialized, then if TRTYPCDI is '*' or SPACES it is stored as LOW-VALUES in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, else the trimmed value is stored; if TRTYDSCI is '*' or SPACES it is stored as LOW-VALUES in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, else the trimmed value is stored

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Input Storage to Working Variables
all_rules.Rule_Description: Transfers the captured screen field values into internal working storage variables, handling special input values and preserving search context when appropriate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a value in the Transaction Type Code field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction type code validation routine (1210-EDIT-TRANTYPE) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The field label 'Tran Type code' is used in all error messages; (1) If the value is blank, LOW-VALUES, or empty (trimmed length = 0): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK is set, and the message '[field] must be supplied.' is generated; (2) If the value is not numeric (TEST-NUMVAL fails): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK is set, and the message '[field] must be numeric.' is generated; (3) If the numeric value equals zero: INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK is set, and the message '[field] must not be zero.' is generated; (4) If all validations pass: FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID) is set to TRUE and the numeric value is computed, converted to a 2-character string, spaces replaced with zeros (zero-padded), and stored back into TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Validation Rules
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the entered Transaction Type code meets all business rules: it must be provided, must be numeric, must not be zero, and is automatically formatted with leading zeros to ensure consistent 2-digit representation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the Transaction Type Description field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) and changes have been detected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The alphanumeric required validation routine (1230-EDIT-ALPHANUM-REQD) is performed with field label 'Transaction Desc' and maximum length 50
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: (1) If the value is blank, LOW-VALUES, or empty (trimmed length = 0): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK is set, and the message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' is generated; (2) If the value contains non-alphanumeric characters (after converting all valid alphanumeric characters to spaces, the trimmed result is non-empty): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK is set, and the message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' is generated; (3) If all validations pass: FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID is set to TRUE; the validation result flags are stored in WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAGS; if INPUT-ERROR is not set, TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED is set to TRUE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Description Validation Rules
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Transaction Type description is provided and contains only alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers), enforcing data quality for the description field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both old details (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE, TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) and new details (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The compare old-new routine (1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: NO-CHANGES-FOUND is set initially; if the UPPER-CASE of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE equals UPPER-CASE of TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE AND the UPPER-CASE of trimmed TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC equals UPPER-CASE of trimmed TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC AND the trimmed lengths are equal: if no prior return message exists, NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is set to TRUE; otherwise if any difference is found: if no prior return message exists, CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED is set to TRUE and processing continues to description validation; if NO-CHANGES-FOUND or TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED or TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE is true, WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS are cleared and validation exits

all_rules.Rule_Name: Change Detection Between Original and New Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: Compares the user's newly entered values against the originally fetched database values to determine whether any actual changes have been made, preventing unnecessary database updates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Input processing and validation have completed and the current state flags are set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision routine (2000-DECIDE-ACTION) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following state transitions apply: (1) If state is Details-Not-Fetched OR PF12 was pressed: if FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID, perform database lookup (9000-READ-TRANTYPE) and set Show-Details if found or Details-Not-Found if not found; if NOT valid: if Confirm-Delete state, set WS-DELETE-WAS-CANCELLED and Details-Not-Fetched; if Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed state, set WS-UPDATE-WAS-CANCELLED and Changes-Backed-Out; otherwise set Details-Not-Fetched; (2) If Show-Details: if INPUT-ERROR or NO-CHANGES-DETECTED or WS-INVALID-KEY, keep current state; else set Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed; (3) If Changes-Not-OK: no state change; (4) If Changes-Backed-Out: set Changes-Not-OK; (5) If Invalid-Search-Keys: no state change; (6) If PF5 and Details-Not-Found: set Create-New-Record; (7) If Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed: no state change; (8) If Changes-Okayed-And-Done: set Show-Details and if no calling transaction context, clear CDEMO-ACCT-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM to zeroes and CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS to LOW-VALUES

all_rules.Rule_Name: Action Decision Logic Based on State and Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: Evaluates the current program state and input results to determine the next appropriate action, orchestrating state transitions for the Transaction Type maintenance workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Transaction Type code is stored in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE and has been moved to DCL-TR-TYPE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A SQL SELECT is executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE retrieving TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION WHERE TR_TYPE equals the entered type code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the record is found (SQLCODE = 0): FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE is set to TRUE; if the record is not found (SQLCODE = +100): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and if no prior message exists WS-RECORD-NOT-FOUND message is set; if a database error occurs (SQLCODE < 0): INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and the message 'Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is generated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Database Lookup by Type Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Queries the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table to retrieve the Transaction Type record matching the entered type code, determining whether the record exists for subsequent display or update operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been successfully retrieved from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The store-fetched-data routine (9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: TTUP-OLD-DETAILS is initialized to defaults, then DCL-TR-TYPE is moved to TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE, and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT (trimmed to the actual length specified by DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN) is moved to TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Fetched Transaction Type Data as Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a Transaction Type record from the database, stores the fetched values as the 'original' baseline data to enable change detection and screen display of original values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has confirmed changes and TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE contains the type code and TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC contains the new description; DCL-TR-TYPE is set from TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT is set from trimmed TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN is computed as the length of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A SQL UPDATE is executed against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE setting TR_DESCRIPTION = DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION WHERE TR_TYPE = DCL-TR-TYPE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If update succeeds (SQLCODE = 0): the transaction is committed (SYNCPOINT) and TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE is set; if no row was updated (SQLCODE = +100): the insert routine (9700-INSERT-RECORD) is performed; if the record is locked (SQLCODE = -911): INPUT-ERROR is set, COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE is set, and TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR is set; if any other error (SQLCODE < 0): TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED is set, TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED is set, and the message 'Error updating: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is generated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Description Update in Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: Executes a SQL UPDATE to modify the description of an existing Transaction Type record in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table, handling all possible outcomes including success, record not found (triggers insert), and lock conflicts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The UPDATE operation returned no rows found (SQLCODE = +100), indicating the Transaction Type code does not yet exist in CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A SQL INSERT is executed into CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE with values (DCL-TR-TYPE, DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the insert succeeds (SQLCODE = 0): the transaction is committed (SYNCPOINT) and TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE is set; if the insert fails for any other reason: TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED is set and the message 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE: [code]: [error message]' is generated

all_rules.Rule_Name: New Transaction Type Record Insertion into Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an UPDATE finds no existing record (the type code does not exist in the database), executes a SQL INSERT to create a new Transaction Type record with the provided type code and description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A SQL UPDATE is attempted on CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The update fails with a lock conflict (SQLCODE = -911)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE, COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE is set to TRUE (if no prior return message exists), and TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR is set to TRUE; the screen is redisplayed with a failure message informing the user that the record could not be updated due to a concurrent access conflict

all_rules.Rule_Name: Concurrent Update Lock Conflict Detection and Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: Detects when a Transaction Type record cannot be updated because it is currently locked by another user's concurrent access, and informs the user of the conflict.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to send a screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (3100-SCREEN-INIT) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The output area CTRTUPAO is set to LOW-VALUES; the current date and time are obtained; CCDA-TITLE01 is moved to TITLE01O, CCDA-TITLE02 is moved to TITLE02O, LIT-THISTRANID is moved to TRNNAMEO, LIT-THISPGM is moved to PGMNAMEO; the current date is formatted as MM/DD/YY and moved to CURDATEO; the current time is formatted as HH:MM:SS and moved to CURTIMEO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Initialization with Date, Time, and Program Identity
all_rules.Rule_Description: Initializes the output screen map with standard header information including the current date, current time, program name, and transaction ID before populating business data fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen variable setup routine (3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE: no field values are set (blank screen); Otherwise based on state: (1) Details-Not-Fetched: show initial blank values (LOW-VALUES in TRTYPCDO); (2) Show-Details, Confirm-Delete, Delete-Failed, Delete-Done, Changes-Backed-Out: initialize TTUP-NEW-DETAILS and display ORIGINAL values (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE to TRTYPCDO, TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC to TRTYDSCO); (3) Changes-Made, Changes-Not-OK, Details-Not-Found, Invalid-Search-Keys, Create-New-Record, Changes-Okayed-And-Done: display NEW/user-entered values (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE to TRTYPCDO, TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC to TRTYDSCO); (4) Any other state: initialize TTUP-NEW-DETAILS and display original values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Field Population Based on Program State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines which set of values (blank, original database values, or user-entered new values) to display in the screen fields based on the current program state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display and the current state is known
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The information message setup routine (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message is selected based on state: CDEMO-PGM-ENTER OR Details-Not-Fetched OR Invalid-Search-Keys → PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS; Details-Not-Found → PROMPT-CREATE-NEW-RECORD; Show-Details OR Changes-Backed-Out with no old type code → PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS; Changes-Backed-Out OR Changes-Not-OK → PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES; Confirm-Delete → PROMPT-DELETE-CONFIRM; Delete-Failed → INFORM-FAILURE; Delete-Done → CONFIRM-DELETE-SUCCESS; Create-New-Record → PROMPT-FOR-NEWDATA; Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed → PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION; Changes-Okayed-And-Done → CONFIRM-UPDATE-SUCCESS; Changes-Okayed-Lock-Error OR Changes-Okayed-But-Failed → INFORM-FAILURE; No-Info-Message → PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS; The selected message is trimmed, its length and midpoint are computed, and it is centered in WS-STRING-OUT before being moved to INFOMSGO; WS-RETURN-MSG is moved to ERRMSGO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Informational Message Selection and Display Based on State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Selects and formats the appropriate informational guidance message for the user based on the current screen state, centering it on the screen for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields are first set to protected (DFHBMPRF) via 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS (TRTYPCDA, TRTYDSCA, INFOMSGA); Then field protection is adjusted: if state is Details-Not-Fetched OR Invalid-Search-Keys OR Details-Not-Found OR (Changes-Backed-Out with no old type code): TRTYPCDA is set to DFHBMFSE (editable); if state is Show-Details OR Changes-Not-OK OR Create-New-Record OR Changes-Backed-Out (with old data): TRTYDSCA is set to DFHBMFSE (editable) and INFOMSGA is set to DFHBMPRF via 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS; Cursor position (-1) is set: to TRTYPCDL when state is Details-Not-Fetched OR Details-Not-Found OR Invalid-Search-Keys OR filter errors OR Changes-Okayed-And-Done OR Changes-Backed-Out with no old data; to TRTYDSCL when state is Create-New-Record OR No-Changes-Detected OR Description errors OR Changes-Made OR Changes-Backed-Out OR Show-Details; to TRTYPCDL for all other states

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Field Protection and Cursor Positioning Based on State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Controls which screen fields are editable versus protected (read-only) and positions the cursor at the appropriate field based on the current program state and validation results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) evaluates error conditions
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE OR TTUP-DELETE-FAILED is TRUE: TRTYPCDC (color attribute of Transaction Type Code field) is set to DFHRED (red); If FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK is TRUE AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE: TRTYPCDO (display value of Transaction Type Code field) is set to '*' as a placeholder AND TRTYPCDC is set to DFHRED (red)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Field Color Highlighting in Red
all_rules.Rule_Description: Sets the color of screen fields to red to visually highlight error conditions, drawing the user's attention to fields that require correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The PF key attribute setup routine (3391-SETUP-PFKEY-ATTRS) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If state is Confirm-Delete: FKEYSA (all PF key labels area) is set to DFHBMDAR (dark/dimmed); otherwise FKEYSA is set to DFHBMASB (bright/visible); If state is Show-Details OR Confirm-Delete: FKEY04A (PF4 label) is set to DFHBMASB (bright/active); If state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Details-Not-Found: FKEY05A (PF5 label) is set to DFHBMASB (bright/active); If state is Changes-OK-Not-Confirmed OR Show-Details OR Details-Not-Found OR Confirm-Delete OR Create-New-Record: FKEY12A (PF12 label) is set to DFHBMASB (bright/active)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Availability Display Based on Screen State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Controls the visual appearance of function key labels on the screen, highlighting available keys and dimming unavailable ones based on the current program state to guide the user on valid actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen map (CTRTUPAO) has been fully populated with data, messages, and field attributes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The send screen routine (3400-SEND-SCREEN) is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: LIT-THISMAPSET is moved to CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and LIT-THISMAP is moved to CCARD-NEXT-MAP; a CICS SEND MAP command is issued with the map name, mapset name, FROM CTRTUPAO, with CURSOR positioning, ERASE (clear prior screen), and FREEKB (unlock keyboard) options; response codes are stored in WS-RESP-CD

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Transmission to User Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: Transmits the fully prepared screen map to the user's terminal, erasing the prior screen content and freeing the keyboard for user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed its current processing cycle and is ready to return to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The COMMON-RETURN routine is executed
