Acceptance_Criteria.Then: WS-RETURN-MSG is moved to CCARD-ERROR-MSG; CARDDEMO-COMMAREA is moved to the first portion of WS-COMMAREA; WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA is moved to the second portion of WS-COMMAREA (starting at position LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1); a CICS RETURN command is issued with the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID), the full WS-COMMAREA, and its length, causing CICS to await the next user interaction and re-invoke this program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session State Persistence Before Returning to CICS
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before returning control to CICS to await the next user interaction, saves the current program state and error messages into the communication area so the session context is preserved for the next entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program has been invoked and is beginning execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program starts its main processing routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card work area (CC-WORK-AREA) and the miscellaneous storage area (WS-MISC-STORAGE) must both be fully initialized to their default empty values, clearing any data that may have existed from a prior execution or session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Working Storage Areas at Program Startup
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution, all working storage areas including the card work area and miscellaneous storage must be reset to their initial default values to ensure no residual data from a previous session affects the current transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program has been invoked and is beginning execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program starts its main processing routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session communication area (WS-COMMAREA) must be fully initialized to its default empty values, clearing any previously held inter-program communication data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Session Communication Area at Program Startup
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution, the session communication area (WS-COMMAREA) used to pass data between programs must be reset to its initial default values to ensure a clean state before any session context is loaded or evaluated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program has been invoked and working storage areas have been initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets up its session context during startup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The literal transaction identifier for this program (LIT-THISTRANID) must be moved into the working storage transaction ID field (WS-TRANID), establishing the current transaction identity for the session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Transaction Identifier in Session Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, the system must record the current transaction identifier into the working session context so that the transaction identity is available throughout the program's execution for tracking, navigation, and return-routing purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update program has been invoked and working storage areas have been initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes its initial setup during startup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The return message flag (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF) must be set to TRUE, suppressing any previously held error or informational return messages and ensuring the screen starts with a clean message state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Error and Return Messages at Program Startup
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, any existing error or return messages from a prior interaction must be cleared so that stale messages are not displayed to the user during the new program execution cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user initiates the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The communication area length (EIBCALEN) is equal to zero, indicating no prior session data exists
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session is identified as brand new and the program proceeds to initialize a completely fresh session context, clearing all program state flags and transaction type working data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Brand New Session with No Prior Interaction Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the current interaction is a completely new session by checking if there is no communication area data passed from a prior interaction. This is the primary gateway condition that routes the program to either initialize fresh context or restore prior session state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A communication area exists from a prior interaction (EIBCALEN is not zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The originating program is the Admin Menu program (LIT-ADMINPGM) AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set (meaning this is not a return back to this same screen), OR the originating program is the Transaction List program (LIT-LISTTPGM) AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session is treated as a first visit and the program proceeds to initialize a completely fresh session context, discarding any previously saved state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect First Visit from Admin Menu or List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the user is arriving at the Transaction Type Update screen for the first time from either the Admin Menu program or the Transaction List program, even when a communication area exists. This prevents stale session state from a prior visit to this screen from being incorrectly restored.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The session has been identified as brand new (no prior communication area data) OR the user is arriving for the first time from the Admin Menu or Transaction List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fresh session initialization is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The general program communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is fully initialized to its default empty state, AND the Transaction Type Update program-specific working area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is fully initialized to its default empty state, clearing all transaction type codes, descriptions, old values, new values, and all program state flags

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Fresh Session Context for New or First-Visit Sessions
all_rules.Rule_Description: Establishes a clean starting state for the Transaction Type Update screen when the session is brand new or the user is visiting for the first time from the Admin Menu or List screen. All previously held program state flags and transaction type working data are cleared to prevent carry-over from prior interactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A fresh session context has just been initialized (either for a brand new session or a first visit from Admin Menu or List screen)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session state markers are being set after initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program entry state flag is set to 'First Entry' (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE), indicating the screen has not yet been re-entered by the user, AND the transaction type details fetch state is set to 'Details Not Yet Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), indicating no transaction type record has been retrieved from the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Session as First Entry with Transaction Type Details Not Yet Fetched
all_rules.Rule_Description: After initializing a fresh session context, the program sets specific state markers to indicate that this is the first entry into the screen and that no transaction type record has been fetched from the database yet. These markers drive the screen display logic to show an empty search prompt to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A prior session exists (communication area length is not zero) AND the interaction is not a first visit from the Admin Menu or Transaction List program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session context restoration is triggered for a returning interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The general program communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is restored by copying the first segment of the CICS communication area (DFHCOMMAREA) with a length equal to the size of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, reloading all general navigation flags, calling program name, calling transaction ID, user type, and last map/mapset information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore General Program State from Prior Session Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a returning user interaction is detected (prior session data exists and it is not a first visit from Admin or List), the general program state including navigation context, calling program identity, calling transaction identity, and user type flags are restored from the communication area passed by CICS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The general program communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) has already been restored from the CICS communication area for a returning interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific working data restoration is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Update program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is restored by copying the second segment of the CICS communication area (DFHCOMMAREA), starting at the position immediately after the general CARDDEMO-COMMAREA segment, with a length equal to the size of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, reloading all transaction type state flags (TTUP flags such as details-fetched state, change confirmation state, delete state) and all transaction type old and new detail values (type codes and descriptions) from the prior interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore Transaction Type Working Data from Prior Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: As the second part of session restoration for returning interactions, the Transaction Type Update program-specific working data is restored from the communication area. This includes all transaction type state flags (such as whether details were fetched, whether changes are pending confirmation, whether delete is in progress) and the actual transaction type code and description values from the prior interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in any screen state (Details Not Fetched, Showing Details, Confirm Delete, Creating New Record, Changes Pending Confirmation, etc.)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the F3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F3 key is marked as VALID and the exit action is allowed to proceed without any restriction

all_rules.Rule_Name: F3 Key Always Valid for Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F3 key (Exit/Return) is unconditionally valid regardless of the current screen state. Pressing F3 always allows the user to exit the Transaction Type Update screen and return to the calling program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key AND the screen is NOT currently in the Delete Confirmation state (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE is not active)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Enter key is marked as VALID and input processing proceeds; BUT if the screen IS currently in the Delete Confirmation state, the Enter key is marked as INVALID and an Invalid Key message is set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enter Key Valid Except During Delete Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Enter key is valid for submitting input or triggering a search in all screen states, with one exception: when the screen is in the Delete Confirmation state, pressing Enter is not a valid action and must be rejected to prevent accidental processing during a sensitive delete workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the F4 key AND the screen is currently in either the 'Showing Details' state (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS) OR the 'Delete Confirmation' state (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F4 key is marked as VALID and the delete action is allowed to proceed; BUT if the screen is in any other state (e.g., Details Not Fetched, Details Not Found, Creating New Record, Changes Pending), the F4 key is marked as INVALID and an Invalid Key message is set

all_rules.Rule_Name: F4 Key Valid Only When Record Is Displayed or Delete Is Awaiting Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F4 key (Delete) is only valid when there is an active record displayed on screen or when the system is already waiting for the user to confirm a pending delete. F4 cannot be used in any other state, such as during initial search, record not found, or while changes are being confirmed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the F5 key AND the screen is currently in one of the following states: 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED) meaning validated changes are awaiting save confirmation, OR 'Details Not Found' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND) meaning the searched record does not exist and a new record can be created, OR 'Delete In Progress' (TTUP-DELETE-IN-PROGRESS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F5 key is marked as VALID and the corresponding save or create action is allowed to proceed; BUT if the screen is in any other state (e.g., Showing Details without pending changes, Details Not Fetched, Confirm Delete), the F5 key is marked as INVALID and an Invalid Key message is set

all_rules.Rule_Name: F5 Key Valid Only for Save Confirmation or New Record Creation or Delete In Progress
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F5 key (Save/Confirm) is only valid in three specific states: when validated changes are awaiting user confirmation before saving, when a search returned no record and the user may choose to create a new one, or when a delete operation is in progress. F5 is not valid in any other state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the F12 key AND the screen is currently in one of the following states: 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), OR 'Showing Details' (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS), OR 'Details Not Found' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND), OR 'Confirm Delete' (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE), OR 'Create New Record' (TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F12 key is marked as VALID and the cancel or refresh action is allowed to proceed; BUT if the screen is in any other state (e.g., Details Not Fetched, Invalid Search Keys, Changes Not OK), the F12 key is marked as INVALID and an Invalid Key message is set

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Key Valid Only for Cancel or Refresh in Specific Active States
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F12 key (Cancel/Refresh) is only valid when the screen is in one of five active operational states where a cancellation or refresh action is meaningful: changes are pending confirmation, a record is currently displayed, a record was not found, delete confirmation is pending, or a new record is being created. F12 is not valid in any other state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in any state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses a key that is either: not one of the recognized function keys (F3, Enter, F4, F5, F12), OR one of those keys but pressed in a screen state where it is not permitted (e.g., F4 pressed when no record is displayed, F5 pressed when showing details without pending changes, F12 pressed when in initial/not-fetched state)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as INVALID (PFK-INVALID is set to TRUE), an 'Invalid Key Pressed' message (WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED) is set to notify the user, and the screen is redisplayed in its current state without performing any data processing or state change

all_rules.Rule_Name: Any Unrecognized or Context-Invalid Key Press Is Rejected
all_rules.Rule_Description: Any key press that is not F3, Enter, F4, F5, or F12, or any of those keys pressed in a screen state where they are not permitted, results in the key being marked as invalid. An Invalid Key message is set to inform the user that the action is not allowed in the current context, and the screen is redisplayed without processing the input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the current screen state is one of: (a) showing details of an existing transaction type record, (b) in the process of creating a new transaction type record, or (c) displaying a 'record not found' result from a previous search
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F12 (Cancel/Refresh key)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Screen State When User Cancels via F12 While Viewing, Creating, or Record Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F12 (Cancel) while the screen is in one of three active states — viewing an existing transaction type record, creating a new transaction type record, or after a search returned no record — the system must discard the current context and reset the screen to its initial empty search state, prompting the user to start a fresh search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the system has just completed a successful save operation (update or insert) to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, with the screen state set to 'Changes Okayed And Done' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE = TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Screen State After Successful Transaction Type Update or Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction type record has been successfully saved to the database — either by updating an existing record or inserting a new one — the system must automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode so the user can perform a new search or operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the system has encountered a failure during a save operation to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, with the screen state set to 'Changes Failed' (TTUP-CHANGES-FAILED = TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Screen State After Failed Transaction Type Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction type save operation has failed (e.g., due to a database error during update or insert), the system must automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode so the user can start a fresh search rather than remaining in a failed/inconsistent state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the current screen state is 'Changes Backed Out' (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT = TRUE) AND the original record data area (TTUP-OLD-DETAILS) contains either LOW-VALUES or SPACES, meaning no prior record data is available to restore
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Screen State When Changes Are Cancelled and No Prior Record Data Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user cancels pending changes (backs out of an update) AND there is no previously fetched original record data available to restore (the old details area is empty), the system must reset the screen to its initial empty search state rather than attempting to redisplay non-existent original values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the system has just completed a successful deletion of a transaction type record from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, with the screen state set to 'Delete Done' (TTUP-DELETE-DONE = TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Screen State After Successful Transaction Type Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction type record has been successfully deleted from the database, the system must automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode since the deleted record no longer exists and cannot be displayed or operated upon.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the system has encountered a failure during a delete operation on the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, with the screen state set to 'Delete Failed' (TTUP-DELETE-FAILED = TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the program state to 'Fresh Entry' mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) AND clears the fetched data flag (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), causing the screen to redisplay as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Screen State After Failed Transaction Type Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction type delete operation has failed (e.g., due to existing child records or a database error), the system must automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode so the user can start a fresh search rather than remaining in a failed delete state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active AND the current screen state is NOT any of the following: (a) F12 pressed while showing details, creating new record, or record not found; (b) changes okayed and done; (c) changes failed; (d) changes backed out with no prior record data; (e) delete done; (f) delete failed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main program evaluates the current screen state at the start of the next user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT reset the program state — CDEMO-PGM-ENTER and TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED flags remain unchanged — and processing continues with the existing screen state and previously fetched data

all_rules.Rule_Name: No State Reset Required When None of the Terminal Conditions Are Met
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the current screen state does not match any of the terminal conditions that require a reset (not F12 cancel from active states, not a completed/failed update, not a cancelled change with no data, not a completed/failed delete), the system preserves the existing screen state and continues processing with the current context intact.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the communication area is either empty (LOW-VALUES) or blank (SPACES), indicating no specific calling transaction was recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F3 to exit the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination transaction ID (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) to the Admin Menu transaction ID (LIT-ADMINTRANID) as the default return destination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default to Admin Menu When No Calling Transaction Is Recorded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F3 to exit and no originating transaction ID was recorded in the communication area, the system defaults the return destination transaction to the Admin Menu transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the communication area contains a valid non-blank, non-empty transaction ID, indicating this screen was launched from a specific transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F3 to exit the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination transaction ID (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) to the previously recorded calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), directing the user back to the originating transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Recorded Calling Transaction When One Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F3 to exit and a specific originating transaction ID was recorded in the communication area, the system uses that recorded transaction as the return destination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and the originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area is either empty (LOW-VALUES) or blank (SPACES), indicating no specific calling program was recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F3 to exit the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) to the Admin Menu program (LIT-ADMINPGM) as the default return destination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default to Admin Menu Program When No Calling Program Is Recorded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F3 to exit and no originating program name was recorded in the communication area, the system defaults the return destination program to the Admin Menu program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and the originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area contains a valid non-blank, non-empty program name, indicating this screen was launched from a specific program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F3 to exit the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) to the previously recorded calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), directing the user back to the originating program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Recorded Calling Program When One Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F3 to exit and a specific originating program name was recorded in the communication area, the system uses that recorded program as the return destination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed F3 to exit the Transaction Type Update screen and the destination program has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is preparing to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current screen's transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) into the originating transaction field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) and the current program name (LIT-THISPGM) into the originating program field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area, and sets the current map set (LIT-THISMAPSET) and map name (LIT-THISMAP) into the last-used map fields (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET, CDEMO-LAST-MAP), so the destination program has full context of the navigation origin

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program Context Before Exiting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system records the current Transaction Type Update screen's transaction ID and program name as the originating context in the communication area, so the destination program knows where the user came from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed F3 to exit the Transaction Type Update screen and the destination program has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is preparing to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the user type flag (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN) to Admin and sets the program entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) to indicate a fresh entry into the destination program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User Type to Admin Before Exiting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program on F3 exit, the system sets the user type indicator to Admin in the communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed F3 to exit the Transaction Type Update screen, the destination program has been determined, and the current program context has been recorded in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system issues a SYNCPOINT to commit any pending database changes before transferring control, ensuring all work performed during this session is permanently saved and the database is in a consistent state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Pending Work Before Exiting to Destination Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system commits any pending database changes to ensure data consistency.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed F3 to exit, the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been set to either the Admin Menu program or the recorded calling program, the current program context has been recorded, and pending work has been committed via SYNCPOINT
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control directly to the destination program identified in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, passing the full CARDDEMO-COMMAREA communication area containing all session context (originating transaction, originating program, user type, last map set, last map), and the current Transaction Type Update screen is exited — the user is now on the Admin Menu or List Screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Program on F3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: After committing pending work, the system transfers control directly to the determined destination program (Admin Menu or List Screen), passing the full communication area so the destination program has all necessary context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user accesses the Transaction Type Update screen under one of the following conditions: (1) No communication area exists from a prior session (first-time entry), OR (2) The calling program is the Admin program and the re-entry flag is NOT set, OR (3) The calling program is the List program and the re-entry flag is NOT set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The main CardDemo communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be fully initialized to its default empty state, AND the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be fully initialized to its default empty state, ensuring no data from any prior transaction or session is retained

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fresh Entry Initialization - Clear All Working Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type Update screen is accessed for the first time, or when navigating from the Admin program or List program without a re-entry flag, all program communication areas and working storage must be fully cleared to ensure no residual data from a previous session is carried forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has determined this is a fresh entry (no prior session, or coming from Admin/List program without re-entry flag) and has cleared all working data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets its operational state flags
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program entry state flag must be set to CDEMO-PGM-ENTER (indicating the user is entering the program fresh), AND the transaction type details state flag must be set to TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED (indicating no record has been retrieved from the database yet)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fresh Entry State Assignment - Set Program Entry State and Details Not Fetched
all_rules.Rule_Description: After clearing all working data on fresh entry, the program must set two specific state flags to indicate that the user is entering the screen for the first time and that no transaction type record has been retrieved from the database yet.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to send the Transaction Type Update screen to the user terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (3100-SCREEN-INIT) is executed as part of the send-map process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen output area (CTRTUPAO) must be cleared to LOW-VALUES, AND the application title lines (TITLE01O, TITLE02O) must be populated from the standard CardDemo title constants (CCDA-TITLE01, CCDA-TITLE02), AND the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) must be placed in the TRNNAMEO field, AND the current program name (LIT-THISPGM) must be placed in the PGMNAMEO field, AND the current system date must be retrieved and formatted as MM/DD/YY and placed in the CURDATEO field, AND the current system time must be retrieved and formatted as HH:MM:SS and placed in the CURTIMEO field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Population - Display Current Date, Time, Program Name and Transaction ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Transaction Type Update screen is sent to the user terminal, the screen header must be populated with the current system date, current system time, the program name, and the transaction ID to provide the user with contextual information about the current session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED (initial state, no record retrieved yet) and the screen variable setup routine is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program determines which values to display on screen based on current state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction type code output field (TRTYPCDO) on the screen must be set to LOW-VALUES (empty), ensuring the user sees a blank field ready for input. The description field is also cleared as part of the overall screen output area initialization to LOW-VALUES performed at the start of screen preparation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initial Screen Field Clearing - Set Transaction Type Fields to Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in the initial 'Details Not Fetched' state, the transaction type code and description fields on the screen must be cleared to empty so the user sees a blank search form.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing the informational message for the screen and the current state is one of: CDEMO-PGM-ENTER (fresh program entry), TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED (no record fetched yet), or TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS (previously entered invalid search criteria)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The information message setup routine (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG) evaluates the current program state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The information message state must be set to PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS, which causes the standard 'prompt for search keys' message text to be centered and displayed in the INFOMSGO field of the screen, and any existing error/return message is displayed in the ERRMSGO field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initial Information Message - Prompt User to Enter Transaction Type Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in its initial state (program entering fresh or details not yet fetched), the informational message area must display a prompt instructing the user to enter a Transaction Type code to perform a search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is setting up screen field attributes and the current state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED (initial state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) executes, first protecting all fields via 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS (setting TRTYPCDA, TRTYDSCA, and INFOMSGA all to protected attribute DFHBMPRF), then evaluating the current state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code input field attribute (TRTYPCDA) must be set to DFHBMFSE (unprotected, with shift-edit), making it editable for user input. The Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCA) remains protected (read-only) as set in the initial protect-all step. The information message field (INFOMSGA) remains protected as set in the initial protect-all step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Field Protection Setup - Make Transaction Type Code Field Editable on Initial Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the initial search screen, the Transaction Type Code field must be made editable so the user can type in a value to search. All other fields start as protected (read-only) and the type code field is then specifically unprotected for input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is setting up screen field attributes and the current state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED (initial state, no record fetched)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) evaluates cursor positioning
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL) must be set to -1, which instructs the CICS terminal handler to position the cursor at the Transaction Type Code input field when the screen is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioning - Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field for Initial Search
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the initial search screen, the cursor must be automatically positioned to the Transaction Type Code input field so the user can immediately begin typing the code to search without needing to manually click or tab to the field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is setting up function key display attributes and the current state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED (initial state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The PF key attribute setup routine (3391-SETUP-PFKEY-ATTRS) evaluates which keys should be highlighted
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F4 Delete key highlight attribute (FKEY04A) must NOT be set to active/bright (DFHBMASB) because the state is neither TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS nor TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, AND the F5 Save key highlight attribute (FKEY05A) must NOT be set to active/bright because the state is neither TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED nor TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, AND the F12 Cancel key highlight attribute (FKEY12A) must NOT be set to active/bright because the state is none of TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, or TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD. The general function key area (FKEYSA) is set to DFHBMASB (bright/active) since the state is not TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Availability - F4 Delete, F5 Save, F12 Cancel Not Active on Initial Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the initial search screen where no record has been fetched yet, the F4 (Delete), F5 (Save/Confirm), and F12 (Cancel) function keys must not be highlighted or made available to the user, as these actions are not applicable until a record is found or a specific operation is in progress.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen output area (CTRTUPAO) has been fully prepared with header information, empty data fields, informational message, field attributes, cursor positioning, and function key attributes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen send routine (3400-SEND-SCREEN) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen map name (LIT-THISMAP) must be stored in CCARD-NEXT-MAP and the mapset name (LIT-THISMAPSET) must be stored in CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET, AND a CICS SEND MAP command must be issued using the map and mapset names, transmitting the prepared CTRTUPAO output area to the terminal, WITH the CURSOR option to position the cursor as specified, WITH the ERASE option to clear any previously displayed screen content, AND WITH the FREEKB option to unlock the terminal keyboard so the user can type

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Initial Screen - Transmit Empty Search Screen Erasing Previous Content
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen fields, attributes, messages, and cursor position have been prepared, the completed screen must be transmitted to the user's terminal, erasing any previously displayed content and unlocking the keyboard so the user can enter input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been successfully sent to the user terminal and the program is ready to suspend execution awaiting user input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The COMMON-RETURN routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current return/error message (WS-RETURN-MSG) must be copied to the screen communication area error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG), AND the main CardDemo communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied into the combined working communication area (WS-COMMAREA), AND the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be appended into WS-COMMAREA immediately after the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA portion (at offset LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1), AND a CICS RETURN command must be issued specifying the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) as the next transaction to invoke, passing the combined WS-COMMAREA as the communication area with its full length, so that all program state is available when the user next interacts with the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session State Preservation - Save Program State and Await Next User Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: After sending the screen to the user, the program must preserve its current state (program flags, communication area data) and return control to CICS, specifying that the same transaction should be re-invoked when the user next presses a key, so the program can resume from where it left off.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record is currently displayed on screen AND the screen is in the 'Confirm Delete' state (user has already pressed F4 once to request deletion and was shown a confirmation prompt)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F4 a second time to confirm the deletion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the delete processing state to 'In Progress' and proceeds to execute the deletion of the Transaction Type record from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Delete Execution on Second F4 Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F4 while the screen is in the Delete Confirmation state, the system initiates the actual deletion process for the displayed Transaction Type record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The delete processing has been initiated AND the original Transaction Type code (TR_TYPE) of the currently displayed record is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the deletion against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system issues a DELETE statement targeting the record WHERE TR_TYPE exactly matches the original Transaction Type code that was fetched and displayed to the user (not any user-modified value)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Execute Deletion of Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system deletes the Transaction Type record from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table using the original Transaction Type code as the exact match key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE operation has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the specified Transaction Type code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database confirms the deletion was successful (no errors returned)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the delete operation as 'Delete Done' AND immediately commits the deletion permanently to the database, making the removal of the Transaction Type record irreversible

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Deletion and Commit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the deletion of a Transaction Type record completes successfully, the system marks the operation as done and permanently commits the deletion to the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE operation has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the specified Transaction Type code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database rejects the deletion because associated child records exist that reference this Transaction Type (referential integrity violation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the record delete as failed AND displays the message 'Please delete associated child records first:' along with the database error details, instructing the user to remove all dependent child records before attempting to delete this Transaction Type record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Block Deletion When Child Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Transaction Type record cannot be deleted because other records in the system reference it (referential integrity), the system informs the user they must first remove all associated dependent records before the Transaction Type can be deleted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE operation has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the specified Transaction Type code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns an error that is not a referential integrity violation (any failure other than child records existing)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the record delete as failed AND sets the screen state to 'Delete Failed' AND displays the message 'Delete failed with message:' along with the database error details to inform the user of the failure reason

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Unexpected Delete Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the deletion of a Transaction Type record fails for any reason other than a referential integrity violation, the system marks the operation as failed and captures the failure details for the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The delete operation has completed with one of the following outcomes: successful deletion, failure due to child records existing, or failure due to another error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the result screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the delete was successful, the screen displays a 'Delete Successful' confirmation message AND the screen state is set to 'Delete Done'; If the delete failed due to child records, the screen displays the child records error message AND the state remains as delete failed; If the delete failed for another reason, the screen displays the failure message AND the screen state is set to 'Delete Failed'; In all cases the updated screen is sent to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Delete Operation Result to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the delete operation completes (whether successful or failed), the system refreshes the screen and displays an appropriate informational message reflecting the outcome of the delete operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is currently viewing a Transaction Type record (program state is SHOW-DETAILS), with the Transaction Type Code and Description displayed on screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F4 (Delete key)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is changed to CONFIRM-DELETE mode, and the screen preparation process is initiated to display the delete confirmation screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Delete Confirmation Mode on F4 Press While Viewing Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses F4 while viewing a Transaction Type record, the program transitions from 'Show Details' state to 'Confirm Delete' state, preventing immediate deletion and requiring explicit user confirmation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state has been set to CONFIRM-DELETE mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen variables are being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The new/edited details are cleared (reset to initial), and the original Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and original Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) as retrieved from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table are populated into the screen output fields (TRTYPCDO and TRTYDSCO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Original Transaction Type Values on Delete Confirmation Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When transitioning to delete confirmation mode, the screen must display the original Transaction Type Code and Description fetched from the database, not any user-modified values, so the user can confirm exactly which record will be deleted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is CONFIRM-DELETE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The informational message area of the screen is being set up
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The information message is set to the Delete Confirmation Prompt text, the message is centered within the available display width, and it is written to the INFOMSGO field of the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Show Delete Confirmation Prompt Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in delete confirmation mode, a specific informational message prompting the user to confirm or cancel the deletion must be displayed, centered on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is CONFIRM-DELETE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen field attributes are being configured
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDA), the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCA), and the Information Message field (INFOMSGA) are all set to protected/read-only mode, preventing any user input or modification

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect All Input Fields in Delete Confirmation Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: During delete confirmation, all input fields on the screen must be set to read-only (protected) so the user cannot accidentally modify the Transaction Type Code or Description while confirming the deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is CONFIRM-DELETE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The function key display attributes are being configured for the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All function key labels (FKEYSA) are set to dark/dimmed (inactive appearance); F4 key label (FKEY04A) is set to bright/highlighted (active appearance) to indicate it is available to confirm the delete; F12 key label (FKEY12A) is set to bright/highlighted (active appearance) to indicate it is available to cancel the delete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable F4 Confirm Delete and F12 Cancel Keys; Dim All Other Keys
all_rules.Rule_Description: During delete confirmation, the available function key options must be restricted: all general function keys are dimmed to indicate they are inactive, while F4 (to confirm delete) and F12 (to cancel) are highlighted as the only valid actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is CONFIRM-DELETE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system validates the key pressed by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: F4 is recognized as a valid key (allowed to proceed with delete confirmation); F12 is recognized as a valid key (allowed to cancel); ENTER key is NOT valid in this state; any other key press is flagged as invalid, and an 'Invalid Key' error message is set and the screen is redisplayed without any processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Allowed Keys During Delete Confirmation State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must enforce that only F4 (confirm delete) and F12 (cancel) are accepted as valid key presses when the screen is in delete confirmation mode. All other keys, including ENTER, must be treated as invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The delete confirmation screen has been fully prepared with original record values, confirmation prompt message, all fields protected, and F4/F12 keys highlighted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is ready to be transmitted to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is sent to the user's terminal using the configured map and mapset, the previous screen content is erased, the keyboard is unlocked for user input, the current program state (CONFIRM-DELETE) and communication data are saved in the communication area, and the program returns control to CICS awaiting the user's next interaction (F4 to confirm delete or F12 to cancel)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Delete Confirmation Screen to User and Await Response
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen content and attributes have been prepared for delete confirmation mode, the fully configured screen is sent to the user's terminal, erasing the previous screen content, and the program returns control to CICS to await the user's next key press.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the current program state is 'Record Not Found' (a previous search returned no matching transaction type)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the F5 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F5 key is recognized as valid and the system proceeds to transition into 'Create New Record' mode. If F5 is pressed in any other state not listed as valid (i.e., not 'Changes OK Not Confirmed', not 'Record Not Found', not 'Delete In Progress'), the key is marked as invalid and an 'Invalid Key' error message is set for display on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: F5 Key Validity Check for New Record Creation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the F5 key press is a valid action when the system is in the 'Record Not Found' state, allowing the user to initiate creation of a new transaction type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen, the current program state is 'Record Not Found', and F5 has been validated as a valid key for this state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the F5 key press in the 'Record Not Found' state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Create New Record' mode, and the screen is prepared and sent to the user to allow entry of new transaction type details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transition to Create New Record Mode on F5
all_rules.Rule_Description: When F5 is pressed and the current state is 'Record Not Found', the program transitions to 'Create New Record' mode, enabling the user to enter details for a new transaction type that does not yet exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the current program state is NOT one of: 'Changes OK Not Confirmed', 'Record Not Found', or 'Delete In Progress'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the F5 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F5 key is marked as invalid, an 'Invalid Key Pressed' indicator is set, and the screen is redisplayed to the user with an invalid key error message without any state change or data processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Invalid Key Message for Unsupported F5 Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When F5 is pressed in a state where it is not a valid action, the system informs the user that the key pressed is not valid for the current screen state and redisplays the screen without making any changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is 'Create New Record' and the screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen variable values for the new record entry form
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field on screen is populated with the value from the new transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) and the Transaction Type Description field is populated with the value from the new transaction type description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User-Entered Values on New Record Entry Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in 'Create New Record' mode, the screen is populated with the new (user-entered) transaction type code and description values so the user can review and complete the entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is 'Create New Record' and the screen information message area is being prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the current program state to determine the appropriate informational message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to 'Prompt For New Data' (PROMPT-FOR-NEWDATA), which instructs the user to enter the new transaction type details. The message is centered in the information message area of the screen (INFOMSGO) and displayed with a bright/highlighted attribute

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Informational Message Prompting New Transaction Type Data Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in 'Create New Record' mode, a specific informational message is displayed on screen to guide the user to enter the details for the new transaction type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is 'Create New Record' and the screen field attributes are being configured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up screen field protection attributes for the new record entry form
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: First, all fields (Transaction Type Code, Transaction Type Description, and Info Message) are set to protected/read-only. Then, the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCA) is set to unprotected with cursor entry enabled (DFHBMFSE - free/stopper/entry), and the Info Message field (INFOMSGA) is set to protected (DFHBMPRF). The cursor is positioned to the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCL set to -1) to guide the user to enter the description

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect Transaction Type Code and Enable Description for New Record Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When in 'Create New Record' mode, the Transaction Type Code field is made editable (unprotected with cursor entry enabled) while the Transaction Type Description field is also made editable, allowing the user to enter the new record's details. All fields start as protected and are selectively unprotected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is 'Create New Record' and the PF key display attributes are being configured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the PF key visual attributes for the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F12 key label on screen (FKEY12A) is set to a bright/highlighted attribute (DFHBMASB), making it visually active and indicating to the user that F12 is available to cancel the new record creation. The general PF keys area (FKEYSA) is also set to bright (DFHBMASB) since the state is not 'Confirm Delete'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable F12 Cancel Key During New Record Creation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in 'Create New Record' mode, the F12 key is highlighted and made visually active on the screen, indicating to the user that they can press F12 to cancel the new record creation and return to the search state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is 'Create New Record', all screen fields have been populated with new values, the informational message has been set to prompt for new data, field protection attributes have been configured with Description field editable, and F12 key has been highlighted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the prepared screen to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type maintenance screen (map CTRTUPAO from mapset LIT-THISMAPSET) is sent to the terminal with: the previous screen erased (ERASE), the keyboard unlocked for user input (FREEKB), and the cursor positioned at the Transaction Type Description field. The next map and mapset are recorded in the communication area for state continuity. The program then returns control to CICS awaiting the next user interaction, preserving the 'Create New Record' state in the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send New Record Entry Screen to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen content, messages, and field attributes have been prepared for the new record creation form, the completed screen is transmitted to the user's terminal, erasing the previous screen content and freeing the keyboard for input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has previously validated and confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record, and the system is about to initiate the save operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The save operation is initiated after the user presses F5 in the 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must populate the database write variables with: (1) the new Transaction Type Code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) moved into DCL-TR-TYPE, (2) the trimmed new Transaction Type Description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) moved into DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT, and (3) the computed length of the description stored in DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN, so that both the type code and description are ready for the database write operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Transaction Type Data for Database Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to save, the system prepares the transaction type code and description by moving the validated user-entered values into the database host variables ready for the SQL operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction type code and description have been prepared in the database host variables (DCL-TR-TYPE and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION), and the system is executing the save operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes an SQL UPDATE statement against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table, setting TR_DESCRIPTION to the new description value where TR_TYPE matches the prepared transaction type code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must capture the SQL result code and evaluate it to determine the outcome: success (SQL code = 0), record not found (SQL code = +100), record locked (SQL code = -911), or other failure (SQL code less than 0), and branch accordingly to the appropriate handling path

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt to Update Existing Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system first attempts an UPDATE operation on the TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the transaction type code as the key. This is the primary save path for modifying an existing transaction type description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement on the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has executed and returned SQL code = 0 (success)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the update was applied successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately issue a database SYNCPOINT (commit) to permanently save the updated Transaction Type Description to the database, making the change durable and visible

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Successfully Updated Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the UPDATE operation succeeds, the changes must be permanently committed to the database to ensure data integrity and visibility to other users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement on the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has returned SQL code = +100, indicating no matching record was found for the transaction type code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects that the record to be updated no longer exists in the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must automatically attempt to INSERT a new record into the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table with both the Transaction Type Code (DCL-TR-TYPE) and Transaction Type Description (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION) as the values for TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION respectively, without requiring any additional user action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert New Transaction Type When Record Does Not Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the UPDATE finds no existing record (the transaction type was deleted by another user between the search and save), the system automatically falls back to inserting a new record rather than failing the operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL INSERT statement into the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has executed and returned SQL code = 0 (success), following a prior UPDATE that found no existing record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the insert was applied successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately issue a database SYNCPOINT (commit) to permanently save the new Transaction Type record to the database, making it durable and visible to other users

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Successfully Inserted Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the INSERT operation succeeds (as a fallback from a failed UPDATE), the new record must be permanently committed to the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The database write operation (either UPDATE or INSERT) has completed successfully and the changes have been committed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the final outcome of the write processing and determines no lock error, no update failure, and no data-changed-before-update condition occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the program state to 'CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE', which causes the screen to display a success confirmation message ('Confirm Update Success') and transition to showing the updated Transaction Type details on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Save as Completed Successfully After Update or Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: After either a successful UPDATE or a successful INSERT, the system transitions to the 'Changes Okayed And Done' state, which triggers a success confirmation message to be displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement on the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has returned SQL code = -911, indicating the record is currently locked by another user or process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the lock conflict during the update attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the INPUT-ERROR flag to true, (2) set the program state to 'CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR', and (3) if no prior error message has been set, set the return message to the predefined 'Could Not Lock Record For Update' message — the screen must then display a failure message informing the user that the record is locked and they should retry the update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Record Locked by Another User During Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the UPDATE operation fails because another user has locked the record, the system must detect this specific condition and inform the user appropriately rather than treating it as a general failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement on the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has returned a negative SQL code other than -911 (i.e., any SQL error code less than 0 except -911)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects a general database failure during the update attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED flag to true, (2) construct an error message containing the literal text 'Error updating: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:' followed by the actual SQL error code and the SQL error message text (SQLERRM), (3) set the program state to 'CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED', and (4) display the failure message on the screen so the user is informed of the specific error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle General Save Failure During Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the UPDATE operation fails for any reason other than record-not-found or record-locked, the system must capture the failure details and inform the user with a descriptive error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL INSERT statement into the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table has returned a non-zero SQL code (any result other than SQL code = 0)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects a database failure during the insert attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED flag to true, (2) construct an error message containing the literal text 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:' followed by the actual SQL error code and the SQL error message text (SQLERRM), (3) set the program state to 'CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED', and (4) display the failure message on the screen so the user is informed of the specific insert error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle General Save Failure During Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the INSERT operation (attempted as a fallback after UPDATE found no record) fails for any reason, the system must capture the failure details and inform the user with a descriptive error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The save operation has completed successfully and the program state is 'CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the post-save state transition in the action decision logic (2000-DECIDE-ACTION)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the program state to 'SHOW-DETAILS' to display the saved record, and (2) if no calling transaction ID exists (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID is LOW-VALUES or SPACES), clear the account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zeroes, clear the card number (CDEMO-CARD-NUM) to zeroes, and clear the account status (CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS) to LOW-VALUES — the screen must then display the updated Transaction Type Code and Description as the current record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Screen Showing Updated Transaction Type Details After Success
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful save (update or insert), the program transitions back to the detail display state, showing the saved transaction type values and clearing any prior account context if no calling transaction exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The save operation has failed due to a record lock (SQL code = -911) and the program state has been set to 'CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the final outcome state in the write processing evaluation block
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the program state to 'CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR', which causes the screen information message to display 'Inform Failure' — the user is shown the lock error message and the screen remains in a state where the user can retry the save operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Screen Prompting User to Retry After Lock Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a lock error during save, the program transitions to the lock-error state, which causes the screen to display a failure/retry message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The save operation has failed due to a database error (non-lock, non-zero SQL code) during either the UPDATE or INSERT attempt, and the TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED flag has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the final outcome state in the write processing evaluation block
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the program state to 'CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED', which causes the screen information message to display 'Inform Failure' — the user is shown the specific error message constructed from the SQL error code and SQL error message text, and the screen remains in a state indicating the save did not complete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Screen Showing Error Message After Save Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a general save failure (either during UPDATE or INSERT), the program transitions to the failed state, which causes the screen to display the specific database error message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and presses F12
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the current screen state against the allowed states for F12: Changes Confirmed Awaiting Save (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), Viewing Record Details (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS), Record Not Found (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND), Delete Confirmation Pending (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE), or Creating New Record (TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current state matches any of the above, F12 is marked as a valid key press and processing continues. If the current state does not match any of the above, F12 is marked as an invalid key press and an 'Invalid Key' error condition is set, causing the screen to be redisplayed with an invalid key message without performing any action.

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Key Validity Check for Cancel Action
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the F12 key press is permitted based on the current screen state. F12 is only a valid action when the user is in specific states: changes confirmed awaiting save, viewing record details, record not found, delete confirmation pending, or creating a new record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in the Delete Confirmation state (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE), meaning a record is displayed and the user was prompted to confirm deletion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F12 and the Transaction Type code filter is not valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID is false) during the action decision evaluation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The delete action is cancelled (WS-DELETE-WAS-CANCELLED is set to TRUE), the screen state is reset to initial search state (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is set to TRUE), and the screen is redisplayed with an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code.

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Cancel During Delete Confirmation - Reset to Initial Search State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F12 while the screen is in Delete Confirmation state, the pending delete action is cancelled, the delete is marked as cancelled, and the screen resets to the initial search state prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in the Changes Confirmed Awaiting Save state (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), meaning the user had entered changes that passed validation and was prompted to confirm saving
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F12 and the Transaction Type code filter is not valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID is false) during the action decision evaluation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The update action is cancelled (WS-UPDATE-WAS-CANCELLED is set to TRUE), the screen state is set to Changes Backed Out (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT is set to TRUE), and processing continues to determine what to display based on whether original record values were previously fetched.

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Cancel During Pending Update Confirmation - Back Out Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F12 while changes have been validated and are awaiting save confirmation, the pending update is cancelled, the update is marked as cancelled, and the screen transitions to the Changes Backed Out state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed F12 to cancel a pending update, the screen state is now Changes Backed Out (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT), and original record values were previously fetched from the database (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE is NOT equal to LOW-VALUES and NOT equal to SPACES)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen variables for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The new/edited details are cleared (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS is initialized), the original Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE) is displayed in the Transaction Type Code field, the original Transaction Type Description (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) is displayed in the Description field, the non-key flags are cleared (WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS set to LOW-VALUES), and the screen prompts the user to make changes (PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES message is displayed).

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Cancel with Original Data Available - Display Original Record Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: After cancelling a pending update via F12, if original record values were previously fetched from the database, the screen displays the original (pre-edit) Transaction Type Code and Description, and prompts the user to make changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed F12 to cancel a pending update, the screen state is now Changes Backed Out (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT), and no original record values were previously fetched (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE equals LOW-VALUES or SPACES)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen variables and informational message for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state transitions to prompt for search keys (PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS message is set), the Transaction Type Code field is displayed as empty (LOW-VALUES), and the user is prompted to enter a Transaction Type code to search.

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Cancel with No Original Data - Display Empty Search Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After cancelling a pending update via F12, if no original record values were previously fetched (the record was never retrieved from the database), the screen displays an empty search screen and prompts the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in the Show Details state (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS), meaning a Transaction Type record is currently displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F12, the system sets FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE to TRUE and calls the action decision routine (2000-DECIDE-ACTION), which then re-fetches the record from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the current Transaction Type code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the record is found in the database, the screen state is set to Show Details (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS) and the original record values are displayed. If the record is not found, the screen state is set to Details Not Found (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND) and the user is prompted to create a new record.

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Cancel While Viewing Record Details - Reset to Initial Search State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F12 while viewing a record's details, the current view is cancelled and the screen re-fetches the record from the database and redisplays it, or resets to initial search state based on the action decision logic.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in the Create New Record state (TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD), meaning the user had initiated creation of a new Transaction Type after a not-found search result
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F12, which is validated as a valid key for this state, and the main action router evaluates the F12 press with the Create New Record state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state is reset to initial entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is set to TRUE and TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is set to TRUE), the program state and miscellaneous storage are re-initialized, and the screen is redisplayed as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code.

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Cancel While Creating New Record - Reset to Initial Search State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F12 while in the Create New Record mode, the creation is cancelled and the screen resets to the initial search state, discarding any data entered for the new record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in the Details Not Found state (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND), meaning a previous search returned no matching Transaction Type record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F12, which is validated as a valid key for this state, and the main action router evaluates the F12 press with the Details Not Found state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen state is reset to initial entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is set to TRUE and TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is set to TRUE), the program state and miscellaneous storage are re-initialized, and the screen is redisplayed as an empty search screen prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code.

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Cancel While Record Not Found - Reset to Initial Search State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F12 while the screen shows a Record Not Found result, the not-found state is cancelled and the screen resets to the initial search state, allowing the user to search for a different Transaction Type code.
