Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state has been reset to initial search state (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is TRUE) as a result of a F12 cancel action
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the informational message for the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to 'Prompt for Search Keys' (PROMPT-FOR-SEARCH-KEYS is set to TRUE), the message is centered and displayed in the information message area of the screen (INFOMSGO field of CTRTUPAO), the Transaction Type Code field is made editable (DFHBMFSE attribute set on TRTYPCDA), and the cursor is positioned to the Transaction Type Code field (length set to -1 on TRTYPCDL).

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prompt User to Enter Transaction Type Code After Cancel
all_rules.Rule_Description: After any F12 cancel action that results in the initial search state, the screen displays a prompt instructing the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen state is Changes Backed Out (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT) and original record values are available (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE is not LOW-VALUES and not SPACES)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the informational message for the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to 'Prompt for Changes' (PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES is set to TRUE), the message is centered and displayed in the information message area of the screen (INFOMSGO field of CTRTUPAO), both the Transaction Type Code field and Description field are made editable (DFHBMFSE attribute set on TRTYDSCA via 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS), and the cursor is positioned to the Description field (length set to -1 on TRTYDSCL).

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prompt User to Make Changes After Backed-Out Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After cancelling a pending update via F12 when original data exists, the screen prompts the user to make changes to the displayed original record values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The F12 cancel action has been fully processed, the appropriate screen state has been set, screen variables and informational messages have been prepared, and field protection attributes and cursor position have been configured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the refreshed screen to the terminal and returns control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is sent to the terminal with ERASE and FREEKB options (clearing the screen and unlocking the keyboard), the current error or return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) is copied to the screen error message area (CCARD-ERROR-MSG), the full program state (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is saved into the communication area (WS-COMMAREA), and CICS RETURN is issued with the current transaction ID and the communication area so the program resumes correctly on the next user interaction.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Refresh and Return After F12 Cancel
all_rules.Rule_Description: After processing the F12 cancel action and setting up the appropriate screen state, the screen is sent to the terminal and the program returns control to CICS, preserving the current state in the communication area for the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and presses any key (ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, PF1 through PF12, or PF13 through PF24)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the terminal key press event (EIBAID value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system maps the key to exactly one internal indicator flag: ENTER maps to CCARD-AID-ENTER, CLEAR maps to CCARD-AID-CLEAR, PA1 maps to CCARD-AID-PA1, PA2 maps to CCARD-AID-PA2, PF1/PF13 map to CCARD-AID-PFK01, PF2/PF14 map to CCARD-AID-PFK02, PF3/PF15 map to CCARD-AID-PFK03, PF4/PF16 map to CCARD-AID-PFK04, PF5/PF17 map to CCARD-AID-PFK05, PF6/PF18 map to CCARD-AID-PFK06, PF7/PF19 map to CCARD-AID-PFK07, PF8/PF20 map to CCARD-AID-PFK08, PF9/PF21 map to CCARD-AID-PFK09, PF10/PF22 map to CCARD-AID-PFK10, PF11/PF23 map to CCARD-AID-PFK11, PF12/PF24 map to CCARD-AID-PFK12. Shifted PF keys (PF13-PF24) are treated identically to their base equivalents (PF1-PF12).

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Terminal Key Press to Internal Key Indicator
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses any function key or action key on the terminal, the system identifies and maps the physical key press to an internal key indicator flag that the program can evaluate for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Update screen in any given state (Details Not Fetched, Show Details, Confirm Delete, Details Not Found, Changes OK Not Confirmed, Create New Record, Delete In Progress, etc.) and a key press has been mapped to an internal indicator
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the pressed key against the current screen state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is considered VALID only under these specific combinations: (1) PF3 is always valid regardless of state; (2) ENTER is valid in any state EXCEPT when the current state is Confirm Delete; (3) PF4 is valid only when the current state is Show Details OR Confirm Delete; (4) PF5 is valid only when the current state is Changes OK Not Confirmed, OR Details Not Found, OR Delete In Progress; (5) PF12 is valid only when the current state is Changes OK Not Confirmed, OR Show Details, OR Details Not Found, OR Confirm Delete, OR Create New Record. Any key press that does not match one of these valid combinations is considered INVALID.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Function Key Against Current Screen State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system enforces that only contextually appropriate function keys are accepted based on the current screen state. Keys that are not valid for the current state are rejected to prevent unintended operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key that is not valid for the current screen state on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key validation check determines the key is not in the list of valid key-state combinations
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the PFK-INVALID flag to TRUE, and if no return message is currently set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE), the system additionally sets the WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED flag to TRUE to indicate an invalid key was pressed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Key as Invalid and Set Invalid Key Pressed Flag
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a key press is determined to be invalid for the current screen state, the system marks the key as invalid and sets a flag to trigger the invalid key message flow, ensuring the user receives feedback about the inappropriate key press.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED flag has been set to TRUE because the user pressed a key not valid for the current screen state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the invalid key condition in the main action router (EVALUATE TRUE block in 0000-MAIN)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes directly to the screen send routine (3000-SEND-MAP) without performing any input processing, database access, or state changes. The WS-RETURN-MSG field (which was set when WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED was flagged) is carried forward as the error message to be displayed in the ERRMSGO field on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Invalid Key Error Message for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an invalid key is pressed, the system prepares an appropriate error message to inform the user that the key they pressed is not valid in the current context, without altering any data or screen state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has identified an invalid key press and is preparing to redisplay the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The WHEN WS-INVALID-KEY-PRESSED branch is taken in the main action router
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs ONLY the screen send routine (3000-SEND-MAP) and then goes directly to COMMON-RETURN. No input processing (1000-PROCESS-INPUTS) is performed, no action decision logic (2000-DECIDE-ACTION) is executed, no database reads or writes occur, and all current state flags (TTUP-* states, CDEMO-* flags) remain unchanged from their values before the key was pressed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Current Screen State on Invalid Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an invalid key is pressed, the system must not alter the current program state, screen data, or perform any database operations. All existing state flags and data values are preserved exactly as they were before the invalid key was pressed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redisplay the Transaction Type Update screen after an invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (3100-SCREEN-INIT) is executed as part of the screen send process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen output area (CTRTUPAO) is cleared to LOW-VALUES, then populated with: (1) Application title lines from CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 in TITLE01O and TITLE02O fields; (2) The current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) in the TRNNAMEO field; (3) The current program name (LIT-THISPGM) in the PGMNAMEO field; (4) The current system date formatted as MM/DD/YY in the CURDATEO field; (5) The current system time formatted as HH:MM:SS in the CURTIMEO field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Screen Header with Current Date, Time and Program Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system refreshes the screen header area with the current system date, current system time, transaction ID, and program name to ensure the header information is always current and accurate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating screen fields for redisplay after an invalid key press, and the current screen state is unchanged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen variable setup routine (3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen fields are populated based on the current state as follows: (1) If state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED: Transaction Type Code (TRTYPCDO) and description fields are set to LOW-VALUES (blank); (2) If state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, TTUP-DELETE-FAILED, TTUP-DELETE-DONE, or TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT: TTUP-NEW-DETAILS is initialized and the ORIGINAL database values are displayed — TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE is moved to TRTYPCDO and TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC is moved to TRTYDSCO; (3) If state is TTUP-CHANGES-MADE, TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, or TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE: the NEW (user-entered) values are displayed — TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE is moved to TRTYPCDO and TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC is moved to TRTYDSCO; (4) If the program is in initial entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER): no field population is performed (CONTINUE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Fields with Existing Data Values Based on Unchanged State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system populates the screen data fields using the existing data values appropriate to the current (unchanged) screen state, ensuring the user sees the same data they were working with before pressing the invalid key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is setting up messages for screen redisplay after an invalid key press, with the current screen state unchanged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The information message setup routine (3250-SETUP-INFOMSG) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message (INFOMSGO) is determined by the current (unchanged) state: if state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED or TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, the message prompts for search keys; if state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, the message prompts to create a new record; if state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS or TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT with no old type data, the message prompts for search keys; if state is TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT or TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, the message prompts for changes; if state is TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, the message prompts for delete confirmation; if state is TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, the message prompts for new data entry; if state is TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, the message prompts for confirmation; if state is TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, the message confirms update success. The informational message is centered in the display field. Additionally, the WS-RETURN-MSG (containing the invalid key error text) is moved to ERRMSGO to display the error reason to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Informational Message on Screen for Invalid Key Redisplay
all_rules.Rule_Description: When redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system sets both the informational guidance message (centered) and the error message area to provide the user with context about what action is expected and what went wrong.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is setting field attributes for screen redisplay after an invalid key press, with the current screen state unchanged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields are first set to protected (DFHBMPRF applied to TRTYPCDA, TRTYDSCA, and INFOMSGA). Then based on the current state: (1) If state is TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, or TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT with no old type data: the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDA) is set to unprotected with cursor (DFHBMFSE); (2) If state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, or TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT with old data: the Description field (TRTYDSCA) is set to unprotected with cursor (DFHBMFSE) and the info message field remains protected (DFHBMPRF); (3) If state is TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, or TTUP-DELETE-IN-PROGRESS: all fields remain protected (no change). Additionally, if the Transaction Type filter flag is invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK) or delete has failed (TTUP-DELETE-FAILED), the Transaction Type Code field color is set to RED (DFHRED). If the filter is blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK) and the program is in re-entry mode, the Transaction Type Code field displays '*' and is colored RED

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Screen Field Protection Attributes Based on Unchanged Current State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system applies the same field protection rules as would normally apply for the current (unchanged) state, ensuring fields remain editable or protected exactly as they were before the invalid key was pressed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is finalizing screen attributes for redisplay after an invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The informational message attribute setup routine (3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current state has no informational message to display (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is TRUE), the informational message field attribute (INFOMSGA) is set to dark/non-display (DFHBMDAR); otherwise, if there is an informational message to display, the informational message field attribute is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Informational Message Display Attributes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system controls the visual display attribute of the informational message area to distinguish between states where no guidance message is needed versus states where an active guidance message should be prominently displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is setting function key display attributes for screen redisplay after an invalid key press, with the current screen state unchanged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The function key attribute setup routine (3391-SETUP-PFKEY-ATTRS) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following function key visibility rules are applied: (1) If the current state is TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE: the general function keys area (FKEYSA) is set to dark/dimmed (DFHBMDAR); otherwise FKEYSA is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB); (2) If the current state is TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS OR TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE: the PF4 key indicator (FKEY04A) is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB); (3) If the current state is TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED OR TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND: the PF5 key indicator (FKEY05A) is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB); (4) If the current state is TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, OR TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, OR TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, OR TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, OR TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD: the PF12 key indicator (FKEY12A) is set to bright/highlighted (DFHBMASB). Keys not meeting these conditions remain at their default (non-highlighted) state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Available Function Key Indicators Based on Unchanged Current State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When redisplaying the screen after an invalid key press, the system highlights only the function keys that are valid and available for the current (unchanged) screen state, providing clear visual guidance to the user about which keys they can legitimately press.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed all screen preparation steps (header initialization, field population, message setup, attribute setting) following an invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen send routine (3400-SEND-SCREEN) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the screen map (identified by LIT-THISMAP within LIT-THISMAPSET) with the fully populated output area (CTRTUPAO) to the user's terminal. The screen is sent with CURSOR positioning (cursor placed at the field designated during attribute setup), ERASE (previous screen content is cleared), and FREEKB (keyboard is unlocked for the next user input). The next map and mapset names are set to LIT-THISMAP and LIT-THISMAPSET respectively in the communication area before sending

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Redisplayed Screen Back to User After Invalid Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: After preparing all screen content, messages, and field attributes following an invalid key press, the system transmits the fully prepared screen back to the user's terminal, erasing the previous screen content and displaying the refreshed screen with the invalid key error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been sent back to the user with the invalid key error message and unchanged data after an invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The COMMON-RETURN routine is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies WS-RETURN-MSG to CCARD-ERROR-MSG, assembles the full communication area by combining CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA into WS-COMMAREA, and returns control to CICS specifying the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) as the next transaction to invoke, passing the assembled WS-COMMAREA as the communication data. This ensures the program state (including all TTUP-* state flags and data values) is preserved for the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to CICS Preserving State for Next Interaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After sending the screen back to the user following an invalid key press, the system returns control to CICS while preserving the complete current program state in the communication area, so that when the user presses the next key, the program can resume with full context of the previous interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and has entered values in the transaction type code and/or description fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the screen input from the Transaction Type Update map (CTRTUPAI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction type code (TRTYPCDI) and description (TRTYDSCI) entered by the user are captured into working storage for further validation and processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive Screen Input for Transaction Type Maintenance
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system captures the transaction type code and description entered by the user from the Transaction Type Update screen into working storage for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current program state is 'Record Not Found' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND), PF5 was NOT pressed, and the trimmed value of the transaction type code entered on screen equals the previously searched transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to store the newly received screen input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips storing the screen input and exits the store-input step without updating working storage, preserving the existing search context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Storing Input When Same Code Re-entered in Not-Found State Without PF5
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system is in 'Record Not Found' state, the user has not pressed PF5, and the same transaction type code is re-entered, the system skips re-storing the input to preserve the existing search context and avoids redundant processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has received screen input and the skip-store condition is not met
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the transaction type code from the screen field TRTYPCDI of CTRTUPAI
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered code is an asterisk ('*') or spaces, the transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) is set to LOW-VALUES (blank); otherwise, the trimmed value of the entered code is stored in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Transaction Type Code from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system stores the user-entered transaction type code from the screen into the new-details working storage area, treating asterisk or spaces as blank (low-values).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has received screen input and the skip-store condition is not met
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the transaction type description from the screen field TRTYDSCI of CTRTUPAI
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered description is an asterisk ('*') or spaces, the transaction type description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) is set to LOW-VALUES (blank); otherwise, the trimmed value of the entered description is stored in TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Transaction Type Description from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system stores the user-entered transaction type description from the screen into the new-details working storage area, treating asterisk or spaces as blank (low-values).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current program state is either 'Create New Record' (TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD) or 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to perform transaction type code validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips the transaction type code validation entirely and proceeds directly to the compare old-versus-new values step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Transaction Type Code Validation When Creating New Record or Changes Pending Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in 'Create New Record' state or 'Changes Pending Confirmation' state, the transaction type code has already been validated in a prior step, so the system bypasses the type code validation and proceeds directly to comparing old and new values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is performing transaction type code validation and the current state is not 'Create New Record' or 'Changes Pending Confirmation'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) is evaluated and found to be LOW-VALUES, spaces, or has a trimmed length of zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state, marks the transaction type code flag as blank (FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK), and sets the error message to 'Tran Type code must be supplied.'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction type code is a mandatory field. If the user leaves it blank or empty, the system raises a validation error and prompts the user to supply the value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction type code has been supplied (is not blank) and the system is performing numeric validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system tests the transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, up to 2 characters) using FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL and the result is not zero (i.e., the value is not numeric)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state, marks the transaction type code flag as not-ok (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), and sets the error message to 'Tran Type code must be numeric.'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction type code must contain only numeric digits. If the entered value contains non-numeric characters, the system raises a validation error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction type code has been supplied and confirmed to be numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the numeric value of the transaction type code using FUNCTION NUMVAL and the result equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state, marks the transaction type code flag as not-ok (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), and sets the error message to 'Tran Type code must not be zero.'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Not Be Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction type code must be a non-zero numeric value. A value of zero is not a valid transaction type code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction type code has passed all validations (non-blank, numeric, non-zero) and the filter flag is set to valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the transaction type code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system computes the numeric value of the code using FUNCTION NUMVAL, moves it to a 2-character alphanumeric field, replaces all spaces with zeros using INSPECT, and stores the zero-padded result back into TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Valid Transaction Type Code with Leading Zeros
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a transaction type code passes all validations, the system formats it by converting the numeric value and replacing any spaces with zeros to ensure consistent 2-digit zero-padded representation (e.g., '5' becomes '05').

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction type code validation has completed and the code was found to be blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the transaction type code validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Search Criteria Received' message (if no prior error message exists), sets the program state to 'Details Not Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED), and exits the input editing step, returning the user to the search prompt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to No Search Criteria Error When Code Is Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the transaction type code validation results in a blank code, the system sets the program state to indicate no search criteria was received and resets to the search prompt state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction type code validation has completed and the code was found to be invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is set, meaning non-numeric or zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the outcome of the transaction type code validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the program state to 'Invalid Search Keys' (TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS), sets the program state to 'Details Not Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED), and exits the input editing step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Invalid Search Keys Error When Code Is Invalid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the transaction type code validation results in an invalid (non-numeric or zero) code, the system sets the program state to 'Invalid Search Keys' and resets to the search prompt state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction type code has passed validation and the filter flag is valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID), but the program state is still 'Details Not Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the record has already been fetched from the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips all further input validation (including description validation and old-versus-new comparison) and exits the input editing step to proceed to the database lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Description Validation When Record Has Not Yet Been Fetched
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the transaction type code is valid but the corresponding record has not yet been retrieved from the database, the system skips description validation and proceeds to the database lookup step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction type record has previously been fetched from the database and the original values (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE and TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) are available in working storage
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the new transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) and new description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) against the original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The comparison is performed case-insensitively (using FUNCTION UPPER-CASE) and with leading/trailing spaces trimmed (using FUNCTION TRIM) on both the type code and description; additionally the trimmed lengths of both descriptions must match for the values to be considered unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare New Values Against Original Fetched Values for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a record has been fetched from the database, the system compares the user's newly entered transaction type code and description against the original values retrieved from the database to determine whether any changes have been made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has compared the new and original transaction type code and description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The upper-cased trimmed new transaction type code equals the upper-cased trimmed original type code AND the upper-cased trimmed new description equals the upper-cased trimmed original description AND the trimmed lengths of both descriptions are equal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Changes Detected' flag (NO-CHANGES-DETECTED) if no prior error message exists, clears non-key flags (WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS to LOW-VALUES), and exits the input editing step without proceeding to description validation or save

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Changes Detected Between New and Original Values
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user's entered values are identical to the original database values (case-insensitive, trimmed), the system notifies the user that no changes were made and does not proceed to save.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Changes have been detected between the new and original values and the system is validating the transaction description field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, up to 50 characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction description is evaluated and found to be LOW-VALUES, spaces, or has a trimmed length of zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state (INPUT-ERROR), marks the description flag as blank (FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK), and sets the error message to 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Description Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction type description is a mandatory field when changes have been detected. If the description is blank or empty, the system raises a validation error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction description has been supplied (is not blank) and the system is performing character-type validation on the description field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, up to 50 characters)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system inspects the description by converting all valid alphanumeric characters (LIT-ALL-ALPHANUM-FROM) to spaces (LIT-ALPHANUM-SPACES-TO) and checks whether any non-alphanumeric characters remain (trimmed length is not zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If non-alphanumeric characters are found, the system sets the input to an error state (INPUT-ERROR), marks the description flag as not-ok (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), and sets the error message to 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Description Must Contain Only Alphanumeric Characters
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction type description must contain only letters and numbers. Special characters are not permitted. The description is validated up to 50 characters in length.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Changes have been detected between new and original values, and the transaction description has passed all validation checks (non-blank and alphanumeric characters only)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The description validation completes successfully with no input errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the program state to 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), indicating the changes are validated and awaiting explicit user confirmation before being saved to the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Changes Ready for User Confirmation After Successful Description Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the transaction description passes all validation checks (non-blank and alphanumeric only), the system advances the program state to indicate that the changes are valid and ready for the user to confirm before saving.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered data on the Transaction Type Update screen and submitted the screen (pressed a key such as ENTER or a PF key)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the screen input from the Transaction Type Update screen map (CTRTUPAI) using the defined map set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All field values entered by the user are captured from the screen and held in memory (CTRTUPAI) ready for further processing, including the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDI) and the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCI)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept User-Submitted Transaction Type Update Screen Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the Transaction Type Update screen, the system must accept and capture all field values entered by the user from the screen map into memory for further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Type Update screen with a value entered in the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDI)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the screen map input from the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field value (TRTYPCDI), up to 2 characters in length, is captured from the screen map (CTRTUPAI) and held in memory for subsequent validation and processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Transaction Type Code Field from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system captures the Transaction Type Code field value entered by the user on the Transaction Type Update screen. This field accepts up to 2 characters and is the primary key used to identify or search for a transaction type record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Type Update screen with a value entered in the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCI)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the screen map input from the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Description field value (TRTYDSCI), up to 50 characters in length, is captured from the screen map (CTRTUPAI) and held in memory for subsequent validation and processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Transaction Type Description Field from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system captures the Transaction Type Description field value entered by the user on the Transaction Type Update screen. This field accepts up to 50 characters and holds the descriptive text associated with a transaction type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully received the screen map input from the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Both the Transaction Type Code (TRTYPCDI) and Transaction Type Description (TRTYDSCI) field values have been captured from the screen into memory (CTRTUPAI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All captured screen field values are held in memory and the process proceeds to the next step of storing the screen input values for validation and business logic processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Input Values Ready for Further Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the system successfully receives all screen field values from the Transaction Type Update screen, the captured data (Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description) is available in memory and the process proceeds to store and validate the input values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is in 'Record Not Found' state (a previous search returned no matching Transaction Type), AND the user has NOT pressed PF5 (Save/Create), AND the Transaction Type Code currently entered on screen (after trimming) is identical to the Transaction Type Code already stored in working storage from the previous search
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to store screen input values into working variables
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips all input storage processing and exits immediately without modifying any working storage variables, preserving the existing search context unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Re-Storing Input When Search Context Is Unchanged
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user is in a 'Record Not Found' state and has not pressed PF5 (Save/Create), and the Transaction Type Code entered on screen matches the value already stored from the previous search, the system skips re-processing the screen inputs to preserve the existing search context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that screen input must be stored (the skip condition was not met), AND there are working storage variables holding new Transaction Type details (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS) that may contain values from a prior screen interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to store the current screen input into working variables
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears and resets the entire new details storage area (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS) to its initial empty state before storing any new values, ensuring a clean slate for the current input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset New Details Storage Before Storing Fresh Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before storing any new screen input values into working variables, the system clears and resets the entire new details storage area to ensure no residual data from a previous interaction contaminates the current input processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is storing screen input into working variables, AND the Transaction Type Code field on the screen contains either an asterisk character ('*') or only space characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Type Code field value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stores an empty value (LOW-VALUES) for the Transaction Type Code in working storage (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE), treating the asterisk or spaces as a signal that no Transaction Type Code was provided

all_rules.Rule_Name: Treat Asterisk or Spaces as Empty Transaction Type Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters an asterisk ('*') or spaces in the Transaction Type Code field, the system interprets this as an intentionally blank or cleared entry and stores an empty value internally, rather than treating the literal character as a valid code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is storing screen input into working variables, AND the Transaction Type Code field on the screen contains a value that is neither an asterisk ('*') nor spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Type Code field value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system trims leading and trailing spaces from the entered Transaction Type Code and stores the resulting trimmed value into the Transaction Type Code working storage variable (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Trimmed Transaction Type Code from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a valid (non-asterisk, non-space) Transaction Type Code on the screen, the system stores the value with leading and trailing spaces removed into the working storage variable for subsequent validation and processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is storing screen input into working variables, AND the Transaction Description field on the screen contains either an asterisk character ('*') or only space characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Description field value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stores an empty value (LOW-VALUES) for the Transaction Description in working storage (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC), treating the asterisk or spaces as a signal that no description was provided

all_rules.Rule_Name: Treat Asterisk or Spaces as Empty Transaction Description
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters an asterisk ('*') or spaces in the Transaction Description field, the system interprets this as an intentionally blank or cleared entry and stores an empty value internally, rather than treating the literal character as a valid description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is storing screen input into working variables, AND the Transaction Description field on the screen contains a value that is neither an asterisk ('*') nor spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Transaction Description field value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system trims leading and trailing spaces from the entered Transaction Description and stores the resulting trimmed value into the Transaction Description working storage variable (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Trimmed Transaction Description from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a valid (non-asterisk, non-space) Transaction Description on the screen, the system stores the value with leading and trailing spaces removed into the working storage variable for subsequent validation and processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and has submitted the form with a Transaction Type Code field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field is blank, contains only spaces, contains only LOW-VALUES, or has a trimmed length of zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Validation fails, an input error is flagged, the Transaction Type Code is marked as blank/invalid, and the error message 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' is set for display on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code field is not left blank or empty before any further validation is performed. This ensures users always provide a value to search or create a transaction type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code contains any non-numeric characters (i.e., it fails the numeric test)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Validation fails, an input error is flagged, the Transaction Type Code is marked as invalid, and the error message 'Tran Type code must be numeric.' is set for display on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code contains only numeric digits. Non-numeric characters such as letters or special characters are not permitted in the Transaction Type Code field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank, numeric Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the Transaction Type Code evaluates to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Validation fails, an input error is flagged, the Transaction Type Code is marked as invalid, and the error message 'Tran Type code must not be zero.' is set for display on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Not Be Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code, after confirming it is numeric, does not have a value of zero. A Transaction Type Code of zero is not a valid business identifier.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a Transaction Type Code that is non-blank, purely numeric, and non-zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All three validation checks (blank check, numeric check, zero check) have passed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code validation status is set to valid, allowing the system to proceed with formatting and database lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Marked as Valid After Passing All Checks
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the Transaction Type Code passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, non-zero), it is formally marked as valid so that downstream processing can proceed with confidence.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type Code has passed all validation checks and is marked as valid
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the validated Transaction Type Code for use
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The numeric value of the code is computed, any spaces within the 2-character field are replaced with zeros to produce a zero-padded result (e.g., '5 ' becomes '05'), and the formatted value is stored back as the Transaction Type Code for use in database operations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Leading Zero Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a Transaction Type Code passes all validations, it is standardized to a 2-digit format by converting it to its numeric value and replacing any leading spaces with zeros. This ensures consistent storage and lookup (e.g., entering '5' is treated the same as '05').

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Transaction Type Code field on the Transaction Type maintenance screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates validation of the Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The validation is applied to exactly 2 characters of the input field, the field is initially marked as not valid, the field label 'Tran Type code' is set for use in any error messages, and the input value is prepared for the blank, numeric, and zero checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Maximum Length Constraint
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Code is defined as a 2-character field. All validation checks are applied only to the first 2 characters of the input, enforcing the maximum allowable length for this business identifier.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered or modified a Transaction Type record and the system is validating the Transaction Description field (labeled 'Transaction Desc') with a maximum allowed length of 50 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Description value is entirely blank spaces, contains only low-value (null) characters, or has a trimmed length of zero — meaning no meaningful content has been provided
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Validation fails; the Transaction Description field is flagged as blank; an error message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' is generated and stored as the return message; the overall input is marked as invalid; and processing of the description validation exits immediately without performing the alphanumeric character check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Description Mandatory Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Transaction Description field is not left blank or empty when a user attempts to save a new or updated Transaction Type record. The description must contain at least one non-space character.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field has passed the mandatory (non-blank) check and contains at least one non-space character, and the system proceeds to validate the character content of the description against the allowed alphanumeric character set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system converts all valid alphanumeric characters in the description to spaces and then checks whether any non-space characters remain — if non-space characters remain after conversion, it means the description contains at least one invalid (non-alphanumeric) character
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If invalid characters are found: validation fails; the Transaction Description field is flagged as invalid (not-ok); an error message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' is generated and stored as the return message; the overall input is marked as invalid; and validation exits immediately. If no invalid characters are found: the Transaction Description is marked as valid and processing continues

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Description Alphanumeric Character Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that the Transaction Description contains only valid alphanumeric characters (letters A–Z, a–z, and digits 0–9). Any special characters, punctuation, or symbols are not permitted in the Transaction Description field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is entering or updating a Transaction Type Description and the system is preparing to validate the description content
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the maximum validation length to 50 characters and performs all character-level checks (blank check and alphanumeric check) strictly within the first 50 characters of the description field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Only the first 50 characters of the Transaction Description are evaluated during validation; any content beyond 50 characters is outside the validated boundary, effectively enforcing the 50-character maximum length constraint on the Transaction Description

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Description Maximum Length Enforcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Enforces that the Transaction Description does not exceed the maximum allowed length of 50 characters. The validation operates on only the first 50 characters of the description field, effectively enforcing the 50-character limit by design of the field boundary used during validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted changes to a Transaction Type record (the record is in 'Show Details' state with detected changes), and the Transaction Type Code has already been validated successfully, and the system is now ready to validate the Transaction Description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system pre-marks the change state as 'Changes Not OK', assigns the field label 'Transaction Desc', copies the user-entered description into the validation work area, sets the maximum validation length to 50 characters, and invokes the alphanumeric validation routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The validation routine is executed against the Transaction Description with a 50-character limit; the resulting validation flags are stored back into the description-specific flag area for use in screen attribute setup and error display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Description Validation Invocation and Field Setup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the process by which the Transaction Description validation is triggered during input editing. Before invoking the validation routine, the system pre-sets the state to 'Changes Not OK' as a default, then passes the description value and its maximum length (50) to the validation routine. This ensures that validation failure is the default outcome unless the validation routine explicitly marks the input as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Description has been validated and no input errors were detected — meaning the description is non-blank, contains only alphanumeric characters, and is within the 50-character limit
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation routine completes without setting the input-error flag
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), indicating that the user's changes are valid and the screen should prompt the user to press PF5 to confirm and save the changes, or PF12 to cancel

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Transaction Description Changes as Valid and Ready for User Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Transaction Description passes all validation checks (non-blank and alphanumeric-only), the system transitions the record state to indicate that the proposed changes are valid and are now awaiting explicit user confirmation before being saved to the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has invoked the Transaction Description validation routine and the validation has detected an error — either the description is blank/empty or it contains characters that are not letters or numbers
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The validation routine sets the input-error flag (INPUT-ERROR) due to a blank description or invalid characters in the description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Changes Not OK' (TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), which was pre-set before validation was invoked; the corresponding error message ('Transaction Desc must be supplied.' or 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.') is retained as the screen error message; and the screen is redisplayed to the user with the error highlighted so the user can correct the Transaction Description

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Transaction Description Input as Invalid and Prompt User to Correct
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Description fails any validation check (blank/empty or contains non-alphanumeric characters), the system marks the overall input state as invalid and retains the 'Changes Not OK' state, causing the screen to be redisplayed with the appropriate error message so the user can correct the description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The change detection process has been invoked to compare the user-entered transaction type details against the originally fetched database values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The change detection routine begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The change status flag is set to 'No Changes Found' as the default starting state before any comparison is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Change Detection Status Before Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before comparing old and new transaction type values, the change detection status is initialized to a neutral 'No Changes Found' state to ensure a clean baseline for the comparison process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted transaction type details on the screen and the system holds both the newly entered Transaction Type Code and the originally fetched Transaction Type Code from the database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a case-insensitive comparison between the new Transaction Type Code and the original Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the two codes match (case-insensitively), the system proceeds to compare the Transaction Type Description; if the codes do not match, the system immediately marks the status as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Transaction Type Code for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The newly entered Transaction Type Code is compared against the originally fetched Transaction Type Code using a case-insensitive comparison to determine if the code has been modified by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The newly entered Transaction Type Code matches the originally fetched Transaction Type Code, and the system holds both the newly entered Transaction Type Description and the originally fetched Transaction Type Description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a three-part comparison of the descriptions: (1) case-insensitive equality of trimmed new description versus trimmed original description, AND (2) the trimmed length of the new description equals the trimmed length of the original description — both conditions must be true simultaneously
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If both the trimmed case-insensitive content AND the trimmed lengths match, the system marks the status as 'No Changes Detected'; if either the content or the length differs, the system marks the status as 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Transaction Type Description for Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type Codes match, the system further compares the Transaction Type Descriptions using a case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed, and length-equal comparison to detect any description-level changes made by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted transaction type details, the system has compared the new Transaction Type Code and new Transaction Type Description against the original database values, and all comparisons have returned a match (case-insensitive, trimmed, same length), AND no prior error or return message is currently active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All three comparison conditions are satisfied: the Transaction Type Codes match case-insensitively, the trimmed Transaction Type Descriptions match case-insensitively, and the trimmed lengths of the descriptions are equal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the change status to 'No Changes Detected', signalling that no update to the database is needed and the user should be informed that no changes were made

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark No Changes Detected When All Values Are Identical
all_rules.Rule_Description: When both the Transaction Type Code and the Transaction Type Description are found to be identical to the originally fetched database values (after case-insensitive and trimmed comparison), the system marks the result as 'No Changes Detected', indicating that no update action is required.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted transaction type details, the system is comparing the new values against the original database values, AND no prior error or return message is currently active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: At least one of the following conditions is true: (1) the new Transaction Type Code does not match the original Transaction Type Code (case-insensitive), OR (2) the trimmed new Transaction Type Description does not match the trimmed original Transaction Type Description (case-insensitive), OR (3) the trimmed length of the new Transaction Type Description does not equal the trimmed length of the original Transaction Type Description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the change status to 'Change Has Occurred', and the comparison process exits immediately to return control to the input processing routine with a change-detected status, which will proceed to validate the changed values and prompt the user for confirmation before saving

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Change Has Occurred When Any Value Differs
all_rules.Rule_Description: When either the Transaction Type Code or the Transaction Type Description differs from the originally fetched database values, the system marks the result as 'Change Has Occurred', triggering the validation and confirmation workflow for the detected changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The change detection comparison has completed and a result (either match or mismatch) has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to set the change status flag ('No Changes Detected' or 'Change Has Occurred') but a prior return message is already active (the return message flag is not in the 'off' state)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not update the change status flag and continues processing without overwriting the existing message context; the status flags 'No Changes Detected' and 'Change Has Occurred' are only set when the return message is in the 'off' (inactive) state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Suppress Change Status Update When Prior Message Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: The 'No Changes Detected' and 'Change Has Occurred' status flags are only set when there is no prior active return message on the screen. If a return message is already present, the comparison result is determined but the status flags are not updated, preserving the existing message context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Fetched' state OR the user has pressed F12, AND the Transaction Type code has been validated as a non-blank, non-zero, 2-digit numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs a lookup of the Transaction Type in the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table using the entered type code as the search key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Database Lookup When Details Not Yet Fetched or F12 Pressed with Valid Type Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in the 'Details Not Fetched' state or the user presses F12, and the Transaction Type code entered is valid, the system initiates a database lookup to retrieve the Transaction Type record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A database lookup has been performed for the entered Transaction Type code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a matching record (successful retrieval)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Show Transaction Type Details', and the retrieved Transaction Type code and description are displayed on screen for the user to view or modify

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Transaction Type Details When Record Found in Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a database lookup, if a matching Transaction Type record is found, the system transitions to the 'Show Details' state so the record can be viewed or edited.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A database lookup has been performed for the entered Transaction Type code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns no matching record (record not found)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Details Not Found', and the user is prompted with the option to create a new Transaction Type record using the entered type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Record Not Found When No Matching Transaction Type Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a database lookup, if no matching Transaction Type record is found for the entered type code, the system marks the state as 'Record Not Found' and prompts the user with the option to create a new record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Fetched' state or F12 was pressed, AND the Transaction Type code is not valid, AND the program was previously in the 'Confirm Delete' state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic evaluates the cancellation context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the delete as cancelled ('Delete Was Cancelled'), resets the program state to 'Details Not Fetched', and the screen returns to the initial search prompt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cancel Delete Operation When F12 Pressed with Invalid Type Code During Delete Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type code is not valid and the program was in the 'Confirm Delete' state, pressing F12 cancels the pending delete operation and resets the screen to the initial search state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Fetched' state or F12 was pressed, AND the Transaction Type code is not valid, AND the program was previously in the 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (awaiting save confirmation) state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic evaluates the cancellation context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the update as cancelled ('Update Was Cancelled'), sets the program state to 'Changes Backed Out', and the screen returns to display the original unmodified values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cancel Update Operation When F12 Pressed with Invalid Type Code During Update Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type code is not valid and the program was in the 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state, pressing F12 cancels the pending update and sets the state to 'Changes Backed Out'.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Fetched' state or F12 was pressed, AND the Transaction Type code is not valid, AND the program was NOT in 'Confirm Delete' or 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic evaluates the cancellation context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is reset to 'Details Not Fetched' and the screen returns to the initial search prompt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset to Initial Search State When Type Code Invalid with No Specific Cancel Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type code is not valid and the program was not in a delete confirmation or update confirmation state, the program resets to the initial 'Details Not Fetched' state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is NOT in 'Details Not Fetched' state and F12 was NOT the triggering key for a reset, AND the program is currently in 'Confirm Delete' state, AND F12 is pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Confirm Delete' and the delete confirmation prompt continues to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Maintain Delete Confirmation State When F12 Pressed During Confirm Delete
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in the 'Confirm Delete' state and the user presses F12 (with a valid type code context), the delete confirmation state is preserved and the confirmation prompt remains displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Show Details' state displaying a Transaction Type record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic detects that: an input validation error exists, OR no changes were detected between old and new values (type code and description are identical case-insensitively after trimming), OR an invalid key was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Show Details' and the screen is redisplayed with the current values and any applicable error or informational message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Remain on Details View When Input Has Errors, No Changes, or Invalid Key While Showing Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is showing transaction type details and the user's input contains errors, no changes were detected compared to the original values, or an invalid key was pressed, the screen remains in the 'Show Details' state without transitioning.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Show Details' state displaying a Transaction Type record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic detects that: there are no input validation errors, AND changes have been detected between the old and new values (description differs case-insensitively or in trimmed length), AND no invalid key was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Changes OK Not Confirmed', and the screen prompts the user to confirm the changes before they are saved to the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Changes Ready for Confirmation When Valid Modifications Detected While Showing Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is showing transaction type details and the user has made valid changes to the description (no input errors, changes detected), the system transitions to the 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state to prompt the user to confirm before saving.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Changes Not OK' state due to prior validation failures
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Changes Not OK', the screen is redisplayed with the validation error message, and the user is prompted to re-enter valid data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Remain in Changes Not OK State When Validation Errors Persist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in the 'Changes Not OK' state (validation errors were found in the previous input), the state is maintained and the user is prompted to correct the errors.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Changes Backed Out' state, indicating a prior update was cancelled by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Changes Not OK', the original values are displayed, and the user is prompted to make changes to the Transaction Type description

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transition to Changes Not OK State After Changes Are Backed Out
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in the 'Changes Backed Out' state (a previous update was cancelled), the system transitions to 'Changes Not OK' to prompt the user to re-enter their modifications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Invalid Search Keys' state due to a previously entered Transaction Type code that failed validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Invalid Search Keys', the screen is redisplayed with the appropriate error message, and the user is prompted to enter a valid Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Remain in Invalid Search Keys State When Search Keys Were Invalid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in the 'Invalid Search Keys' state due to a prior invalid Transaction Type code entry, the state is maintained and the user is prompted to re-enter a valid search key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in 'Details Not Found' state, indicating no Transaction Type record exists for the entered type code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses F5 (Save/Confirm key)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Create New Record', the screen transitions to allow entry of a new Transaction Type description, and the user is prompted to enter the new record details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Switch to Create New Record Mode When F5 Pressed and Record Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses F5 after a search returns no matching record, the system switches to 'Create New Record' mode, allowing the user to enter details for a new Transaction Type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is currently in 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state, meaning the user's changes have passed all validation checks and are awaiting final confirmation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state remains as 'Changes OK Not Confirmed', the screen continues to display the confirmation prompt asking the user to press F5 to save or F12 to cancel

all_rules.Rule_Name: Remain on Confirmation Prompt When Changes Are Validated But Not Yet Confirmed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in the 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' state (changes have passed validation and are awaiting user confirmation to save), the state is maintained and the confirmation prompt remains displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in 'Changes Okayed And Done' state, meaning the Transaction Type record has been successfully updated or inserted in the database and committed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The action decision logic is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program state is set to 'Show Details' to display the saved Transaction Type record; additionally, if no calling transaction ID or program is present (values are blank or low-values), the account ID, card number, and account status fields are cleared to zero or low-values respectively

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return to Show Details View After Changes Are Successfully Saved
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a Transaction Type update or insert has been successfully committed to the database, the program transitions back to the 'Show Details' state to display the saved record. If no calling transaction context exists, account-related fields are cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has initiated a transaction type lookup by entering a Transaction Type Code on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the Transaction Type Lookup process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All previously stored transaction type details (old Transaction Type Code and old Transaction Type Description) are cleared/reset before the new database query is executed, ensuring no residual data from a prior lookup remains

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Previously Fetched Transaction Type Details Before New Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before performing a new transaction type lookup, any previously retrieved transaction type details stored in memory must be cleared to prevent stale data from being displayed or compared against new results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a valid, non-blank, numeric, non-zero Transaction Type Code (2 digits, zero-padded if necessary, e.g., '05') on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to query the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entered Transaction Type Code is set as the search parameter (TR_TYPE) to be used in the database query for an exact match lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Transaction Type Code as Search Key for Database Query
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Code entered by the user on the screen must be used as the exact search key when querying the Transaction Type database table.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code has been prepared as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the database query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the condition that TR_TYPE exactly equals the entered Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the TR_TYPE (Transaction Type Code, 2 characters) and TR_DESCRIPTION (Transaction Type Description, up to 50 characters) for the matching record, if one exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Query TRANSACTION_TYPE Table for Matching Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system queries the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table using the entered Transaction Type Code as an exact match filter to retrieve the corresponding Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has executed a query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the entered Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The query returns exactly one matching record (successful retrieval with no errors)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the transaction type as 'Found in Table', indicating that a valid record exists and its details are available for display, editing, or deletion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Transaction Type as Found When Record Exists in Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database query returns a matching record for the entered Transaction Type Code, the system marks the transaction type as successfully found, enabling the record details to be displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has executed a query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the entered Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The query returns no matching record (the entered Transaction Type Code does not exist in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the input as having an error, flags the Transaction Type Code filter as invalid/not-found, and sets a 'Record Not Found' message to inform the user that no transaction type exists for the entered code; the user may subsequently be offered the option to create a new record with that code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle No Matching Transaction Type Record Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database query finds no record matching the entered Transaction Type Code, the system marks the search as unsuccessful and sets the appropriate status so the user can be informed and optionally prompted to create a new record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The database query has successfully retrieved a transaction type record with a Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and a Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) from the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched record details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The retrieved Transaction Type Code is stored as the original Transaction Type Code, and the retrieved Transaction Type Description is stored as the original Transaction Type Description (trimmed to its actual character length, up to 50 characters); these original values serve as the baseline for display on screen and for comparison against any user modifications to detect changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Retrieved Transaction Type Details for Display and Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a transaction type record from the database, the system stores the retrieved Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description as the original baseline values. These stored values are used for screen display and to detect whether the user has made any changes during an edit operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully retrieved a Transaction Type record from the TRANSACTION_TYPE table and is about to store the fetched data into the Old-Details working storage area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The store-fetched-data process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields within the Old-Details working storage area (TTUP-OLD-DETAILS), including the Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description, are reset to their initial empty state before any new values are moved in, ensuring no previously retrieved transaction type data remains

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Previously Held Transaction Type Details Before Storing New Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before storing newly retrieved transaction type data from the database, any previously held old-details in working storage must be cleared to prevent stale data from persisting across lookups.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The TRANSACTION_TYPE table has returned a valid Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE, 2-character field) and the Old-Details working storage area has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched transaction type data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The retrieved Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) is saved exactly as-is into the Old-Details Transaction Type Code field (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE), making it available for old-versus-new comparison and for redisplaying the original database value on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Retrieved Transaction Type Code into Old-Details Storage
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Code retrieved from the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table must be saved into the Old-Details working storage area so it can be used for subsequent comparison against user-entered values and for display on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The TRANSACTION_TYPE table has returned a Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION, variable-length up to 50 characters) along with its actual character length indicator (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN), and the Old-Details working storage area has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched transaction type description data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Only the exact number of characters specified by the database-returned length indicator (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN) are copied from the retrieved description text (DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT) into the Old-Details Transaction Type Description field (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC), ensuring the stored description precisely matches the database value without padding or truncation beyond the actual data length, making it available for old-versus-new comparison and for redisplaying the original database value on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Retrieved Transaction Type Description Using Exact Character Length into Old-Details Storage
