all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Description retrieved from the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table must be saved into the Old-Details working storage area using only the exact number of characters returned by the database (variable length), so it can be used for accurate comparison against user-entered values and for display on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has confirmed changes to a transaction type record and PF5 has been pressed with validated data, where TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE contains the transaction type code and TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC contains the new description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the data for the database write operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets DCL-TR-TYPE to the value of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE, sets DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-TEXT to the trimmed value of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, and sets DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN to the full length of TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, making the data ready for the UPDATE statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Transaction Type Data for Database Write
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before executing a database update, the system prepares the transaction type code and description by mapping the validated user-entered values into the database host variables, trimming the description to its actual content length.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The host variables DCL-TR-TYPE and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION have been populated with the transaction type code and new description respectively
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the SQL UPDATE statement against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table setting TR_DESCRIPTION equal to DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION where TR_TYPE equals DCL-TR-TYPE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database attempts to update the TR_DESCRIPTION column for the matching TR_TYPE row, and the resulting SQLCODE is stored in WS-DISP-SQLCODE for subsequent outcome evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Execute Update on Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system attempts to modify an existing transaction type description in the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table by matching on the transaction type code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned equals zero, indicating the UPDATE was successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system issues a SYNCPOINT to permanently commit the changes to the database, and the program state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, which triggers a success confirmation message to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Successful Transaction Type Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database UPDATE completes successfully, the changes are permanently committed to the database and the screen state is set to reflect a successful update.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned equals +100, indicating no existing row was found for the specified transaction type code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to execute the INSERT operation (9700-INSERT-RECORD) to create a new transaction type record using the same DCL-TR-TYPE and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION host variables, without displaying an error to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt Insert When Transaction Type Record Does Not Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the UPDATE finds no existing record for the given transaction type code, the system automatically attempts to create a new record by switching to an INSERT operation instead.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The UPDATE operation returned SQLCODE +100 indicating no existing record, and DCL-TR-TYPE and DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION host variables are populated with the transaction type code and description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the SQL INSERT INTO CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE statement providing values for TR_TYPE from DCL-TR-TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION from DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database attempts to insert a new row into the TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the specified type code and description, and the resulting SQLCODE is evaluated for success or failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert New Transaction Type Record into Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no existing record is found during the UPDATE attempt, the system inserts a new transaction type record into the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the prepared type code and description values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL INSERT INTO CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE statement has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned from the INSERT equals zero, indicating the new record was successfully created
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system issues a SYNCPOINT to permanently commit the new record to the database, and the program state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, which triggers a success confirmation message to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Successfully Inserted New Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a new transaction type record is successfully inserted into the database, the changes are permanently committed and the screen state reflects a successful creation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL INSERT INTO CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE statement has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned from the INSERT is any value other than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED to TRUE, constructs an error message in WS-RETURN-MSG by concatenating the literal 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:' with WS-DISP-SQLCODE and SQLERRM from SQLCA, and the program state is subsequently set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED, which triggers a failure message to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Insert Failure for New Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the INSERT operation fails for any reason, the system sets a failure state and constructs an error message containing the SQL error code and database error text to inform the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned equals -911, indicating the record is currently locked by another user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets INPUT-ERROR to TRUE, and when WS-RETURN-MSG is currently off (no prior message), sets COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE to TRUE; the program state is subsequently set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR, which triggers a lock conflict message to be displayed to the user indicating the record could not be updated due to concurrent access

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Record Lock Conflict During Transaction Type Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the UPDATE operation cannot proceed because another user currently holds a lock on the transaction type record, the system informs the user of the concurrent access conflict.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The SQL UPDATE statement has been executed against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SQLCODE returned is a negative value other than -911, indicating a general database error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED to TRUE, constructs an error message in WS-RETURN-MSG by concatenating the literal 'Error updating: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:' with WS-DISP-SQLCODE and SQLERRM from SQLCA, and the program state is subsequently set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED, which triggers a failure message to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle General Update Failure for Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the UPDATE operation fails due to any database error other than record-not-found or lock conflict, the system sets a failure state and constructs a detailed error message for the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The write processing (UPDATE and optionally INSERT) has completed and the outcome flags have been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the final outcome flags in order: COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE, TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED, DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE, or none of the above
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If COULD-NOT-LOCK-REC-FOR-UPDATE is TRUE, the state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR and a lock error message is shown; if TABLE-UPDATE-FAILED is TRUE, the state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-BUT-FAILED and a failure message is shown; if DATA-WAS-CHANGED-BEFORE-UPDATE is TRUE, the state is set to TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS and the current database values are redisplayed; otherwise (all other cases including successful UPDATE or INSERT), the state is set to TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE and a success confirmation message is shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Final Program State After Write Processing Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all write processing outcomes are evaluated, the system sets the final program state that determines which message and screen layout will be presented to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted a Transaction Type Code and Description for saving, and the system attempted to update an existing record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The update operation determines that no existing record matches the provided Transaction Type Code (record not found condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must automatically initiate an INSERT operation to create a new Transaction Type record using the same Transaction Type Code and Description values that were prepared for the update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Insert When Update Finds No Existing Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an attempt to update a Transaction Type record finds that no matching record exists in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, the system automatically switches from an update operation to an insert operation to create the new record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that a new Transaction Type record must be inserted because no existing record was found during the update attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the data for the INSERT operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code (2-character numeric, zero-padded) and the trimmed Transaction Type Description (up to 50 characters, alphanumeric only) that were previously validated and staged must be used as the values for the new record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Transaction Type Values for Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before executing the INSERT, the system prepares the Transaction Type Code and Description values that were already validated and staged during the write processing phase, ensuring the correct data is used for the new record creation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code and Description values have been prepared and validated, and no existing record was found for the given Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the INSERT operation against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new record must be created in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the provided Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and Transaction Type Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) as the column values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Execute SQL INSERT for New Transaction Type Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system executes a SQL INSERT statement to create a new Transaction Type record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the prepared Transaction Type Code and Description values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has executed an INSERT operation for a new Transaction Type record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The INSERT operation completes successfully with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately commit the transaction to permanently save the new Transaction Type record to the database before proceeding

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit New Transaction Type Record on Successful Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the INSERT operation completes successfully, the system immediately commits the transaction to permanently persist the new Transaction Type record to the database, ensuring data durability.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The INSERT operation for the new Transaction Type record has completed successfully and the transaction has been committed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the final outcome of the write processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the program state to 'Changes Okayed And Done' (success), which will cause the screen to display a success confirmation message and transition to showing the newly created record details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Success Status After New Transaction Type Record Created
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful INSERT and commit, the system sets the program state to indicate that the Transaction Type record was successfully created, which drives the subsequent screen display to show a success confirmation message to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has executed an INSERT operation for a new Transaction Type record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The INSERT operation fails for any reason (any SQL error condition other than success)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the internal status to 'Table Update Failed' to indicate the record creation was unsuccessful, and this failure status must be carried back to the write processing routine to set the final program state to 'Changes Okayed But Failed'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Failure Status When Transaction Type Insert Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the INSERT operation fails for any reason, the system sets a failure status flag to indicate that the record creation was unsuccessful, which drives the subsequent error handling and user notification.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The INSERT operation for a new Transaction Type record has failed with any SQL error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the INSERT failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must build an error message for display to the user that includes all of the following components concatenated together: the text 'Error inserting record into: TRANSACTION_TYPE Table. SQLCODE:' followed by the actual SQL error code number, followed by ':', followed by the SQL error message text describing the specific error — and this complete message must be stored for display on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build User-Facing Error Message When Transaction Type Insert Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the INSERT operation fails, the system constructs a descriptive error message combining a fixed error description, the SQL error code, and the SQL error message text, to inform the user about the nature of the failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The INSERT operation has completed and control has returned to the write processing routine
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write processing routine evaluates the final outcome of the insert attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the insert failed (Table Update Failed status is set), the program state must be set to 'Changes Okayed But Failed' which will display a failure message to the user; if no failure status is set (insert succeeded), the program state must be set to 'Changes Okayed And Done' which will display a success confirmation to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Insert Failure to Final Program State for Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the INSERT operation completes (success or failure), control returns to the write processing routine which evaluates the outcome flags and sets the final program state that determines what message and screen state the user will see.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Transaction Type record has been retrieved and displayed, the user has confirmed the delete intent by pressing PF4 a second time, and the original Transaction Type Code is stored as the confirmed delete key (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The delete processing begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must use the original confirmed Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE) — not any user-entered or modified value — as the sole key to identify the record targeted for deletion in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Confirmed Transaction Type Code as Delete Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a delete operation is initiated, the system must use the previously confirmed (original) Transaction Type Code — not any newly entered value — as the key to identify the exact record to be removed from the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The confirmed Transaction Type Code has been set as the delete key and the delete processing has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the DELETE operation against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table with a WHERE clause matching TR_TYPE equal to the confirmed Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database attempts to remove the matching Transaction Type record; the outcome (success, referential integrity violation, or other failure) is captured for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Execute Delete on Transaction Type Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system executes a SQL DELETE statement against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the confirmed Transaction Type Code as the exact match key to remove the record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE statement has been executed against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the confirmed Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The DELETE operation returns a successful outcome (no errors, record was found and deleted)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system permanently commits the deletion to the database (SYNCPOINT), sets the program state to 'Delete Done', and the screen subsequently displays a delete success confirmation message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Transaction Type Deletion on Success
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the DELETE operation completes successfully, the system must permanently commit the deletion to the database and set the screen state to indicate the record has been deleted successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE statement has been executed against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the confirmed Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The DELETE operation fails because other records in the database reference this Transaction Type Code (referential integrity constraint violation — child records exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must NOT delete the record, must NOT commit any change, must set the record-delete-failed indicator, and must display the message 'Please delete associated child records first:' along with the database error code to inform the user they must first remove all dependent child records before this Transaction Type can be deleted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Block Deletion When Child Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: A Transaction Type record cannot be deleted if other records in the system reference it (child records exist). The system must detect this referential integrity violation and instruct the user to remove the dependent child records before attempting to delete the Transaction Type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE statement has been executed against the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for the confirmed Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The DELETE operation fails for any reason other than child records existing (i.e., any database error that is not a referential integrity violation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must NOT delete the record, must NOT commit any change, must set both the record-delete-failed indicator and the 'Delete Failed' program state, and must display an error message to the user containing the text 'Delete failed with message:' followed by the database error code and the database error message text, so the user is informed of the specific reason for the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle General Delete Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the DELETE operation fails for any reason other than a referential integrity violation, the system must set the delete-failed state and display an error message containing the failure details to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Transaction Type Update screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All existing output fields on the Transaction Type Update screen are cleared (set to LOW-VALUES), ensuring no residual data from a previous display remains visible

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Output Before Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the Transaction Type Update screen with fresh data, all existing screen output fields must be cleared to prevent stale or residual data from appearing to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header preparation step is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system date and time are retrieved from the system clock and stored in the working storage date-time area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must retrieve the current system date and time at the moment of screen preparation so that the screen header reflects the accurate date and time of the current user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized and the screen output area has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header fields are being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first screen title line (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the Title Line 1 output field (TITLE01O) of the screen map, displaying the application title to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Screen Title Line 1 in Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first line of the application screen title must be placed in the screen header area to identify the application context to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized and Title Line 1 has been placed on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header fields are being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The second screen title line (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the Title Line 2 output field (TITLE02O) of the screen map, displaying the secondary application title to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Screen Title Line 2 in Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The second line of the application screen title must be placed in the screen header area to provide the secondary title or subtitle context to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header fields are being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID) is placed into the Transaction Name output field (TRNNAMEO) of the screen map, making the active transaction ID visible to the user in the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Current Transaction ID in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The identifier of the currently executing transaction must be displayed in the screen header so the user can identify which transaction they are working with.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header fields are being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (LIT-THISPGM) is placed into the Program Name output field (PGMNAMEO) of the screen map, making the active program name visible to the user in the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Current Program Name in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The name of the currently executing program must be displayed in the screen header to allow the user and support staff to identify which program is active.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in the working storage date area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The date is being formatted for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) is moved to the MM position (WS-CURDATE-MM), the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) is moved to the DD position (WS-CURDATE-DD), and the last two digits of the year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR positions 3 through 4) are moved to the YY position (WS-CURDATE-YY), resulting in a combined MM-DD-YY formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) that is placed into the Current Date output field (CURDATEO) of the screen map

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Date as MM-DD-YY in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system date must be formatted in MM-DD-YY format and displayed in the screen header. The year is represented as a 2-digit value extracted from positions 3 and 4 of the 4-digit year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date and time have been retrieved and stored in the working storage date-time area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The time is being formatted for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) is moved to the HH position (WS-CURTIME-HH), the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) is moved to the MM position (WS-CURTIME-MM), and the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) is moved to the SS position (WS-CURTIME-SS), resulting in a combined HH-MM-SS formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) that is placed into the Current Time output field (CURTIMEO) of the screen map

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Time as HH-MM-SS in Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system time must be formatted in HH-MM-SS format and displayed in the screen header, showing hours, minutes, and seconds to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program state indicates this is a fresh program entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER flag is set to TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen field population logic is skipped entirely — no Transaction Type Code, no Transaction Type Description, and no other field values are populated or overwritten; the screen retains the blank initialized state from the screen initialization step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Screen Field Population on Fresh Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type Update screen is accessed for the very first time in a session (fresh program entry), the screen field population step is bypassed entirely because the screen has already been initialized with empty values during screen initialization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step AND this is not a fresh program entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is either 'Details Not Yet Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) OR 'Invalid Search Keys Entered' (TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code display field (TRTYPCDO) on the screen is set to LOW-VALUES (blank/empty); the screen is presented as a clean blank search screen ready for the user to enter a Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Empty Search Screen for Initial or Invalid Search States
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in an initial state (details not yet fetched) or the user has entered invalid search keys, the screen is populated with empty/blank values to present a clean search entry screen to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step AND this is not a fresh program entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: 'Showing Record Details' (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS), 'Confirming Delete' (TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE), 'Delete Failed' (TTUP-DELETE-FAILED), 'Delete Completed' (TTUP-DELETE-DONE), or 'Changes Backed Out' (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All pending new/changed detail fields (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS) are reset to their initial empty state; the Transaction Type Code display field (TRTYPCDO) is populated with the original Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE) fetched from the database; the Transaction Type Description display field (TRTYDSCO) is populated with the original Transaction Type Description (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) fetched from the database; the non-key flags (WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS) are reset to LOW-VALUES

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Original Database Values for View, Delete, and Backed-Out States
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in a state where the original database record should be shown — such as viewing details, confirming or completing a delete, or when a user has backed out of changes — the screen is populated with the original values fetched from the database, and any pending new/changed values are cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step AND this is not a fresh program entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: 'Changes Made' (TTUP-CHANGES-MADE), 'Changes Not Valid' (TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), 'Record Not Found' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND), 'Invalid Search Keys' (TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS), 'Creating New Record' (TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD), or 'Changes Confirmed and Saved' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code display field (TRTYPCDO) is populated with the newly entered Transaction Type Code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE); the Transaction Type Description display field (TRTYDSCO) is populated with the newly entered Transaction Type Description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User-Entered New or Updated Values for Change and Creation States
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in a state where the user's newly entered or modified data should be shown — such as during active editing, validation failure, creating a new record, record not found, or after a successful save — the screen is populated with the user's most recently entered values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen program is executing the screen variable setup step AND this is not a fresh program entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state does not match any of the explicitly handled states (none of the defined TTUP state flags match — falls into the WHEN OTHER branch)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All pending new/changed detail fields (TTUP-NEW-DETAILS) are reset to their initial empty state; the Transaction Type Code display field (TRTYPCDO) is populated with the original Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE); the Transaction Type Description display field (TRTYDSCO) is populated with the original Transaction Type Description (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC); the non-key flags (WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS) are reset to LOW-VALUES

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default to Original Values Display for Unrecognized Program States
all_rules.Rule_Description: As a safety fallback, if the program encounters any program state not explicitly handled by the screen variable setup logic, it defaults to displaying the original database-fetched values and clearing any pending new changes, ensuring the screen always shows consistent and safe data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is any of: Fresh Entry (first time on screen), Details Not Yet Fetched (initial/reset state), Invalid Search Keys Entered (previous search had invalid input), or no informational message is currently set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Search Prompt on Fresh Entry or Reset State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in an initial, reset, or invalid-search state, the informational message area should prompt the user to enter a Transaction Type code to begin a search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has submitted a valid Transaction Type code for search
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is 'Details Not Found' (the searched Transaction Type code does not exist in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to notify the user that the record was not found and prompt them to press PF5 to create a new record with that Transaction Type code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Create New Record Prompt When Record Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a search for a Transaction Type code returns no matching record in the database, the informational message should notify the user that the record was not found and offer the option to create a new record using PF5.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and a Transaction Type record has been retrieved from the database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is either 'Show Details' (record found and displayed) OR 'Changes Backed Out' (user cancelled a pending update and original values are restored, meaning old Transaction Type code is not blank or low-values) OR 'Changes Not OK' (validation failed on entered changes)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to make changes to the displayed record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Change Prompt When Record is Displayed or Changes Were Cancelled
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Transaction Type record is currently displayed on screen, or when a previously initiated change was cancelled and original values restored, the informational message should prompt the user to make changes to the displayed record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user had initiated changes that were subsequently cancelled
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is 'Changes Backed Out' AND the previously stored original Transaction Type code (old type code) is blank or contains only low-values (no prior record was loaded)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search (same as initial state), not to prompt for changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Search Prompt When Changes Backed Out With No Prior Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When changes are backed out but there is no previously loaded record (old Transaction Type code is blank or empty), the informational message should revert to prompting the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search, rather than prompting for changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and a Transaction Type record is currently displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is 'Confirm Delete' (user has pressed PF4 once and the system is waiting for confirmation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to confirm the deletion by pressing PF4 or cancel the deletion by pressing PF12

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Delete Confirmation Prompt When Awaiting Delete Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has pressed PF4 to initiate a delete and the system is awaiting confirmation, the informational message should prompt the user to confirm the deletion by pressing PF4 again or cancel by pressing PF12.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has confirmed a delete operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is 'Delete Failed' (the delete operation was attempted but did not complete successfully)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to a failure notification informing the user that the delete operation did not succeed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Failure Notification When Delete Operation Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a delete operation on a Transaction Type record fails (e.g., due to referential integrity constraints or other database errors), the informational message area should display a failure notification to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has confirmed a delete operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is 'Delete Done' (the delete operation completed successfully and was committed to the database)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to confirm that the delete operation completed successfully

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Delete Success Confirmation When Delete Completes Successfully
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Transaction Type record has been successfully deleted from the database, the informational message should confirm to the user that the delete operation completed successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and a previous search returned no matching record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is 'Create New Record' (user pressed PF5 after being informed the record was not found)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to enter the details (Transaction Type Description) for the new Transaction Type record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display New Data Entry Prompt When Creating a New Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has chosen to create a new Transaction Type record (after a search returned no results and PF5 was pressed), the informational message should prompt the user to enter the details for the new record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active, a Transaction Type record is displayed, and the user has entered changes that have passed all validation checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is 'Changes OK Not Confirmed' (changes are validated and waiting for user confirmation before being saved to the database)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to prompt the user to confirm the changes by pressing PF5 to save, or cancel the changes by pressing PF12 to revert to original values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Confirmation Prompt When Changes Are Validated and Awaiting Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has entered changes to a Transaction Type record and those changes have passed all validation rules, the informational message should prompt the user to confirm the changes by pressing PF5 or cancel them by pressing PF12.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is 'Changes Okayed And Done' (the update or insert operation completed successfully and was committed to the database)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to confirm that the update completed successfully

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Update Success Confirmation When Changes Are Saved Successfully
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Transaction Type record has been successfully updated or inserted into the database, the informational message should confirm to the user that the update completed successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the user has confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is any of: 'Changes Okayed Lock Error' (record was locked by another user at time of update), 'Changes Okayed But Failed' (the database update operation failed for a non-lock reason), or any other unhandled failure state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to a failure notification informing the user that the operation did not succeed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Failure Notification for Lock Error or Update Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a save operation fails due to a record being locked by another user, a database update failure, or any other operational failure, the informational message area should display a failure notification to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An informational message has been selected based on the current program state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message text is being prepared for display on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The length of the trimmed message text is calculated, the starting position is computed as: (total message field length minus trimmed message length) divided by 2 plus 1, and the trimmed message text is placed at that calculated starting position within the output string so that it appears centered in the display area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Center Informational Message Text Within Display Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the appropriate informational message is determined based on program state, the message text must be centered within the available display area before being placed on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The informational message text has been centered within the output string
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The centered message string is placed into the informational message display field (INFOMSGO) on the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Centered Informational Message onto Screen Display Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the informational message has been centered, the centered message string is moved to the informational message output field on the screen so it is visible to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display and there may be a validation or system error message present
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen output fields are being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current error or validation message (WS-RETURN-MSG, which may contain messages such as field validation errors, database error details, or operation failure descriptions) is placed into the error message display field (ERRMSGO) on the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Validation or Error Message onto Screen Error Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: In addition to the informational message, any validation error or system error message that was generated during input processing or database operations must be placed into the dedicated error message area on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is about to be displayed to the user and field attributes are being prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field, the Transaction Description field, and the Informational Message field are all set to read-only (protected) as the default baseline before any state-specific rules are applied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect All Screen Fields Before State-Based Attribute Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying any state-specific field editability rules, all screen fields are set to read-only (protected) as a baseline. This ensures no field is accidentally left editable from a prior interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured after the baseline protection is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Waiting for Search Input (Details Not Fetched), Invalid Search Keys entered, Record Not Found, or Changes were Backed Out and there is no prior record data (old Transaction Type Code is blank or LOW-VALUES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field is set to editable (unprotected with cursor entry enabled), allowing the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search

all_rules.Rule_Name: Make Transaction Type Code Field Editable When Awaiting Search Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in a state that requires the user to enter or re-enter a Transaction Type code for searching, the Transaction Type Code field is made editable so the user can type in it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured after the baseline protection is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Showing Record Details, Changes Have Validation Errors (Changes Not OK), Creating a New Record, or Changes were Backed Out but prior record data exists (old Transaction Type Code has a value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Description field is set to editable (unprotected with cursor entry enabled), and the Informational Message field remains read-only (protected)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Make Transaction Description Field Editable When Viewing or Editing a Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a record is being displayed for editing, a new record is being created, or changes have validation errors requiring correction, the Transaction Description field is made editable while the Informational Message field remains read-only.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured after the baseline protection is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Changes Confirmed and Not Yet Saved (Changes OK Not Confirmed), Changes Successfully Saved (Changes Okayed And Done), or Delete In Progress
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All screen fields remain read-only (protected) with no cursor repositioning change applied at this stage

all_rules.Rule_Name: Keep All Fields Read-Only When Changes Are Confirmed or Delete Is In Progress
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has already confirmed changes awaiting save, when a save has been completed, or when a delete operation is in progress, all fields remain read-only to prevent further input until the operation resolves.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured and cursor positioning is being determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state or condition is one of: Waiting for Search Input (Details Not Fetched), Record Not Found, Invalid Search Keys, Transaction Type Code filter flag is blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK), Transaction Type Code filter flag is invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK), Changes Successfully Saved (Changes Okayed And Done), or Changes Backed Out with no prior record data (old Transaction Type Code is blank or LOW-VALUES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Type Code field is set to -1, positioning the cursor to that field when the screen is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor to Transaction Type Code Field for Search-Related States
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor is automatically moved to the Transaction Type Code field when the user needs to enter or correct a search key, when a search returned no results, when the filter input was invalid or blank, or when changes have been saved and the screen resets.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured and cursor positioning is being determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state or condition is one of: Creating a New Record, No Changes Detected between old and new values, Transaction Description validation failed (Description Not OK flag or Description Blank flag), Changes Have Been Made, Changes Backed Out with prior record data, or Showing Record Details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Description field is set to -1, positioning the cursor to that field when the screen is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor to Transaction Description Field for Edit and Data Entry States
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor is automatically moved to the Transaction Description field when the user is expected to enter or correct description data, such as when creating a new record, editing an existing record, or when description validation has failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured after cursor positioning has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code filter flag is set to invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK is true) OR the current program state is Delete Failed (TTUP-DELETE-FAILED)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The color attribute of the Transaction Type Code field is set to red (DFHRED) to visually indicate an error to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Transaction Type Code Field in Red When Input Is Invalid or Delete Failed
all_rules.Rule_Description: To visually alert the user to an error condition, the Transaction Type Code field is displayed in red when the entered code failed validation or when a delete operation has failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes are being configured and the Transaction Type Code color attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code filter flag is blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK is true) AND the program is in re-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code output field value is set to '*' (asterisk) as a visual placeholder, and the color attribute of the Transaction Type Code field is set to red (DFHRED)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Asterisk Placeholder and Red Highlight When Transaction Type Code Is Blank on Re-Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has returned to the screen (re-entry mode) and the Transaction Type Code field was left blank, an asterisk '*' is displayed as a placeholder in the field and the field is highlighted in red to draw attention to the missing required input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen field attributes have been configured for field protection, cursor positioning, and color highlighting
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state or condition is one of: Waiting for Search Input (Details Not Fetched), Record Not Found (Details Not Found), Invalid Search Keys, Transaction Type Code filter flag is blank (FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK), or Transaction Type Code filter flag is invalid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No further screen attribute changes are applied and the screen attribute setup process completes immediately, skipping any additional attribute configuration steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Further Attribute Processing When Screen Is in a Search or Not-Found State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in a state where only the Transaction Type Code search field is relevant (no record data to display), no further field attribute changes are needed beyond what has already been set, and processing exits early.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display after user interaction, and the Transaction Type Code field has been evaluated for validity and/or a delete operation has been attempted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code is flagged as invalid (failed numeric, zero, or format validation) OR the delete operation on the Transaction Type record has failed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field color attribute is set to RED so that the field is visually highlighted in red on the screen, alerting the user that the entered code is invalid or that the delete operation was unsuccessful

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Transaction Type Code Field in Red on Invalid Code or Failed Delete
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type Code entered by the user fails validation (is not a valid numeric non-zero 2-digit code) OR when a delete operation has failed, the Transaction Type Code field on the screen must be visually highlighted in red to draw the user's attention to the error condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display and the program is in re-entry mode (the user has previously submitted the screen at least once)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field was left blank or contained only spaces by the user during re-entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An asterisk character ('*') is placed into the Transaction Type Code display field as a placeholder, AND the Transaction Type Code field color attribute is set to RED, visually indicating to the user that the Transaction Type Code is a required field that must be supplied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Asterisk Placeholder and Red Highlight for Blank Transaction Type Code on Re-entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has already interacted with the screen at least once (re-entry mode) and the Transaction Type Code field was left blank, the system must display an asterisk ('*') as a visual placeholder in the Transaction Type Code field and highlight it in red, indicating that a required search key was not provided.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display after user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code is not flagged as invalid AND no delete operation has failed AND the Transaction Type Code field was not left blank during re-entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No color attribute change is applied to the Transaction Type Code field, and the field is displayed in its default color, indicating no error condition exists for that field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retain Default Color for Transaction Type Code Field When No Error Condition Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type Code is valid and no delete failure has occurred, and the field was not left blank during re-entry, the Transaction Type Code field retains its default display color with no special highlighting, indicating normal screen state to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and the current program state is Delete Confirmation (user has pressed F4 once and is being asked to confirm the deletion of the displayed Transaction Type record)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared to send to the user and PF Key display attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All PF Key option labels (FKEYSA) on the screen are set to hidden/dark (non-displayed) so that no function key options are visible to the user on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Hide All PF Key Options During Delete Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in Delete Confirmation state, all available function key option labels are hidden from the user to prevent unintended actions during the critical delete confirmation step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and the current program state is NOT Delete Confirmation (i.e., the state is any of: initial search, showing details, record not found, creating new record, changes pending confirmation, changes completed, delete done, delete failed, or invalid search keys)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared to send to the user and PF Key display attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All PF Key option labels (FKEYSA) on the screen are set to visible/bright (displayed) so that the function key options area is visible to the user on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Show All PF Key Options in Non-Delete-Confirmation States
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in any state other than Delete Confirmation, all available function key option labels are shown to the user so they can see which actions are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is either Showing Details (a Transaction Type record has been retrieved from the database and is displayed on screen) OR Delete Confirmation (user has already pressed F4 once and is being prompted to confirm the deletion)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F4 Delete function key option label (FKEY04A) on the screen is set to visible/bright (enabled), indicating to the user that the Delete action is available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable F4 Delete Option When Record Is Displayed or Delete Is Pending Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F4 Delete function key option is made visible and active on the screen only when a Transaction Type record is currently being displayed to the user, or when the user is being asked to confirm a pending delete operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is NOT Showing Details AND NOT Delete Confirmation (i.e., the state is any of: initial search, record not found, creating new record, changes pending confirmation, changes completed, delete done, delete failed, or invalid search keys)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F4 Delete function key option label (FKEY04A) on the screen is NOT set to visible/bright, meaning the Delete option is not highlighted or enabled for the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: F4 Delete Option Not Available in All Other States
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F4 Delete function key option remains hidden and inactive when the screen is not in a state where a record is displayed or a delete is pending confirmation, preventing accidental deletion attempts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is either Changes Confirmed but Pending Save (user has entered and validated changes to the Transaction Type Description and the system is awaiting final confirmation to write to the database) OR Record Not Found (a search was performed but no matching Transaction Type record exists in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F5 Save function key option label (FKEY05A) on the screen is set to visible/bright (enabled), indicating to the user that the Save/Confirm action is available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable F5 Save Option When Changes Are Pending Confirmation or Record Was Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F5 Save function key option is made visible and active on the screen only when validated changes are awaiting the user's final confirmation to be saved, or when a search returned no record and the user has the option to create a new one.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is NOT Changes Confirmed but Pending Save AND NOT Record Not Found (i.e., the state is any of: initial search, showing details, delete confirmation, creating new record, changes completed, delete done, delete failed, or invalid search keys)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F5 Save function key option label (FKEY05A) on the screen is NOT set to visible/bright, meaning the Save option is not highlighted or enabled for the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: F5 Save Option Not Available in All Other States
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F5 Save function key option remains hidden and inactive when there are no pending changes awaiting confirmation and no opportunity to create a new record, preventing premature or unintended save actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is any one of the following: (1) Changes Confirmed but Pending Save - validated changes are awaiting final confirmation, (2) Showing Details - a Transaction Type record is currently displayed, (3) Record Not Found - search returned no matching record, (4) Delete Confirmation - user is being asked to confirm deletion of the displayed record, OR (5) Creating New Record - user is entering data for a new Transaction Type
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F12 Cancel function key option label (FKEY12A) on the screen is set to visible/bright (enabled), indicating to the user that the Cancel action is available to abandon the current operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable F12 Cancel Option Across Multiple Active States
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F12 Cancel function key option is made visible and active on the screen whenever the user is in a state where cancelling the current operation and returning to a prior state is a meaningful and valid action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type maintenance screen is active and PF Key display attributes are being set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is NOT Changes Confirmed but Pending Save AND NOT Showing Details AND NOT Record Not Found AND NOT Delete Confirmation AND NOT Creating New Record (i.e., the state is any of: initial search/not fetched, changes completed successfully, delete done, delete failed, invalid search keys, or changes backed out)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The F12 Cancel function key option label (FKEY12A) on the screen is NOT set to visible/bright, meaning the Cancel option is not highlighted or enabled for the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: F12 Cancel Option Not Available in All Other States
all_rules.Rule_Description: The F12 Cancel function key option remains hidden and inactive when there is no active operation in progress that can be meaningfully cancelled.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed preparing all screen content, field values, informational messages, field protection attributes, and PF key attributes for the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to transmit the screen to the user terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must assign the Transaction Type Update screen map name (LIT-THISMAP) to the target map field (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and assign the Transaction Type Update map set name (LIT-THISMAPSET) to the target map set field (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET), so that the correct screen layout is used for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Target Screen Map and Map Set for Transmission
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transmitting the screen to the user, the system identifies and assigns the correct screen map and map set that should be displayed. This ensures the right Transaction Type Update screen layout is used for the current interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The target screen map (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and map set (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET) have been assigned, and the output screen area (CTRTUPAO) has been fully populated with field values, informational messages, error messages, field colors, field protection attributes, and cursor positioning
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen transmission command
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must send the prepared screen output area (CTRTUPAO) using the assigned map name and map set to the user's terminal, with the cursor positioned at the field designated during screen attribute setup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transmit Prepared Screen to User Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system sends the fully prepared Transaction Type Update screen — including all field values, informational messages, error messages, field attributes, and cursor position — to the user's terminal for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is transmitting the Transaction Type Update screen to the user terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is sent to the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must erase all previously displayed content on the terminal screen before rendering the new screen, ensuring the user sees only the current screen content without any leftover data from the previous screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Erase Previous Screen Content so User Sees Fresh Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When displaying the Transaction Type Update screen, the system must clear any previously displayed content on the user's terminal so that the user always sees a clean, current screen without residual data from prior interactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen has been successfully transmitted and displayed on the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen transmission is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must release (free) the keyboard so that the user can immediately begin entering data into the available input fields or press PF keys (PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12, or ENTER) to perform the next action without any keyboard inhibit delay

all_rules.Rule_Name: Free the Keyboard so User Can Enter Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Transaction Type Update screen is displayed, the system must release the keyboard lock so the user is able to type input, enter data into fields, and press PF keys to interact with the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request has been made to validate an alphanumeric field (e.g., Transaction Description) with a specified maximum length
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The alphanumeric field validation routine is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The field validation status flag is immediately set to 'Not OK' (invalid) as the default state before any content checks are performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Alphanumeric Field Validation State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any validation checks are performed on an alphanumeric field, the field's validation status is pre-set to 'Not OK' (invalid). This ensures that the field must explicitly pass all checks to be considered valid, preventing any accidental acceptance of unvalidated data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field is being validated with a maximum length of 50 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The field value within the specified length is entirely LOW-VALUES (null), entirely spaces, or has a trimmed length of zero (no meaningful content)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The validation status is set to 'Input Error' and 'Field Blank', and the error message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' is generated; validation ends immediately with a failure result

all_rules.Rule_Name: Alphanumeric Field Must Not Be Blank or Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: An alphanumeric field under validation must contain at least one non-blank, non-empty character within its specified length. If the field is entirely empty, contains only spaces, or has no meaningful content after trimming, it is rejected with a mandatory supply error. This rule applies to the Transaction Description field (up to 50 characters).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field has been confirmed as non-blank and contains at least one character within the specified 50-character length
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The character scan is performed on the field content up to the specified length
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All characters that are valid alphanumeric characters (A through Z uppercase, a through z lowercase, 0 through 9 digits) within the specified length are replaced with spaces, leaving only any invalid/special characters visible as non-space characters for subsequent detection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Scan Alphanumeric Field for Valid Characters
all_rules.Rule_Description: To determine whether a field contains only permitted characters, all valid alphanumeric characters (uppercase A-Z, lowercase a-z, and digits 0-9) within the field's specified length are temporarily replaced with spaces. Any characters that remain non-space after this replacement are considered invalid. This technique isolates invalid characters for detection.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field has been scanned and all valid alphanumeric characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9) have been temporarily replaced with spaces within the 50-character length
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The trimmed length of the modified field content is greater than zero, meaning non-space (invalid) characters remain after the replacement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The validation status is set to 'Input Error' and 'Field Not OK', and the error message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' is generated; validation ends immediately with a failure result

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Alphanumeric Field Containing Non-Alphanumeric Characters
all_rules.Rule_Description: After replacing all valid alphanumeric characters with spaces, if any non-space characters remain in the field, it means the original field contained special characters, punctuation, or other non-alphanumeric content. Such a field is rejected with a character-type error. The Transaction Description field must contain only letters and numbers.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Description field has been checked and confirmed as non-blank and containing only alphanumeric characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9) within the 50-character length
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All validation checks pass without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The field validation status flag is set to 'Valid' (FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID), indicating the field content is accepted and no error messages are generated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Alphanumeric Field as Successfully Validated
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an alphanumeric field passes all validation checks — it is non-blank, non-empty, and contains only letters and digits — the field is marked as valid. This successful validation status signals that the field's content is acceptable for further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified the Transaction Description field on the Transaction Type Update screen, and the system has detected that a change has occurred compared to the original value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The alphanumeric validation routine is invoked for the Transaction Description field with a maximum length of 50 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If validation fails (field is blank or contains non-alphanumeric characters), the error state is retained and the description-level error flags are set from the validation result flags; if validation passes, the transaction state is advanced to 'Changes OK - Not Confirmed', enabling the user to confirm and save the update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Alphanumeric Validation to Transaction Description and Determine Change Confirmation Eligibility
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Description field entered by the user is submitted to the alphanumeric validation routine. The field name 'Transaction Desc', the user-entered description value, and the maximum allowed length of 50 characters are passed to the validation routine. Based on the validation outcome, the program either retains the error state or advances the transaction to the 'Changes OK - Awaiting Confirmation' state, enabling the user to confirm and save the changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type maintenance screen and the Numeric Field Validation routine is invoked for the 'Tran Type code' field with a maximum length of 2 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field is empty, contains only spaces, or has no trimmed content (length of trimmed value equals zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input is marked as an error, the field status is set to 'Blank', and the error message 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' is generated and stored as the return message for display to the user; validation exits immediately without checking further rules

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code field has been entered by the user and is not left blank or empty before any further validation is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank value in the Transaction Type Code field and the Numeric Field Validation routine has confirmed the field is not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered value fails the numeric test, meaning it contains one or more non-numeric characters (letters, symbols, or mixed content) within the 2-character length
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input is marked as an error, the field status is set to 'Not OK', and the error message 'Tran Type code must be numeric.' is generated and stored as the return message for display to the user; validation exits immediately without checking further rules

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Purely Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code entered by the user contains only numeric digits, rejecting any value that includes alphabetic characters or special characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank, purely numeric value in the Transaction Type Code field and the Numeric Field Validation routine has confirmed the field is not empty and is numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the entered Transaction Type Code evaluates to zero (e.g., '00' or '0')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input is marked as an error, the field status is set to 'Not OK', and the error message 'Tran Type code must not be zero.' is generated and stored as the return message for display to the user; validation exits immediately without proceeding to mark the field as valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Not Be Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the Transaction Type Code, after passing the numeric check, has a meaningful non-zero value, preventing the use of '00' or '0' as a valid transaction type identifier.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Transaction Type Code field and the Numeric Field Validation routine has been invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code is non-blank, contains only numeric digits, and its numeric value is greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The field is marked as valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID is set to TRUE), no error message is generated, and the validation routine exits successfully allowing the calling process to proceed with the zero-padded Transaction Type Code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Passes All Numeric Validations
all_rules.Rule_Description: Confirms that the Transaction Type Code has successfully passed all numeric validation checks — it is supplied, purely numeric, and non-zero — and is therefore accepted as a valid input for further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current user interaction has completed processing and the program is preparing to return control to CICS, and a return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) may or may not have been set during processing (e.g., validation error, record not found, update success, invalid key message)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the session state persistence step (COMMON-RETURN) prior to returning control to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) must be copied into the error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG) of the shared communication area so that the message is preserved and available for display during the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Persist Pending Error or Return Message into Shared Session Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before returning control to CICS, any pending error or informational return message generated during the current interaction must be copied into the shared communication area so it is available for display on the next screen interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing the current user interaction and is preparing to return control to CICS, and the general session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains current values for shared session context including: calling program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), calling transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), destination transaction (CDEMO-TO-TRANID), user type (CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN), program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER / CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), last mapset (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), last map (CDEMO-LAST-MAP), account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID), card number (CDEMO-CARD-NUM), and account status (CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the session state persistence step (COMMON-RETURN) and begins building the combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire general session data area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied into the beginning of the combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA), occupying the first portion of the combined area, so that all shared session context is preserved for the next interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save General Session Data into Combined Workspace Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: The general CardDemo session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which includes shared session context such as calling program identity, transaction IDs, user type, and navigation state, must be saved into the combined workspace communication area before returning to CICS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The general session data has already been saved into the first portion of the combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA), and the program-specific state area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) contains the current values for: screen state flags (e.g., TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, TTUP-CONFIRM-DELETE, TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, TTUP-DELETE-DONE, TTUP-DELETE-FAILED, TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), the original transaction type code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE), the original transaction type description (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC), the new/updated transaction type code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE), and the new/updated transaction type description (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the session state persistence step (COMMON-RETURN) and appends program-specific data into the combined workspace communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire program-specific state data area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be copied into the combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA) starting immediately after the end of the general session data area (at offset: LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1), for a length equal to the size of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, so that all screen state flags and transaction type data values are preserved contiguously in the combined area for the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Append Program-Specific Transaction Type State Data into Combined Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program-specific state data for the Transaction Type Update screen (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), which includes the current screen state flags, the transaction type code being worked on, and the transaction type description (both old/original and new/updated values), must be appended into the combined workspace communication area immediately after the general session data, so the program can resume from the correct state on the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The combined workspace communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully populated with both the general session data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific state data (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), and the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) identifies this Transaction Type Update screen transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes the CICS RETURN command at the end of COMMON-RETURN
