Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control must be returned to CICS specifying: the same transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) so the Transaction Type Update screen remains active and will be re-invoked on the next user action, the full combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) as the COMMAREA to be passed to the next invocation, and the exact byte length of WS-COMMAREA as the LENGTH parameter, ensuring the complete state (general session context plus program-specific screen state, transaction type code, and transaction type description) is available when the user next interacts with the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to CICS with Full Combined Communication Area for Next User Interaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all session state data has been assembled into the combined workspace communication area, control must be returned to CICS specifying the same transaction ID so the screen remains active and ready for the next user interaction, passing the full combined communication area so all state is available when the user next interacts with the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record and pressed F5 to save, and the system attempts to update the TRANSACTION_TYPE table with the new TR_DESCRIPTION for the matching TR_TYPE code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a lock conflict error (record is currently held by another user's active transaction) during the UPDATE attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the save attempt as failed due to a lock conflict, (2) set the program state to 'Changes Could Not Be Applied Due to Lock' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR), and (3) NOT commit the transaction or apply any changes to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Record Lock Conflict During Transaction Type Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to save confirmed changes to a Transaction Type record, the system must detect if the record is currently locked by another user (concurrent access conflict) and handle it appropriately without saving.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected a record lock conflict (SQLCODE -911) during an attempt to update the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, and the program state has been set to 'Changes Could Not Be Applied Due to Lock' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the informational message for the screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the information message to a failure notification (INFORM-FAILURE) indicating that the update could not be completed, and this failure message must be displayed in the information message area (INFOMSGO) of the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Lock Conflict Failure Notification Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a record lock conflict is detected during a Transaction Type update attempt, the system must prepare and display an appropriate failure notification message to inform the user that the record could not be updated due to concurrent access.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is 'Changes Could Not Be Applied Due to Lock' (TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-LOCK-ERROR) after a failed update attempt due to a concurrent access conflict
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the screen attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) protect ALL input fields (Transaction Type Code field TRTYPCDA and Transaction Type Description field TRTYDSCA and Information Message field INFOMSGA are all set to protected/read-only), (2) NOT activate the F5 Save key (F5 is only highlighted when state is CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED or DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, neither of which applies here), and (3) NOT activate the F12 Cancel key (F12 is only highlighted for CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, SHOW-DETAILS, DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, CONFIRM-DELETE, or CREATE-NEW-RECORD states)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect All Screen Fields After Lock Conflict - No Save Option Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a lock conflict failure, the screen must be displayed with all input fields protected (read-only) and no save option (F5) available, preventing the user from attempting another save directly from the failure screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is displaying a lock conflict failure message with program state 'TTUP-CHANGES-FAILED' (which encompasses the lock error and other failure states) and all fields are protected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user interacts with the screen on the next program entry (e.g., presses a key to proceed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must reset the program to the initial entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) and set the details state to 'Not Fetched' (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED = TRUE), effectively returning the user to a clean search screen where they can re-enter a Transaction Type code to search and retry the update

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset to Search State After Lock Conflict on Next Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a lock conflict failure is displayed, when the user returns to the screen (next interaction), the program must automatically reset to the initial search state so the user can re-enter the Transaction Type code and retry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pending confirmed changes (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED state) and the Transaction Type code input is not valid or the user presses F12 to cancel
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the cancel action in the action decision logic (2000-DECIDE-ACTION) and the transaction type filter is not valid
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set a 'Update Was Cancelled' indicator (WS-UPDATE-WAS-CANCELLED = TRUE), (2) set the program state to 'Changes Backed Out' (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT = TRUE), and (3) redisplay the screen showing the original database values, effectively returning the user to the search/view state so they can retry later

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cancel Lock Conflict and Return to Search via F12
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user is in a state where changes were pending confirmation (prior to the lock conflict scenario) and presses F12, the system cancels the pending update and returns to the search state, allowing the user to start over.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been reset to the initial search state (TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) following a lock conflict failure, with the Transaction Type Code field editable (set to DFHBMFSE - unprotected with cursor)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters a Transaction Type code and presses ENTER to search
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) validate that the entered Transaction Type code is numeric, non-zero, and exactly 2 digits (zero-padded if needed, e.g., '5' becomes '05'), (2) search the TRANSACTION_TYPE table for an exact match on TR_TYPE, (3) if found, display the current record values and set state to 'Show Details' (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS), and (4) position the cursor on the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCL = -1) so the user can re-enter their changes and attempt the save again

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retry Save by Re-entering Transaction Type Code After Lock Conflict
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a lock conflict failure, the user can retry the save by re-entering the Transaction Type code to search for the record again, then re-entering their changes and confirming the save.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An informational message text (WS-INFO-MSG) has been selected based on the current program state and is ready to be formatted for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the display length of the message by trimming all trailing spaces from WS-INFO-MSG and measuring the length of the remaining text
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The actual message length (WS-STRING-LEN) is stored as the count of non-trailing-space characters in the informational message, representing only the meaningful content to be displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Measure Actual Information Message Length After Trimming
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before centering the informational message on screen, the system determines the actual printable length of the message by removing trailing spaces and measuring only the meaningful content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The actual message length (WS-STRING-LEN) has been determined by trimming trailing spaces, and the total available display field length for the information message (WS-INFO-MSG full field length) is known
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system computes the center starting position using the formula: (Total Display Field Length minus Actual Message Length) divided by 2, plus 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The calculated center starting position (WS-STRING-MID) represents the character position within the display area at which the message text must begin so that it appears horizontally centered on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Calculate Center Starting Position for Information Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system calculates the exact starting position within the screen display area where the message text should begin so that it appears visually centered to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The actual message length (WS-STRING-LEN) and the center starting position (WS-STRING-MID) have both been calculated, and the output display buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system copies the message content from WS-INFO-MSG starting at position 1 for a length of WS-STRING-LEN characters into the output buffer WS-STRING-OUT starting at position WS-STRING-MID for a length of WS-STRING-LEN characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The output display buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) contains the message text placed at the center position, with surrounding positions remaining as spaces, producing a visually centered message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Information Message Text at Calculated Center Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system positions the trimmed message text into the output display buffer starting at the pre-calculated center position, ensuring the message appears centered within the available screen area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The output display buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) contains the informational message text correctly positioned at the calculated center location within the available display area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system moves the contents of the output display buffer (WS-STRING-OUT) into the screen information message output field (INFOMSGO of CTRTUPAO)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen information message field (INFOMSGO) contains the centered message text and is ready to be rendered on the user's screen during the next screen send operation, displaying the message centered within the information message area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Centered Information Message into Screen Display Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully centered and formatted informational message is transferred from the internal output buffer into the actual screen map field so it is presented to the user on the next screen send.

Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the key press as the ENTER key indicator (CCARD-AID-ENTER is set to TRUE), making it available for subsequent PF key validation and action routing

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key indicator has been successfully set to TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the PF Key Validation step (0001-CHECK-PFKEYS) where the recorded key indicator will be evaluated against the current screen state to determine if the key press is a valid action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to PF Key Validation After Key Indicator is Recorded
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once any terminal key press has been captured and recorded as a standardized internal key indicator, the system proceeds to the PF key validation step to determine whether the pressed key is valid for the current screen state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the validation process for the Transaction Type Code field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Default the Transaction Type Code status to INVALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK), (2) Identify the field under validation as 'Tran Type code', (3) Load the entered Transaction Type Code value (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) into the validation working area (WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY), and (4) Set the expected field length to 2 characters (WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-LENGTH = 2), before proceeding to individual validation checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Transaction Type Code Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating the Transaction Type Code entered by the user, the system prepares the validation context by defaulting the code status to INVALID, setting the field name to 'Tran Type code', loading the entered value into the validation area, and setting the expected length to 2 characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and has submitted the screen (pressed ENTER or a valid PF key)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type Code field contains LOW-VALUES, spaces only, or has a trimmed length of zero (i.e., is effectively blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Input Error flag (INPUT-ERROR) to TRUE, (2) Mark the Transaction Type Code flag as BLANK (FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK), (3) Display the error message 'Tran Type code must be supplied.' to the user (stored in WS-RETURN-MSG, only if no prior error message exists), and (4) Stop further validation of this field immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Supplied
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Code is a mandatory field. If the user submits the screen without entering a Transaction Type Code, or enters only spaces, the system must reject the input with a specific error message indicating the field is required.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Transaction Type Code value (up to 2 characters) fails the numeric test — meaning it contains one or more non-numeric characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Input Error flag (INPUT-ERROR) to TRUE, (2) Mark the Transaction Type Code flag as NOT OK (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), (3) Display the error message 'Tran Type code must be numeric.' to the user (stored in WS-RETURN-MSG, only if no prior error message exists), and (4) Stop further validation of this field immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Be Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Code must consist entirely of numeric digits. If the entered value contains any non-numeric characters (letters, special characters, etc.), the system must reject the input with a specific error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a non-blank, numeric Transaction Type Code on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The numeric value of the entered Transaction Type Code evaluates to zero (e.g., '0' or '00')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Input Error flag (INPUT-ERROR) to TRUE, (2) Mark the Transaction Type Code flag as NOT OK (FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK), (3) Display the error message 'Tran Type code must not be zero.' to the user (stored in WS-RETURN-MSG, only if no prior error message exists), and (4) Stop further validation of this field immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Must Not Be Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: Even if the Transaction Type Code is numeric, a value of zero (0 or 00) is not a valid Transaction Type Code. The system must reject zero as an invalid code with a specific error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a Transaction Type Code that is non-blank, fully numeric, and not equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All three validation checks (blank, numeric, zero) have passed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the Transaction Type Code filter flag to VALID (FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID = TRUE), indicating the code is acceptable for further processing (e.g., database search or save operation)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Type Code Passes All Validations — Mark as Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type Code passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, non-zero), the system marks the code as valid, enabling subsequent processing such as database lookup or record creation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code has passed all validation checks and is marked as VALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID = TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the validated Transaction Type Code for formatting
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Convert the entered Transaction Type Code to its numeric value using NUMVAL function, (2) Move the numeric value to a 2-character alphanumeric field (WS-EDIT-ALPHANUMERIC-2), (3) Replace all spaces in that field with zeros (leading zero padding), and (4) Store the resulting zero-padded 2-digit code back into the Transaction Type Code working field (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE), so that, for example, an entry of '5' becomes '05' and '1' becomes '01'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Transaction Type Code with Leading Zeros
all_rules.Rule_Description: A valid Transaction Type Code must always be stored and used as a 2-digit zero-padded number. If the user enters a single digit (e.g., '5'), the system automatically formats it to its 2-digit equivalent (e.g., '05') before using it for any database operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Code validation routine (1245-EDIT-NUM-REQD) has completed execution — either successfully or with an error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Control returns from the numeric validation routine to the Transaction Type Code validation procedure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the validation outcome flags from the generic alphanumeric validation flags (WS-EDIT-ALPHANUM-ONLY-FLAGS) into the Transaction Type Code-specific flag (WS-EDIT-TTYP-FLAG), so that the Transaction Type Code field is correctly marked as either VALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-ISVALID) or INVALID (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK / FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK) for use by downstream screen attribute and error display logic

all_rules.Rule_Name: Propagate Transaction Type Code Validation Result
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the numeric validation routine completes, the resulting validation status flags (valid, blank, or not-ok) are transferred from the generic validation working area back to the Transaction Type Code-specific flag, so that subsequent screen display and processing logic can correctly respond to the validation outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered or modified a Transaction Type Description on the Transaction Type Update screen, and changes have been detected between the old and new description values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the Transaction Description validation process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the field label to 'Transaction Desc', load the new description value (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE-DESC) into the validation work area, and set the maximum validation length to 50 characters before performing any validation checks

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Up Transaction Description Validation Parameters
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating the Transaction Description, the system prepares the validation context by identifying the field name as 'Transaction Desc', loading the user-entered description value, and setting the maximum allowable length to 50 characters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update screen and has submitted a Transaction Type Description value for validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The description field contains only spaces, is entirely empty (low-values), or has zero non-space characters after trimming
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the overall input as invalid, (2) mark the description field specifically as blank, and (3) display the error message 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Description Must Not Be Blank or Missing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Description is a mandatory field. The system must reject any submission where the description is blank, contains only spaces, or is entirely empty (low-values). The error message must clearly identify the field and the requirement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a non-blank Transaction Type Description on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: After removing all valid alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers) from the description, any non-space characters still remain within the 50-character validation length
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the overall input as invalid, (2) mark the description field as containing invalid characters, and (3) display the error message 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Description Must Contain Only Alphanumeric Characters
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Type Description may only contain letters (A-Z, a-z) and digits (0-9). Any special characters, punctuation, or symbols are not permitted. The system validates this by converting all valid alphanumeric characters to spaces and checking if any non-alphanumeric characters remain.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Description has been submitted for validation on the Transaction Type Update screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The description is non-blank AND contains only alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers) within the 50-character limit
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the description validation flag as valid (FLG-ALPHNANUM-ISVALID), indicating the description field has passed all validation requirements

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Transaction Description as Valid When All Checks Pass
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type Description passes all validation checks — it is non-blank and contains only alphanumeric characters — the system marks the description field as valid, allowing the process to proceed to the final outcome determination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Description validation process has completed and the description validation flags have been stored in the description flag work area (WS-EDIT-DESC-FLAGS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether any input errors were found during the description validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If no input errors exist: the system must set the program state to 'Changes OK - Pending Confirmation' (TTUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED), indicating the changes are valid and ready for the user to confirm before saving; If input errors exist: the system must keep the program state as 'Changes Not OK' (TTUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK), requiring the user to correct the description before proceeding

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Transaction Update State Based on Description Validation Outcome
all_rules.Rule_Description: After completing the Transaction Description validation, the system evaluates the overall validation result to determine the next program state. If validation passed, the changes are marked as ready for user confirmation before saving. If validation failed, the program remains in an error state requiring the user to correct the description.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has retrieved a Transaction Type record and has submitted the screen with potentially modified values for Transaction Type Code and/or Transaction Type Description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the process of comparing the newly entered values against the original values fetched from the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The comparison status is initialized to 'No Changes Found' as the default starting state before any field-level comparison is evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Comparison Status Before Evaluating Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before comparing new user-entered values against the original database values, the comparison status is initialized to 'No Changes Found' as the default assumption. This ensures a clean baseline before any field-level comparisons are performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The comparison status has been initialized to 'No Changes Found', and both the original Transaction Type Code (from the database) and the newly entered Transaction Type Code (from the screen) are available for comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a case-insensitive comparison between the new Transaction Type Code and the original Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the two Transaction Type Codes differ (case-insensitively), the system immediately sets the status to 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process without evaluating the description; if they match, the system proceeds to compare the Transaction Type Descriptions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Transaction Type Codes Case-Insensitively to Detect Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system compares the newly entered Transaction Type Code against the original Transaction Type Code retrieved from the database. The comparison is performed in a case-insensitive manner. If the codes differ, a change is immediately flagged without evaluating the description fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Codes have been confirmed to match, and both the original Transaction Type Description (from the database) and the newly entered Transaction Type Description (from the screen) are available for comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a case-insensitive comparison between the trimmed new Transaction Type Description and the trimmed original Transaction Type Description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the trimmed descriptions differ (case-insensitively), the system sets the status to 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process without evaluating description lengths; if they match, the system proceeds to compare the trimmed description lengths

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Transaction Type Descriptions Case-Insensitively After Trimming Whitespace
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming the Transaction Type Codes match, the system compares the newly entered Transaction Type Description against the original description from the database. Both descriptions are trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace before the case-insensitive comparison is performed. If the trimmed descriptions differ, a change is flagged.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the Transaction Type Codes and the trimmed case-insensitive descriptions have been confirmed to match, and the trimmed lengths of both the new and original Transaction Type Descriptions are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the character length of the trimmed new Transaction Type Description against the character length of the trimmed original Transaction Type Description
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the trimmed lengths differ, the system sets the status to 'Change Has Occurred' and exits the comparison process; if the trimmed lengths are equal, the system proceeds to evaluate whether all three conditions collectively confirm no changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Trimmed Description Lengths to Detect Whitespace-Only Differences
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming the trimmed descriptions match case-insensitively, the system additionally compares the character lengths of the trimmed new and original descriptions. This extra length check ensures that descriptions that appear identical after trimming but have different effective content lengths are still correctly identified as changed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The comparison of Transaction Type Code (case-insensitive), Transaction Type Description (case-insensitive, trimmed), and trimmed Description Length between the newly entered values and the original database values has been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All three conditions are simultaneously true: the Transaction Type Codes match case-insensitively, AND the trimmed descriptions match case-insensitively, AND the trimmed description lengths are equal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the comparison status to 'No Changes Detected', indicating the user has not made any effective modifications, and no database update action will be triggered for this record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm No Changes When All Three Comparison Conditions Are Satisfied
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all three comparison conditions are simultaneously satisfied — the Transaction Type Codes match case-insensitively, the trimmed descriptions match case-insensitively, and the trimmed description lengths are equal — the system confirms that the user has made no effective modifications to the record. The status is set to 'No Changes Detected', which prevents an unnecessary database update from being triggered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is comparing the newly entered Transaction Type Code and Transaction Type Description against the original values retrieved from the database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: At least one of the following conditions is true: the Transaction Type Codes differ (case-insensitively), OR the trimmed Transaction Type Descriptions differ (case-insensitively), OR the trimmed description lengths differ
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the comparison status to 'Change Has Occurred', indicating the user has made at least one effective modification, and the comparison process exits immediately to proceed with validating and confirming the detected changes before any database update is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Change Has Occurred When Any Comparison Condition Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: If any one of the three comparison conditions fails — the Transaction Type Codes differ, or the trimmed descriptions differ case-insensitively, or the trimmed description lengths differ — the system sets the status to 'Change Has Occurred'. This triggers the downstream validation and confirmation workflow to process the user's modifications before saving to the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a Transaction Type Code on the screen and the system is ready to perform a database lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the Transaction Type lookup process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system uses the user-entered Transaction Type Code (TTUP-NEW-TTYP-TYPE) as the exact search key by assigning it to the database query parameter (DCL-TR-TYPE) before querying the TRANSACTION_TYPE table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Entered Transaction Type Code as Database Search Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system uses the Transaction Type Code entered by the user as the exact search key to query the TRANSACTION_TYPE table. The entered code is moved directly into the database host variable before the query is executed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user-entered Transaction Type Code has been assigned as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes a SELECT query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using an exact match condition on TR_TYPE equal to the entered code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves both the TR_TYPE (Transaction Type Code) and TR_DESCRIPTION (Transaction Type Description) fields from the matching record, if one exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Query TRANSACTION_TYPE Table by Transaction Type Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system queries the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE database table to retrieve the Transaction Type Code (TR_TYPE) and its Description (TR_DESCRIPTION) for the exact Transaction Type Code provided by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has executed a query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the entered Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The query returns a matching record (successful retrieval with no errors)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the indicator FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE to TRUE, confirming that the Transaction Type Code and its Description have been successfully retrieved from the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Successful Transaction Type Record Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database query returns a matching record for the entered Transaction Type Code, the system marks the lookup as successful, indicating the transaction type exists and its details are available for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has executed a query against the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the entered Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The query returns a 'no data found' result indicating no record exists for the entered Transaction Type Code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the input to an error state, marks the transaction type filter as not valid (FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK), and sets the message indicator to 'Record Not Found' to inform the user that no matching transaction type exists in the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Transaction Type Record Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the database query finds no matching record for the entered Transaction Type Code, the system marks the search as unsuccessful and sets an informational message to notify the user that the record does not exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The database query has successfully retrieved a Transaction Type record with its Code (TR_TYPE) and Description (TR_DESCRIPTION)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the fetched data into the working storage area for original values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system saves the retrieved Transaction Type Code into TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE and saves the retrieved Transaction Type Description (trimmed to its actual stored length as indicated by DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN) into TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE-DESC, making both values available for screen display and future change-detection comparison

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Retrieved Transaction Type Details for Display and Comparison
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Transaction Type record is successfully found, the system saves the retrieved Transaction Type Code and Description as the original (old) values. These stored values are used for screen display and to detect any subsequent changes made by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type lookup has completed and the FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE indicator is set to TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the lookup within the action decision logic
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS, which prepares the screen to display the retrieved Transaction Type Code and Description to the user and enables edit and delete options

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Screen State to Show Details After Successful Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a Transaction Type record is successfully found and its details are stored, the system transitions the screen state to 'Show Details', enabling the user to view the record and take further actions such as editing or deleting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type lookup has completed and the FOUND-TRANTYPE-IN-TABLE indicator is NOT set to TRUE (record was not found in the database)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the lookup within the action decision logic
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen state to TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, which prepares the screen to inform the user that no matching Transaction Type exists and activates the option (PF5) for the user to create a new Transaction Type record using the entered code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Screen State to Record Not Found After Unsuccessful Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type lookup finds no matching record, the system transitions the screen state to 'Details Not Found', which informs the user that the entered Transaction Type Code does not exist and offers the option to create a new record with that code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is one of: (1) Details Not Fetched - no search has been performed yet, (2) Details Not Found - the searched Transaction Type Code does not exist in the TRANSACTION_TYPE table, (3) Invalid Search Keys - the entered Transaction Type Code failed validation, (4) Transaction Type Filter is flagged as Not OK - the code is non-numeric or zero, OR (5) Transaction Type Filter is flagged as Blank - no code was entered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL set to -1), prompting the user to enter or correct the Transaction Type Code to initiate or retry a search

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioned on Transaction Type Code Field When Search Input Is Needed or Invalid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in a state where the user needs to provide or correct a Transaction Type Code for searching (no details fetched, record not found, invalid or blank search key, or search filter error), the cursor is automatically placed on the Transaction Type Code field to guide the user to enter a valid search value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is Changes Backed Out (user cancelled a pending update or delete), AND the previously stored original Transaction Type Code (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE) contains either LOW-VALUES or SPACES, meaning no prior record data is available to restore
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL set to -1), prompting the user to enter a new Transaction Type Code to start a fresh search, since there is no prior record to return to

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioned on Transaction Type Code Field When Changes Are Backed Out With No Prior Record Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user cancels an in-progress operation (changes backed out) but there is no previously fetched record data available (the old Transaction Type Code is empty or blank), the cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field to prompt the user to start a fresh search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is Changes Okayed And Done, meaning the update or insert to the TRANSACTION_TYPE table was completed successfully and committed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL set to -1), signalling that the update is complete and the screen is ready for the user to search for another Transaction Type Code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioned on Transaction Type Code Field After Successful Update
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a Transaction Type record has been successfully updated or inserted, the cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field to allow the user to perform a new search or look up another transaction type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is one of: (1) Create New Record - user is entering a new transaction type, (2) No Changes Detected - the entered description is identical to the existing one, (3) Description field flagged as Not OK - description contains invalid characters, (4) Description field flagged as Blank - description was not provided, (5) Changes Made - user has made modifications, (6) Changes Backed Out - user cancelled changes but prior record data exists (TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE is not LOW-VALUES or SPACES), OR (7) Show Details - the fetched record is being displayed for potential editing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Transaction Type Description field (TRTYDSCL set to -1), directing the user's attention to enter, review, or correct the description value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioned on Description Field When Description Input or Correction Is Required
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in a state where the user needs to enter, review, or correct the Transaction Type Description — such as when creating a new record, when no changes were detected, when description validation failed, when changes are in progress, when details are being shown, or when changes were backed out with prior record data available — the cursor is placed on the Description field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state does not match any of the explicitly defined cursor positioning conditions: not Details Not Fetched, not Details Not Found, not Invalid Search Keys, not Filter Not OK, not Filter Blank, not Changes Okayed And Done, not Changes Backed Out with no prior data, not Create New Record, not No Changes Detected, not Description Not OK, not Description Blank, not Changes Made, not Changes Backed Out with prior data, and not Show Details
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display and cursor positioning is being determined
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor must default to the Transaction Type Code field (TRTYPCDL set to -1) as the standard fallback positioning, ensuring the user always has a defined field to interact with regardless of the program state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Defaults to Transaction Type Code Field for All Other Unspecified States
all_rules.Rule_Description: For any screen state not explicitly handled by the cursor positioning rules above, the cursor defaults to the Transaction Type Code field as a safe fallback, ensuring the user always has a clear starting point for interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display after any user interaction, and the program has evaluated all current state flags including: TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, TTUP-DETAILS-NOT-FOUND, TTUP-INVALID-SEARCH-KEYS, FLG-TRANFILTER-NOT-OK, FLG-TRANFILTER-BLANK, TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT with TTUP-OLD-TTYP-TYPE value, TTUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE, TTUP-CREATE-NEW-RECORD, NO-CHANGES-DETECTED, FLG-DESCRIPTION-NOT-OK, FLG-DESCRIPTION-BLANK, TTUP-CHANGES-MADE, and TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The cursor positioning logic evaluates all state flags in priority order using an EVALUATE TRUE construct
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Exactly one cursor position is selected: (1) Transaction Type Code field when search input is needed or invalid (highest priority), (2) Transaction Type Code field when changes are backed out with no prior record data, (3) Transaction Type Code field when update was just completed successfully, (4) Description field when description input or correction is needed, OR (5) Transaction Type Code field as the default fallback for all other states — ensuring the screen is always ready for the user's next appropriate action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Overall Cursor Placement Determination Based on Program State Hierarchy
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor placement on the Transaction Type Update screen is determined by evaluating a prioritized hierarchy of program state flags. The evaluation follows a specific order: search-needed states take highest priority, followed by backed-out-with-no-data, then successful update, then description-related states, and finally a default fallback. This ensures the cursor always guides the user to the most relevant field for their next action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display in any program state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen field protection attributes are being set up
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All three fields — Transaction Type Code, Transaction Description, and Info Message Area — must be set to protected (read-only) as the baseline before any state-specific rules are applied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Lock All Fields as Read-Only Before State-Based Unlocking
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying any state-specific field access rules, all input fields on the Transaction Type Update screen are locked as read-only by default. This ensures no field is accidentally left open for editing unless explicitly permitted by the current program state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Details Not Fetched (initial search), Invalid Search Keys, Details Not Found, or Changes Backed Out with no prior Transaction Type data (old type code is LOW-VALUES or SPACES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field must be set to unprotected (open for user input), allowing the user to enter a Transaction Type code to search; all other fields remain read-only

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Transaction Type Code Field for Input During Search States
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in a state that requires the user to enter or re-enter a Transaction Type code for searching — including the initial search state, invalid search key state, record not found state, or when changes were backed out and no prior record data exists — the Transaction Type Code field must be made editable while all other fields remain read-only.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Show Details, Changes Not OK, Create New Record, or Changes Backed Out with prior Transaction Type data present (old type code is not LOW-VALUES and not SPACES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Description field must be set to unprotected (open for user input) to allow the user to enter or modify the description; the Transaction Type Code field and Info Message Area must remain read-only (protected)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Transaction Description Field for Editing During Data Entry States
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is displaying an existing record for editing, showing validation errors, allowing creation of a new record, or restoring after a cancelled change where prior data exists, the Transaction Description field must be made editable. The Transaction Type Code field remains read-only (the key cannot be changed), and the Info Message Area remains read-only.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Changes OK Not Confirmed (pending save), Changes Okayed And Done (saved successfully), or Delete In Progress
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields — Transaction Type Code, Transaction Description, and Info Message Area — must remain protected (read-only); no field is opened for user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Keep All Fields Locked During Confirmation and Completion States
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is in a state where changes have been confirmed and are pending save, have already been saved successfully, or a delete operation is in progress, no user input is permitted. All fields remain locked as read-only to prevent any modification during these transitional states.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state does not match any of the explicitly defined states (not: Details Not Fetched, Invalid Search Keys, Details Not Found, Changes Backed Out, Show Details, Changes Not OK, Create New Record, Changes OK Not Confirmed, Changes Okayed And Done, Delete In Progress)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field must be set to unprotected (open for user input) and the cursor must be positioned on the Transaction Type Code field as the default fallback

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Cursor to Transaction Type Code Field for Unrecognized States
all_rules.Rule_Description: For any program state not explicitly handled by the field protection rules, the system defaults to positioning the cursor on the Transaction Type Code field, ensuring the user can always initiate a search even in unexpected situations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes are being configured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type code filter flag is set to 'Not OK' (validation failed — code is non-numeric, zero, or blank) OR the current state is Delete Failed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field color attribute must be set to RED to visually indicate an error condition to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Transaction Type Code Field in Red on Validation Error or Delete Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type code entered by the user fails validation (is not a valid numeric code) or when a delete operation has failed, the Transaction Type Code field must be visually highlighted in red to draw the user's attention to the problem area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes are being configured and the program is in re-entry mode (user has previously interacted with the screen)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Transaction Type code filter flag is set to 'Blank' (the user submitted the screen without entering a Transaction Type code) AND the program is in re-entry mode
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An asterisk character '*' must be displayed in the Transaction Type Code output field AND the Transaction Type Code field color attribute must be set to RED to alert the user that the field is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Asterisk Placeholder and Red Highlight When Transaction Type Code Was Left Blank on Return
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user returns to the screen (re-entry mode) and the Transaction Type Code field was left blank in the previous interaction, the system must display an asterisk '*' as a visual placeholder in the field and highlight it in red, prompting the user to provide the required search key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes have been configured including any error highlighting
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Details Not Fetched, Details Not Found, Invalid Search Keys; OR the Transaction Type code filter flag is Blank or Not OK
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Field attribute setup must terminate immediately without performing any additional cursor positioning logic; the cursor remains on the Transaction Type Code field as already set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Further Cursor Refinement When Screen is in Search-Required or Error State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in a state where the user needs to enter a Transaction Type code (initial search, not found, invalid keys) or when the Transaction Type code field has a validation error (blank or invalid), no further cursor refinement is needed — the cursor is already correctly positioned on the Transaction Type Code field and processing of field attributes ends.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes have been fully configured and the early-exit condition was not triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any of the following conditions are true: the Description field has a validation error (blank or invalid characters), no changes were detected between old and new values, changes have been made (TTUP-CHANGES-MADE), changes were backed out (TTUP-CHANGES-BACKED-OUT), or the screen is showing existing record details (TTUP-SHOW-DETAILS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor must be positioned on the Transaction Description field (cursor length set to -1 for the description field); otherwise, the cursor must be positioned on the Transaction Type Code field (cursor length set to -1 for the type code field)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Refine Cursor Position to Description Field Based on Editing Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: After passing the early-exit check, the system performs a final cursor refinement. When the context indicates the user needs to work with the description field — such as a description validation error, no changes were detected, changes were made or backed out, or details are being shown — the cursor is moved to the Transaction Description field. Otherwise, the cursor defaults to the Transaction Type Code field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes are being configured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state is one of: Details Not Fetched, Details Not Found, Invalid Search Keys, Transaction Type filter flag is Not OK or Blank, Changes Okayed And Done, Changes Backed Out with no prior data (old type code is LOW-VALUES or SPACES), or any unrecognized state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Type Code field must be set to -1, directing the cursor to that field when the screen is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field for Search and Error Recovery
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor is directed to the Transaction Type Code field when the user needs to enter or correct a search key. This applies during initial search, after invalid search keys, when a record was not found, when changes were backed out with no prior data, after a successful save, or in any default/unrecognized state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen field attributes are being configured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current program state or condition is one of: Create New Record, Description validation error (blank or invalid), No Changes Detected, Changes Made (TTUP-CHANGES-MADE), Changes Backed Out with prior data present, or Show Details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length indicator for the Transaction Description field must be set to -1, directing the cursor to that field when the screen is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor on Transaction Description Field for Data Entry and Editing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor is directed to the Transaction Description field when the user is expected to enter or modify the description. This applies when creating a new record, when description validation has failed, when no changes were detected, when changes have been made or backed out with prior data, or when existing record details are being shown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update/Maintenance screen and has either: (a) entered a Transaction Type Code that failed validation — meaning it was non-numeric, equal to zero, or otherwise invalid — setting the 'Transaction Type Code Validation Failed' flag; OR (b) a delete operation was attempted on the currently displayed Transaction Type record and that delete operation failed, setting the 'Delete Failed' state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display after processing the user's input or the failed delete operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field on the screen is highlighted in red color to visually indicate the error condition to the user; no asterisk placeholder is added by this rule alone; the red highlighting applies regardless of whether the failure was due to invalid input or a failed delete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Red Highlighting to Transaction Type Code Field on Validation Failure or Delete Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Type Code entered by the user fails validation (is not a valid numeric, non-zero, 2-digit code) or when a delete operation on a Transaction Type record has failed, the Transaction Type Code field on the screen must be visually highlighted in red to alert the user to the error condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update/Maintenance screen in a re-entry state (the program has been previously entered and is now being re-entered, meaning this is not the very first interaction with the screen) AND the Transaction Type Code field was left blank by the user — meaning the field contained no value, spaces, or low-values — setting the 'Transaction Type Code Blank' flag
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Type Code field is populated with an asterisk character ('*') as a visual placeholder to indicate that input is required, AND the Transaction Type Code field is highlighted in red color; both the asterisk placeholder and the red color are applied together as a combined visual indicator that the field is mandatory and was left empty

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Asterisk Placeholder in Red for Blank Transaction Type Code During Re-entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has left the Transaction Type Code field blank and the screen is in a re-entry state (the user has already interacted with the screen at least once and is returning to it), the system must display an asterisk ('*') as a placeholder in the Transaction Type Code field and highlight that field in red, prompting the user that a value is required.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Type Update/Maintenance screen AND the Transaction Type Code validation has not failed (the 'Transaction Type Code Validation Failed' flag is not set) AND no delete operation failure has occurred (the 'Delete Failed' state is not active) AND it is NOT the case that both the Transaction Type Code field is blank AND the screen is in a re-entry state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen attributes for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No red color highlighting is applied to the Transaction Type Code field; no asterisk placeholder is inserted into the Transaction Type Code field; the field is displayed in its default color and appearance without any error indicators

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Error Color Applied to Transaction Type Code Field When No Error Conditions Are Present
all_rules.Rule_Description: When neither a Transaction Type Code validation failure, nor a delete operation failure, nor a blank field during re-entry condition is present, the Transaction Type Code field is displayed without any error color highlighting, retaining its default appearance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is one of: Details Not Fetched (initial/reset state), Invalid Search Keys (type code failed validation), Record Not Found (search returned no match), OR Changes Backed Out where no prior Transaction Type Code was loaded (old Transaction Type Code is empty or blank)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display and determines where to position the cursor
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field, prompting the user to enter or correct the Transaction Type Code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field When No Record Context Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in a state where no transaction type record has been loaded or the search criteria are missing or invalid, the cursor must be automatically positioned on the Transaction Type Code field to guide the user to enter or correct the search key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is Changes Saved Successfully (update or insert was committed to the database)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display and determines where to position the cursor
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field After Successful Save
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a Transaction Type record has been successfully updated or inserted, the cursor is repositioned on the Transaction Type Code field, allowing the user to initiate a new search or review the saved record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state is one of: Creating New Record (user is entering a new transaction type), No Changes Detected (user submitted without modifying any data), Description Validation Failed — either Description is invalid (non-alphanumeric characters) or Description is blank/empty, Changes Made (edits are in progress), Changes Backed Out where a prior Transaction Type Code was loaded (old Transaction Type Code is not empty), OR Showing Details (an existing record is displayed for review or editing)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display and determines where to position the cursor
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor is placed on the Transaction Description field, directing the user to enter or correct the transaction description

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Cursor on Transaction Description Field When Record Is Loaded or Description Needs Attention
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction type record is currently displayed, being created, or when the description field requires user attention due to validation errors or no changes being detected, the cursor is automatically positioned on the Transaction Description field to guide the user to the appropriate input area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Type Update screen is active and the current program state does not match any of the following: Details Not Fetched, Invalid Search Keys, Record Not Found, Changes Backed Out with no prior record, Changes Saved Successfully, Creating New Record, No Changes Detected, Description Invalid, Description Blank, Changes Made, Changes Backed Out with prior record, or Showing Details
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display and determines where to position the cursor
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor is placed on the Transaction Type Code field as the default fallback position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Cursor on Transaction Type Code Field as Default Fallback
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the current program state does not match any of the specifically handled cursor-positioning conditions, the system defaults to placing the cursor on the Transaction Type Code field as a safe fallback to ensure the user always has a field focused for input.

description:
COTRTUPC is an online CICS program that manages the maintenance of Transaction Type records in the CardDemo application, supporting search, display, create, update, and delete operations on the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE DB2 table. The program presents a BMS screen to the user, validates inputs such as transaction type code and description, and guides the user through a multi-step confirmation workflow before committing or rolling back changes to the database.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: DB2 - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize working storage areas, set transaction ID context, and clear any existing error messages at program startup 2: Communication Area Processing - Restore previously saved session context (commarea) including program state flags and transaction type data from prior interactions, or initialize fresh context for new sessions 3: PF Key Validation - Validate that the function key pressed by the user is appropriate for the current screen state and context; mark key as valid or invalid accordingly 4: State Reset on Completion - Automatically reset the screen state to initial entry mode when certain terminal conditions are met such as successful update, successful delete, failed operations, or user cancellation from specific states 5: Exit and Return to Calling Program - When user presses F3, navigate back to the calling program (admin menu or list screen) by transferring control via XCTL, committing any pending work before exit 6: Initial Screen Display - When entering the program fresh or from admin/list program, clear all data and display an empty transaction type search screen prompting the user to enter a transaction type code 7: Delete Confirmation Processing - When user presses F4 after being shown the delete confirmation prompt, execute the actual deletion of the transaction type record from the database 8: Delete Confirmation Request - When user presses F4 while viewing transaction type details, prompt the user to confirm the deletion before proceeding 9: New Record Creation Initiation - When user presses F5 after a record is not found, transition to new record creation mode prompting user to enter details for the new transaction type 10: Save Confirmed Changes - When user presses F5 after changes have been validated and confirmed, execute the database write (update or insert) to persist the transaction type changes 11: Cancel Action - When user presses F12 during confirmation, delete confirmation, or detail view states, cancel the pending action and return to an appropriate prior state 12: Invalid Key Handling - When an invalid function key is pressed, redisplay the current screen with an appropriate invalid key message without changing data state 13: User Input Processing - Receive user input from the screen, store the entered values, and perform validation edits on the transaction type code and description fields 14: Receive Screen Input - Accept and capture all field values entered by the user from the transaction type update screen map 15: Store Screen Input to Working Variables - Transfer the received screen field values (transaction type code and description) into internal working storage variables for processing, handling special characters like asterisk and spaces 16: Transaction Type Code Validation - Validate that the transaction type code entered is numeric, non-blank, and non-zero; format it with leading zeros if valid 17: Transaction Description Validation - Validate that the transaction description is supplied and contains only alphanumeric characters within the allowed 50-character length 18: Change Detection - Compare the newly entered transaction type details against the originally fetched values to determine if any actual changes were made by the user 19: Action Decision Logic - Based on current program state flags and user actions, determine the next appropriate action such as fetching data, showing details, confirming changes, or handling errors 20: Transaction Type Lookup - Query the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table using the entered transaction type code to retrieve existing record details 21: Store Fetched Transaction Type Data - Save the database-retrieved transaction type code and description into the old-details working storage area for later comparison and display 22: Transaction Type Update - Execute a SQL UPDATE statement to modify the transaction type description in the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table for the specified type code 23: Transaction Type Insert - When an update finds no existing record (SQL code +100), execute a SQL INSERT to create a new transaction type record in the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table 24: Transaction Type Delete - Execute a SQL DELETE statement to remove the transaction type record from the TRANSACTION_TYPE database table, handling referential integrity constraints by informing user to delete child records first 25: Screen Initialization - Prepare the output screen map with current date, time, program name, transaction ID, and screen titles before sending to the user 26: Screen Variable Setup - Populate the screen display fields with appropriate data values based on current program state: initial empty values, original fetched values, or updated new values 27: Information Message Setup - Determine and set the appropriate informational message to display to the user based on current program state (e.g., prompts for search, confirmation requests, success or failure notifications) 28: Screen Field Attribute Setup - Set field protection attributes to control which fields are editable versus read-only based on current program state, and position the cursor to the appropriate field 29: Screen Color Attribute Setup - Set color attributes for screen fields to highlight errors (red for invalid transaction type code or failed delete) based on validation results 30: PF Key Attribute Setup - Enable or disable the display of available function key options (F4, F5, F12) on the screen based on what actions are valid in the current program state 31: Send Screen to User - Transmit the fully prepared screen map to the user terminal, erasing the previous screen content and freeing the keyboard 32: Alphanumeric Field Validation - Generic reusable validation routine that checks a field is supplied, non-blank, and contains only alphanumeric characters within a specified length 33: Numeric Field Validation - Generic reusable validation routine that checks a field is supplied, non-blank, purely numeric, and non-zero within a specified length 34: Session State Persistence - Save the current program state, transaction type data, and commarea back to the communication area before returning control to CICS for the next user interaction 35: Concurrent Update Conflict Handling - When attempting to save changes, detect if the transaction type record is locked by another user and inform the user that the record could not be updated due to a concurrent access conflict, prompting them to retry 36: Information Message Centering - Format and center the informational message text within the available display area on the screen before presenting it to the user 37: Function Key Capture - Identify and record which function key or attention key was pressed by the user (Enter, Clear, PA keys, or PF1-PF24) by mapping the terminal key press to a standardized internal key indicator for subsequent processing
